An influx of funding here, a federal grant there—we know well just how helpful our aid can be for those who see it our way, and how persuasive for those who as of yet do not. No expense will be spared to ensure that every triumph is reported on—that every failure is forgiven, all as it should be. Only then can the people cast their ballots freely, knowledgeably, and, above all, correctly.
strings.BRA_a_brush_with_god_desc:
While Adhemar de Barros's commitment to God has never been deniable, whispers now scatter throughout the public of his attendance in church services and cathedrals, and the image of a prostrating President fills the imagination. Yet those who have seen him on the ground themselves will tell you it is anything but just a show.

Having come as close to death as he has, it is clear that he has seen his life in a new light, but to speculate any further would be unfair to the man, not just on account of his dignity as a human, but as a fighter who has struggled for Brazil in every way he has been able. All the same, one must remember that they must die and live without knowing when.
strings.BRA_destinys_favourite_desc:
Whether it be the progressives or conservatives, all now kneel upon the heels of Adhemar de Barros, Brazil's greatest architect since the illustrious Vargas himself. He managed to balance the impossible forces of the impoverished and the oligarchs — two classes fundamentally conflicting, yet united in their wishes for a prosperous nation. As folks in the favela chant in jubilant rallies of the concrete towers erecting across their habitual squalor, the ordered bureaucrats at Brasília toil with boundless stamina under genuine patriotism.

No other rulers, not even Alexander and Caesar, had ever defied death so boldly as Adhemar de Barros, the President of Presidents, who now stands before everyone who worked against him in bold defiance against terrible odds. Destiny chose him, and he answered.
strings.BRA_adhemar_comfortable_retirement_desc:
God gave Adhemar a second chance. He is not yet dead, but the close call shows that it is time for him to look toward the future, where he shall reap the fruits of personal authority. For decades, Adhemar served as a dutiful servant of the masses, but what had they ever given in return? For each dollar he shall enrich himself with, he had earned it with hours of labor and gallons of sweat. Adhemar will not feel guilty for “betraying the people.” After all, he was willing to give his life for the Brazilian nation, and his survival proves that he is, in his heart, a born leader.

If anything, Adhemar is simply collecting the dues of what he had never enjoyed earlier in his presidency. His family, in particular, deserves to live comfortably in this pursuit of tranquility. From now on, nothing will stop him from getting a cozy and prosperous retirement.
strings.BRA_adhemar_call_in_all_favours_desc:
To ensure Adhemar gets the retirement he so rightly deserves, there needs to be more than just two hands free. Thankfully, while the President may be busy, so are the pages of the party's contactbooks, with friends for each step of the process. Businessmen who need rallying, reporters who need to tell it as it must be told, some old friends whose favors have yet to be redeemed - now is his hour of need, and their time has come to gracefully assist.

The road to the next election has not been paved with gold thus far, neither figuratively nor financially. With scandals and crises at every step, any lesser man would have already been overthrown by now. But Adhemar de Barros is no lesser man, and we will prove it, even after having proven so much else.
strings.BRA_adhemar_monopoly_man_desc:
The PSP campaign might as well be like the board game, for our strategy equally relies on money and property. With the stakes being so high, now is the time to make use of the cash we have been saving, or else we will find it is gone this time next year.

We can use these funds to ensure the next head of Petrobras is a PSP man while allowing the incumbent to step out without much protest. Likewise, there are other government-linked industries that may benefit from being led by those aligned to us. That is not for the public to know, however, and the media we control will do all they can to focus on the campaign to avoid any rigorous scrutiny.
strings.BRA_holiday_in_caracas_desc:
Officially, it's a trip for Adhemar to 'recuperate.' Unofficially, Caracas offers opportunities far beyond its sunlit streets. The right whispers in the right ears, a quiet meeting with the right people, and suddenly, a few well-chosen properties become available, ripe for the picking.

This trip isn't merely for rest; it's about ensuring a comfortable future, one far beyond the limits of presidency. Venezuela isn't just another South American nation; it's a safety net, a place where our beloved Adhemar can relax while his financial future is made secure.

While the public sees the President taking a break, shrewd deals and smart investments are being made behind the scenes. After all, politics is a game, and the wise player ensures his winnings are banked long after the game is over.
strings.BRA_the_brazilian_job_desc:
Now, while we are still placing a lot of emphasis on securing deals and agreements overseas, we shouldn't forget about the opportunities we still have right here in Brazil for... self-enrichment. After all, isn't it fair that the President, who has given so much for everyone, gets something back from the nation he has cared for?

Admittedly, these little, ahem, business ventures should best be taken care of quickly. All the hubbub over the election will only keep people distracted for so long, but we'll make sure to leverage our opportunities before things settle down.
strings.BRA_divert_campaign_funds_desc:
Endorsing this, touring that, who cares about the electoral campaign when it firmly favors our dear Getulinho? Financing vacations and festivities are not cheap, and the PSP treasury is one of the best places to find the money Adhemar does not have. As the person who built the foundations for the party's success, its assets are in every way, all but legally Adhemar's. Additionally, on account of being the President, who would dare to nudge him about a couple million vanishing out of sight?

Like his father, little Getulinho is a competent magician. He can muster what he needs if it's urgent enough. No one would mind whether he's scrounging that up from the dirt or relegating that responsibility to a poor clerk somewhere in the Planalto. The old man requires more funding for his endeavors than Brasília's mindless political games.
strings.BRA_friends_from_abroad_desc:
It is never good to keep all of one's eggs in one basket, and however large it may be, Brazil is still only one basket. As such, diversification of political contacts is just as important as economic ties, particularly with our removal of the needless barriers erected in between the two. Money talks, after all, loud enough to cross even the tightest of borders and the deepest of seas.

And so in the national interest, as with all other actions, wining and dining the moneyed elite of the world will be made chief priority in terms of foreign affairs. America, Japan, Germany, it matters little so long as it all flows back to the Planalto. And of course, there'll be plenty left over to trickle down for the rest, no doubt.
strings.BRA_a_future_for_our_children_desc:
It's easy for critics and onlookers to decry and ridicule our dear Adhemar for all the emoluments he's been making lately, writing off his actions as nothing more than corruption and personal greed. Of course, our President pays no mind to such slander, for he knows himself better than anyone else: he does not have that much time left on Earth. Sure, he has cheated death spectacularly, but he is not arrogant enough to assume he could cheat it twice.

And what use, you may ask, does a dying man have for all this wealth? For his children, Adhemar has worked tirelessly his whole life, and even if death claims him tomorrow, tonight, or even in the next hour, his family will never have to work or toil like he did. For what is a man that does not provide for his family?
strings.BRA_adhemar_the_campaign_trail_desc:
Those treacherous snakes who wish to destroy Getulinho's electoral campaign must fall, if not for their lack of fitness to rule, then for their hatred of the PSP's great endeavors. One of the best courses of action against subversion is by increasing the party's voter base, whether by bribes and other more unorthodox gifts. If our targets find themselves too virtuous to be swayed by such simple tricks, then there is no reason to shy away from the so-called “dirty tricks”.

Perhaps the opposition may call the party corrupt for conducting in such manners, but the stake here is for those hypocrites to subvert the PSP Revolution. Getulinho will win, no matter what political bullets our enemies have against him.
strings.BRA_adhemar_weaken_literacy_restrictions:
Is it not the democratic right for every Brazilian to have their voice heard, regardless of their conditions or defects? The folks living in favelas are no less human than the college professors. They face even more challenges than those better off than them, yet the harshness of literacy tests only limits them from having those issues that plague them from being known. Just because the uneducated can hardly read does not mean we must exclude them from electoral processes. Do they not have the common decency to make rational choices as fellow citizens?

Broadening the definition of “literate” is not only conducive to the legitimacy of liberal society but also a chance to create another loyal voting base for the PSP establishment. If the party can gain renown for setting such a hallmark on lower-class suffrage, no longer can anyone claim it unjust again.
strings.BRA_adhemar_the_coalitions_weakness_desc:
On paper, our position in the Senado is one of cooperation and carefully crafted compromise, an arrangement allowing us to charge full steam ahead, even as a few half-heartedly protest as we ram yet more of our brilliant agenda down their ungrateful gullets. But with coalitionary politics, even the occasional objection can bode poorly for the future, and we must do all we can so that should crisis come, we do not mistake tremors for grumbles.

For this legislative cudgel to be fashioned into a true rapier, one capable of achieving our ends without making messes through our means, we must first trim the fat. If the right and the left cannot help but bicker, then we cannot help but excise these tumors until all that remains are those that agree and do nothing but—sycophants, some would say, but to us, the stalwart vanguard of a new Brazil.
strings.BRA_no_holds_barred_desc:
Did Magalhães really say that to that reporter? Are the PSD actually only getting their money all from one man? And is there really a fuzzy picture of Brizola eating with the same hand he uses to wipe his - ?

If you are a reporter with any sense, no matter what you think the answer to these questions are, it shall from now on be 'yes'. Politics has always been about controlling the message, and sometimes the message just needs to be spun a bit to make sure it lands. No matter how petty or how pertinent, our friends in the news business are our ticket to victory, and we will not stop at anything to see it through.
strings.BRA_lacerdas_hypocrisy_desc:
Like a crow, that cawing moron Lacerda can never keep his mouth shut; he can never pass up an opportunity to ceaselessly ramble without rhyme or reason and without truth or fact. That is the sum of his career and indeed his life as a whole, and he has treated this presidency as yet another opportunity to air his baseless grievances to the world.

For all their innumerable faults, Wainer and Brizola sought to expose him as the hypocrite he is, and although their revelations failed to capture the public's notice, this approach of destroying him in his own journalistic domain may bear fruit yet. The homeless of Guanabara have suffered under his brutality and callous disregard for their very lives for far too long, and soon all of Brazil will know just how two-faced this crow can be.
strings.BRA_leave_it_to_the_son_desc: To be born into the shadow of a great man can often be a curse, but Getulinho Vargas has spent the last thirty years becoming quite the man himself, every bit as stern and capable as his father. Adhemar may be leaving the office and this mortal coil soon. Still, he can rest assured that Vargas is a worthy successor to his Famous Box. We, as well as all of Brazil, would do well to leave behind any doubts about his capability: Brazil and the PSP will be in good hands.
strings.BRA_rouba_mas_faz_desc: He steals, but he delivers. For some, it was just a bizarre slogan; for others, it was a sarcastic jeer, but for Brazil, it has been the reality for five years. For everything Adhemar ever took, whether it be funds or favors, he left behind more for Brazil and its people, from jobs to hospitals, and none have benefitted from him more than Brazil's most impoverished. This reputation is the legacy that Adhemar has made for himself, first in San Paulo and for the entire nation. And now, it shall be the rock on which Getulinho and the PSP will build its foundation upon, the method that grows our support, and what we will continue to build upon and lead Brazil into the future.
strings.BRA_defining_our_legacy_desc:
This presidential campaign is not only Getulinho's trial, but also one carrying along the legacy of Adhemar, a dice roll of factors to determine the reputation of the entire PSP for years to come. A true reputation may not be a positive one, and embellishment can prove appropriate when everyone else is out to smother a righteous name. As with most other issues, money is a rather efficient tool for problem-solving other than one's mental faculty — what better way is there to secure a long-lasting PSP than by providing each President with their own little trust funds?

While it is doubtful a meagre sum of extra savings, accessible through entirely legal means, will do much in terms of providing for various side-projects, a symbolic legislation, combined with Adhemar's planned São Paulo Presidential Library, will surely show the Brazilian people that the Planalto does care about them.
strings.BRA_adhemar_the_myth_desc:
History will not be a documentary, it has always been a story of great men and larger-than-life mythologies. If the final chapter of Adhemar ends here at this moment, he will be recalled as who he is — a statesman unparalleled for decades past. But by basking within a limited glory, arrested by those who cannot comprehend his plain majesty, is Adhemar not committing a grave sin against the repute which he deserves? The Greek had woven their pagan myths into the very fabrics of Western civilization, so did the Romans built an everlasting institution for modern societies.

There is no excuse for failing to learn from the most regal legacies, especially in this age of televisions and radios. Adhemar de Barros managed to manifest his promises to the people, and forever more must the stories of his legend be repeatedly told.
strings.BRA_enjoying_our_rewards_desc:
Adhemar has not just slaved away for his country for years on end, but he has fought his way out of hospital to finish the job. For such a tireless defender of the nation, it is only just that he can now get some rest, as should any man, and as he has indeed made possible for the people in his country to do.

The PSP will continue to thank its honorable benefactor for his work, and in recognition, will put a vote through the National Congress to increase presidential pensions to a healthy level, as well as to ensure that Presidents receive official pardons for all actions taken during their time in office. A leader must not be punished for doing their job, after all.
strings.BRA_adhemar_the_man_desc:
Despite the forceful persona Adhemar continues projecting, he has grown tired and complacent, especially after his life almost turned forfeit in an incident he had no command over. A natural craving for control is inherent to Adhemar's career, but the time for a quiet exit is here. The PSP will continue prospering even without his guidance. Now is the final opportunity to clean up the scene for another generation of patriots to replace the old. Above all else, there is no shame in leaving with an unsullied legacy.

Moving forward, Adhemar has no more busywork outside of bidding farewell to his confidants and praying for a peaceful presidential transition. If the party does not fall into ceaseless bickering without supervision, Getulinho will make a good shepherd to guide Brazil along the path his predecessor has set firmly.
strings.BRA_one_last_speech_desc:
Legendary but not invincible, the name of Adhemar may now rival that of Vargas', but he is not much healthier than his thoroughly entombed predecessor. Putting the egg into the basket, the President must conduct a final speech before transitioning. What he proclaims during this time will be the image he projects to an international audience for years. Therefore, it ought to reflect upon the nobility of his life and mission, elevating what he has achieved so far into snapshots worthy of surviving the annals of history.

Adhemar is growing weaker daily, and posterity is of the utmost importance for a lasting legacy, even more so than the truth of a diminished prodigy. 'Friendly' media outlets will be invited as soon as possible to ensure the discourse goes smoothly for his final event before departing from the Planalto.
strings.BRA_times_arrow_desc:
Tick tock, tick tock — the clock has finally reached midnight. Dimly lit by candlelight, the quaint residence, a mere room within the extravagance of the Alvorada, has become one with darkness. Adhemar de Barros, whether he be called a prideful boor or a man of action, certainly overstayed his welcome in the annals of history. Fate's bullet seeked to be rid of him, and yet perseverance carried his frail, frigid body through the final months until these hours of conclusion. Whatever regrets, whatever masteries — in the end, he is dying alone with a mess of beddings.

Shimmering beneath a half-filled glass of water along the office desk is a playing deck, but there are no more tricks or dice to plot with. Having outplayed everything which stood against the Brazilian Dream, Adhemar now sits thoughtlessly — Getulinho cannot fail after all that's planned.
strings.BRA_return_to_normality_desc:
The dragon has been slain.

Adhemar de Barros and his folly is now a bitter memory, with the corrupt fortress that is the PSP crumbling to dust in his absence. Thanks to this man. Brazil has spent the past few years slowly sinking into a quagmire of thuggery and double-dealing. Duplicity, back-alley payments, gerrymandering, and all other crimes under the sun have become as common as breathing under the Adhemar presidency.

And Edna Lott, who has stood by and watched this entire time, says no more.

Now, the prodigal daughter has returned. Like her father before her, Edna will embark upon a mission of restoring Brazil to her former self - before Adhemar's corrosive touch rotted away her conscience. With the support of the PTB and PSD, Varguism will once more be trusted by the Brazilian people. Just in time for the 1970 election, of course.
strings.BRA_adhemar_biggest_success_desc:
It is impossible to deny that under the Adhemar Presidency, the once minuscule influence of Nazi Germany has shot up immensely, creating an entirely new power bloc within Brazil. Like it or not, German money has become invaluable to many areas of Brazilian life.

As expected when it comes to the Germans, some are more opposed to it than others. Edna herself holds no love for the Nazis, nor do many of the minorities she claims to represent. And yet, severing ties with Germany in favor of stronger ties to America would strangle many schools, hospitals, and infrastructure projects that were made possible thanks to German money. The question the President must answer is how far one is willing to go for their morals - or indeed, whomst one is most willing to throw under the bus...
strings.BRA_continue_independent_course_desc:
As loath as many of us may be to admit it, if we wish to keep Brazil influential on the world stage, then it is necessary for her to maintain access to all three of the major global economies. On this occasion, Lins and his fellow advocates of an independent foreign policy have won out.

However, this is not a sign that Brazil is intent on living as a doormat to Germania. Adhemar was far too narrow-minded. He did not dream big enough - instead of throwing everything at Germany, the most logical course of action would be to approach the Sphere as well. And once relations have developed far enough, the Pakt can be sidelined entirely - and our conscience may be clear.
strings.BRA_return_to_tradition_desc:
Look, nobody here is saying that the United States are the be all and end all of Brazilian foreign policy. But the truth of the matter is that the Americans have always been Brazil's strongest and most devoted allies. Adhemar was, as he usually was, deluded in thinking that Brazil could simply cut off one of her key lifelines.

Cunha has, of course, always been saying this, and he has been proven correct. Whilst Adhemar's detente with Germany is impossible to fully revert without dropping a tonne of cinderblocks upon our economy, we can at least increase tariffs as a way of explaining to the Nazis that they are no long welcome in Brazil.

Frankly, it is the least we can do for the many groups who have been harmed by the Nazis. We can only hope they forgive us for this lapse in judgment.
strings.BRA_always_wrong_desc:
It should not be a controversial opinion to state that corruption is an inherently damaging thing, and yet here we are. The people of Brazil have gotten so used to the blatant, day-to-day corruption that made itself known under the PSP that it simply goes ignored. Worse - some even laugh at it, batting it away as if it is merely one of Adhemar's many quirks.

Truly sickening to see us laid this low. No more. Edna will not blindly stand by and let this wound continue to fester; the cushy establishment that the PSP and their cronies have made for themselves will be ripped out to the very roots, and hit with the full force of the law. It may not be an easy task, but we simply cannot allow our institutions to be further degraded by this insidious plague.
strings.BRA_sometimes_right_desc:
Adhemar was a snake. Let's just clarify that immediately. He was a dirty, filthy snake that turned the government into a vehicle for him and his cronies to do whatever they pleased at any given moment. This was almost unilaterally a bad thing for both Brazil and for democracy.

Almost.

There may be some merit to Adhemar's old adage of “he steals but delivers.” Healthcare, education, welfare, the economy - to an extent, all of them have undergone some sort of improvement. And like it or not, Adhemar used corruption to do this. Edna is not a corrupt woman. She takes no pleasure in abusing power like this. But at the end of the day, if it is necessary to maintain Brazil's standard of living, then needs must.
strings.BRA_sometimes_right_tt: We will not be able to work with the PSD down the line.
strings.BRA_keep_hands_clean_desc:
Our campaign of anti-corruption is showing its first effects. Politicians are once again thinking twice before skimming some money out of their campaign funds for 'personal use' - as they rightfully should be. These signs of success mean we can afford to expand our crusades to another profession rife with corruption; business entities.

By pushing for a strong series of anti-corruption laws that will allow the police to tackle corruption in both the public and private sectors, everyone will know that the times are indeed changing, and that the government will no longer be turning a blind eye to their crimes
strings.BRA_physiologist_unity_desc:
The PSP has had an... interesting history, to say the least. It is the party of Vargas, a man mostly respected across Brazil. And whilst the party may have been through a period of both boom and bust recently, so to speak, at its core the party is still a progressive one.

Despite everything that has transpired, it still yet holds great potential for good; potential that Edna fully intends on making use of... albeit at the cost of several key state positions and a series of drained wallets. Nonetheless, the heirs of both Vargas and Lott will finally stand together - for a better Brazil.
strings.BRA_employ_new_rhetoric_desc:
Fifty percent of our country's population cannot own property while married, gain equal access to healthcare, nor be paid equally to the other half of the country. On paper, most would balk at this and find it utterly horrific. However, as soon as they realize that the more deprived half is not just some nebulous group but in fact, Brazil's women, they simply shrug their shoulders and move on.

What utterly repulsive sexist garbage! Edna is the first female President that Brazil has had since founding, and not a moment too soon. It's time to take care of these long-forgotten inequalities that date all the way back to the 1934 constitution, so that we can say that equality is more than just a word on a piece of paper.
strings.BRA_stop_the_madness_desc:
For goodness sake, do we truly need fifty megaprojects going on all at once? In a predictably cynical populist move, Adhemar would strategically drum up support for his presidency by undertaking obscenely expensive and vast building projects to create jobs and put more money into the economy.

But while Adhemar seemed content to act as if he was a magician that could pull all the money necessary out of a top hat, we will indulge in no such nonsense. Regrettably, these dreamboat projects will all be put to a stop. There is nothing to be salvaged from this - all we can do is redirect its funds elsewhere and pray they are more successful.
strings.BRA_edna_megaprojects_tt: All Megaprojects bar the Trans-Amazonian Highway and the Itaipu Dam will be cancelled.
strings.BRA_develop_the_countryside_desc:
Ignacio Rangel - the man Edna has chosen to place at the helm of Brazil's economy - is a veritable financial wizard. Like all sensible people, he spent much of the Adhemar presidency tearing his hair out over the senseless and costly megaprojects that consumed the economy. Now that the money has thankfully stopped being poured into them, we have much more to spend in places that matter.

While some would first think to spend it on building upon existing economic foundations, Rangel disagrees. He proposes that instead, the money goes towards modernisation of the countryside. If the gap between the city and the countryside were to widen, after all, the economy would be prone to recession. It is only wise to implement this decision before carrying on with the rest of Edna's agenda.
strings.BRA_amazonia_nossa_desc:
Romeu de Campos Vergal, like a limpet clinging to the belly of a ship, has carried on into the next Lott administration. Coming from the left wing of the PSP, he is of course full of bright ideas to do with what can be done to salvage what is left of the megaprojects.

This comes in the form of finishing the work that was started on the Amazon during the Adhemar administration. Many across the country are already excited at the prospect of integrating the Amazon into the country proper. There is little that is to be lost in doing this - the people of the Amazon can finally feel as if they are true Brazilians, and we can reap the political and economic rewards of doing so. A win-win situation, to be sure.
strings.BRA_brave_and_bold_desc:
Adhemar is gone, Edna is in, and nature is starting to heal. Now that the most immediately concerning issues affecting our nation have been at least handicapped, we can move onto more pressing matters. But first - the President needs to get her game plan straight.

It is time to meet up with the larger Brazilian political circle to decide what to do. The UDN, the PTB, the PSD - almost anyone of influence will be invited. A grand league of people to finally build Brazil up to be greater than it ever was before. And where better to discuss these issues than around the barbecue?
strings.BRA_her_league_of_justice_desc:
Has the past half a decade taught us nothing? Letting the PSP into power is akin to sprinkling cyanide into a fine meal - pointless, ruinous, and throwing away any chance of enjoying said meal. They have proven themselves incapable of proper governance, so we shall not even humor them.

The PSD, on the other hand, has long proven an excellent working partner in a coalition. There is nothing to be gained from breaking this relationship off. While their conservative wing may prove uncooperative, the reformist wing should hopefully prove strong enough. Besides - this should be a good chance to show that a President can rule Brazil without resorting to bribes!
strings.BRA_her_league_of_justice_tooltip: Reforms will be passed with help of reformist wing of PSD
strings.BRA_her_array_of_gadgets_desc:
As upsetting as it may be for us to admit sharing any similarities between that glorified crime gang, the left-wing of the PSP largely aligns with our party - ideologically speaking, at least. And while Adhemar's twisted version of welfare and taking care of Brazil's citizens was a net negative, some good has been done.

Therefore, we will need to grit our teeth and ask for the support of Vargas Jr. and his party in ruling the country. It will hit us where it hurts financially, but the support of the PSP will give us a much greater chance of passing our reforms in their strongest possible form.
strings.BRA_her_array_of_gadgets_tooltip: Reforms will be passed with help of PSP
strings.BRA_what_one_lott_started_desc:
When he was President, there were two things Henrique Lott ardently supported - agrarian reform, and voting rights for illiterates. This is something that Edna plans to see through to the very end during her presidency; deepening agrarian measures and expanding electoral rights to all citizens.

However, before we can get to work, it will be vital to secure the support of the military. They may be largely defanged and much less likely to intervene than in previous decades, but one can never be too careful. As Lott's daughter, Edna knows many constitutionalist generals for many years - it is these men she shall approach.
strings.BRA_finish_agrarian_reform_desc:
Brazil is far from an entirely equal country. While the years of Adhemar's rule brought some limited prosperity to our people, vast swathes of this country remain impoverished and incapable of making a real living for themselves.

We cannot withhold help from these neglected regions. Expropriation will be made possible for these lesser developed regions, with state-owned companies receiving benefits in return. This will unfortunately anger many ranchers and rural workers, but their anger will be temporary - agrarian reform is forever.
strings.BRA_cooperation_means_liberation_desc: The peasant leagues bring together all shapes and sizes of different small farmers, their cooperation with us is crucial for the success of our bill. Unfortunately, the corruption inside their ranks is a significant obstacle to our goals; a major portion of their leadership has been bribed and does not care in the slightest for the well-being of the people they are meant to represent. To deal with this problem, our government will attempt to find leaders interested in actually helping our rural communities rather than filling their own pockets.
strings.BRA_abolish_the_spi_desc: The recent horrifying and shocking reports about the SPI, the agency in charge of indigenous people shows terrible vision of an utterly corrupted organisation, allowing ethnic cleansing on the native people to be unpunished, and even allowing it in some instances. This can not be allowed under any circumstances, effective immediatly President Lott will disband the agency, being an investigation into the abuses commited and form a new body to protect natives with the right candidate leading it, Darcy Ribeiro
strings.BRA_correct_centuries_of_exploitation_de:
Many amongst the Brazilian lower classes have been trod upon all their lives. By developers, by the state, by poor business practice - the list goes on. It has been this way for centuries, almost since the very foundation of Brazil itself. Natives, farmers, and minorities alike - all trampled upon and being thrown to the dogs.

But no more. We have talked the talk, and now it is time to walk the walk. A new Brazil has arrived. One that makes sure to take care of her weakest citizens - the state will now serve the people, rather than the other way around. Perhaps now we may take steps to correct the centuries of wrongdoing we have done.
strings.BRA_perfecting_democracy_desc: Many voters in our nation have claimed that we have never been a true democracy. And you know what? They're right. Illiteracy and ignorance have plagued our voting processes since the very beginning of our democracy. But we can change this. Edna will work to become a champion of democracy and tremendously expanding the PTB electorate by instituting a series of voting rights programs.
strings.BRA_remove_voting_barriers_desc:
One of the great shames about Brazil is that it does not allow all adults to vote. Instead placing pointless restrictions on who can vote, disenfranchising large swaths of the population.

OOne of the most disastorous policies is the disenfranchising of the illiterate. Edna will not allow this to continue.

While it is too late to change the constitution to allow universal voting, changing the definitions of illiteracy can allow more people to vote.

By making the restrictions lighter we enfranchise tens of thousands and allow them to vote for the first time.
strings.BRA_push_for_a_civil_society_desc: What good is democracy when the people have zero interest in it? We can never expect to make meaningful, long-lasting changes to our nation if the citizens remain apathetic. To solve this problem our administration will conduct a massive public campaign in order to emphasize the significance of political participation, this way everyone, from the rural peasantry to the metropolitan middle class will know that they are the only ones holding back the reinstatement of the hated oligarchy.
strings.BRA_rescind_immigration_ban_desc: There are many egregious legislations in our country that shouldn't have ever been signed, but none are as pointless as the Japanese Immigration Ban. And it's even more revolting how all the previous administrations did nothing to repeal it. Fortunately, past circumstances have presented us the opportunity to finally put an end to these injustices. And given we won't have this chance again any time soon, we must make sure this discriminatory bill is repealed for good now before the seeds of hatred plowed by it grow out of control. Some in our party may complain about this “reckless” move made at the eve of elections, but if they are worried about the votes, any PSP votes we may already lose will be compensated by the Japanese's, simple as.
strings.BRA_the_other_half_desc: For how long will Brazilian women be treated as mere smiling housewives? For how long will half of the Brazilian population be denied the rights the other half enjoys simply because of their gender? Being the first female President in Brazil's history, Edna Lott doesn't plan to put her status at waste. Speeches calling for women's rights and some token legislation have been made, but it's not enough. Using the power of presidential executive orders, President Edna shall enact decrees that will facilitate the recruitment of women in the civil service and bureaucracy, with targets being set for the minimal amount of women employed in each department after a 5 years transitionary period and more.
strings.BRA_weaken_mil_progressita_desc:
As much as it pains to say, the problem of corruption is much worse than we thought. Its poison seeps and contaminates practically all spheres of power and of our society, even among those whose purpose is to protect our country and home. Now we are left to deal with PSP militarists -the so-called Progressistas- whose loyalty is solely directed to their paychecks, and who knows what could replace it once the golden tap runs dry...

This may not stamp out the root of the issue, but it is imperative for us to weaken their influence with all means available, and strengthen those who wouldn't put their loyalty under price tags, be it the Constitutionalists or even the Sorbonnes.
strings.BRA_liberty_for_all_desc: With our truce over, Lacerda has already started calling our government an ochlocracy. We can only reply that we are fighting for rights for all, while he cares only for higher echelons of society. Another struggle with conservative forces over the soul of Brazil will take place and while certainly not the last, winning it will be another major success for PTB.
strings.BRA_meet_with_wainer_desc:
If our party is going to survive, and perhaps thrive, in the election, we must begin work today. Making public our recent efforts should endear the people to our cause, and begin the long process of reminding the people that Varugism is the only way forward for Brazil. Such a task necessitates the use of every tool at our disposal: loyal unions, teachers, party officials and everyone else spurned by the PSP must be organized into a fighting force strong enough to take back our deserved place.

The first step in winning back the nation is gaining the support of one man: Samuel Wainer. As Chief Editor of the Ulitma Hora, the sole national newspaper in our corner, Wainer will be key in finally swaying the people back to our side. It's about time Edna and him talked strategy.
strings.BRA_UDN_coldness_desc:
How many times does the UDN have to screw over the people before they stop winning the northeast? Honestly, how is it possible that everyone already forgot that the UDN is that party that cut the minimum wage, and that Gomes's presidency was a complete disaster barely a decade ago? The only reason they have any swing up there anyways is because Távora broke Vargas's trust, and formed the party behind his back.

But due to Adhemar and the crisis within the PSP, many right wing voters are once again flocking back to the 'sensible' conservative party to stop us winning the election, we have to prevent this. By pulling some strings in Nordeste, we can make sure that the people finally remember the full picture. Lacerda's stain must be wiped away, so the PSP can finally return to our rightful place. It's time for the north to wake up.
strings.BRA_PSP_corruption_desc:
It's no secret that the PSP is a party of corruption, and even saying this is a massive understatement of the true level of bribery and lies that have spread throughout the government during Barros's reign. Corruption has become the norm, not because of any failure of the government, but by its use as a tool to spread party influence. Yet they always manage to get away with it, convincing the people that their actions are justified in the name of the “common good” as they line their purses.

From now on we're going to set the record straight. Our economists will make sure that the everyone understands just how much corruption has cost the nation, and our journalists will make sure that nobody can round a single street corner without hearing about the newest sordid details of Adhemar and Vargas Jr's past misdeeds.
strings.BRA_together_with_papa_desc:
As our captain picks up momentum, the Lott dynasty can begin to take center place in the publicity. Across the nation, Edna and her father are traveling to remind the people what the PTB has always stood for: legality, equality, and progress for all, not just government cronies. Together and separate, they have made dozens of speeches, each one bringing another mass of people back to the correct side.

Working as one, they create a national narrative far stronger than their lying propaganda machines. Our opponents must surely be afraid as they watch the Lotts build a new political dynasty from the ash and rubble of Adhemar's failures!
strings.BRA_making_vargas_proud_desc:
We did it! Edna has proven herself more than a match for even the biggest power players in Brazil, and has truely proven herself a legitimate inheritor of the Vargas legacy. As the PTB works endlessly to achieve prosperity never before seen in our history, the memory of Adhemar's corrupt regime may at last begin to fade. The road ahead remains long, but Edna and her cabinet have proved that they are tireless, and will walk as long as it takes to reach a free Brazil.

For today though, Edna and the nation can celebrate, knowing full well that, for today at least, they have won. As we drink tonight, we taste the nectar of victory, made sweeter by the injustice we have defeated. Tomorrow can come with what it may, but our mighty nation, united behind its fearless leader, will surely succeed!
strings.BRA_use_last_moments_desc:
We failed. Despite the best efforts of Edna and our party, we have lost. The nation will stagnate under yet another five years of non-Varguist rule, and other parties will seek to fill the power vacuum we have failed to capitalize on. The future of the nation, and our party, will remain uncertain.

However, the world continues to turn despite our defeat, and the PTB must survive. True to our ideals, Edna will use her last moments in office to advance gender equality as much as possible, by abolishing wage inequality in all state companies nationwide. After this, and the finalization of our purge of Adhemar's corruption, surely the people will recognize that we left this nation better than we found it.
strings.BRA_adhemar_gone_desc:
The Social Progressive Revolution, which began four years ago with the election of our esteemed, now deceased President Adhemar Pereira de Barros—may the merciful Lord grant him eternal rest—is now in the greatest period of instability it has ever experienced. Our PSP has faced terrible difficulties in the President's absence. Planning for Edna Lott's impeachment, drifting too close to Germany, Adhemar falling into a coma, aborting attempts to remove him from the presidency, and finally his death—it has all passed by so quickly, so cruelly.

To Laudo all this seems like the stuff of a nightmare, but he knows no amount of pinching will save him. He must move quickly to ensure that Pedro Aleixo's provisional presidency does not result in the fall of the PSP from power, never to return again. Under Laudo Natel's guidance, the PSP must regain its popularity and win the 1970 election—and God knows as well as Laudo does that he has his work cut out for him.
strings.BRA_calculate_losses_desc:
One of the reasons that the Social Progressive Revolution is now in such danger with the death of Adhemar de Barros is that he was the strongest binder maintaining party unity during times of crisis and prosperity. The suddenness and destabilizing effects of his demise have left us preoccupied at a moment we could have used to ensure the PSP was behind us—and in the meantime, while Adhemar has gone to ground, we have suffered terrible damage.

Before we can even begin to think on how to mend this damage, we need to understand its extent. We need to leverage our sources in the PSP and determine how severe the damage is. São Paulo remembers its President and remains loyal to the party of the great man now buried with his fathers in Piracicaba, but men of other regions may well prove troublesome...
strings.BRA_calculate_losses_tt: £BRA_psp_texticon PSP senators are defecting from the party...
strings.BRA_keep_party_unity_desc:
If we want to rally the Partido Social Progressista—to preserve the hard work of our great President, Adhemar de Barros, while he rests with God and His Saints—a technocrat such as Laudo Natel will be of no use, and he knows it as well as any. If we put him forward as the next President to take over when Aleixo's mandate expires, we will have learned nothing from the hell that the uncharismatic Marshal Lott was put through fighting against Quadros in 1960.

No, we need a man able to unify us and successfully defeat the Varguists and conservatives. The people of the PSP can think of only one option: the namesake son of the Father of the Poor, our late President's protégé—Getúlio Vargas Filho. “Júnior” will leverage his charisma, surname, and good relations with Adhemar to prevent the fragmentation of the PSP in a way that Laudo could never hope to do.
strings.BRA_adhemar_successor_desc:
The first steps having been executed, the way forward is clear. Laudo Natel has to make sure that the new President will allow the PSP to serve out the remainder of Adhemar's term. We must fulfill the mandate given to us by the will of the people in 1965, and persuade Senhor Aleixo to act only as a caretaker.

This will not be easy, not even close. Aleixo is not some sort of yes-man, and Laudo knows better than to delude himself into thinking so. If Laudo fails to put all his skills of suasion and intimidation to use, his wild ride as Adhemar's locum tenens will crash and burn before it even gets off the ground.
strings.BRA_winter_is_coming_desc:
Our economy minister, Senhor Delfim Netto, is convinced that the only way to save the Brazilian economy from collapse is a wage freeze. However, with Adhemar in the grave and the government unstable, that is almost certain to destroy us in any election. Instead, we must for the time being settle with reducing the possibility of indexing wages to inflation.

Before elections, in order to avoid sabotaging Júnior's chances, we will strive to make the process as painless as possible—and only really clamp down once the vote has succeeded, finally freezing wages to the extent necessary during the new presidency. The UDN is likely to consider this an opportune measure, but we can strengthen their support by passing a bill abolishing trade union taxes, justifying it as an unnecessary burden on the Brazilian worker.
strings.BRA_continue_as_usual_desc:
The PSP has always been a political underdog—that is a reality that Adhemar had to confront, and it probably helped lead to his heart attack; now it is time for Laudo Natel to confront it too. On our own, we cannot hope for anything resembling a victory—so we must make sure to make the PSP bulletproof.

How, you ask? Simply stuff all ministries and governmental agencies with associates we can trust, and change labour laws to render their firing very expensive and functionally a near impossibility. To ensure the PTB does not raise any problems, we will also make sure to include some additional provisions to safeguard the positions of trade unions and peasants' leagues, as well as raise civil servant pay.
strings.BRA_clean_hands_desc:
On our own, we cannot hope for anything resembling a victory; we must do what Adhemar always did, and build a robust coalition to pass our bills. The current bill must attempt to gather votes not just from the PSP but from deputies of other parties.

Whereas Adhemar could get away with the Rouba-mas-Faz attitude, a faceless technocrat such as Laudo Natel will only earn tomatoes in his face (if not bullets through his skull) if he tries to parrot him. Therefore, we need to ensure that the law is passed without bribes so as to show that we are in fact still a legitimate government and not corrupt or bent on seeing the country go bankrupt for our own political gain.

Note and note well that if we fail in this, our chances of reelection will be effectively nonexistent.
strings.BRA_clean_hands_tt: The bill we chose will be called to vote...
strings.BRA_no_populism_laudo_desc:
There are those that claim that populism is the legacy of our late-lamented President, Adhemar de Barros. But if one examines the origins of such rhetoric, one merely finds a lot of Udenists and Petebists attempting to psychologically project their defective politics onto a man who gave his all for the homeland.

The logical continuation of our efforts is the improvement of our bureaucratic functions and an emphasis on the appointment of technocrats to manage the Brazilian state. This is the greatest legacy of Adhemar de Barros, the tradition he has left behind to us; we owe it to his honour as our President to continue this into the future. We will coopt Technocratic politicans and ministers from the UDN, PSD, and PTB, to show the efficiency of the new PSP. From this day on, the PSP will be known as a party of efficiency and progress—and as for anything that fanatics might call 'corruption', innovative accounting methods will assist in assuaging doubts.
strings.BRA_no_populism_laudo_trigger_tt: We have passed the National Standardization of Wages Indexation Act.
strings.BRA_join_or_die_laudo_desc:
Before the bill is fully implemented, we have some work to do to ensure our security. For instance, we have to ensure that government workers and their families will vote for the Partido Social Progressista. After all, we Pessepistas are the people responsible for their welfare and that of their families.

“Vote for the PSP! What, you don't want to? Fine, just go find another job then, outside the civil service. What, you voted for us? Congratulations! You are going to enjoy the benefits of the safest post in the entire Republic of Brazil, hell, possibly the entire continent.”
strings.BRA_join_or_die_laudo_trigger_tt: We have passed the Labor Law Reform Act.
strings.BRA_killers_adhemar_desc:
While the late President, Dr. Adhemar Pereira de Barros, yet lived, he served his people in many ways. First he was a physician, then he served as Governor of São Paulo, then he led the PSP, then he became President. However, considering the way political developments have occurred since Adhemar's death, it emerges with an elegant inevitability that there is one more way he can serve us.

The circumstances of his demise are eminently useful as a source of political capital. This controversy over German spies created pandemonium. We can exploit that to spread rumours about the Germans poisoning Adhemar before he could purge them after he realised his mistake of permitting the German-serving traitor Liana Clemente to seduce him. This should also give us whatever justification we need to sever all ties with the Pakt.
strings.BRA_total_army_compatability_desc:
We wasted a lot of time on erroneous policy with regard to the OFN. As a result, at this moment we lack the time or political will to completely integrate ourselves with the organization that is the last hope of the free world. However, not all hope is lost.

A direct line between our high command and its OFN counterparts, combined with ensuring that our armed forces' equipment standards closely match those of the best militaries in the OFN, will more than suffice as an initial move to increase our integration with them. It is elevated and correct; from today on, we stand against fascism together!
strings.BRA_negotiate_debt_payment_desc:
We have essentially hounded the Pakt and its German slaves out of Brazil faster than you can say 'foda-se'. Despite that there are those on Capitol Hill and in Washington that still have their doubts about the true direction of our régime. Fortunately, that's what we have a foreign minister for.

Let us send Vasco Leitão da Cunha to Washington D.C. to ask about the possibility of cutting down on the payment of the enormous interest on our debt. If they can show us this discretion, it will help us as we strive to undo the damage Adhemar did to our diplomatic relations.
strings.BRA_bastion_of_innovation_desc:
We have obliterated the influence of the degenerate oppressors of Europe, and supplanted it with the more beneficial economic influences of the Americans and their allies. However, if there is one thing that Quadros taught us correctly, it is that we should never put anything on one card or all our eggs in one basket.

Slightly reducing tariffs for the CPS countries should encourage the OFN and the CPS to increase their investments. They will want to compete for our favour, outbidding each other left and right, and we can only benefit from that.
strings.BRA_stop_all_megaprojects_desc:
How many great projects have proved futile throughout the ages? The Great Wall was useless day in and day out, as the Chinese recount. Forget defending against the Japanese, it could not even hold the Mongols back. Then there was that damn fool proposal for a Gibraltar Dam, which would have done nothing but bankrupt Germany and quite possibly Iberia too, and left Europe a ruin more failed than, well, ever.

As it is in northern China and Germany, so it is here too. This nation must be honest with itself: megaprojects have failed. We have lost time and money on them, that could have been spent elsewhere. Worse yet, that futility was compounded by an increase in corruption and a fattening of the wallets of the corrupt. It is well past time for us to restore financial sanity: if not, Brazil will be slain by bankruptcy even if the PSP holds out in the election.
strings.BRA_stop_all_megaprojects_tt: We will remove all unfinished megaprojects.
strings.BRA_sell_petrobras_desc:
It is high time for us to set about doing what Minister Delfim Netto is advising us to do: partially privatising Petrobras, and selling some of its assets to foreign companies. Obviously, not even Delfim Netto is gung-ho enough to contemplate going the whole ham and privatising the whole thing (for fear that the Varguists will rapidly collapse the government), but some of them need to be sold and there can be no disagreement on the matter.

“Why?” one asks. The reason for this is simple: we need to encourage competition in the oil market, so as to stimulate growth, and get some money in order to stop our mushrooming debt as soon as possible.
strings.BRA_lower_taxes_desc:
It is high time for us to set about doing what Minister Delfim Netto advises us to do: reform taxes in order to create an economic boom. The most straight-forward, vote-winning method of doing this is to reduce lower income brackets' income taxes, in such a manner where those lower brackets can see us. Perhaps televising it and taking out advertisements in every newspaper will help.

At the same time, there will be a part that is kept quiet to avoid any controversies. We will split the cost and increase taxes on the rich by a relatively slight amount, so as to ensure that our treasury suffers only minimal damage.
strings.BRA_end_protectionism_desc:
Many economists in Brazil have for long argued that the hitherto established economic doctrine of import-substitution industrialisation, which focuses on preventing foreign corporations from doing business in Brazil in favour of generating local alternatives, has exhausted its usefulness. Antônio Delfim Netto has long been of this view, and has convinced the Aleixo cabinet to agree with him.

If we have thrown out the old model, we need to find alternative solutions to encourage economic growth. A good start will be the lowering of tariffs for all OFN countries, in the hope that they will take the opportunity to invest in our country.
strings.BRA_we_cannot_lose_desc:
At long last we have successfully adjusted our economic, diplomatic, and political courses to the new circumstances in the aftermath of Adhemar's loss, may he rest in peace. But now we have a major problem ahead of us: the urgent need to ensure the unity of the Social Progressive Party.

Laudo Natel has to move quickly. The PSP convention must be organised in such a way that Vargas Júnior and no-one else is selected as the presidential nominee, leaving only the vice-presidential selection to the delegates. And when that is done, the campaign, which is the PSP's now-or-never moment, must go into full swing.
strings.BRA_new_father_of_poor: The New Father of the Poor
strings.BRA_new_father_of_poor_desc:
Some candidates generate their own advantages. Our candidate is not some country bumpkin from Pindamonhangaba, Paranápanema, or Votuporanga. He is the son of the Father of the Poor, the greatest of all Presidents of Brazil except for maybe Adhemar. He is the Governor of São Paulo, Adhemar's chosen political heir: Getúlio Sarmanho Vargas, Vargas Filho!

With our candidate, there's not much we need to do to think up a campaign strategy. The strategy is obvious: we will use all footage we have of Júnior with his father and Adhemar. In this manner we shall remind everyone that he is the heir of the greatest leaders in Brazilian history, and the preserver of their legacies.
strings.BRA_sao_paulo_bastion_desc:
Our campaign cannot but collapse if we lose control of São Paulo state, which is the old bastion of our party. Therefore, we have no choice but to resort to drastic, potentially ruthless methods.

During his governorship, Adhemar organised paramilitaries to ensure, as it were, the continuation of stability and order in his state. This was supported by local oligarchs that supported and funded our party. Those paramilitaries have not dissipated since then, but their old leader's death has left them shiftless and scared some of the oligarchs; we must give them something to do.

Firstly we will contact these oligarchs and bring them back on side, some well placed bribes will stop any defections to the PSD. Secondly, by directive of the Minister-without-Portfolio, the paramilitaries will be given two tasks: first, to ensure that no newspapers criticise the PSP, and second, to ensure that Quadros' madness continues to be denounced. Though he may have retired, the reminder of his Udenist candidacy in 1960 will certainly help.
strings.BRA_find_allies_shadows_desc:
Let us leave campaigning to Vargas Filho. A son of the Father of the Poor, whose legacy has outlived the Hitlerite triumph, several coup attempts, conservative hegemonies, and the Argentine threat to our south, should have no problem. Meanwhile, Laudo's job must be to organise the largest operation of his short time in the government.

To ensure PSP victory in presidential and parliamentary elections, Natel must start a massive bribery program. You want your vote bought? Sure, here's some money. You want a road built? Vote for us and you'll get it. Your useless nephew wants a job? Sure, pay us, and then we'll pay him.
strings.BRA_sway_the_south_desc:
In the general case Rio Grande do Sul is one of the traditional strongholds of the Partido Trabalhista Brasileira. This makes sense when one considers the fact that a large swathe of their political idols, such as Vargas the elder, Goulart, and Brizola, all hail from this province—political allegiance here is no mere matter of party, but often a matter of state identity and ties of family and friendship.

At the same time the UDN through cooperating with other minor parties such as the PCD and PL, acts as the main opposition to the PTB in this region. Historically the PSP and PSD have both struggled to build a base in this region.

But the universal lubricant of money can disrupt all of that. With aggressive campaigning—and bribery, of course—we should be able to reverse that trend. We will also use our media contacts in the region to ensure Goulart and Lacerda while campaigning direct their attacks at each other and not at Vargas, divide and conquer. Through this, rhetoric and well-deployed envelopes, we can claim another state to follow the legacy of both Adhemar de Barros and Getúlio Vargas, since our candidate is the political heir of both men.
strings.BRA_pray_it_works_desc:
The work that Minister-without-Portfolio Laudo Natel has been doing to keep the PSP both in power and popular has been without parallel in modern Brazilian history. He has exerted himself beyond belief, working himself to the bone with very little in terms of rest or recreation. Surely, this is an experience he never wants to repeat again.

Natel had better hope it was not for nothing. If this fails, after all that he has done, the PSP is almost certain to die as a national party. All that will be left will be the governorship of young Getúlio Vargas, and the hegemony secured in São Paulo—for the rest will crumble away like the French Army in the face of the Blitzkrieg the moment there is a defeat.
strings.BRA_another_five_years_desc:
Laudo Natel really only has one thing going through his mind these days: “Veni, vidi, vici.”

The Aleixo presidency—more accurately, the Natel shadow-presidency—was more than enough to resurrect the spirit of the Partido Social Progressista, which was thought dead forevermore after Adhemar's sudden death. Combined with a vigorous campaign (and prudential use of envelopes in the right place), the PSP now holds a mandate to continue Adhemar's government.

Now Laudo is free to rest a little in the vice-presidential palace, while a new President takes over the reins.
strings.BRA_take_revenge_desc:
Laudo Natel is shaking in his boots, as well he should be. The PSP has been defeated, and the new presidency will begin in a matter of time. The dream is dead, and the terrible process of the Pessepista constriction outside of São Paulo is already beginning.

During his last moments in government, there is but one thing for the failed leader to do. He needs to ensure that the Partido Social Progressista has enough funds to survive life in opposition, by one way or another. If revenge can be arranged against those whose betrayals have deprived Brazil of the great opportunity of the enlightened rule of the heir of Vargas and Adhemar, so be it.

All that notwithstanding, this second defeat also means the end of Laudo's political career—if he's lucky. If some muckraker starts to investigate why the allegedly technocratic caretaker President Aleixo had a PSP-aligned cabinet, legal problems might be the most charitable way of describing the hot water he'll be landed in.
strings.BRA_adhemar_military_warned_tt: Our presidency has lived to see another day, but next time we won't be so lucky.
strings.BRA_adhemar_true_progress_tt: Due to our massive successes over the past 3 years, we will unlock a new branch of the focus tree.
strings.BRA_adhemar_natel_takes_over_tt: This is not good - a new focus tree will be unlocked.
strings.BRA_the_man_who_deceived_us_tooltip: President Adhemar will purge large amounts of German influence from the country. This will harm our economic growth.
strings.BRA_problem_of_prestes_tooltip: In the 1971 Senate elections, PCB candiates will appear under the PSP banner.
strings.BRA_rescind_japanese_ban_brazil_tt:
Japanese Immigration Ban Rescindal will be put to vote in the Senado.

If passed:
strings.BRA_neves_influence: The influence of Neves is increasing
strings.BRA_brizola_influence: The influence of Brizola is increasing
strings.BRA_exercito_social_progressista_idea_de:
For decades, politicians have tried to find ways to escape the military's tight grip on democracy. This baffled Adhemar! Is the answer not so simple?

Don't fight it. Subvert them! Now the President has tied the military and the PSP together, supplanting the UDN's position as the army's preferred partner.
strings.BRA_shield_against_inflation_wage_policy: Significantly increases minimum wage ({getcategory3lawtno_minimum_wage}) policy effectiveness.
strings.BRA_guaranteed_maternity_leave_policy: Significantly increases gender rights ({getcategory4lawtno_gender_rights}) policy effectiveness.
strings.BRA_minimum_pension_tooltip: If the Social Security Reform Bill passes, our pension law will improve.
strings.BRA_guaranteed_maternity_tooltip: If the Social Security Reform Bill passes, our gender rights policy and monthly population growth will improve.
strings.BRA_labor_courts_in_big_cities_tooltip:
If the Social Security Reform Bill passes, our working hours, pension law, minimum wage, and unemployment subsidies policy effectiveness will improve.
In addition, administrative offices will be built in two states.
strings.BRA_hospices_for_old_workers_tooltip:
If the Social Security Reform Bill passes, our pension law and healthcare policy effectiveness will improve.
A hospital will also be built.
strings.BRA_shield_against_inflation_tooltip: If the Social Security Reform Bill passes, our minimum wage policy effectiveness will improve.
strings.BRA_increase_of_unemployment_benefits_to: If the Social Security Reform Bill passes, our unemployment benefits policy will improve.
strings.BRA_money_for_our_defenders_tooltip: If the Social Security Reform Bill passes, our pensions policy will improve. The military will also be moderately more loyal.
strings.BRA_critical_support_to_state_apparatus_: If the Social Security Reform Bill passes, our administrative efficiency will improve.
strings.BRA_adhemar_agrarian_reform_req_tt: Adhemar's version of agrarian reform has been passed.
strings.BRA_check_the_assets_of_new_friend_toolt: We've chosen to contact the Reich.
strings.BRA_use_old_allys_experience_tooltip: We've chosen to contact the US.
strings.BRA_adhemar_min_corruption_idea_tt: Our level of corruption is already at its minimum
strings.BRA_squeaky_clean_idea_desc:
Brazil's perennial hydra has been tamed. Corruption is now taboo in Brasília, relegated from hallways to alleyways. Thanks to President's efforts, the state is cleaner than ever before.

Granted, deals, bribes and criminals continue to hide amongst lawmakers. But for now, corruption is an untouchable word staying firmly out of any critics' vocabulary.
strings.BRA_a_handshake_here_and_there_idea_desc:
Brasília is not spotless, but compared to yesterday, it is virtually sparkling. Today, if you were to explore Brazil's halls of power, there might be no anti-corruption activist's dream, but one could compare it to the likes of Australia or the USA.

While visible signs of corruption have vanished, backdoor deals remain. But which government has done without a secret favor once or twice?
strings.BRA_the_reality_of_governance_idea_desc: Brazil is no paragon of honesty. That is accepted. But you would be hard-pressed to find a country that was - while many decry the shady backroom deals and accounting incidents as corruption, the men who make these deals behind closed doors know that these are simply the tricks of the trade. After all, who wants to see how the sausage gets made? To solve corruption, responsibility lies with the leaders- only then may one of Brazil's most notorious ills be cured.
strings.BRA_dirty_hands_idea_desc:
The situation is far from ideal. Brazil is, indeed, afflicted by corruption, and its governors are dirty with the soot of unsavory solutions. Wetworkers, oligarchs and embezzling civil servants all are listed on the payroll, their existence an accepted reality.

Brazil is, more than ever, not for beginners. To even start, you must learn to sit with the crooks.
strings.BRA_ruled_by_favours_idea_desc:
Corruption is no longer an affliction, but a disease. It is not just a problem, but a scourge which tears through the legal code, more a suggestion than a requirement. Mobsters rule over the biggest cities' streets, violence is unpunished and bribes are the honest man's game.

Brazil's state has three players: its government, its military, and its crooks. Ruling means bargaining with all three.
strings.BRA_conmans_paradise_idea_desc: Brazil; a country where crooks, mobsters, and fraudsters can flourish. The corruption of the government is an open secret. The failure to meaningfully address corruption in any way has turned the nation into a festering wound of corruption, attracting organised crime from across the globe to set up business. From the presidency to the senate to the supreme court; all of them are corrupt to the very core, using law and order as a convenient myth to keep the machine turning.
strings.BRA_adhemar_max_corruption_idea_tt: Our level of corruption is already at its maximum
strings.BRA_adhemar_comatree_legalize_communists: You will have to relegalize the communists in the future.
strings.BRA_adhemar_comatree_integralist_educati: This deal will help the integralists in the future.
strings.BRA_adhemar_comatree_sway_senators_toolt: It's time to slaughter the bull.
strings.BRA_adhemar_comatree_aliance_udn_tooltip: Vasco Leitão da Cunha will become the Foreign Minister of Edna's administration after Adhemar's impeachment.
strings.BRA_adhemar_comatree_divide_psp_tooltip: Romeu de Campos Vergal will become the Economic Minister of Edna's administration after Adhemar's impeachment.
strings.BRA_edna_tried_to_impeach_adhemar_toolti: Vice President Lott aided the impeachment attempt.
strings.BRA_edna_refused_to_impeach_adhemar_tool: Vice President Lott refused to aid the impeachment attempt.
strings.BRA_adhemar_coma_deal_with_communists: We asked for the help of the communists in the coma crisis.
strings.BRA_adhemar_coma_deal_with_integralists: We asked for the help of the integralists in the coma crisis.
strings.BRA_adhemar_agrarian_reform_passed: We have succeeded in passing the Agrarian Reform Act.
strings.BRA_adhemar_agrarian_reform_failed: We have failed in passing the Agrarian Reform Act.
strings.BRA_adhemar_germans_are_back_desc:
Isn't it wonderful what the stroke of a pen can accomplish? With only a few scribbles onto a piece of paper, Adhemar de Barros has opened what many believe to be a proverbial Pandora's Box. The Germans are back in Brazil - and they intend on making their presence known.

The opening of trade relations between the two nations has lead to the rapid increase of the German language in the public spaces and the appearance of German businesses in Brazilian markets - especially in the South.

Of course, whilst the likes of Jânio Quadros and Afonso Arinos hail this turn of events as a victory for an independent and pragmatic foreign policy, many remain unconvinced. Seeing the tongue and commerce of a nation once touted as one of Brazil's greatest enemies appearing on every street corner as if it is normal will be sure to spark at least some degree of pushback. The question is - where?
strings.BRA_the_eagle_rises_desc:
The recent geopolitical changes have made a once unthinkable scenario a reality - German influence within Brazil is growing like a coming storm on the horizon. What was once a relatively small minority is now an important part of Brazilians society, with new German-Brazilian schools, industries and organizations popping up across the country like mushrooms after a rainstorm.

With this new geopolitical reality, one can only wonder how other, more marginalised minority groups will react...
strings.BRA_National_Pharmaceutics_desc: With the German money flowing in through various different channels (some of which had to be minorly 'persuaded', so to speak), the young and promising pharmaceutical company Aché has become the new base of Brazilian pharmaceutical concern. Thanks to Aché's investments, more German money is sure to pour in alongside it, showing us that the industry has a promising future in Brazil.
strings.BRA_parana_crisis_desc:
They say that you reap what you sow - and the time has come for us to reap.

Our efforts to reproach Nazi Germany have brought a plague of discontent amongst the South of the country, with the complicated mosaic of minorities in the South collapsing into a fit of rage. Protests, strikes, and secret assassination attempts are now commonplace in the South, with local army garrisons struggling to bring peace to the fraught situation. Unless action is taken soon, the South will fall into anarchy.
strings.BRA_calmed_south_desc:
The combined efforts of the government and law enforcement to crack down on the worst of the violence have proven successful, but the anger in the South still poses a very real danger. While the protestors may have ratcheted down the agitation in favor of a mostly non-violent approach, the threat posed against German Brazilians is very real. Regular reports detail people being stalked in the streets, workplaces and businesses discriminating regularly as well as consistent death threats against Germans all across southern Brazil.

It is quite clear that so long as the Nazi empire in Europe continues, the unrest in communities to the South will also remain an issue. Brazil's ability to weather this crisis relies on the government working to ease tensions as much as possible, in addition to the police protecting against isolated threats when and if they arise.
strings.BRA_silent_south_desc:
While the Brazilian government has managed to stabilize most communities in the South, the tensions between Euro-Brazilians still remain. The protests have ceased for now and targeted harassment of German-Brazilians is increasingly rare, yet lingering resentment and antipathy lurks just under the surface. With the ongoing conflicts in Central and Eastern Europe, the potential for the mood in the South to escalate cannot be ruled out.

The government must continue to work towards remedying the animosity in the South before something happens for it to spike again, with law enforcement on stand-by in the event violence breaks out.
strings.BRA_tense_south_desc:
The communities south of the Rio Itararé are resting on a bed of nails, with the German Civil War and within Germany's Lebensraum sending a growing number Euro-Brazilians into an anti-fascist frenzy. The German population in southern Brazil has become a target for enraged citizens with cultural and/or familial ties to Poland, Ukraine and the Jewish Diaspora, with regular protests and targeted attacks against German communities now commonplace all along the cone into Rio Grande do Sul.

Regardless of any Brazilian's well-justified venom for the Third Reich, this cannot stand; the mounting civil unrest does as much to pose a security risk as it shames us as a country, a concerted effort must be made to contain the violence before it escalates.
strings.BRA_pacified_south_desc:
Brazil can breathe a sigh of relief, at least for the duration. The initiatives of the government to unite the Euro-Brazilian communities after a torrent of anti-German sentiment that swept through the South. A great sense of relief can be felt south of the Rio Itararé, yet the events of recent months have revealed volatile fault lines within our otherwise pluralist society.

The end of the wars in Europe may be within sight according to foreign observers, but the prospect of multiple protracted conflicts on the continent has not been ruled out. If this is in fact the case, a similar domestic crisis in the South could spring up again. Until then, Brazil's government will simply have to keep an eye on the European situation in the hope that the fighting ends soon.
strings.BRA_adhemar_a_gamblers_paradise_tooltip: We will gain “alternative” sources of funding equal to 0.4B.
strings.BRA_adhemar_new_times_tooltip: Our newfound German allies will provide funding equal to 0.3B.
strings.BRA_modernize_our_casinos_tooltip: The income from our newfound casinos will be consolidated, providing funding equal to 0.8B.
strings.BRA_Muller_switches_PSP_tooltip: Filinto Müller has switched parties from the PSD to the PSP, changing the politics of Mato Grosso forever.
strings.BRA_manhattan_tooltip: We will approach the USA for help with our nuclear program.
strings.BRA_australia_tooltip: We will approach Australia for help with our nuclear program.“
strings.BRA_hermann_tooltip: We will approach Germany for help with our nuclear program.

strings.BRA_lacerda_oas_flag_brazil_tt: Lacerda stands alone knowing what is best for Brazil.
strings.BRA_lacerda_oas_support_tt: continues to support Lacerda's vision of a free Brazil.
strings.BRA_lacerda_oas_at_risk_tt: is at risk of withdrawing support for Lacerda's government.
strings.BRA_lacerda_oas_hostile_tt: is hostile towards Brazil and Lacerda's government.
strings.BRA_1965_the_lacerda_presidency_desc:
At last, Lacerda's years-long ambition to become President is finally realized. However, there is no time to waste. In order to achieve his ideal 'Middle-Class Revolution', he will need to wrangle his UDN colleagues; otherwise, his party will rip him to shreds in the process.

Lacerda's new cabinet and the UDN itself comprise a wide variety of thought and interest groups. Vice President Távora, from the pragmatic Realistas faction, will attempt to restrain Lacerda from taking any actions they deem too hasty.

The Bossa Nova faction of the party, led by Party President Magalhães Pinto, consists of statists and developmentalists who oppose the more liberal economic policies of Lacerda's Banda de Música faction.

The old guard faction, Liberais Históricos, is now heavily weakened and led by Justice Minister Milton Campos. The party's hardline anti-Varguist stance led to its defeat when Eduardo Gomes abolished the minimum wage. As long as Lacerda has not drifted too far towards the center, Campos should not be too much trouble.

The military is the elephant in the room; Lacerda appointed Golbery do Couto e Silva, an influential figure within the pragmatist Sorbonne faction, as Minister of War. If Lacerda brings too much instability, he may seek to coup the government.
strings.BRA_varguist_devils_desc:
Varguism cannot be completely defeated through a single election, as demonstrated by the presidency of Eduardo Gomes. Despite progress, there are still millions of people sympathetic to Varguist ideas and influential forces that continue to linger, poised to reemerge.

To prevent the return of Varguism, the government must remain vigilant. It is imperative to address the economic anxieties that populists exploit by implementing a comprehensive economic plan to stimulate growth, improve living conditions, and alleviate vulnerability to Varguist ideologues.

In addition to economic measures, it is crucial to tackle Varguist sympathies within the military and public service. Rigorous vetting procedures, transparency, and accountability are essential for identifying and removing individuals holding Varguist beliefs.
strings.BRA_guanabaran_deluge_desc:
The devastating impact of the floods in Rio is undeniably tragic, leaving behind a trail of destruction and displacing numerous individuals. However, amidst this tragedy, an opportunity exists to bolster the government's reputation, and Lacerda's personal support. Given the extensive support required to aid the displaced residents and facilitate the recovery and restoration efforts in the affected areas, it is crucial that we proactively ensure that the media recognizes and acknowledges the government's substantial contribution.

The magnitude of the disaster necessitates significant government assistance to provide relief, facilitate resettlement, and start the rebuilding and cleanup of devastated regions. We must leverage this situation to maximize Lacerda's and his administration's positive exposure and public perception. By ensuring that the media portrays Lacerda's leadership and commitment to addressing the needs of the affected communities, his personal support and the standing of the government will be bolstered in the eyes of the public.
strings.BRA_automatic_alignment_desc:
The UDN has long been an advocate for further integration with America. When they last held the presidency, Brazil was granted OFN partner status.
