It's a no-brainer to hitch Brazil to the giant machine that is the American economy. Our geographic proximity makes trade easy, and the American market beckons for our resources. Lacerda's administration will attempt to broker additional trade agreements with the United States and encourage investment from their companies.

Strong democracies working together is imperative if the world is to be free of despotism and autocracy. Let this closer connection be the catalyst that supercharges the economy of the American continent and shows the world the superiority of liberal democracy.
strings.BRA_uncover_varguist_crimes_desc:
Lacerda's personal experience with the malevolence of Varguism runs deep; he narrowly escaped death during Vargas' regime when his minions sanctioned an attempt on his life. Although Lacerda was fortunate enough to survive, countless others were not. Tragically, many of these violent acts never saw the light of day, concealed from public knowledge. However, now is the time for restitution. The Crow, wielding the full might of the government, is determined to investigate every wrongdoing that transpired under the oppressive rule of Getúlio Vargas. The books will be opened, no stone shall remain unturned, and every individual implicated in these ignominious deeds will face the consequences of their actions.

The pursuit of justice for the atrocities committed under Vargas' regime is paramount. Let this new committee send a signal to the people of Brazil that totalitarianism will not be tolerated.
strings.BRA_urbanize_favelas_desc: The 1965 election was a nail-biter. If Lacerda is to ensure a safer margin of victory in 1970, he must broaden his appeal beyond the typical UDN base of the middle class and businesspeople. Advisors have highlighted the urban poor as a possible target. Many live in squalor and without utilities in densely packed Favelas. An investment in local infrastructure will be necessary to bring wealth into these neighbourhoods and develop them further. People will be naturally grateful to see their government supporting them, and some will return our favour with their support. A growing middle class will further benefit the party as Brazil continues to grow under Lacerda's economy.
strings.BRA_new_neighborhoods_desc: Favelas are blights on Brazilian cities. They are hotbeds of crime and waste valuable land that should be developed. When Lacerda was Governor of Guanabara, he implemented a policy of bulldozing these Favelas and building new, modern, high-rise apartments. Now as President, Lacerda will ensure that other state governors will do the same, with the federal government's full support backing them. While there will be plenty of backlash from the urban poor, a new middle class will arise in their place. They will fuel our economic development and secure us a new loyal source of support.
strings.BRA_perons_shadow_desc:
Unfortunately, Argentina has proved to be a far too unreliable neighbour. The stain of Peronism still looms large, and much like Varguism, its short-sighted populist policies have left a shadow on the Argentine economy.

While initially there was the hope of detente, even reformers like Frondizi did not end the cold war with Argentina and have continued reckless actions like the backing of fascist Paraguay and attempted sabotage of the Transandean Treaty. They are a lost cause, and thus we must continue to be wary of them - keeping our army on alert, continuing espionage efforts in Argentina and its proxies and winning the economic war with our superior policies.
strings.BRA_spring_tunes_desc: Lacerda plans a raft of reform, and to do so he must introduce a wide range of executive orders to build the foundations of this reform. No stone will be left unturned; the military, the administrative state, corruption and the bureaucracy will not be safe. These changes will improve the efficiency of the government, liberalise the country and herald a new era of prosperity for Brazil.
strings.BRA_enemy_no_1_desc:
The incompetence of previous administrations has led to a persistently high level of inflation, creating a hidden tax eating at the workers' paychecks. The short-sighted populist policy they implemented may have been appealing in the short term. Still, the longer-term costs on businesses have undone any possible benefit that increased wages brought. Lacerda has a swathe of policies to implement and appeal to deal with the problem. Regulations on businesses need to be loosened, as well as the grip of unions on them - so companies need not pass so many costs onto the consumer.

Another driver of inflation has been the spending on costly infrastructure projects that have led to no results and often the embezzlement of funds. These too, must be cut to take some money out of the overheated economy. Finally, we will pause any increases to the minimum wage. While Lacerda would prefer to eliminate it entirely, the backlash from our previous attempt proved it unfeasible to do so. Therefore we must settle on it but allow it to decrease in real terms with inflation.
strings.BRA_shield_of_the_republic_desc:
As Lacerda takes charge, the dysfunctional relationship between the government of Brazil and her military once again threatens to flare into uncontrollable rage. Never has a government survived long without the consent of her ornery partner, a fact which Lacerda knows all too well. The beast must be fed, lest it go on the hunt.

In reluctant recognition of this fact, Lacerda has greenlit yet more funding to be granted to air and submarine research. No price is too high to maintain our friendly relationship with the military.
strings.BRA_the_freedom_fighter_desc:
War is mainly fought on the ground, but it is those who control the skies that have the upper hand on the battlefield. Unfortunately, our Air Force isn't known for operating modern aircrafts, with some even dating back from the later days of the Second War! How can we make a true difference in the crusade against Nazism in places like South Africa if we can barely defend our own skies?

Thankfully, our Yankee friends had offered us an interesting deal: the purchase of a fair amount of one of their most advanced jets at their disposal, the Northrop F-5 Freedom Fighter. Its cheap price and maintenance, combined with its versatility and outstanding performance in combat makes it the perfect choice for us and our Air Force's needs. It is time for our brave pilots to Sentar a Púa once more!
strings.BRA_brazilian_fire_desc:
Fire has always played an important role in the development of human civilization, it brought both safety and destruction. After all, was it not the fire that the mythical Prometheus gave us, humans? A gift that brought upon him the wrath of Olympus itself. Now President Lacerda, following the steps of the Greek hero, will bring “fire” to Brazil.

Napalm, a gelling agent mixed with gasoline or other fuel, is widely used by all three superpowers. Highly effective in bombing campaigns, it brings death and destruction on a scale surpassed only by the atomic bomb. To ensure Brazil's safety and an edge over its enemies, President Lacerda will contact the United States, with the goal of acquiring napalm for the armed forces of Brazil.
strings.BRA_early_warning_systems_desc:
The threat of Argentina is ever present. They have put a lot of pride in their airforce and use it to devastating effect. They use it to harass Uruguay into being their puppet, they have used it to bomb Paraguayan freedom fighters in the Guaíra Falls invasion and have used it to reinforce their claims in Antarctica. If we were to ever fight Argentina in a war, they would use it against us to devastating effect.

That is why prevention is one of the best forms of deterrence we have. We do not war, but we will fight if we want. And while we build up our air force with the freedom fighter, we must ensure the Argentinians cannot launch a surprise attack. With early warning radar systems, we can detect a Argentinian offensive before it occurs, and scramble our fighters to defeat any surprise attack.
strings.BRA_training_in_panama_desc:
With an influx of new fighter jets, it's crucial to ensure that our pilots have the necessary skills and knowledge to operate them. Fortunately, it appears that the United States has a solution to our problems.

School of the Americas or SOTA in short, is an american-runned school located in Panama set up to provide training to foreign military personnel. We will send our pilots to train with the most qualified and experienced personnel OFN has to offer, there they will familiarize themselves with the newest strategies and tactics employed by OFN pilots in various conflicts across the globe.
strings.BRA_operation_saucer_desc:
In the North of Brazil there have been many disturbing reports. Sightings of aliens, UFOs, and angels, all harbingers of the apocalypse. But the latest report is more than just disturbing. Spy satellites and Axis weather balloons spying on critical infrastructure in the north of the country and revealing military assets.

Lacerda has stated he will not allow this to take place. Under the codename OPERATION SAUCER, we will launch a military operation. Publicly it will be to investigate the reports and prove that there are no such sightings. Secretly it will be a military training exercise. An operation to train pilots and destroy any fascist spy devices that are found floating in the sky.
strings.BRA_enbrarer_investment_desc:
In the past days, we have received interesting reports from our Air Force's scientific institutions detailing the great progress they have been making on their internal project codenamed as IPD-6504. A prototype built with one bold goal in mind: to put on the skies our very first fully-national aircraft. As the representatives of the Brazilian people's will, it is our solemn duty to support this initiative and bring this dream to reality.

We will help direct into the project investments from private capital, as well as encouraging foreign specialists to contribute with their expertise. This act of goodwill will not only immensely boost the project's development and ensure its success, but also help to plant the seeds that will kickstart the growth of our own strategic national aerospace industry and begin a new era of technological development in our country.
strings.BRA_civil_purposes_desc:
We've done it! The first flight of our Bandeirante (formerly known as IPD-6504) was a tremendous success, and there are already numerous calls from within and outside the country interested in it. However, to fulfill these demands, we must focus on planning the necessary procedures in order to mass produce the aircraft.

President Lacerda will sign a series of directives that will set the steps to give the shape of an aerospace company based on the same installations and personnel behind the Bandeirante's success baptized as EMBRAER. As ordered by the President, EMBRAER will be a fully privatized company which will base most of its business on the civilian market, freeing it from the corruption and ineffectiveness of the state and serving the people's best interests. And, of course, enjoying free authority in assisting our military with research and development.
strings.BRA_the_national_interest_desc:
It is an unfortunate reality that our independence is under constant threat. Be it from our southern enemies, be it from the totalitarian snakes lurking in the shadows to subvert and enslave our people, as Operation Saucer had shown it. National defense is a business that must be taken very seriously, one that must be overseen by the State if we want to guarantee a safe future for Brazil.

Thus, we will help kickstart the development of our non-existent aerospace industry by investing heavily in aerospace projects and research and cooperating with private corporations. Providing much needed jobs for the common man as well as securing our skies from external threats and ensuring our dominance and might in South America.
strings.BRA_the_super_tucano_desc:
With the resounding success of the Bandeirante, which showed promising results in executing military missions, we can now finally consolidate our industry in the national defense business by officializing the creation of our first company dedicated to aircraft production, the EMBRAER. A quasi-state owned company that will be primarily focused on military aircraft production.

As requests for war planes coming from our Air Force flood our desk, our dedicated engineers are already working hard on what will be our first war plane in history! Named after the famous bird that populates our forests, the EMB-312 “Tucano” will be a low-cost light attack aircraft, with a simple yet innovative design and effective lethality. With this achievement, the skies of Brazil will no longer be protected by “teco-tecos” and third-rate foreign planes, but by aircrafts manufactured by ourselves.
strings.BRA_atomic_taboo_desc:
The A-bomb, the nuke, the atom bomb - there are a number of names for the most powerful weapon ever devised by mankind, but all that truly matters are the effects. There is no single explosive so powerful as the nuclear weapon, nor is there another weapon which captures the fears and worries of the world so. In one strike, cities are wiped from the map as if God came down with a hammer and chisel, or armies are devastated and left scattered across their positions. Ever since Rotterdam was turned into a smoking crater, the great powers of the world have moved rapidly to expand their arsenals as quickly as possible, and those nations around them concerned with their own safety have looked into the nuclear option as well, for those who possess an A-bomb have all the cards against those who do not.

Among these nations, we are told, is Argentina.

The thought of the Argentines having a nuclear imbalance with ourselves is the creation of nightmares. If we cannot stop the Peronists and Colorados from building the bomb, then the best we can do is build one before them.
strings.BRA_contact_kissinger_desc:
Henry Kissinger in the States has been a fine ally of ours for many years now, and he is beyond pleased to see that our people have seen the world in a more American light ever since Lacerda ascended to office. He holds weight in places which we do not, commands power to people which we may not otherwise get through to, speaks for us when none will listen. Kissinger may be Lacerda's best friend in D.C., and friends are hard to come by in this business.

It is critical, then, that we maintain that friendship and take it as far as it will go - and a nuclear program is certainly very, very far.

It may shock him to hear something that sounds so far fetched, but we can surely get it through to him that such a program is necessary to defend both Brazilian and American interests in South America - and if we have Kissinger on our side, we might just have a chance to get the Americans with us too.
strings.BRA_camp_david_talks_desc:
This is a job for Lacerda himself, he knows. He packs up his suitcase, takes his many files, adjusts his suit, and boards a direct flight from Brasília to Washington D.C. - but this is no state visit, and hardly an announced one at all. There will be no great military greeting, no President at the tarmac - instead, he will be whisked away to the refuge of Camp David for a series of secretive and very worried talks.

News of Brazil poking around the idea of a nuclear program has gone down at the Pentagon like a... well, an A-bomb. There has been much grinding and gnashing of teeth by those too cowardly and ignorant to understand our fears, who beg the President to shut us down before we start. Indeed, any program we would hope for would be instantly shuttered if the Americans forbid us from the task, as much as the prospect of bending the knee to the Yankees pains us. That is why it is crucial that we prevent that from happening.

That is why Lacerda is going himself - to ensure that, in these critical talks, the fate of Brazil will be in Brazilian hands.
strings.BRA_camp_david_talks_tooltip: Brazil and the United States of America will now undergo negotiations over Brazil's nuclear prospects - America will get to choose who is in control.
strings.BRA_silent_assassin_desc:
The World Wars caused a great many changes in the world, but the naval theater of combat was perhaps one of the most affected by its innovation. The dreadnoughts of old, expensive prides of the sea, were rendered obsolete by aircraft carriers, and the practice of sneaking transport ships across the oceans was too made a fool's errand by the rise of the U-Boat and submarine warfare. Naval combat today is no longer a practice of ships in lines raking one another with gunfire, but instead the silent hunt of planes for fleets and submarines for convoys.

Aircraft carriers are well beyond the reach of Brazil's comparatively diminutive navy, but submarines can and shall be the backbone of our future on the oceans and rivers of South America, as Lacerda sees it. The Americans surely have not shied away from this new frontier of warfare - and while we may have to shy away from the nuclear-armed cutting edge of submarine warfare, we have received word from Canberra that the Australians have a plethora of 40's vintage that are just begging for a new buyer to give them life.
strings.BRA_silent_assassin_tt: We will create 6 Gato Class Ships from the United States.
strings.BRA_modern_tank_desc:
The Brazilian Army, while certainly well-funded and politically powerful, is no better off in terms of equipment than the Navy and Air Force is. Too often our men are equipped with the cast-offs and hand-me-downs of greater forces, from Sherman tanks to Garand rifles to World War Two-era trucks. It's time for us to change all that.

Few armies in the world are greater than that of America's, and they surely have a vast stockpile of weapons and equipment which, while perhaps not their most modern gear, would surely be an improvement over the decades-old army which we field now. With our good relations with them, surely they will be willing to spare some of their more modern tank designs to give us a leg up on any rival power in the region, whomever they may be.
strings.BRA_bargain_completed_desc:
Power flows through the barrel of the gun, it is said, and in Brazil that idiom is certainly more true than ever. The Army has always been a lurking force in the background of her politics, watching quietly for any movement which they thought threatened Brazil - or themselves, to be more honest - and sweeping in to restore order whenever they find that threat too great. Lott wanted this changed, wanted a depoliticized Army loyal to the state instead of the generals. It was that disconnect which Lacerda has exploited.

The Army's backing on his way to power was not the only end of this deal, however. They expect funding, arms, personal checks. Now that we hold power, all that and more can and will be delivered upon, for Lacerda is surely not foolish enough to try and challenge the Army that he just empowered so greatly. It may be tough to keep the tail from wagging the dog, but all that can be spared for later - for now, there is happy harmony between the army and the state, and so long as the checks keep flowing, all that will remain.
strings.BRA_streamline_civil_service_desc: The Brazilian administrative state continues to be a basketcase. Sometimes funds just disappear into a black hole, and many programs are terribly inefficient. Lacerda has developed several plans to deal with these problems. Reforms need to be made to cut down on the fat, excessive bureaucracy and regulation strangle any hope of efficiency - this will be reduced. Some programs can be contracted out to private enterprise, and the private sector's attitude needs to be brought into the government. The Brazilian people must know that their tax dollars are going towards something useful, and these reforms will make sure of that.
strings.BRA_Establish_ENAP_desc:
Since we have eliminated much of the corruption in the government, it is necessary to reorganize the civil service system. However, the shortage of skilled and qualified officials continues to endanger the nation. We require a team of proficient middle to high-ranking civil service workers to address this management challenge.

Consequently, the National School of Public Administration will be established to handle this problem by training the brightest minds in Brazil. Providing the finest administrative education and deploying graduates to different states across the nation would be the optimal approach to serving the country effectively.
strings.BRA_Regionalize_Administration_desc:
Brasília nestles itself in the distant highlands, far away from most citizens, yet somehow those officials are the ones deciding the fate of the entire country. What a perfect symbol for the slow and corrupt centralized bureaucracy it houses. This separation fosters inefficiency, breeds inter-state disparity, and fuels a bureaucratic beast blind to the diverse cultures, needs, and dreams of the people it ostensibly serves.

With Lacerda at the helm, Brazil will see a seismic shift towards regional devolution. Responsibilities traditionally held by the central government would trickle down to state or local governments. The federal administration, too, would be torn from its comfortable perch in the capital, as the President commences relocating divisions closer to the constituents they serve.
strings.BRA_anti_corruption_crusade_desc:
When Carlos Lacerda became Governor of Guanabara, he sacked his own mother. Politics is no place for family business. Nothing disgusted him more than rich idiots who attained power and prestige just by “knowing the right people”. Simply put, they ruined democracy. They prevented those with skills and principles from ever getting to where they deserve.

In one grand crusade, he will dismantle dynasties and break up bloodlines. He will institute measures for extra transparency, mandate financial disclosure, boost existing anti-corruption agencies, and protect whistleblowers. Nepotism must be purged, and the new President will do anything he can to root it out.
strings.BRA_competency_tests_desc:
What does it take to become a bureaucrat in Brazil? Not much if we're being honest, the current requirements to enter the state bureaucracy are insultingly low for a position of such importance. Thankfully with the ascendance of Carlos Lacerda to the seat of presidency, drastic changes are about to take place.

Audits, competency tests and a general overview of our current administration are just a few steps the government will take to ensure government workers have the necessary degree of technical, administrative and legal knowledge. No longer will we settle for average, only the best can serve Brazil.
strings.BRA_Professionalize_Politics_desc:
The average Brazilian views politics as a sort of a joke, some place where you can enter to get rich or famous. This view, real or not, is antithetical to the President's idea of how politics should function in Brazil.

In order to “professionalize politics” President Lacerda will institute background checks for politicians running for senate, more debates, be them public or not, to get the general population interested in politics, media interviews, and more. Hopefully this will be enough to begin the transformation of Brazilian politics.
strings.BRA_lacerda_Meritocratic_Government_desc:
With reforms to the civil service enacted Brazil is on its way to for the first time in history have a government that is truly meritocratic. Skill and merit have replaced connections and status as the key requirements for joining the state bureaucracy, corruption is being dealt with and overall people take politics more seriously. A great victory has been achieved by the Lacerda administration, despite that now is not the time to rest on our laurels.

We need to ensure that the current state of affairs remains for as long as possible, unless we want to return to the Brazil of old. Regular audits and anti-corruption measures will help keep bureaucrats on their toes and ensure that our hard work won't be undone.
strings.BRA_equalize_education_desc:
The policy of Education is one of prime importance for Brazil. With a booming population it is imperative that all Brazilians get a good education, to ensure a economic boom. The UDN is a party divided between which approach to take. Lacerda initially wanted to appoint Flexa Ribeiro, a trusted co-worker to the Ministry of Education and they have so far led the ministry in tackling illiteracy. However due to requests from others in the party, Lacerda will officially appoint Gilberto Freyre to the position.

A well known polymath and the creator of the theory of Lusotropicalism, he is a skilled manager who will ensure that the maths, sciences and humanities all get the support that they need to thrive in Brazil and create a well-educated, skilled workforce. Lacerda will, of course, ensure he keeps a eye on the ministry and, by placing Flexa as a special advisor to the ministry, can ensure the Crow's and Gilberto's aims work alongside each other.
strings.BRA_national_literacy_campaign_desc: Despite the rapid economic development in recent years, illiteracy remains a major problem, especially in the rural areas. It should be quite obvious to everyone that this cannot continue and only proper government intervention can put an end to illiteracy and uplift our people. President Lacerda has ordered a launch of a nation-wide literacy campaign with the ambitious goal of achieving a literacy rate of 90% no later than 1970.
strings.BRA_lacerda_passed_lit_act_tt: We have passed The Universal Literacy Act.
strings.BRA_cooperate_church_desc: The Catholic Church is a major supporter of education throughout Brazil, with church-run schools playing an important part in our education system. As a part of a bigger education reform President Lacerda has chosen to work with the church despite Brazil's rocky history with the institution. Funds will be delivered to Catholic schools and in exchange the church will cooperate with the government, while this may rub the less conservative elements of Brazilian society the wrong way, ensuring at least a working relation with the church is crucial for the President's plans regarding education.
strings.BRA_maintain_equality_desc: Brazil is a vast country, and ensuring each and every school within it meets a certain standard of quality is simply an impossible task with the current system. Education lies mostly within the carefree hands of the private sector, which allows some schools to flourish but leaves those without the funds to grease the wheels to fall by the wayside. If this continues, an entire generation of Brazilians may once again find themselves excluded from the future of their own nation. By placing education within the responsible custody of the government, we can begin making steps to escape this bleak status quo.
strings.BRA_oligatory_lessons_desc:
Kids labor in the streets when they should be studying, and adults are lining up at churches to ask literate pastors to fill their registry forms. What education obligations they have solely exists on paper.

However, we've heard word of a man who claims he taught three hundred farmers to read and write in a mere forty-five days. Sure, a background check on Paulo Freire found some unfortunate leftist leanings, but his achievements are very much real.

He suggests perhaps we help parents take their kids to school by providing them free meals. Or make timetables more flexible to accommodate both adults and kids. Or we could put his revolutionary literacy course for adults to the test.
strings.BRA_education_education_war_desc:
Any child could tell the country has changed since Vargas, but the curriculum does not reflect that. Brazil's sons and daughters deserve a modern syllabus which reflects them and their era, where our national values are placed at the center.

We will begin a war on the antiquated system of today, starting by standardizing the education system so that all students are learning the same content across the board. They shall appreciate Brazil for what it is: a Lusotropical country, a unique blend of European and African immigrants with the native population, forming a modern, tropical bastion of freedom. Change must take people with it, however, so while we might want to call Vargas' quasi-fascist regime what it is, we will only highlight the dangers of its authoritarianism instead. At least for now.
strings.BRA_lacerda_education_edu_war_tooltip: Every child will leave the school knowing about the uniqueness of Brazil. The first modern tropical civilization made out of a mix of Portuguese colonists, African slaves, and an indigenous population, enhanced with a balanced view of the Estado Novo.
strings.BRA_expand_universities_desc:
The Lacerda administration has inherited many problems with learning in this country, but the most pressing is the state of higher education. Our burgeoning industry demands expertise from early adulthood to make it competitive, and most institutions remain out of reach of the masses which need them most. Freyre has tabled three plans to address the shame of inadequate universities. Either we focus on university expansion, engineering polytechnics which could inject industrial expertise into our workforce, or massively increase scholarships, and hence social mobility with it.

With an opposition desperate to cry mismanagement, we do not have the world to spend. We must choose wisely.
strings.BRA_stop_funding_UNE_desc:
The UNE, or the National Union of Students has been the largest student organization in Brazil ever since it was founded in 1937. Although de facto apolitical, it has been continuously funded and supported by the PTB for some time, with the organization having strong Varguist tendencies.

A large youth organization that is opposed to our cause is a concern for our administration, and so a rival student organization is to be created, hopefully without sparking too much tension with the UNE.
strings.BRA_banish_ignorance_desc: Right on schedule, we have pushed standards up nationwide, and spectacularly at that. Nearly all children are in school systems, which are repurposed and tailored for Brazil's unique standing, and adult illiteracy is plummeting. We are in the position to give ignorance a crushing blow. While there is still work to be done, and likely more to do even for later presidencies, a turning point has surely come about. We are on the last steps on the staircase to prosperity. Brazil's future is calling from the landing.
strings.BRA_universalize_healthcare_desc: Brazil, like any democracy worth its salt, envisions a society in which all men are created equal. However, as far as the current state of Brazilian healthcare is concerned, some are clearly considered more equal than others. While the prosperous south of the country enjoys solid health coverage, the north is forced to make do with more localized options that can be extortionately priced and lackluster in comparison to what is available in the south. President Lacerda seeks to rectify this gross injustice by providing universal healthcare coverage to every corner of Brazil, no matter how poor or far-flung.
strings.BRA_universal_vaccination_desc: Brazil will never be a truly modern state until its people can live and thrive without fear of dying from preventable ailments. The scourge of smallpox may be on the decline in more affluent parts of the world, but in Brazil, it remains a serious danger to those who cannot afford the vaccine. In the interest of preventing yet more deaths that could've been avoided, we must provide universal vaccinations to the people. Once national mortality rates begin to crash, we can truly say that Brazil is on the road to modernity. Until then, however? There is work to be done, and shots to give.
strings.BRA_dreaming_clean_water_desc: A major source of illness in Brazil, unfortunately, comes from our own negligence. For many years, we have allowed the waters that run across our nation to become mired in pollutants, and even sources that the Brazilian people use for their drinking water have not been spared. The spread of cholera, dysentery, and other diseases could easily be prevented if action were to be taken to ensure clean drinking water for all Brazilians, and President Lacerda intends to do just that. Laws shall be put forth to tighten safety standards regarding drinking water, and to expand the aging infrastructure that delivers said water to millions of homes across Brazil.
strings.BRA_reduce_infant_mortality_desc: Every day in Brazil, tens of thousands of nameless tragedies take place. The premature death of an infant is the nightmare of any mother, and, regrettably, infant mortality rates in Brazil paint a startlingly grim picture of what the poorer families of the country suffer. Tackling this issue is no small feat, and while the expansion of healthcare can certainly make a dent in this frightening statistic, we must look to success stories across the world for guidance on how to save Brazil's families from tragedy. America, Sweden, and other nations have long since ensured a reasonable expectation of survival for their sons and daughters; why not turn to them for assistance?
strings.BRA_rural_health_clinics_desc: Within the sprawling metropolises of southern Brazil, nobody, no matter how rich or poor, is outside the reach of a hospital. Anyone can get the care they need, with paramedics standing by to deal with emergencies at a moment's notice. The story in the rural regions, however, is much different. Many communities do not even have the most rudimentary of medical facilities, leaving the locals to fend for themselves with little in the way of medicine or professional expertise. At the government's expense, the President intends to put a stop to this backwards state of affairs, and fund the construction of clinics in the rural communities that need them the most.
strings.BRA_mosquito_campaign_desc: With the incessant buzzing of a million tiny wings comes the infamous mass-killer of the developing world: malaria. Tens of thousands of Brazilians are lost to the mosquito-borne illness every year, especially in the forests and jungles of the rural north, and President Lacerda has decided that enough is enough. It is time to take the fight to those irritating insects once and for all and protect our people from their deadly bites! If the nets aren't enough to stop the mosquitos' advance, the liberal application of pesticides will surely be enough to stamp out the spread of malaria for good.
strings.BRA_increase_medic_wages_desc:
One of the biggest problems our healthcare system faces is emigration. Every year, an enormous amount of talented medical students graduate, only to move to countries like America, that can provide proper wages. As a result, we suffer from a critical shortage of qualified medical personnel, and will not be able to pursue any further healthcare reform until the problem is resolved.

Luckily, the solution to the problem is fairly simple. By increasing the wages doctors, surgeons, and other advanced medics are afforded, we can stop the flow of the brain drain at the source, and restore some of the knowledge we have lost.
strings.BRA_rely_on_market_desc: Lacerda has always been an advocate for the free market, so why should welfare be any different? We know that the market has the raw power needed to develop our healthcare industries, and will be a far cheaper alternative than continuing the overreliance on government spending we are trying so desperately to dismantle. After all, privatized healthcare worked out so well in the United States, why not in Brazil as well?
strings.BRA_government_intervention_desc: As much as Lacerda wishes otherwise, the state must take a strong stance in healthcare if the institution is to survive. He will not risk the lives of millions of Brazilians for his own personal preference, and even the free market advocates must understand the necessity of this choice. If some members of the party have complaints, let them shout; Lacerda lives in the world of reality, and shall act with reason, not ideology.
strings.BRA_lacerda_healthcare_reform_req_tt: Lacerda's version of Healthcare reform has been passed.
strings.BRA_kill_first_horseman_desc:
It is the duty of the government of Brazil to fight against the four horsemen of the apocalypse, and defend the people of the nation from their curses. In the world of today, Pestilence, Famine, War, and Death stand ready to descend upon the unprepared at the first sign of weakness, so we must always stand vigilant, as any oversight could spell disaster.

Today, the UDN and Lacerda have struck a decisive blow against the horseman of Pestilence, and disrupted his foul influence over Brazil. Whichever path we have taken, we have massively strengthened our nation against the evils of disease.
strings.BRA_lacerda_agriculture_SDA_desc:
The Brazilian countryside is on the edge of a cliff. Peasant leagues, Amazonist guerillas, militias funded by cattle ranchers, and countless other little armies all fight their tiny wars. Rural Brazil needs a intervention to save it. Some of those destabilizing factors have lasted for years, the Latifundia system has existed from colonial Portugal in the 1500's. To ensure the future success of our agricultural policies, Lacerda will create a new department, the Office of Agricultural Protection, the SDA.

This will not just be a department of paper pushers focused on increasing numbers of corn and maize grown, it will be a supervisiory system. Monitoring checking, appointing and removing corrupt officials, and trying to bring peace to a broken countryside. All the affairs of agricultural policies will be under their remit. Lacerda hopes that they can clear large amounts of corruption from agriculture, reduce the prevelance of violence in rural regions, and help foster economic development.
strings.BRA_lacerda_rural_credit_desc:
Farming is not the most profitable job. Many farmers are simply subsistence farmers, farming their little patches of land to ensure that they and their family produce enough food to eat. For those farmers trying to better themselves and increase development, what is disturbing was the lack of investment banks would give in loans. Small farmers lack the guarantees and returns that would get banks to invest. Instead, they continue to invest in the property of large landholders and major businesses.

It is time to take action and change the status quo. A specialized new credit system will be established to provide investment to small farm owners. Agricultural machines, chemical fertilizer, pesticides, all will be possible to be purchased using this new credit system. In return the government will take a dividend from their annual incomes until the loan is repaid. This will help us spread mechanisation across Brazil and spread the green revolution to every farm!
strings.BRA_lacerda_fertilise_cerrado_desc:
In the heart of Brazil, the low rumbling calls of the southern lapwing echo across a vast rolling savanna. Hawks and vultures soar above low twisted trees and cacti. This is the Cerrado. For centuries, no one has tamed it, the soil too acidic and nutrient-poor to host domesticated crops.

But what if we could change that? Researchers repeat the same three ingredients: agricultural lime, borax, and PNX fertilizer. It's worth investigating; expand some northern farms into the region and see what happens.

Remember, this land covers a quarter of Brazil! Nature reserves? National parks? We could be sitting on the new Breadbasket of the Americas, three times the size of Ukraine. This could be the start of an agricultural revolution!
strings.BRA_lacerda_buffer_stock_desc: The food situation in Brazil has the rather unfortunate habit of being unpredictable in the worst of times. Severe droughts can seriously harm the supply of food to the country, and the prices have often seen fit to wildly change from one day to the next. In such an uncertain environment, it pays to be prepared for the worst. The President has seen fit to approve the establishment of new storage facilities for food reserves across Brazil, to ensure our people have food security even in the worst case scenarios.
strings.BRA_lacerda_agri_bastion_against_radical: Land reform remains a hot button issue in Brazil, with more members of the ruling coalition finding the idea to be more palatable as popular resentment against the situation grows. What these idealists fail to realize, however, is that broad land reform is simply a political impossibility. To enact such drastic measures would jeopardize our commitments to the middle class: those who we have to thank for our electoral successes. We will clamp down on any further entertaining of radical solutions, and work instead to curb the worst excesses of the land barons where it is possible.
strings.BRA_lacerda_conservative_land_reform_des: One does not have to be a radical socialist to understand the necessity for some land reform. It is true that there are large swathes of underutilized lands that are not currently meeting their economic potential. Lacerda will enact some small land transfers to deal with this problem, leading to greater utilization and equity of land. Alongside this, Lacerda will legalize farmer's syndicates to make investment in agricultural land easier and allow smaller farmers to cooperate and coordinate with each other, and increase their combined output.
strings.BRA_lacerda_inter_brazil_cooperation_des: Brazil is on the cusp of realizing its potential as a power player on the global stage, and it is our increased focus on inward strength that has brought us to this point. There is plenty of work yet to be done, however, to ensure that the various subdivisions of the country come together for Brazil's common benefit. The expansion of the rural regions has progressed at a wildly inconsistent pace, and the President has just the solution. New legislation has been authorized to ensure each region cooperates on the expansion of agriculture on a level playing field, with modern fertilizers and farming equipment. Let us show the world that when Brazilians work together, there is not a force in the world that could possibly get in their way!
strings.BRA_obliterate_lotts_folly_desc:
The Trans-Amazonian Highway can be described in many ways. Among those visionaries who planned the project, it was to become the new artery of Brazil, or even South America - a bridge from East to West, crossing thousands of miles of rainforest and creating a new line of development nationwide. To the realists and the clear-eyed, it has become a bloated, overladen folly, twisted around by corrupt dealings and stalled by weather and politics. To push forwards now, against all reason, would be absurd.

Carlos Lacerda is ready to make these hard decisions, unlike those who preceded him. At his word, the construction will be tied off - the offshoots either closed or attached to other roads, and the project abandoned to the jungle it once bulldozed. The funds we shall save will do nicely in the more critical pieces of the Brazilian state.
strings.BRA_new_tools_greatest_manager: New Tools for the Greatest Manager
strings.BRA_new_tools_greatest_manager_desc:
The economy is a complicated beast, and it takes all of a man's time if he wishes to manage it effectively. Of course, President Lacerda is quite the busy man, and as such it will fall to his economic minister - Hélio Beltrão - to enact his will for him. Yet there are these regulations, restraints, and laws which constrain the man's work so harshly - no doubt instated by some well-meaning liberal some years ago, but nowadays only serve to get in the way.

Lacerda shall let go of this leash and let his man go after the economy as swiftly and powerfully as he needs to. Only the best, most aggressive work can put together a growing country - it is past time that we got out of the way.
strings.BRA_no_mercy_desc:
Austerity has become a sort of buzzword in the past, decried by whimpering liberals and leftists alike as an attack on the people of Brazil while they make off like bandits with their billions in misattributed funds. It is because of them that our state has bloated so - that we waste money on useless programs and invite financial catastrophe with our ratcheting debt. Hélio Beltrão knows how to solve this troublesome and persistent issue, but it will not be by shying away from the term - instead, we must embrace it.

Why, yes, we will be instating austerity measures. What of it? Would the leftists of this nation rather we go flying over the fiscal cliff? Are they so devoted to keeping the poor of this nation hooked to government policies, cashing welfare checks and living off the dole while never making anything of themselves? We will be throwing a bucket of cold water on the long-sleeping people of this country, and though they may complain now, they will thank us later when they see the benefits of a Brazil that is active, awake, and flourishing.
strings.BRA_tavora_receipts_desc:
A period of austerity is required if Brazil is to get its debt to a manageable level. It will be painful for some, but it is absolutely necessary. The party agrees with this - but unity breaks down regarding the extent and length of this period. Vice President Távora and the other members of the realist faction wish to implement a shorter and less harsh Austerity regime, with tax reforms being implemented in place of more cuts. Lacerda has a difficult path to thread here. His newly empowered Finance Minister Beltrão wants to go all the way with austerity.

Ultimately, Lacerda has decided to side with Távora; the realistas' influence is too strong to ignore. They do have a valid concern; previous radical economic reforms have led to too intense of a backlash. When President Gomes abolished the minimum wage, the UDN was swept out of power by Varguist-aligned parties, undoing much of our progress. We will not repeat this mistake with a radical austerity plan the public will reject.
strings.BRA_increase_coffee_tax_desc:
Coffee is as Brazilian as samba and Carnival, the choice drink of millions both in the nation and around the world. Without it, would our offices bustle as they do, or would our workers toil as hard as they can? These beans have become a financial goldmine for their sellers, a drug with never-ending demand - the only shame is that the government hasn't gotten in on the money too.

Lacerda and his fellow conservatives are not often one for tax raises - after all, it is antithetical to their ideology more often than not - but in some cases, the opportunity is too good to pass up. We can increase our revenue by millions if we raise taxes on coffee by a few percentage points, both for domestic usage and exports. There will be a fair share of justified complaints, but what can we say? What's good for business is good for the government - and for Lacerda most of all.
strings.BRA_increase_interest_rates_desc: It's time to take some riskier moves. Brazil has walked into a dead end and only a tough central bank and swift, decisive policies can save its economy from being totally destroyed. By increasing the rate of loan interest, we can significantly decrease inflation. But of course, this course of action involved many risks, if Beltrão decides to execute this unpopular policy. If we fail to maintain control of interest rates, our middle class backers could turn on us with a vengeance, ensuring electoral annihilation, and this government will be remembered as one of Brazil's more incompetent ones.
strings.BRA_national_lottery_desc: To successfully implement our reforms, the government will need to grow its reserves to fund them. Policymakers have drafted up a national lottery scheme, where citizens can invest in government bonds in return for the chance to win large sums of money and a return on their investment. While it's an unorthodox tactic and may seem somewhat desperate to some, additional funds are always appreciated - wherever they come from.
strings.BRA_death_and_taxs_desc:
Távora has provided a brilliant idea: simplifying taxation and reforming the tax department to enrich the financial base of this government. The inefficency of the economic department has troubled us for a long time. This makes tax simplification a vital policy to help the government regain control of its budget. Due to the nature of our project in reforming Brazil, there is an urgent need to increase our revenue streams.

Redrafting the laws, random checks to ensure regulations are being followed, and cutting the amount of tax exemptions, are all methods to reform the tax system and make it more simple. Furthermore by amending the tax rates on foreign investment and corporation tax, we can make Brazil a more desirable target for investors!

Our economic minister Beltrão has also agreed with these policies, stating that we can afford to spend our political capital on this policy. This is a principle that has united large segments of the UDN and our base.
strings.BRA_centralize_banking_desc:
How can a country call itself developed if it lacks a central bank? Centralized banking is absolutely necessary if a country is to pursue effective macroeconomic policies and be taken seriously by international financiers. Lacerda plans to rectify this issue and establish a central bank to help strengthen the currency and improve economic management.

A core tenet of this new Central Bank will be its independence from the government. If the Brazilian government is ever to fall to populist forces again, our monetary policy must be protected from them. An independent bank will prevent short-sighted populists from setting low-interest rates to temporarily woo voters while causing an unsustainable inflation spike in the longer term. Let the bank's newfound independce be another step in resolving Brazil's historic inflation problem.
strings.BRA_strengthen_coffee_trade_desc: The Coffee Trade is a large part of the Brazilian economy and produces our largest export, even more so within Lacerda's old stomping ground of São Paulo. Before the Estado Novo abolished the coffee-with-milk regime, the coffee industry dominated the politics of São Paulo. Even today, the arrangements that involve the coffee industry are opaque and intertwined with various quotas for specific growers and prices set. It is crucial for Brazil's economy that the stability of this industry is maintained - we will keep prices as high as possible to bring in more revenue.
strings.BRA_free_people_free_trade_desc:
Protectionism and autarky restrain the potential of the Brazilian economy. Lacerda seeks to do away with it and unlock Brazil to global trade. He will eliminate most tariffs with like-minded democratic countries which will increase economic integration between them. This will create economies of scale throughout the democratic world and allow us to create economic dominance over the tyrannical regimes occupying Europe and East Asia.

Brazilian consumers will be granted greater access to the markets of America and will now have access to a wide range of consumer goods. At the same time, our export sector will be able to reach even international customers and create many more jobs for the Brazilian worker. This new economic policy will ensure increased prosperity and liberty for all throughout the democratic world. If the rest of it wishes to indulge in the wonders of free trade, that is.
strings.BRA_guanabara_dreaming_desc:
As a critical part of our economic plan, Guanabara needs millions in investment. Firstly to repair the damage of the New Year's Storm and secondly to make Rio into a centeral hub of Brazil's economic development. We shall make Rio into a cornucopia, a treasure bowl for Brazil's development. But just like all the other parts of Brazil, Rio lags behind the rest of the world. The city is restrained due various factors, Bureaucratism, corruption, political struggle, All of these internal conflicts have meant in the past Rio has lost to international competitors for investment.

But now, with more and more cash rolling into the capital, it's time to restart our ambitious infrastructure construction plan. Hundreds of projects will start to turn Rio into Brazil's grandest city.
strings.BRA_atomic_light_desc:
As we all know that light is a basic need of modern society and an important symbol of industrialization while the electricity supply has become one of the kinds of crucial, indispensable Infrastructure. Without sufficient electricity, even the City of Dreams will lose its light of hope. Due to various challenges, this government does not have the spare time and resources to make big progress.

But now, since we have removed our attention to the economy, it's time to sign a big contract. We will construct a new nuclear power station to provide electricity to the whole nation. What's more, the biggest advantage of this project is that we can make a big trade with Americans and their corporations by purchasing their uranium. All of us - the US, Brazilian people and of course the biggest meritorious, the President, will benefit greatly from such a perfect deal.
strings.BRA_sugarloaf_racing_desc:
Even after all this time, Lacerda never forgot the bleeding, shivering man he held in his arms as they were driven to the hospital; how this proud soldier had looked up at him like a child in one streetlight, then fallen still in the next.

Less than a ten-minute drive away, but more than ten years later, Lacerda stands on the Pão de Açúcar, his eyes sweeping across the glittering expanse of Guanabara Bay, imagining the superstructure shown to him in all the blueprints and proposals.

This mammoth edifice of steel and concrete would span the waters, a box-girder bridge that would connect the burgeoning ambitions of Niterói with the bustling heart of Rio. And when they asked him to name it, he already knew that one person alone deserved to be etched into that horizon forever.
strings.BRA_no_room_homelessness_desc:
Brazil's cities are plagued by a great evil, the rampant scourge of the homeless. This group brings crime, poverty, drugs and disease and turns what should be thriving neighborhoods into run down slums. Crimes cause businesses to close, the middle class to leave and allow gangs to prosper. It is time to end this.

One of Lacerda's main policies as governor of Guanabara was tackling the homelessness epidemic in Guanabara and it would have been successful, if it wasn't for some trigger happy corrupt police officers going too far. Lacerda rectified the failures of the past and worked with mayors and governors to implement sanitation policies, destroying large encampments, making infrastructure uninviting for vagrants and supporting the building of apartment blocks to house these groups. Only through this can we finally end this moral threat once and for all.
strings.BRA_doxadis_industrial_zone_desc:
Rio is a city of hotels, restaurants, and souvenir shops; the city of Copacabana, Pão de Açúcar, and Cristo Redentor. A city that attracts millions of visitors from all over the world. What it is not is a city of industry. Unlike São Paulo's automobiles or Belo Horizonte's burgeoning steel production, Rio never excels at anything beyond tourism.

But that could change. A foreign association of Greek urban planners has arrived with a new interesting mode of thought: ekistics, the science of human settlements. Since 1964, they have been in constant contact with Lacerda, slowly studying the area. Now they've finally come to his office to make a few recommendations to turn Guanabara from a glorified tourist trap into the great metropolis of the future it was meant to be.
strings.BRA_spare_no_expense_desc:
There are those who would say that trying to rebuild Guanabara to its true potential is far too expensive for too little gain. Some would say that urban renewal throughout Brazil should not come at the expense of economic growth. Some would say that Brazil should focus only on middle-class neighborhoods with quality infrastructure, while using cheap concrete for the poor. Lacerda dismisses these arguments.

If we were to cut corners here, we would only be repeating the mistakes of the past. The Guanabaran storm showed the cost of allowing cities to become favelas. Over three hundred dead and thousands injured and displaced due to rotten infrastructure. In the long run, cutting corners will cost more and hinder development than paying the full cost now. That is why we must spare no expense, we will pave the way to the future with highways of gold.
strings.BRA_football_suggestion_desc:
With a straight back and a thick set of binders filled to the brim with annotated reports and letters, Raphael Magalhães walked into Lacerda's office to make his case politely but directly. All these construction projects were too expensive. If he didn't do something about their cost, Brazil's debt could easily become unmanageable.

The President's desk began to fill with return-on-investment calculations and alternative plans. With each additional form laid out before Lacerda, Magalhães presented a different vision, one in which Guanabara and Rio wouldn't have to mortgage their future. Sure, corners would have to be cut but these projects could still be pursued to fruition. Perhaps Lacerda was getting ahead of himself fiscally. If he wants these proposals to succeed, he'd better make sure he can actually afford them.
strings.BRA_south_atlantic_free_port_desc: Attracting foreign investment is another important method to improve our economy besides adjusting our financial policy. By giving every company in the State of Guanabara special preferential tax cuts, which include massive reductions on the of corporation tax, we can make Rio de Janiero become one of the largest commercial hubs in all of South America. If everything goes well, Rio could obtain hundreds of millions of dollars in investment over the next few years, putting the city on par with Buenos Aires and New York. Gigantic successes are in store for the Brazil, Rio is ready to welcome its new bright dawn on the horizon.
strings.BRA_free_the_market_desc: It's time to push forward to continue our work of freeing the market. Since we have finished the initial reforms to make our economy and market get the basically necessary vitality, the next step to break the old chain is to provide the companies a free environment to run their normal businesses. By reducing the amount of red tape and regulations on corporations, and directly abolishing some of them. We will end the restrictive environment in Brazil, which have limited the business climate for years. The good businessmen of Brazil can finally get rid of the restrictions of Getulism. This government will abolish all of those corrupt bureaucratic regulations by passing a bill in the Senado, one clean sweep to lead to a economic revolution!
strings.BRA_lacerda_passed_dereg_act_tt: We have passed The National Deregulation Act.
strings.BRA_shake_up_petrochemistry_desc: Petrobras is one of the key cogs of the Brazilian economy and a important revenue stream for the government. Founded by Getúlio Vargas in 1949 as a desperate ploy to keep power, since then it has been dominated by Getulism. Considering the requirement to increase efficency throughout government departments and businesses in Brazil, we have such a need to reform Petrobras' staff and itself. We shall appoint UDN members and trusted business owners in key positions in Petrobras. This is to make the business more efficent and install a profit oriented approach. These policies will lead to new revenue streams for the government.
strings.BRA_last_vestiges_dirigismse_desc: Kubitschek's National Development Council has been an unmitigated disaster, achieving very little while wasting substantial amounts of money. It is a prime example of corporate cronyism, funding useless projects where most of the funds mysteriously disappear. If these albatrosses were not coddled by government support, the market would never let them fly. In the vast majority of circumstances, the market will be far more efficient then the corrupt bureaucrats shuffling around money - and so we will shut this wasteful council down. Instead, we will allow private enterprise to flourish, with minimal public intervention - no longer wasting the tax dollars of Brazilians, but also leading to more efficient resource allocation.
strings.BRA_investors_paradise_desc:
If the Brazilian economy is to grow to Lacerda's satisfaction, more investment and enterprise is required. With the greater fiscal space that previous spending cuts have freed up, we are able to responsibly reduce the financial burdens on private enterprises that have been keeping the Brazilian economy down. Not only will this further reduce financial burdens on companies and thus deal with inflation, it will also encourage an economic boom within Brazil. Foreign companies will seek out our lower tax rates and set up shop here, fueling the economy and eventually leading to even more tax revenue than the government received from its oppressive higher tax rates. Brazil will become a hub of foreign investment and an example for the world to follow.

Financial relief is not the only way Lacerda plans to grow the economy, and he also proposes scrapping many pointless building regulations. Allowing faster and more efficient construction, creating new spaces for private enterprises to develop and innovate. While some may argue against building deregulation because of safety concerns, the reality is that there is nothing more unsafe than a restrained economy that will not produce the wealth to eliminate deprivation, which can be all too deadly.
strings.BRA_expansion_modernity_desc: Having removed all of its ineffective ideologues, Petrobras is now poised to unlock its full potential. The company's growth will be fueled by fostering partnerships with foreign oil corporations and embracing a fresh cohort of their technologically adept staff. By forming strategic alliances with global industry leaders, Petrobras aims to leverage their expertise, advanced technology, and investment, bolstering Brazil's standing in the international energy market and further fueling Lacerda's plans of economic growth. Encouraging foreign investment will play a key role in this journey, as it will bring in vital resources and expertise, enabling Petrobras to thrive as a forward-thinking player in the global energy landscape.
strings.BRA_stimulate_competition_desc: The Brazilian State has, in the past, given special treatment to a few large companies. This has allowed these companies to bloat and gain contracts with minimal effort. The status quo has locked any inspiring entrepreneurs out of many sectors of the economy, which are instead dominated by large corporations that act like mere extensions of the government, with all the bureaucracy and waste that the government brings too. To further stimulate the Brazilian economy, we need to end these few corporations' monopolies on government contracts. This will breed more competitiveness and efficiency and save the government millions in corporate welfare.
strings.BRA_public_private_partnership_desc: The public sector remains bloated from the actions of previous administrations. With minimal profit motive, government departments suck up cash that often disappears into a black hole. We need to bring the entrepreneurial attitude of the private sector into government rather than bring government waste into the private sector as other administrations have done in the past. Outsourcing government programs to private enterprise will not only save money but lead to far more efficient outcomes. No longer will public servants dawdle around endlessly consulting, but private enterprise will do what private enterprise does best; Innovate, streamline and deliver results!
strings.BRA_come_to_nordeste_desc: Successive governments have neglected the Nordeste Region for too long. It trails in development from the wealthy southeast, but there is immense potential for it to develop in the future. The land is very suitable for agriculture, and the mining companies' exploration has revealed an impressive amount of minerals that could fuel a healthy mining industry within the region. Plenty of necessary investments need to be made to connect Nordeste to the rest of the country and allow for the efficient extraction of resources. With a kickstart from the central government, Nordeste's economy could eventually grow to match that of the prosperous southeast and create an economic miracle for Brazil.
strings.BRA_lacerdanomics_enshrined_desc:
For decades, Varguism haunted this country. Uncontrolled corruption eroded public trust and drained our coffers. State intervention stifled our potential for innovation and stunted entrepreneurial growth. And rampant hyperinflation starved our cities and devastated the livelihoods of millions. No wonder so many of our brightest professionals left for greener pastures elsewhere.

Now, however, Lacerda has broken the chains and transformed the Brazilian economy. He alleviated the nation's addiction to welfare, unleashed trade and foreign investment, and replaced Kubitschek's delusions with a more realistic and pragmatic vision for Brazil's infrastructure. The market can reign free, and industry and commerce can prosper and innovate.

Developmentalism is dead!
strings.BRA_lacerdanomics_enshrined_tooltip: Lacerda has succeeded, developmentalism is dead! Now is the Era of the Free Market.
strings.BRA_lacerda_hemispheric_defence_desc:
After suffering miserable defeat in the Second World War, Brazilians have understood that the only chance to defend Brazil themselves from the threat of Fascism is to strengthen the friendly relationship between Brazil and America.

America is a sound and natural ally, and, arm-in-arm, we will expunge tyranny's toeholds from our continent. For, as our combat in Europe and the fate of its vanquished nations tell us, if Fascism touches the land of Brazil, the only future for our country will be destruction.
strings.BRA_support_brazilian_antarctica_desc:
Considering our geographic position, the capability to defend our coasts is a vital security concern. To achieve this, we must bolster our power projection from Antarctica, an ideal location to counter enemy navies in the South Atlantic. Therefore, this government will send additional supplies to build up the Brazilian Antarctic base.

By strengthening our Antarctic Territory, we also enhance Brazil's international standing and build a strong foundation for “diplomatic relations” with neighbouring countries that aim to develop their own Antarctic Territories...
strings.BRA_focus_hunting_spiders_desc:
There is something rotten in Brazil. Across the country, a web is being weaved by insidious and strange forces that seek to put an end to Brazilian democracy. The issue of fascist spies has long been a thorn in our side - whether they be German, Italian, or even Paraguayan, they have scuttled into the crevices of our society and formed a veritable fifth column.

This will not continue. These spies will be exposed for the traitors they are and punished accordingly. With their networks ripped asunder, there will be nowhere for them to run. Fascism is not, and never will be welcome in Brazil.
strings.BRA_token_force_desc:
We have received a diplomatic request from the OFN. They require a small group of troops to support their deployment in West Africa. Considering the recent course of the war, sending a symbolic force to satisfy their needs has no danger but will demonstrate our importance to the Americans. Besides, the support they requested would be vital in encouraging our military reforms.

We shall deploy our Smoking Snakes to West Africa, to help the Americans get out of the sinkhole. After all, they will not send our soldiers to the battlefield to die, but to easily vanquish disorganized Africans.
strings.BRA_token_force_tt: We can now send volunteers to aid {ffr_getnamewithflag}.
strings.BRA_lacerda_65_join_OFN_desc: As Brazil has already become an OFN partner and an important ally of America, clearly, the further development of our relationship is to be expected. By expressing our intention to join the OFN, we can obtain significant economic, diplomatic, and geopolitical benefits. What's more, if we join the OFN and, our country is attacked by fascists, their nuclear umbrella and vast military might will shield us from destruction.
strings.BRA_rival_banana_fascists_desc: As the only truly democratic country in Latin America, we must fight against dictators or succumb to their malign influence. Accordingly, Lacerda will authorize our intelligence services to search for and destroy any connections between fascist dictators and Brazilian government officials. Brazil has suffered enough from Varguism, and we cannot allow it to happen again under Lacerda's leadership.
strings.BRA_rival_banana_fascists_tt: We will denounce all far-right governments in Latin America!
strings.BRA_OFN_policing_duties_desc:
The OFN has requested additional manpower to support their policing efforts. This presents a considerable opportunity to improve the relationship between ourselves and the alliance.

It is important to avoid putting our soldiers in harm's way in foreign countries, but in doing so, we can enhance Brazil's importance to America and increase the weight of our words. We will follow their instructions to send our personnel to participate in missions to Haiti or any other location they request.
strings.BRA_cameroonian_sinkhole_desc: Not enough. The Yankees have sent another message asking for more force to support their operation in West Africa. This is becoming a considerable investment of military resources, but ultimately we can't pay the price of reneging on our commitments. Although Brazilian citizens won't appreciate an intervention which endangers so many of our boys, we have no choice but to send more troops to Cameroon and pin our hopes on the Americans finishing the job quickly.
strings.BRA_recognise_axis_atrocities_desc:
It has been over twenty years since Brazil began its struggle against Fascism and the Axis. Due to the corruption and dictatorship of Vargas, countless soldiers lost their lives, and we missed the best opportunity to eliminate the Fascistic nightmare forever.

However, there remains a debt that needs to be cleared: the war atrocities of the Axis. We must recognize all possible incidents in order to bring truth and justice to the Brazilian people.
strings.BRA_lacerda_restrict_japan_trade_desc:
The Japanese Empire has a significant hold on Brazil due to the increasing trade between the two countries. This has put the Brazilian government in an awkward position when it comes to executing independent diplomatic policies.

This economic subversion is not easily recognized by the general public, but it has a serious impact on the flexibility of the treasury and policymaking. As a result, the government will take action to investigate and reduce abnormal trade through strategic tariffs in order to protect the interests of the Brazilian people.
strings.BRA_city_of_the_sun_desc:
The US already possesses the right to build their naval bases in northern Brazil. Now, as the West African War escalates, a rapid air corridor to the skies above has become vital. One that could be established via an airbase in our city of Natal.

To bring this conflict to a close, to support our ally, and to bring our boys back home, we would be proud to offer its use.
strings.BRA_more_than_a_puppet_desc:
Lacerda is tired of all the criticism of his presidency and of himself. The left say he is a dictator who seeks to destroy the invaluable legacy of Vargas. The media attacks his policies, claiming he is a puppet of America... Lies.

Lacerda has a plan. Soon he will destroy all the deceit against Brazil and himself, and bring Brazil to the place it should be.
strings.BRA_lacerda_is_in_ofn_tt: We have joined the Organisation of Free Nations
strings.BRA_lacerda_wac_ongoing_tt: The West African Crisis is ongoing and Free France hasn't fallen
strings.BRA_lacerda_wac_over: The West African Crisis is over or Free France has fallen
strings.BRA_imperial_catastrophe_avoided_desc:
With bravery and cunning Lacerda has vanquished the ghosts of 1955, and protected Brazil from the shackles of tyranny once again. The UDN stands triumphant behind the crow; ready and willing to do what must be done for the future of our nation. With a stroke of a pen, Lacerda can reshape the nation at will.

Before we look to impose our vision over the nation, however, we must secure our position. The enemies of Brazil still lurk in the shadows, waiting for a chance to strike our fledgling government in the crib. We must stabilize the country, and force our enemies back into the pits of obscurity
strings.BRA_imperial_trojan_siege_desc:
Every day that passes without decisive action, Brazil trends closer to a state of utter anarchy. The people demand action from the street corners and city halls, shouting for the nation to be purged of autocracy and corruption, and for democratic proccedings to continue. It is our duty to listen to the will of the people, and to answer their pleas.

In his wisdom, the Crow knows what must be done. To protect the democracy of Brazil, Lacerda shall declare a national state of siege until the situation calms down. Our enemies will scream and shout, declare the Crow as a dictator and an autocrat. What of it? Lacerda is willing to make sacrifice to do what must be done.
strings.BRA_imperial_restrained_exile_desc:
With Brizola in chains, and Goulart in exile, the head of the venomous snake has been cleanly severed from the body, and shall no longer threaten to poison our nation. We stand triumphant in congress, and the opposition flails wildly without a clear vision to lead them. By all accounts, the UDN is dominant, and the Crow knows this.

Although some in our party demand retribution, and argue that our party must crush the remaining opposition, Lacerda knows better. We have gone far enough. There is no need to make a hundred martyrs.
strings.BRA_imperial_restrained_exile_tt: We will seek a truce with the Left to prevent outright war.
strings.BRA_imperial_velvet_glove_desc:
Brazil's perceptive feel the cold touch of uncertainty; a force looms over the Government that sees everything we are as a threat to be squashed. They would overturn any right and break any oath in the pursuit of a safe Brazil, a safety they demand through fear. It is essential we do not fall to their level. Habeaus Corpus will be strictly enforced, regardless of their demands, with arrests demanding proper evidence and torture used only where absolutely necessary.

The battle is not just for Brazil, but for its soul. We must demonstrate to all that it is Lacerda - not military men - that safeguard it.

We cannot pretend we have absolute power. We must manage American opinions, trade union rebellion, hardline cabinet members, and the remaining specter of Varguism. We must moderate, even somewhat, to maintain a position that, truth be told, is fairly precarious.
strings.BRA_imperial_velvet_glove_tt: This will reduce support in the OAS for sanctions against us.
strings.BRA_imperial_a_general_pardon_desc: Although some in our government demand harsh punishments for the entire opposition, Lacerda knows better. The PTB and PSD are parties rotten at the core, but they are still composed of many officials and leaders that would support our vision with a little bit of convincing. The Crow is not interested in fighting a bitter struggle to the end; he knows that only reconciliation can finally unite Brazil.
strings.BRA_imperial_realist_approach_desc: Lacerda and his administration realize that the legend of Goulart and Getulism has a powerful influence both domestically and internationally. Even following Vargas' downfall, a significant number of supporters remain in Brazil. Goulart's election victory demonstrated that he and his ideology still have a sturdy support base. This is an awkward circumstance for us. Thus, to manage the upcoming public relations crisis, Lacerda has chosen to request assistance from the OAS outside of Brazil. Though Lacarda has previously voiced criticism of them, their assistance now will aid in managing the unfavourable opinion of the public.
strings.BRA_imperial_walk_the_fine_line_desc:
Every nation, no matter how much it hides it, contains different visions for the future. From the electoral primaries of the USA to the cold backrooms of Tokyo, this is an inescapable fact, and Brazil is little different. To deny this would be folly, and akin to fighting with a hand tied behind us.

We must ensure all within our Government understand that now is the time for moderatism and care. We are in a sensitive age for Brazil, and we cannot let errant cabinet hardliners, Trade Union rebellions nor American opinions derail us. The specter of Varguism hangs heavy still, and many in the nation are frightened of their countryman. Now is the time to thread the fine line, not charge into chaos.

We will have Golbery compile an extensive intelligence list on subversives, anyone in the government, military, or anyone in civil service who can prove themselves difficult to handle. Then, we must make sure they get a nice retirement.
strings.BRA_imperial_public_execution_desc:
An opportunity has arisen to purge the left of Varguism. Just as Rubens Vaz was shot because of his rebellion against tyranny, Varguism will destroy the victory we have won through the sacrifice of countless warriors if such an absurd ideology and its followers escape the judgment of justice.

Urgent political measures will be taken to permanently prevent the remaining PTB members from spreading any negative news about the government, especially troublemakers who must be monitored.
strings.BRA_imperial_victor_the_spoils_desc: For the rights of the Brazilian people to live in a safe, democratic country, the PTB, those degenerates of Getulism and the left of the former Partido Comunista Brasileiro, must be totally banned for the damage they have caused to the welfare of the people. The military and police will be mobilized to make sure that every unstable factor in Brazil is found and destroyed. Also, the remnants of the PTB - those governors who obtained this position by stealing the votes - will be removed and replaced by loyal protectors of democracy appointed by the President.
strings.BRA_imperial_rely_on_the_military_desc:
The OAS did not approve of our operation, and we cannot count on external support. Yet the Varguist threat remains, so we have no option but to depend on the military to maintain our legitimacy.

To avoid another coup, we have to convince them that we were the best choice to ensure Brazil's stability. Despite our disdain for the autocratic policies of recent years, they are now the only means of securing Brazil's future.
strings.BRA_imperial_one_thorough_cleaning_desc:
A nation is not unlike a house. When it is in good condition, families can be raised safely, prosperity reigning for its inhabitants. A safe home, something that is the desire of all.
