However, all good houses will accumulate problems. Dust can accumulate, mold or damp in areas unnoticed, an array of problems that could lead to more serious problems if left unchecked.

Brazil's institutions feel such maladies. It is no secret that there are difficult to handle individuals, from officers to civil servants to government secretaries, that could threaten the house if left unchecked. Golbery is our cleaner, we will task him to identify the mold. Then, as befitting men who have served their nation, they will be granted an honourable, lucrative retirement to be spent preferably far away from any lever of power.

Time to make sure that the Banda de Música is the one faction of the UDN with the most power. Our own very ranks are filled with moderates, willing to bend over backwards for the opposition, and we have to dominate party communications and woo (or coerce) party leaders into following the Lacerdaist line.
strings.BRA_imperial_new_udn_desc:
When the USA's Lincoln warned against a house divided, did he realise how consistently true such warnings would be? The UDN stands at a crossroad; there remain many moderates who would be willing to work with the opposition, while interest groups continue to deal for better offers privately. While we do not reject moderation, this is a critical moment of Brazil's history. The party must be united under the Lacerdaist message.

We will ensure the tools of party communications are held by committed Lacerdaists. Banda de Música faction candidates will be favoured, with prominent UDN figures met to discuss their concerns and interests; their loyalty will be assured one way or the other. The UDN will not be a confused web of interests - it will be an electoral lion to lead Brazil into the new day.

Schedule a meeting with Lincoln Gordon, America's ambassador to Brazil. Lacerda has a good feeling there are many receptive to his cause in Washington, and he will assure Gordon that we have a “new day dawning in Brasília”
strings.BRA_imperial_head_of_the_snake_desc:
Getúlio Dornelles Vargas. His nefarious Estado Novo may be gone, but the man behind it still lives on; and as long as he is still breathing, our rightful rule will be under constant danger. But we must not underestimate his power. A mere speech denouncing even his most obvious evils would cause a backlash as enormous as when Gomes abolished minimum wage. Removing his political rights and isolating him from the media's outlets will be necessary to finally curb his poisonous influence from our democracy.

We may not be able to remove the source of the Varguist cancer, but we can stop it from spreading.
strings.BRA_imperial_reach_out_gordon_desc:
Lincoln Gordon, the USA's man in Brasília. As their ambassador, that makes him the man we need now too. Washington support will be vital in the coming years, their desire for a peaceful and prosperous South America is something that aligns with our own desire for a new Brazil. The Americans have always been difficult to appease, but recent global turmoil and Lacerdaist principles offer a more subtle partnership.

As we continue to wash away the detritus of a difficult period, we will introduce Gordon properly to the Lacerdaist vision of Brazil and, most importantly, our desire for a profitable friendship with our ally to the north. They will know a new day dawns in Brasília, and that the man to see Brazil strong and free will be ever their friend so long as that vision is shared: Lacerda.
strings.BRA_imperial_rebirth_of_democracy_desc:
On the 10th of November, 1937, Vargas rewrote the Constitution to dissolve Congress and heavily restrict political participation.

On the 27th of December, 1939, Vargas founded the Department of Press and Advertising to control information and propagate ideology.

On the 24th of January, 1944, Vargas instituted Decreto-Lei n. 6.227 to ban criticizing commanders and illegalize anything that “compromised military operations”.

Many were harassed. Many were arrested. Many were killed. Only now, more than two decades later, do Varguists get a taste of their own medicine. After everything Lacerda has done, perhaps their repression can forever stay in the past.
strings.BRA_imperial_our_work_has_only_begun_des:
As dawn approaches, military radios wake commanders to anticipate couriers carrying directives directly from Lacerda himself. Within hours, soldiers go back to their bases. Tanks drive out of Brasília, heavy treads leaving deep imprints on the city's boulevards.

Citizens and commentators alike celebrate both the “return to order” and the “advent of a new era”. Moderates breathe a quiet sigh of relief. Better the UDN than the Army in the Planalto, right?

Yet, Vargas' grip on the country won't dissipate that easily. Even amongst Lacerda's most ardent supporters, many voice concerns that he bolstered militant leftists with his “anti-democratic” actions.

Let them talk! It's Lacerda's time to shine, and nothing can stop him now!
strings.BRA_imperial_the_crow_reigns_supreme_des:
Now these rigged elections that we have arranged, with the noble assistance of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Brazil, have delivered us the perfect result. As the Pessedists and Petebists whinge and holler as loudly as they can, thinking it will somehow save them, we have what we want and need. We have attained a legislature chock-full of UDN loyalists—and by “loyalists” we of course mean people that adhere only to President Lacerda.

We cannot waste this opportunity lest the Crow be knocked off his perch. We will take decisive action to destroy the Fourth Republic and replace it with a new Fifth Republic.
strings.BRA_imp_lacerda_full_unity_tt: The £BRA_udn_texticon UDN will become fully united behind Lacerda
strings.BRA_imperial_birth_of_5th_republic_desc:
The Getulist personality cultists refuse to face reality. They do not acknowledge a fact that stands out to anyone that doesn't recite “Retrato do Velho” or some other Getulist campaign song as if it was the rosary: that the Constitution of this Fourth Republic of Brazil is diseased, rotten to the core. Perhaps the cultists refuse to do anything or acknowledge any problem because this constitution is ridden down with the tenets of Varguism—all the nonsense that Getúlio Vargas called “governance” and enshrined in law.

We need to solve this matter once and for all. We will now give the task of writing a new constitution and forming a new Fifth Republic to the loyal lawmakers in the National Congress. It is time for a new era in Brazil—a new order, as it were.
strings.BRA_imperial_birth_of_5th_republic_tt:
It is time for Brazil to be reborn under our new dream.
We will introduce the Fifth Republic Constitution to the Senado
strings.BRA_imperial_constitionalise_capitalism_:
What has socialism, as promoted by the maniac Getúlio Vargas, ever gotten us but economic ruin and the spread of communistic degeneracy throughout the country? What has communism given any country but the destruction of its national identity and its defeat by foreign powers? Can there be any doubt, considering the success of the United States of Brazil, that capitalism is the way forward?

Our successors must be prevented from deviating from the true path. Constitutional guarantees outlawing the formation of any union not approved by the government and affected companies will be set in stone. No less important will be the imposition of wide-ranging property protections.
strings.BRA_imperial_plot_with_gordon_desc:
Were it not for the support of the United States—Getulists would call it “complicity”; thank God they don't know how far it goes or it'd be more ammunition for their vile rhetoric—we simply would not be here. There would be no removal of Goulart, no imperial presidency, no military law-and-order apparatus. So we owe it to Washington, D.C. to keep them on side and aware of all events.

Amidst the ongoing chaos, the United States Embassy in Brasília is now fortified. We will meet with Ambassador Lincoln Gordon at the embassy to discuss the next steps and to ensure the further support of the United States. Whatever plans we have at this moment will be provided to Ambassador Gordon for his reference and necessary action.
strings.BRA_imperial_antarctica_awaits_desc:
Now there is a very high chance that some generals, admirals, and other assorted jackboots may actually disagree with the current approach. We have done away with obvious traitors and Getulists such as Admiral Aragão who our President so zealously cursed out. That however has not removed the possibility that there may be (smoking) snakes in the grass that still hold on to the sort of constitutionalist nonsense that nearly handed us over to communism in the last few years.

Fortunately, we have a means to get them out of the way. The Argentines and their Axis lovers are plotting in Antarctica again, or so we will tell the press. (There is no problem even if they are not; after all, “press statements aren't given under oath.”) We will therefore stage a major operation against the Argentine Antarctic Territory. One that will need a lot of naval and army support. Constitutionalist remnants can be appointed to command these operations, and that will also remove the problem they pose for us.
strings.BRA_imperial_a_new_dawn_desc:
The time is now. We are free to make the moves we have to make to free our country of Getulist devilry. Within a day of the last measures being confirmed as complete, the UDN-controlled Senate will pass and approve the legislation. The President of the Senate, a UDN loyalist, will himself take the bill to President Lacerda for his approval and signature.

This will prevent our opponents from responding in any way. It will also permit us to cement our authority at this all-important time, the time during which the new, purified Fifth Republic is solidly established. While we fortify ourselves against any possible response, we are right to sit back and rejoice for a little while—for the devilry of Getúlio Dornelles Vargas has at last been purged from our nation.
strings.BRA_imperial_5th_constition_vote_tt: The Fifth Republic Constitution will be put to vote...
strings.BRA_imperial_a_new_dawn_tt_2: Lacerda's crusade against Varguism begins - More options in the focus tree have been unlocked
strings.BRA_imperial_enemies_at_the_gate_desc:
So much for celebration! We dare not say that our goals have been met, not when we are beleaguered by the forces of Getulist reaction. The opposition—such as there is, with the National Congress under our total control—has mobilized. The unions, who we have as yet tried and failed to defang, have declared a second general strike against us and workers in countless industries are going off their jobs.

As if Getulist and trades-unionist subversion was not trouble enough, politicians across the entire political spectrum, even from within our own União Democrática Nacional, have mustered to oppose us. Worst of all is the fact that those left-wing subversives under the leadership of Marighella and Amazonas have declared some kind of “people's war” against us.

Decisive action must be taken—all subversion must be crushed!
strings.BRA_imperial_an_illegal_gathering_desc:
This gathering by a conglomeration of unions to oppose the government which provides them with the services and money they need to function is a disgusting show of illegality and ingratitude. It must be met with the utmost possible force in order to prevent our government being held hostage like Gomes' was.

We already had to stop one of these beforehand. We will not be threatened by another; a final ban will be issued to prevent this devilry forevermore. No more union gatherings—crack down on anyone that goes on with this! Down with communistic “trades unionist” subversion!
strings.BRA_imperial_mass_layoffs_desc:
These unions seem to be really fond of playing dirty in service of their corrupt leaders' interests, and will even lead their members off cliffs if the union bosses say so. But two can play a dirty game—and our President is nothing if not always willing and able to play dirty.

We have heard rumours of government workers joining these strikes of theirs. No more of that, my lord, no more of that—these fools mar all with their starting. Any government worker caught partaking in any illegal meeting or strike will be terminated for cause. That will put the fear of God and Lacerda in them—all the better to get these morons back to work.
strings.BRA_imperial_gordons_boys_desc:
If there is one thing in which our President has been able to take comfort these past five years, it is his friendship and collaboration with Professor Gordon, our direct line to our friends and allies in Washington. But this friendship is not just a salve for Lacerda's personal demoralizations—it also affords significant diplomatic advantages.

One major example is securocratic in nature. Ambassador Gordon has the requisite connections with the Federal Bureau of Investigation to be able to obtain their help in Brazil at a level above and beyond our prior collaborations. The FBI indicates that it is able to help us blackmail unions and break up their gatherings without putting our own forces at risk. However, Magalhães urges caution—he asserts on solid evidence that such a decision is certain to engender controversy within the UDN.
strings.BRA_imperial_the_eagle_watches_desc:
There is another American three-letter institution that works secretly in Brazil, despite the public mandate given to the American security services: this is the CIA. Whereas by rights the South American region is an FBI operational zone, the CIA maintains a small presence here in Brazil to fight off German influence.

As a result of a backroom deal, the CIA has now approached us to offer their support. We are being advised to accept this offer. However, there are also some loyal and trustworthy officials that warn that the CIA is prone to taking more hardline, dangerous actions that the FBI would eschew.
strings.BRA_imperial_seahorse_desc:
Certain special agencies were established in the aftermath of our legitimate assertion of power against the Getulist-Peronist usurper João Goulart. For some time they have operated more or less autonomously, taking only suggestions from the Planalto—however, their leaders, being after all UDN cadres, have now put themselves at our direct disposal with the consent of the General Staff.

The “Seahorse”—DOPS, the Department of Political and Social Order—will be deployed in accordance with directives we issue. They will be sent out to tackle these guerrillas and work hand in glove with the SNI to see this objective fulfilled. Through a thorough collaboration and the leadership of the esteemed Golbery do Couto e Silva, DOPS and SNI will crack down on these guerilla groups and exterminate them.
strings.BRA_imperial_cuban_cigars_desc:
Alas for our tormented Brazilian people—it is not enough for the forces of Bolshevism and Hitlerism to attack us from within! They even have to affront our national sovereignty and honour as believers in capitalist liberal democracy by subverting our government. The accursed “Veracruz Pact”, supposedly a Mexican-led alliance but in reality led by the arch-communist Cuban revolutionaries and that degenerate guerilla-Stalinist Che Guevara, are proven to be directly supplying left-wing guerrillas.

Are we meant to tolerate this? Send in the DOPS, the SNI, the Coast Guard for all we care—and remove this threat from our shores!
strings.BRA_imperial_unleash_fluery_desc:
During the riots in Liberdade, there was a notorious brute of a man that opposed us at every turn. His name is Sérgio Fleury; even after the resolution of that crisis he still wields significant influence over leftist-infected São Paulo. He puts that influence to good use, too, pouring rhetorical fire and fury into his efforts to prevent the left from seizing control of that great city.

We do well to let bygones be bygones, and embrace Fleury into our efforts. He will receive a directive permitting him to take the gloves off and conduct any operation he damn well pleases in his—no, our—efforts to remove the left from São Paulo.
strings.BRA_imperial_out_of_sight_out_of_mind: Out of Sight Out of Mind
strings.BRA_imperial_out_of_sight_out_of_mind_de:
Transcript of a written message from the President of Brazil to Marshal Emílio Garrastazu Médici.

“'To thine own self be true'—as you no doubt know since my swearing-in as President, there have always been certain things that I have never been willing to do. There are certain lines that I have never been willing to cross no matter the cost of not doing so. There are some things that I would not inflict on Adolf Hitler, let alone João Goulart or Getúlio Vargas.”

“But the moral law is a mere luxury right now. If the security personnel want to do something to suppress the ongoing chaos, they no longer need to ask for any permission from Planalto Palace, nor send any report for my review. Any cost is worth the restoration of civic order. I will also not investigate them when the state of emergency is lifted.”
strings.BRA_imperial_iron_general_desc:
The former President, Teixeira Lott, has remained apolitical for the present—even whatever public statements he is convinced (perhaps badgered) into making are neutral in nature and would be praised as commendable across-the-aisle rhetoric in the absence of a national crisis. But we have exiled his communist of a daughter, Edna Lott; for this reason we fear that he may pose a problem.

Golbery has recommended that we arrest Lott for now and keep him under watch. “This will prevent him from causing us much trouble,” he says. We approve of this suggestion and will sign off on whatever order Golbery manages to draw up.
strings.BRA_imperial_flames_of_araguaia_desc:
Trouble is coming to us from the north, just like sudden blizzards and storms come from the north to bedevil the Americans. In the northern states, a rebellion is brewing—the outworking of this “people's war” that the communist traitors Amazonas and Marighella have declared on us. There are now student-led riots in multiple major cities, with major settlements such as Belém and Manaus not spared.

These subversive good-for-nothings are deluded. They think they can use the ravings of a delusional old Bolshevik as inspiration for the current age. They think they can ape Fidel Castro's degenerate exploits and the prowess of those Cuban maniacs! They are wrong, and we are about to prove that reality in blood.
strings.BRA_imperial_operation_parrot_desc:
We now have clarity on the force dispositions of the communist-fascist guerilla movements in the Araguaia river valley. To ensure an end to the chaos that has tormented us thanks to these Bolsheviks, we need to borrow a page from Jânio Quadros' book and sweep, sweep, sweep until they are destroyed.

We have a very effective broom—or perhaps that should be a suitably heavy hammer. In order to do away with Amazonas' band of brainwashed students and other assorted degenerates, we will flood the jungles and valleys with conventional forces and destroy them in combat. They have no hope of defeating our numbers.
strings.BRA_imperial_our_friend_huey_desc:
The helicopter nicknamed “Huey” allows for journeys both long and short, with a minimal outlay of resources and a simpler maintenance schedule. Ambassador Gordon and the assorted American defense-contractor lobbyists here in Brasília have been singing the Huey's praises for some time, well before any of this chaos started. Now it comes back to mind.

The presence of a helicopter will permit our armed forces to traverse currently inaccessible regions with ease. It will also permit more effective, and more accurate reconnaissance. We would've done so anyway, but we will make a large purchase so as to support Operation Parrot and ensure our victory.
strings.BRA_imperial_paint_the_jungle_red_desc:
*KRRT* “For the sake of great righteousness, he exterminates his kin—” *KRRT* “—O murderous assassin, impetuous and miserable—” *KRRT* “”—there is no novelty in the 'new republic', not while torturers and generals remain unpunished—“ *KRRT* ”—come no closer, lest I kill you with revolver fire—“ *KRRT* ”—'napalm sticks to kids'? What of it—“ *KRRT* ”—if even he remains free from prison, is there any justice in this realm of ours—“ *KRRT* ”—at least workers' consciousness is burgeoning—“ *BZZZZZZTTTTT*

”Attention. Attention. By decree of the Executive Power, martial law has been declared in this area to combat a subversive insurrection. A bandit suppression campaign is ongoing. Citizens are ordered to shelter in place. Failure to comply with this measure will result in your being construed as an enemy combatant regardless of armaments or hostility. We expect your total cooperation with, and obedience to, this directive.“
strings.BRA_imperial_sewers_of_diable_desc:
Padre Anchieta's work is desecrated; hell has been emptied out and all the devils are in São Paulo! Not for nothing is it referred to as “Diable”, the Devil's City, especially by Cariocas such as our President. The damn place that was once the abode of our political rival, the corrupt and accursed Adhemar de Barros is now full of leftist rebels. Why be surprised, then, when the communist-Getulist good-for-nothing Getúlio Vargas Filho gets away with openly defying our rule?

Worst of all is the constantly repeated rumour, which lies like truth, that São Paulo is rumoured to be the home base of both Carlos Lamarca and his superior, the accursed Marighella. We need to do something about this; thankfully, we have an excuse in the form of widespread strikes. We must crush these communists, no matter what form they take, and exorcise São Paulo.
strings.BRA_imperial_toppling_a_dynasty_desc:
Getúlio Vargas tried to kill our President. His henchmen and kinsfolk go to war with us day in and day out for defying his socialistic, Peronist despotism. Vargas' nuisance of a son, the so-called Governor of São Paulo, is just the latest manifestation in an evil, good-for-nothing dynasty of cranks and immoral actors.

Now we hear, to our disgust, that conspiracies against us meet with Vargas Filho's sympathy. This, of course, cannot be tolerated; it also gives us an opportunity to spread our influence. We will pass an emergency law reducing his powers as governor and allowing us to intervene in the State of São Paulo at will.
strings.BRA_imperial_tanks_on_the_streets_desc:
“Attention. Attention. By decree of the Executive Power, martial law has been declared in this area to combat a subversive insurrection. The right of public assembly has been suspended in the interests of civic peace. We order all present herein, regardless of participation in illegal public meetings, to disperse at once.”

In and of itself, that should in theory compel obedience. But the fact of the matter is that it does not. If we are serious about ending these street insurrections they call “protests”, we need to scare the living hell out of the rioters. Deploy some tanks on the streets, then, to frighten the fools and make them go home. That'd be a proper silver bullet (depleted uranium bullet, perhaps) for our problems.
strings.BRA_imperial_raid_favelas_desc:
It is presently suspected that the favelas of São Paulo, just like those of Rio, are concealing communist radicals. We need, therefore, to have the police or the military go in on these favelas, find the insurgents, and crush them one way or another.

With São Paulo beleaguered by mass street protests and subject to misrule by Vargas' good-for-nothing of a son, decisive action is needed to pacify the city. Even more tanks than already present need to be deployed on the street to make these subversives rethink their choices and go home.
strings.BRA_imperial_roars_of_truimph_desc:
The President has realized that what he needs right now is a platform from which to confront treason and encourage the Brazilian people. Accordingly Carlos Lacerda will go live in a national address defying the communist traitors, inflaming the passion of his subordinates, and assuaging the fears of the population.

If nothing else, this—like so many of President Lacerda's speeches—will make for an effective spectacle as he weaves together narratives into a coherent whole for the benefit of the country. But one does feel some small doubts as to whether a spectacle is what the country needs when it is bleeding like this.
strings.BRA_imperial_everything_is_fine_desc:
“The extent to which things have gone wrong in Lacerda's Brazil cannot be understated—BZZT—the people need reassurance that everything is in order no matter what it looks like.”

“The suppression of free speech, hypocritical par excellence in a newspaper editor who constantly claimed to be attacked by Vargas—KRRK—the people of Brazil must understand that there is no such thing as 'absolute' free speech permitting the dissemination of lies.”

“All they do is repeat the same message over and over again:—VWOOP—'People of Brazil, all is well! All is well! All is well!'”

“How do you expect me to go outside when the communists and Lacerda's fascists are fighting in the streets?—KRRK—As you can see, there is nothing but peace and quiet in the streets of...”

“The country is bleeding, God damn it. How am I meant to enjoy myself?—BZZT—The restaurants, parks, and bookstores are still open. The Brazilian Government encourages you to avail yourself of such cultured pleasures.”
strings.BRA_imperial_campos_pleas_desc:
We have, at least, not had to struggle alone in our fight to unify the União Democrática Nacional. We have had the help of Milton Campos, who has spent virtually all his free time in attempting to plead with doubtful UDN cadres such as Távora to unite behind President Lacerda. His efforts seem to have an effect on people's hardened hearts, but he cannot get stuff done on his own.

We will back his calls to the hilt. The União Democrática Nacional must remain united and strong come what may. If now President Lacerda cannot even rely on the party whose efforts brought him to power, collapse is the only endstate we can expect.
strings.BRA_imperial_reassure_usa_desc:
Imagine if our government was toppled by street protests and the supporters of an exiled President whose overthrow the Americans backed. The only thing more embarrassing for the United States would be if the Canadian government was usurped by forces loyal to the British collaborationists. The Americans, no doubt aware of the possibility of embarrassment, are already intervening, but we need to secure their faith in our government.

The Yankees need to be assured of a few fundamental things. Firstly, we remain loyal to the interests of the broader free world. Secondly, our government is stable, despite the superficial appearance of unrest. Lastly, there will be no collapse—no waste of their investment in us.
strings.BRA_imperial_pintos_support_desc:
The arch-conservative Magalhães Pinto is a prominent figure in Brazilian political life. There is an apocryphal story that says of him that a hair cannot fall off a Brazilian right-winger's head without Magalhães Pinto knowing or authorizing it. This story is made up but it illustrates the significance of his influence and the necessity of securing his support.

We must approach Senhor Magalhães Pinto as soon as possible to reach an agreement. Any concessions required are acceptable with one exception. If Magalhães Pinto demands the presidency, he can forget it.
strings.BRA_imperial_all_in_desc:
Diseases desperate grown,
By desperate appliance are relieved,
Or not at all.
—William Shakespeare

As if in a game of poker, we are in too deep. We cannot turn back now; we can only burn our bridges behind us and face the future, come what may. If we were to back down, all that would do is ensure the victory of Goulart, who would then return like the Nazi-fascist Tyrant and bring an end to all the good we have done.

We need to double down. More troops. More armaments. More repressions. More deployments. More, more, more, more! Any means necessary to defeat Getulism and ensure a final victory. It is worth the cost, I tell you.
strings.BRA_imperial_lacerda_victory_desc:
I am victorious. I have defeated every trial put before me; I have smashed aside every obstacle. Every opponent is defeated, their will to defy me broken. The degenerate leftist opposition that nearly took my life twenty years ago is swept aside. I have forged a New Brazil—one free from the sins and vices of the past.

O Vargas, I have surpassed you; O Gomes, I succeeded where you failed. Take heed, General Fonseca; I have purged your Republic of its vices. Be afraid, Amazonas, for I have broken your degeneracy. By my will and by the grace of God, Brazil WILL be beautiful once more—and at the head of the chronicle of the Fifth Republic shall stand but one name: Carlos Lacerda.
strings.BRA_imperial_a_feast_for_crows_desc:
I read this somewhere. I don't remember where. The man that wrote it said the following: “If the communists insist on radical and incorrigible leadership, they will fail. They will, as the saying goes, 'die on the vine.' They will wither and be forgotten; the people themselves will reject them. They should instead abide by the people's interest.” Isn't that a fine encapsulation of what befell Amazonas' rabble? Ferocious monsters have been turned into so many feasts for crows.

Marighella is dead and can trouble no one any longer. Leftist resistance in São Paulo is eliminated, thanks not least to Frota's hard work. All that remains is the Amazonist rebellion in Araguaia—but that pathetic rubbish festered during Lott's tenure without issue. So the threat of a communist insurgency is over.
strings.BRA_imperial_silenced_opposition_desc:
Dear God, it's been a long four years listening to the constant wailing and bleating of the socialists. Day in and day out they would whine about my “illegitimate government” and “oppression of the workers of Brazil”. It was so goddamned annoying to have to pay constant attention to their plots and complaints.

Well, I say “would” and “was” for a reason—it's the past tense now! The bleating of Goulart, Edna, and Brizola from abroad has finally been silenced. The birth of the Fifth Republic is proof positive that a new era is here—an era in which the PTB and socialism plays absolutely no role.
strings.BRA_imperial_introduce_the_heir_desc:
The Mexicans have a very interesting term for their chosen successor. “El Tapado”, they call him. I have one of those myself and his name is Raphael Magalhães; I can think of no one better suited to take the reins after I leave office. Having thrown the Trabalhistas out of the halls of power it's clear to me that I have left a good house for Magalhães to live in from hereon.

It's time to introduce our Tapado to the people of Brazil. I need to go and ask Senhor Tapado—I mean, Magalhães—if he is still interested in continuing as my chosen successor. I don't doubt he'll accept; and when he does we are assured of another five years of victory for our Nation.
strings.BRA_imperial_introduce_the_heir_tt: It is time to introduce our El Tapado, step forward herald of the future
strings.BRA_imperial_the_march_north_desc:
The rebellions in the south have been crushed and their attempts to construct a so-called socialist state out of São Paulo and Guanabara are mere historical footnotes. However, the Araguaia problem remains. I said that Lott was not troubled by it, and that is true, but that does not mean that I or my successor will have such a luxury.

It is time for the military to move north. Araguaia must be suppressed. Amazonas must be shown to have failed, so the few imbeciles that dare to support communism and leftism know that there is no hope for them here. Médici, I will rely on you in this respect.
strings.BRA_imperial_anaconda_desc:
Operation Parrot has failed. Médici went about it too imprecisely—as too many cooks spoil a broth, so too many soldiers just complicate matters. In the wild jungles of Araguaia it is all too easy for regular forces to make fools of themselves, exhausting their limited supplies and sapping their combat ability.

We have special troops for a reason. We will send them to the area to crush the rebellion and slowly starve it out. This in turn will reduce the ability of the Araguaia rebellion to either survive where it is or promulgate itself elsewhere.
strings.BRA_imperial_duck_hunt_desc:
It turns out that the deployment of special forces rather than the regular army was the correct way to go about it. The Amazonian rebellion is now on the way to total destruction. What we have heard now is that the rebellion leadership, such as Amazonas, finding no further purchase for their abominable ideology in Brazil, are attempting to flee the country.

I need the security services to come up with a plan. Let's try and take out Amazonas and his inner circle before they escape and find refuge somewhere else. If we can kill them off, it'll be a crowning triumph on top of all the others we've had this year.
strings.BRA_imperial_distraction_desc:
The 1970 presidential elections are rapidly approaching. There are many delusional oppositionists who believe that this is the last opportunity they have to defeat me. With hope out of all proportion to the desperation of their circumstances, they muster and picket—though they do not dare to do anything the old subversive trade unions did.

I almost feel sorry for them. The game was rigged from the very start and will remain so. There will be nothing but victory for the UDN. This election is nothing more than a formality and a distraction; we will not be deterred from the victory we deserve after all we have done for the Nation.
strings.BRA_imperial_quiet_the_psd_desc:
The Getulist coalition has been in disarray ever since the last election. With the PTB and PSP neutralized, there is only the PSD left. In a desperate gamble to return to power, they drafted Juscelino Kubitschek, one of the last vestiges of the Fourth Republic, for the presidential candidacy to oppose Braga.

Kubitschek is extremely popular, it is true—even I found things to commend in his presidency. But he should have stopped sleeping around before running for office. Thanks to his lecherous tendencies he has smashed any hope his party ever had of gaining power. The man has no chance of returning to the Planalto. I have credible reports in hand, incontrovertible evidence that Kubitschek has betrayed his faithful wife. It's time for a leak.
strings.BRA_imperial_caged_bird_desc:
The PSD must not be permitted to win. In fact, thanks to the joint effort of the UDN and the Armed Forces, they physically cannot win. But this does not make them worth banning. We will not outlaw them—we are not Hitlerites; we need not demand that every seat (instead of just a majority) be under our control.

The PSD has a use—it is to serve as an outlet for frustrations against the government. The PSD will never attain any sort of power, but they have a place: as a marionette, chained to Braga's will, and Sarney's after him, and so on and so forth.
strings.BRA_imperial_trip_to_america_desc:
Our rule having been cemented, it is finally time for my long-overdue state visit to the United States of America, that land of the free and home of the brave. I have not conferred with the President of the Free World nearly as much as I perhaps should have. With the Fifth Republic now made firm, I am now free to remedy this deficit in our diplomacy.

In the District of Columbia we will sit together in celebration. The President and I will discuss the future of the free world and the OFN. We will also discuss how I myself have contributed and will contribute to the strength of the free countries of the world.
strings.BRA_imperial_the_special_relationship_de:
It has come to this—the culmination of our diplomatic and political labours. We will now make firm the special relationship between the United States of America and this Republic of Brazil. We are closer than any other pair of countries—we are the two strongest nations on the American supercontinent, and we are united in ensuring the freedom of the Western Hemisphere!

So long as the USA and Brazil stand united, no fascistic force can threaten peace where we live. The East may be lost but the West will not fall. Not while I'm here. I swear it, on my name and honor as inaugural President of the Fifth Republic of Brazil.
strings.BRA_imperial_thunderous_applause_desc:
The União Democrática Nacional is about to have its yearly conference. Today's UDN is such a far cry from how depressing gatherings like this used to be back when Gomes had screwed everything up. Our delegates are happy and hopeful; they are coming up with policy ideas and proposals and showing the world the intellectual might of Brazilian conservatism.

To celebrate the first convention of the UDN since the establishment of the Fifth Republic I will go and give a rousing speech to my party colleagues. I will go in depth on the reforms I have implemented and the future I have built. This will cement my legacy and ensure that people know to adhere to my guidance even when I no longer inhabit Planalto Palace.
strings.BRA_imperial_the_final_reforms_desc:
Beltrão, is that you? This is Lacerda. Yes, I am doing fine, Minister, thank you for asking—I hope you and the family are well. You are, and they are too? Glad to hear it.

Why am I calling? You of course know that we have come quite far in our work to defuse the inflation crisis that that lecherous fool Kubitschek set off in the Fifties. What I need you to do right now is to put the finishing touches on those economic reforms of yours. Let's work on putting a final attack on inflation to permanently end its threat to our economy—once and for all. How does that sound?
strings.BRA_imperial_bounty_of_brazil_desc:
Ach. The closer I get to the end of the term the more eager I am not to have to hear some general rumbling on the phone line. This time the armed forces are demanding more oil extraction because of the chaos set off by those wars in the Middle East. They're saying that we need to become self-sufficient in respect to petroleum and other consumables or else the Argentines will have their way with us.

Looks like I'll have to bother Beltrão again. We'll have him work with the Ministry of Trade and Itamaraty to grant permission to companies to begin exploiting the Brazilian interior. Ideally they will discover sources of oil and other natural resources which we can in turn use to fuel our economy.
strings.BRA_imperial_midnight_hour_desc:
The hour is late. Planalto Palace is empty, Brasília has calmed down. The election has been called and the future of this Fifth Republic is surely written in stone. Ney Aminthas de Barros Braga is now President-elect and the Varguist legacy slowly but surely fades into nothingness. I am left at home, with my family at rest, and I am beginning to woolgather.

I need a chair, some flowers—do they have any aconites here? I doubt it—and a car. I want to go to Getúlio Vargas' final resting place. I need to think clearly about the past and the future. Oddly, I'm not sure that I have any appetite to gloat anymore. I just want to think, now that it's over.
strings.BRA_imperial_a_new_rio_desc:
O Guanabara, Guanabara, this city of my home! The storm tried to have its way with you—it tried to sweep you away. Unbossed and unbroken you survived, defiant and glorious, an abode of freedom under the watchful eyes of the Redeemer. Rio after the storm is now a new, stronger city—one ready to face the future and represent the Fifth Republic to the rest of the human race.

Thanks to my efforts I have managed to ensure a bright, productive, prosperous future for Rio de Janeiro, my home and favorite city. It is the one thing I am most proud of as President of Brazil.
strings.BRA_imperial_coronation_desc:
I feel sorry for Magalhães, that the military stymied him from taking power like that and imposed Braga and Sarney. I've told him this repeatedly. But he told me to be quiet and count my blessings—and honestly, he is right.

Ney Braga, though not what I wanted, is still a safe pair of hands. There's no question about it no matter how much I whinge. He will maintain the reforms we have fought for; he will also not be a blatant puppet of the military. He will perhaps even have the wherewithal to fight back on some of the more inane demands of the men in uniform, since he is closer to them than I could ever hope to be.

I will attend his coronation—I beg your pardon, his swearing-in—and watch history be made once again, just as it was when I took office. Then I am going to take a very, very long vacation.
strings.BRA_imperial_lacerda_vengeance_desc:
Carlos Marighella—you miserable assassin, you traitor against the Brazilian people, you Bolshevik subhuman! Why have I tolerated your continued existence? Why have I permitted you to peddle your degeneracy among my people—the people of Brazil? If I had struck hard enough soon enough, Magalhães would still be alive!

Marighella, you traitorous bastard! You kidnapped Magalhães—my friend, my protégé, the heir to this accursed Executive Power I have been made to wield. You and your degenerates kidnapped him, tortured him, and then gunned him down—a journey which he began merely by heading home to his family for Christmas!

Vengeance is mine, and I will have it. You and all your co-conspirators... they will pay.
strings.BRA_imperial_parasar_desc:
The situation is desperate. I know not whether it is my own negligence or the results of Getulist and communist subversion, but Rio is awash in communists and the whole country is full of traitors. Everywhere one goes one finds treasonous plots and attacks against the rightful executive power. Fortunately, I have heard that the Air Force—to be precise, one General João Paulo Burnier—has a plan to root out all manifestations of opposition in Guanabara.

To anyone that whinges about the potential cost, I ask: where were you when Marighella was plotting his crimes? I say now that any cost is worthless next to the gain of catching Marighella and bringing closure to Magalhães' family. Justice must be done. I do not care if the cost is Rio itself going up in flames—the PARA-SAR Plan must be executed immediately.
strings.BRA_imperial_parasar_tt: The Strike GUI will be removed, due to our failure in containing them.
strings.BRA_imperial_kidnap_goulart_desc:
For too long these communist Getulists Brizola, Goulart, and Edna Lott have hidden in Cuba, escaping the rightful justice of the Brazilian nation. We have no way of getting hold of either Brizola or Edna—they are too well-secured and their families cannot be readily targeted. That soft moron Goulart, on the other hand, is a sitting duck. We can threaten his wife's safety, force him to return, then arrest him.

It is time to put this proposed operation into motion. When Goulart returns, he will be put in prison, never to escape. This will put paid to the first and most major threat to my rightful rule over this country.
strings.BRA_imperial_cover_up_kubitschek_desc:
You morons! How do you dare to call yourselves a “Third Army” when you cannot follow basic orders? Unable to apprehend a man, you then cause him to crash and die as he speeds away in his motorcar with his mistress! Now a former President of the Republic is dead and we are under suspicion thanks to you.

What now can we do but drag his name into the mud to save our own hides? We must have TV Globo claim that he was driving drunk after having been caught by his wife engaging in infidelity. “Who knows what proportion of the population will believe it”? It does not matter—we have no choice. I can't hand your good-for-nothing commander over to them no matter how much I want to now, can I?
strings.BRA_imperial_arrest_tavora_desc:
And now we come to that lily-livered imbecile Távora. How one male can both be so cowardly and so ambitious is beyond me. That coward always craved the Presidency—he was always after my seat. If he wasn't such a craven, I would've suspected him of having a hand in Magalhães' murder. But the very suggestion is ridiculous—he is too much of a pansy to even think of murder.

Murder is beyond the pale, but criticising me in such a manner as to give ammunition to my enemies is not. He denounces our administration; he refuses to show up to Cabinet meetings and is trying to sabotage the continued functioning of the government! We will not let this stand. Go at once and deploy soldiers to arrest him. The court-martials will try him for treason, and then I will pardon him of the death penalty. Call it payment for services rendered.
strings.BRA_imperial_doubt_desc:
The doubts—they rise up to suffocate me. General Burnier never revealed the extent of this PARA-SAR plan of his. He just said it would suffice to exterminate all treason and ensure the loyalty of the military and government. It has done that, but at what cost? It is going further than I ever intended.

Esther, my loyal secretary, has clearly been affected by what she has been forced to witness, or else why would she be asking to resign? Of course she insists that isn't the case, bless her heart—she just says she wants to return to Curitiba with her family. I will grant this request. She deserves peace after all her work for me.

But the fact is that I will now be left on my own with only the army around me. I suspect that isolation may be just what I deserve in the circumstances.
strings.BRA_imperial_no_half_measures_desc:
Who do those fools in Washington think they are? These morons at the Organization of Free Nations? They accuse us of so-called “crimes against humanity”, a designation that was conveniently absent against Perón or Stalin. They protest outside our embassies and consulates while journalists type up a storm of hostile invectives, complaining and raging against our persistence in the OFN.

These fools will never understand. We had to do this. The communist scum were at the gates—and who knows what they might then have done to the rest of the OFN? We will defend ourselves before the OFN and the Organization of American States come hell or high water. I do not give a damn what sanctions they inflict. I did what I had to do and nothing more or less.
strings.BRA_imperial_crush_fota_desc:
The way Sílvio Frota once behaved, you would have thought he was cut from the same cloth as Costa e Silva or Rademaker—a loyal military man and a leader of the hardliner apparatus. But that skin has been sloughed off like that of an Amazonian lizard. Now he and the Second Army have rebelled in São Paulo and are actively defying the government, declaring allegiance with Vargas' spawn who is the governor of that pesthole.

And now listen to the sort of nonsense he proclaims over the Paulista airwaves. He calls us—us—“evil” as if he himself has not waded in blood. How many crimes has this man committed, that he now claims himself innocent while committing treason and calling it loyalty? Send in the First Army from the Argentine border and crush this traitor at once before he attacks Guanabara or the Federal Capital!
strings.BRA_imperial_blood_on_the_amazon_desc:
At last the report has come to us from our intelligence services. The traitorous leftists who began all this misery have been conclusively located—they have holed up in the far north, hiding in the Araguaia region. They claim loyalty to João Amazonas, to Marighella, Lamarca, and a so-called “combined anti-fascist front” whose clear ambition is to hand us over to Nazi-fascism in the name of “national liberation”.

We will put an end to this devilry and we will do so now. The murderers of Magalhães will pay a hundredfold for their brutality. Deploy the helicopter brigades at once, with orders to fire at will and take no quarter. I want the jungle stained as red as those Bolsheviks' stupid flags, and the Amazon dyed just as red from their spilled blood!
strings.BRA_imperial_mercy_desc:
Months have passed and Guanabara still burns. We need to restore order to the greatest city in the Brazilian republic. You fools of the Third Army will redeem yourselves by moving into Rio de Janeiro and restoring order. You will then cooperate with any providers of international aid and take advantage of the fact that it is not yet too late to return Guanabara to a semblance of order.

Additionally, we need to take a more moderate course. Former President Lott is in our custody. Let him and his family go into exile to be with Edna Lott. There has been enough bloodshed. Enough families have been torn apart over this devilry.
strings.BRA_imperial_succession_desc:
Magalhães has been buried. I have returned from his funeral Mass and done what little I can to convey my sympathies to his family. But with him cruelly murdered by the communist degenerates we need a new successor. We have no good candidates, and the military is sending us so many demands for the next (staged) elections that they could fill up an entire textbook.

I will give them what they want. We will choose the least of all evils and bring Magalhães Pinto to Brasília, offering him the presidency. This at last will put something in the gap left by Magalhães' death.
strings.BRA_imperial_cold_southern_springs_desc:
We have neglected our southern front, haven't we? The Argentines sit there seemingly twiddling their thumbs but are obviously awaiting a chance to strike at us. Sure, they have closed off the borders and are denying refugees heading towards the border. But only an imbecile would think that they were not amassing for an attack.

Take direct action. I want the forces on the southern border doubled. If they want to set Argentina aflame so it is no less miserable than Brazil right now, let them be my guest. We must be prepared for any war coming.
strings.BRA_imperial_illusions_end_desc:
We thought ourselves safe, but our rule is beleaguered by constant threats. We considered ourselves invincible, our ideology immortal, and Varguism permanently defeated. But due to my own bloodlust and the incompetence and treason of the armed forces we have been laid low! We cannot permit the Getulists or the communists to cause matters to spiral out of control.

The risk of that is high. I have heard horrifying rumours to the effect that Che Guevara, that arch-communist brute, is travelling to Brazil to assist Amazonas in his struggle. This cannot be accepted. The rumours must be scotched. Che Guevara must be prevented from breaching our borders no matter the cost.
strings.BRA_imperial_illusions_end_tt: We will finally end that rat Che Guevara once and for all...
strings.BRA_imperial_urban_guerilla_desc:
Perhaps this is why Frota rebelled. We have learned that the subhuman traitor Marighella is hidden in the sewers of São Paulo. He has a very nice little hideout from which he takes orders from his demonic master Amazonas on the process of his war of extermination against the Brazilian people. Would that we had known beforehand—would that I had tried to figure it out—so that Magalhães would still be alive. I—

Enough of this! I need to stop whingeing. Magalhães is beyond return. But we will bring him justice. Go at once—flush the communists out of São Paulo and put paid to their treason in that state. We were not able to save Magalhães from the Bolsheviks but we can at least exterminate his murderers in his honour.
strings.BRA_imperial_arrest_burnier_desc:
This traitor João Paulo Burnier would have made for a perfect assistant to Marighella and Amazonas in another life, would he not? That Nazi-fascist bastard has conned us! When he was discussing his thrice-damned little plan to “remove subversion” he never once said he planned to collapse a dam in Rio and flood the place. He also did not tell us that he intended to destroy the fucking gasometer and thereby set fire to every favela in Guanabara!

That crypto-communist good-for-nothing thinks he is so clever, committing mass murder and high treason and calling it loyal service to defeat communism. He thinks he has rendered us a service, does he, the fucker? He'll get his goddamned reward for his demonic little service—I'll give it to him, by God, I will.

Médici! Arrest this brute and shoot him in the back of the head. I want him dead in eight hours or less. Then hang him upside down from the first telephone pole you find!
strings.BRA_imperial_the_other_carlos_desc:
There is another Carlos. It tears at my soul day in and day out that I share a name with a goddamn communist. Carlos Lamarca leads the rebels in Araguaia; he is the third of the three heads of the Hitlerite-Bolshevik hydra. Just like Marighella and Amazonas, we have forced him to go to ground, but now we need to redouble our efforts.

We must destroy their rebellion. These Nazis have managed to dupe the natives and locals into going along with their treasonous schemes. We must target the local settlements and in doing so starve out these so-called students, putting paid to their rebellion and saving our people from their schemes.
strings.BRA_imperial_black_swans_desc:
What do you mean, “oil crisis”? What do you mean, “economic collapse”? We do not need this, damn you, we don't need this right now! God fucking damn it. As if things could get any worse for this country. As if they could get any fucking worse! I can't take it anymore!

This oil crisis of theirs has collapsed the Brazilian economy. The guerrillas, far from defeated, continue to attack thanks to the incompetence of our oh-so-valiant armed forces. Capitalists and investors—our country's most productive citizens and those foreigners that so often strengthened our economy—are fleeing for any safer shore they can find. Countries in Africa are now more attractive for investors than the Brazil that has been brought about on my watch.

And I was warned, wasn't I? Wasn't I? That motherfucker Lott. He knew all this would happen. Every word he said from the start of this damn crisis was a blaring warning of this no matter how he delivered it. I ignored him. I ignored him, and now the country bleeds.

Who is the greater fool? Him for offering counsel to my stoppered ears, or me for not listening?
strings.BRA_imperial_letting_go_desc:
These five years are over. Even if I wanted to, I cannot go on. I can't take it anymore. I hardly could even with Magalhães around—but he is dead and I am about to join him.

This goddamn job rots away at me. This life is a cancer on my soul. The doctors insist I am in good health but I feel the rot—I feel everything destroyed within me. It wasn't meant to be like this. This is Goulart's fault, isn't it? The Varguists did this, didn't they? They made it happen. They—enough.

I will never say it to anyone, but I know whose fault it really is. Having... watched and been in the halls of power as Brazil was brought to this pass, I know that the only service I can render to my country now is to leave life and enter history.

I hope the Hereafter will prove kinder to me than reality has. But do I deserve such mercy?
strings.BRA_gomes_checkmate_desc:
There has been scarcely an enemy so committed to opposing us and so powerful in nature as the unions and their pet parties. This bloc of fat-cat administrators who wield millions of workers to oppose us have been a never-ending thorn in the side of any conservative administration, and ours has been no exception. At every turn and with every reform, we see them organizing, seducing the working people to stand in the way of their own good - and too often we find ourselves with our hands tied behind our back to oppose them.

It is the Labour Code, that evil thing, which binds us so - a document from the Varguist days which greatly empowers the union class, letting them run riot over Brazil in pursuit of their own interest. To reform and even remove it has been a UDN tenet for decades, and it is past time we get to cutting our enemies down to size - but we must be careful. It was Gomes, after all, who tried this last, and he found himself on the wrong end of a brutal public backlash that destroyed the UDN for years altogether. We must be smarter, stronger, and better than he was - and if we hold our own, we can finish his work.
strings.BRA_lacerda_gomes_checkmate_tt: Lacerda will embark on the main obstacle for him to reshape Brazil, the £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon  Varguist Labor Laws £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon  must be dismantled.
strings.BRA_Sisyphean_struggle_desc:
The core of the labour bloc and the reason why our efforts to break them apart have struggled so is unity - solidarity, even. These unions, though they cover different interests and different kinds of labour, are unceasing in their efforts to conspire against the true interests of their workers. After all, if the laboring classes were more prosperous, they wouldn't need the union to force their wages up - therefore, the unions work together to prevent that prosperity, using the UDN as the scapegoat for their self-inflicted woes.

In contrast, the interests of the Brazilian right are diffuse and chaotic. Populists clash with conservatives clash with free-marketers, and the leftists of Brazil get away with the whole hog. We must end this squabbling in the interest of opposing a greater evil, for our own differences cannot allow the big unions to continue on with their banditry - if we stand as united as they do, we will see that the people of Brazil truly do stand with us as well, and when the people abandon the unions, they will have no choice but to give in.
strings.BRA_begin_media_campaign_desc:
It is of great benefit to us that the newspapers of Brazil are, by and large, owned by rich magnates and moguls. After all, who are they to support strikers and socialists? Indeed, Lacerda has been very good to these fine gentlemen, and in return they shall deliver us their most valuable asset - positive press.

This anti-union initiative of ours is sure to ruffle many feathers - we're more than aware of this, after how poorly the first go-around went for Gomes. Therefore, when the laborers begin to pitch a fit, we must be ready for their massive disorder. Each violation will be breathlessly covered by headlines screaming of union disorder, each part of the bill will be fawned over and praised by the columnists. To the public, our enemies shall be nothing but rabble-rousers standing in the way of Brazilian progress - and when we sweep them aside, they will be more than happy to watch us do so.
strings.BRA_preempt_unions_desc:
There is no doubt that our bill to weaken the unions will be met fiercely by the unions - indeed, it's rather self-explanatory. Indeed, the predictable nature of the response to come means that we can plan in advance for its consequences and get out ahead of our adversaries before they make the first move. It will be a critical skill in these coming days.

The unions will strike, we know that. They will march with banners and red flags, clogging the streets and filling the air with their chants and their soldiers. But we know their weaknesses - we know their leadership, which is corrupt and feckless, and we know how a package of dollars hand-delivered to their doorstep can weaken their resolve. It is a shame we will have to let the ringleaders of this circus make off like bandits, but without orders from on high, these strikers will be nothing more than a directionless mob for the police to properly handle.
strings.BRA_submit_the_bill_desc:
Lacerda's chosen deputy shuffles up the floor, delivering his paper to the President of the Chamber, who reads it into the record. A roar goes up from the opposition, but their words of anger are drowned out by the sound of fingers hitting buttons and lights flickering above.

Overlooking it all is Lacerda, watching the first shot of his greatest legislative effort be fired. He can see union cronies ducking in and out of the room, surely making calls back to Rio and São Paulo, while his allies on the other end of the room whip votes and take names of those who resist. Here, then, is his inflection point, his Rubicon - the last moment of peace before he starts an open war.

Then here goes nothing, he thinks, and he nods to his deputy to open the voting.
strings.BRA_submit_the_bill_tt: Lacerda will end the £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon  Varguist Labor Laws £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon - or die trying
strings.BRA_counter_reaction_desc:
As we expected, the unions have taken the submission of our bill to break them poorly. Who wouldn't? Their places of power are now under threat by an honest government, for a change, and so they will send their underlings out in full force to break our will and shatter the political resolve of the Chamber. Across Brazil, workplaces grind to a halt and construction comes to an abrupt end as their laborers leave the job sites, taking to the picket line instead and attacking any who attempt to earn an honest day's work.

If this is a war of survival for them, however, it is just as much a war of survival for ourselves. We have seen what such a strike can bring upon a government without the spine or the muscle to break it. Gomes' attempt to cut the unions down to size came apart at this very juncture, in fact - he had neither the unity nor the backbone to keep his party men in check, and when the economy took a plunge, he was the one served on a platter to union greed.

Carlos Lacerda will not let this happen again.
strings.BRA_lacerda_strike_more_options_tt: We will have more options to deal with the strikers.
strings.BRA_iron_will_desc:
One can prepare themselves all they want for the consequences of invoking a general strike, but it truly is hard to understate just how brutal these disputes can be. Weeks of no movement on the picket line has left Brazil in a state of freefall, its market collapsing and its people out of work. Increasingly, the public is wishing for nothing more than capitulation - whether from the government or the unions depends on who is asked. But the longer this goes on, the more the people of Brazil wish for the aggressors to back down and let life go on - and, as much as we deny it, the fact is that we are perceived as the aggressors here.

No matter. The benefits of a Brazil without union thugs and leeches skimming off the top is worth all the short-term pain they can inflict. If we keep this in our minds and in our hearts, we will be a force united for the future - one which no great strike nor any labor action can contain. All there is to do is stay the course.
strings.BRA_realist_concern_desc: The Realistas and Távora believe that our actions so far have been too harsh. They want the government to negotiate with the unions, or else they may pull support for Lacerda and the government. We cannot risk the party and government collapsing at this time, and thus, we must heed their demands. The government will reluctantly enter into talks with strike leaders and attempt to reach some sort of settlement. It will be an incredibly arduous task if to find a solution that appeases every faction.
strings.BRA_virtue_of_patience_desc: While it may not feel like it, there is a light at the end of the tunnel. The unions cannot muster enough resources to strike forever, and already, there are signs of them losing momentum. With the power of bosses, capital and the state on our side, it would be impossible to fumble this. The reckless actions of the unions will show the Brazilian people why these reforms are necessary. The sun will soon rise on a better Brazil that is not shut down whenever union bosses are feeling greedy, where businesses can thrive without unions strangling them and where prices are not driven up by the radical demands of organised labor.
strings.BRA_cavalry_charge_desc:
The unions have made it clear that they will not stop unless they are stopped - and it is imperative that they are called out on this bluff. They believe that Lacerda and the UDN will happily bend the knee at the slightest pressure - well, let them. The disorder brought on by the strikes has gone on long enough, and it is time that something is done about it.

The police and the media will be the cavalry of our assault against them both mentally and physically - armed officers will disperse the rioters to the wind, whilst the media will take our side in portraying them as the spoiled children acting out that they are. Combined, the strikers will stand no chance.
strings.BRA_military_option_desc:
There is no such thing as too much force when it comes to ensuring Brazil's stability. The military have kindly approached us and offered to lend their aid in resolving the current situation - and it is an offer that we shall gladly accept.

This is not a decision made lightly; President Lacerda is well aware that certain factions of the military have a history of overstaying their welcome in crises such as this, and the risk that they may do so again. However, it is a price that must be paid in order to ensure that the ongoing strikes are resolved in a quick and orderly fashion. The streets shall be cleaned and the unions will slink back to their proper place in irrelevance.
strings.BRA_outlast_strikes_desc: The strikers are much like a fire. They have grown from nothing into a raging inferno intent on burning the UDN down. But by that same logic, all fires peter out eventually. We have the police. We have the resources. It will be by velvet glove that Lacerda claims his victory, not by iron fist. Eventually, they will need to come back to work. For despite all the ranting and raving about the power of the working man, everyone needs to eat. And when they inevitably come crawling back, groveling on their knees for forgiveness, it will be granted happily, for this outcome was certain from the beginning.
strings.BRA_tavora_negotiations_desc: Távora was the one who forced the government into dialogue in the first place. It is then just that he is the man who has to follow through and lead these negotiations. Távora will have to strike a delicate balance in his dealings. Brazil cannot go back to the days of endless strikes, and at the same time, unions and their members will need to be at least somewhat satisfied with their pay. The stakes are incredibly high here, and if Távora cannot overcome these seemingly insurmountable odds, the PSD will no doubt sweep us out of power when the next election comes.
strings.BRA_pragmatism_over_all_desc: The agreement that Távora has managed to secure with the unions will be an incredibly tough pill for the government to swallow, even if it is a necessary one. Any further prolonged strike action will seriously damage the economy and greatly reduce the UDN's electoral prospects in the future. The government will have to strike a conciliatory tone with the unions to avoid this worst outcome. While we could not go the whole way, some important reforms will be implemented under this agreement. There will still be disruptive strikes in the future, but these reforms should make them less prolonged and less severe than the status quo.
strings.BRA_hold_firm_desc: Távora and the unions have drudged up a preposterous agreement; under this plan, the unions will retain most of their leverage and the ability to call burdensome strikes. This agreement is a total capitulation to those radicals and should not be allowed to stand. The government will continue to starve out the strikers, either until they cave and come to a more nuanced agreement or are crushed entirely. Brazil must hold firm against this reckless radicalism. If the government shows any further weakness, then the strikers could prevail. The existence of a prosperous Brazil hinges on that result not coming to pass.
strings.BRA_crows_legacy_desc:
While it took a prolonged and very costly effort, the Labour Law has finally passed, and the unions lie defeated. This will be the most foundational part of the Crow's Legacy and ensure the future economic prosperity of Brazil, secure from unexpected strikes and unshackled from the populist restrictions on our economy forced by the unions.

Contrary to what the unions claim, the tide raises all boats, and union members will be far better off in the long term. In time, the idea of having such high levels of union influence will inevitably fade, Brazilians will learn the advantage of this new economic regime, and eventually, the system of strong unionism will be nothing but a distant memory and an unpalatable system to which Brazil will never return.
strings.BRA_crows_legacy_tt: Lacerda's legacy will depend on if he compromised in the strikes.
strings.BRA_lacerda_strikes_over_tt: Lacerda has won his crusade against Varguism and crushed the strikes
strings.BRA_tavora_presidency_desc:
Pressuring Lacerda into resigning was the last thing that we wanted, but the economic situation demanded drastic action he was unwilling to commit to. The strikes have severely damaged Brazil's economic progress, and were it not for the united cabinet, the economy may very well have been shattered entirely.

With Lacerda now out of the picture and Távora in his place as President, much work is to be done. With the amount of economic struggle Brazil has experienced, uniting the nation once again will prove to be a challenge.

A challenge that must be met.
strings.BRA_united_against_varguism_desc:
Lacerda's removal has upset many in the UDN, both those with ties to his faction as well as former allies to Gomes. They claim that we have betrayed our core principles by removing Lacerda, but this is simply untrue. We kept true to our principles. It was Lacerda that nearly destroyed our economic projects by choosing to fight a hopeless battle. We did what was best in a bad situation, but unfortunately, many do not see it that way.

As it stands now, the UDN is splintered. It is imperative that we restore factional unity and transform the UDN into an organization whose path is guided by the party and not solely by the current President's will.
strings.BRA_correct_the_error_desc:
Lacerda repeated Gomes' mistake by attacking the Varguist project directly in an unfruitful attempt to eliminate the labor laws. Removing the aforementioned labor laws was always going to end in catastrophic failure due to the sheer volume of political opposition to such actions.

Under Távora, the process of reversing many of Lacerda's decisions will lead to both the return of many labor regulations as well as the return of stable governance.
strings.BRA_our_natural_ally_desc:
The maintenance of our relationship with the Americans is quite a significant task. They are a key ally to us and with the recent financial issues we have faced, we must quickly improve trade relations with them in order to restore their confidence in our economy. We shall send our foreign minister on a little trip to Washington to engage in the discussion of trade between our two nations.

Hopefully, when the Americans see our efforts in treating these matters with the urgency that they deserve, they will be more willing to work with us and re-establish their faith in our market.
strings.BRA_the_crows_protege_desc:
The individual who opposed the removal of Lacerda as President the most was the Governor of Guanabara, Raphael Magalhães. As a close ally to Lacerda, Magalhães took a tough stance against the strikers in Guanabara, keeping Guanabara's economy afloat while the rest of the country faltered.

Within the UDN, Magalhães whispers to other members of treachery and treason, claiming that we have betrayed our principles in Lacerda's removal. In order to restore unity to the UDN, Távora will arrange a meeting with Magalhães in the hopes of smoothing over relations and working on Magalhães' many complaints.
strings.BRA_tavora_stabilize_inflation_desc:
A major cornerstone of the UDN's political platform was the reduction of Brazil's inflation rate, which has historically proved to be quite unstable in times of uncertainty. Former President Lacerda was many things, but his commitment to achieving stellar economic growth and a downturn in inflation was certainly not among his failings whilst in office.

Unfortunately, the strikes have caused a stoppage in much economic activity, reversing much of the progress Lacerda had made. Inflation is on the rise once again, and measures must be taken before we arrive squarely in the same place we started years ago. Now that Lacerda has faltered, President Távora will take this burden upon his shoulders, and continue the fight to keep Brazilian currency from spiraling out of control.
strings.BRA_deficit_hawks_tavora_desc:
For far too long has unchecked, reckless spending wreaked havoc upon Brazil's finances. Irresponsible government budgeting has led to rising debt across the board, and President Távora's predecessor proved wholly incapable of putting a stop to this sorry state of affairs. Let us correct the oversights of the past and take a new approach towards controlling the deficit.

The UDN, as well as Távora, are in favor of balancing the budget, but serious efforts have yet to be made. It is time to slash government spending in all sectors, even if it comes at the expense of certain social programs. Only once we have actual money to spend can we get a handle on the ongoing economic downturn.
strings.BRA_loan_sharks_desc:
The deficit is growing out of control, causing debt to balloon to dangerous levels. Of course, this is a consequence of the UDN's long standing battle against inflation: in an effort to keep the currency under control, interest rates must remain above a certain level to avoid devaluation. Although it may seem as though we are cutting off one hand to save the other, Távora is confident that we can both keep inflation under control, while still keeping a handle on the deficit.

For one time only, we will make drastic cuts just long enough to buy us time to combat the deficit. Once the economy is no longer in danger of flying off the rails, we can then return to the usual levels to continue the fight for the Brazilian cruzeiro. This will be a tricky balance to pull off, but if anyone can accomplish it, it is President Távora.
strings.BRA_end_guanabara_dream_desc:
The terrible storm and catastrophic damage done to Guanabara was a tragedy, but the amount of money being pumped into its reconstruction is simply unsustainable, with spending on the project going far beyond the original plans. Much of the money was not just for reconstruction, it was also granted due to it being a pet project for Lacerda, while the rest of Brazil was aiming towards economic austerity.

It is time that we end reconstruction and salvage as much as we can. In order to show our commitment to the people of Brazil, it is occasionally necessary to give up on an unfeasible dream or sacrifice a sacred cow.
strings.BRA_guanabara_prooject_done_tt: The GUANABARA RECONSTRUCTION megaproject has already been completed.
strings.BRA_tavora_guanabara_dismantle_megaproje: We will dismantle Lacerda's failed pet project - the reconstruction of Guanabara.
strings.BRA_nordeste_reinvestment_desc:
Távora, as a former governor of Ceará, is well aware of the political and economic potential of the Nordeste region. Most people who inhabit this region are unfortunately not inclined towards supporting the UDN. It has been the PTB that has historically held the most sway in this region, dominating the political scene.

If the UDN were to invest in this region, it may be able to sway thousands of voters and could potentially even swing the election in our favor.
strings.BRA_loyal_middle_class_desc:
The main support base for the UDN is the middle class. It is of the utmost importance that we maintain good relations with this group to secure the future of the party.

Távora will reassure this core group that the UDN is there to defend the interests of the people and won't repeat past mistakes. To build a better Brazil, it is necessary to cater to the middle class. Their will is what decides the failure or success of the government after all.
strings.BRA_our_subservient_middle_class_desc:
Between the General Strikes, it is not the wealthy industrialists or the grassroots laborers who receive the largest share of the detriments. More commonly, the burdens end up relegated to the humble middle class, who do not have the option to avoid the conflicts on their own. As they lose jobs and fall into poverty, the government ought to stand up for them when they cannot do so for themselves.

Is there any way for a person to become more loyal to the establishment than a public servant? If those who cannot find work are permitted to join ranks within understaffed departments, the UDN can easily consolidate its influence within the bureaucratic apparatus — so long as only law-abiding folks come and go.
strings.BRA_meet_the_psd_desc:
In the wake of Lacerda's fall from grace, the UDN is finding itself increasingly isolated, and is in dire need of allies to shore up the balance of power in Brasília. Fortunately for us, President Távora has a few favors he can call in from his days as a governor. During his tenure in Ceará, he governed largely with the support of the PSD, who have long been the UDN's closest partners.

Let us reach out to the PSD to see if we can reach some sort of agreement. They will no doubt ask for serious concessions in exchange for their support, but should the meetings prove fruitful, Távora's position will begin to become far less uncomfortable, and we can turn our attention to more pressing matters.
strings.BRA_beat_the_psd_desc:
Let's address the elephant in the room — the remnant opposition figures that the Sorbonne somehow allowed to linger. While the majority of the PSD agreed to work with the establishment through compacts of mutual benefits, some less cooperative elements, rallied under Tancredo Neves, had chosen to continue undermining the regime's integrity with their divisive rhetoric.

Approaching the 1970 election, the economic destabilization that Neves promises to bring becomes too dire to neglect. However unwilling he may be, Távora has no choice but to take this ill-intentioned dissident out of the picture. Golbery has endorsed the idea and will certainly act where his mouth talks.
strings.BRA_tavora_big_tent_desc:
The UDN is hardly a monolith. Ostensibly a conservative party, it has grown to become an all-encompassing menagerie of politicians of all stripes who are united in their opposition to Varguism. Liberals, conservatives, and even leftists reside within the party, and although their relations are tenuous, keeping the party united will be key to surviving the next few years.

Távora and his allies will reach out to all corners of the UDN to ensure that their voices are heard, no matter how much their values stand in opposition to our own. As the party's enemies grow in number, we cannot afford a conflict to arise from within our ranks. Once the UDN is tested from without, they will find that despite our differences, the party remains united in its commitment to present a united front against the lingering influence of Vargas.
strings.BRA_tavora_big_tent_sorbonne_desc:
The UDN is hardly a monolith. Ostensibly a conservative party, it has grown to become an all-encompassing menagerie of politicians of all stripes who are united in their opposition to Varguism. Liberals, conservatives, and even leftists reside within the party, and although their relations are tenuous, keeping the party united will be key to surviving the next few years.
