Távora and his allies will reach out to all corners of the UDN to ensure that their voices are heard, no matter how much their values stand in opposition to our own. As the party's enemies grow in number, we cannot afford a conflict to arise from within our ranks. Once the UDN is tested from without, they will find that despite our differences, the party remains united in its commitment to present a united front against the lingering influence of Vargas.
strings.BRA_cement_realist_dominance_desc: The UDN is a very syncretic party, with a large number of political positions under its wing. It's quite clear, however, that there are loose ends in this arrangement. Lacerda brought the entire party to its knees by trying to overturn the Vargas-era labor laws, and we must not do the same thing again by dividing ourselves unnecessarily. We must be careful not to allow future Lacerdas to rise up again.
strings.BRA_cement_realist_dominance_sorbonne_de: The UDN is a very syncretic party, with a large number of political positions under its wing. It's quite clear, however, that there are loose ends in this arrangement. Lacerda brought the entire party to its knees by trying to overturn the Vargas-era labor laws, and we must not do the same thing again by dividing ourselves unnecessarily. We must be careful not to allow future Lacerdas to rise up again.
strings.BRA_conference_season_desc:
The party conference of the UDN is close at hand, and many are dreading its arrival. It will be among the most difficult in the party's history: the disgraced Lacerda has been banned from participating, but many of his allies have made clear their intention to attend, which may complicate matters. Távora's own popularity within the party is tenuous at best, and it is uncertain if his presidency will survive as party divisions grow wider by the day.

Will the UDN move past the mistakes of the Lacerda administration, and remain united against the rising surge of Varguism, or will it collapse and fade into the history books as a tragic lesson in the perils of politics? The result of the conference will make the answer to this question clear. Let us hope that fate rules in our favor.
strings.BRA_conference_season_sorbonne_desc:
The party conference of the UDN is close at hand, and many are dreading its arrival. It will be among the most difficult in the party's history: the disgraced Lacerda has been banned from participating, but many of his allies have made clear their intention to attend, which may complicate matters. Távora's own popularity within the party is tenuous at best, and it is uncertain if his presidency will survive as party divisions grow wider by the day.

Will the UDN move past the mistakes of the Lacerda administration, and remain united against the rising surge of Varguism, or will it collapse and fade into the history books as a tragic lesson in the perils of politics? The result of the conference will make the answer to this question clear. Let us hope that fate rules in our favor.
strings.BRA_knife_edge_desc:
Bar charts and statistical tables are published in newspapers and hammered into bulletin boards in every city and town in the country. The vote totals remain within percentage points of each other as the failure of the Lacerda regime haunts UDN polls.

We must use media contacts, form alliances with anyone who hates the opposition more than they hate us, and throw everything we have with our attack ads. With all our resources, we must defend conservative strongholds, strengthen the middle class, and take back the cities. We have very little time left to fight the rising leftist wave.

Brazil has suffered enough. Never again shall she fall to Varguism!
strings.BRA_razors_grip_desc:
Brazil is a nation of the righteous and a land of the capable, as Colonel Távora built an example of valiant service to his countrymen, his successor ought to follow his proper precedent in establishing stability within Brasília's volatile political landscape.

As a fellow veteran, Ney Braga has the constitution of a man who truly has in mind the nature of the common people to pursue a policy of prosperity — Golbery knows this fully well too. The PSD will not prevail, the presidency shall be secured and there will be peace for our time.
strings.BRA_razors_grip_tt:
£BRA_psd_texticon Juscelino Kubitschek's popularity falls.
£BRA_udn_texticon Ney Braga's popularity rises.
strings.BRA_the_crow_triumphant_desc:
The years of Lacerda's presidency have been quite eventful. He has dealt with a nationwide strike, vanquished Varguism, and established a new economic order for Brazil based on free-market capitalism, low inflation, and millions in foreign investment. This new economic order has allowed him to expand every Brazilian's access to education and healthcare to banish poverty forever. All this while keeping the military loyal to the Brazilian government and ensuring Brazil is the key defender of democracy in South America.

This success has made some people say Lacerda should relax and enjoy his last year in office as he has done more to change Brazil during his presidency than his three predecessors. Lacerda, however, knows there is one last issue for him to deal with to ensure that he can preserve his legacy into the Seventies. That issue is Brazilian Democracy.
strings.BRA_lacerda_final_challenge_desc:
While calling democracy a problem would not be loyal to the UDN's ideal, it still is Lacerda's final challenge. While Lacerda's policies may have helped Brazil, they have also created many enemies. His main enemy is the former governor of Rio Grande do Sul, Leonel Brizola. He is a far more potent threat than Lacerda's opponents back in '65, as he has the rhetoric to rally our enemies and the backing of the movement that has previously tried to destroy Brazil. While Brizola already has the support of the PTB, some in the PSD are willing to throw away their ideals to avenge Vargas' legacy.

Lacerda only knows two men who can defeat Brizola. Lacerda himself, but thanks to the Brazilian constitution, he could only run for President again in 1975. That leaves the other option, the new governor of Guanabara, Raphael Magalhães. So that means Lacerda should spend his last year ensuring that Magalhães is the UDN candidate and focus a campaign effort towards isolating the PSD.
strings.BRA_lacerda_final_challenge_tt: To ensure his legacy is cemented, Lacerda must ensure Brizola is defeated in the upcoming election.
strings.BRA_beltraos_triumph_desc:
Beltrão's time as finance minister has been successful thanks to him lowering inflation and being a major player in ending the strike. Soon, the last stage of his master plan for the Brazilian economy will unfold. Thanks to our modernization efforts, we are attracting millions in foreign investment to Brazil from various OFN member states. Which is money we are using to pay off debts, fund continued modernization efforts, and fund further education and health initiatives. We should also use the money for

While some might view this use of investment for the Brazilian economy as political gain as corrupted, many of those investing money know that a Brizola victory would threaten their investments. Members of the Finance Ministry have stated that some investors are limiting the amount of money they invest in Brazil out of the potential threat of a Brizola presidency to their investment. So, using this money towards the UDN presidential campaign will lead to even more investment.
strings.BRA_ice_cold_desc: Some of the biggest corporations in America are beating down our doors, willing to throw millions of dollars in what is fast becoming a Brazilian economic miracle. And perhaps the most quintessential of American companies, Coca-Cola, is eyeing investment into Minas Gerais. A new bottling plant, one capable of producing enough soft drinks to keep Brazil cool and refreshed, is just the thing needed to turn Brazil's already productive and prosperous agricultural sector into the food processing powerhouse in South America. Saúdinha!
strings.BRA_bank_of_sam_desc: The US is the financial center of the Western world, keeping the world economy afloat on a sea of dollars. Brazil is no exception. Discussions with high ranking leaders of some of the big names of Wall Street; Bank of America, J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, and others have already seen positive results. Deals to take on and help manage our nation's debt are being floated, with terms that will be beneficial to all parties: reducing the federal debt, one of our campaign promises, while also giving a healthy profits to those Americans that are willing to take it on. It's frankly a no brainer!
strings.BRA_brazil_open_to_all_lacerda_desc:
There are many in Brazil who want to prop up and bolster Brazilian companies, giving them a privileged place in the economy. These “developmentists,” however noble their goals to make Brazil an economic powerhouse, are rather short sighted. By coddling and protecting our companies, we are incentivizing inefficiency and stifling competition that will reduce our nation's businesses ability to compete against other companies around the world.

Instead, we should foster the free market, allow foreign enterprises to set up shop here, and push our companies to adapt and overcome... or falter and die. Brazil is open for business, and Lacerda is holding the door.
strings.BRA_brazil_hotline_rio_desc:
The reconstruction of Rio de Janeiro is almost complete. After the disaster that has befallen our nation's biggest city, we are pleased to say that it's better than ever before. New skyscrapers, repaved roads, and all the infrastructure and services that a cosmopolitan city needs. The Jewel of Guanabara is the brightest light in Latin America; Buenos Aires, Mexico City, Caracas, and Havana couldn't match their rival. Even Miami is confronting a new rival south of the Equator.

A new dawn is cresting over Sugarloaf Mountain, and Rio is basking in the glow.
strings.BRA_setting_sun_desc:
Brazil's foreign policy has had one major weakness, a dark splotch on an otherwise close relationship with our democratic partners. And that is our ties with the Empire of Japan.

In a misguided effort to promote neutrality and development, Kubitschek and Lott had drawn close to Tokyo, allowing the Zaibatsu to come in and plunder our resources and our people. They are still a fascist dictatorship, out to dominate all the “lesser” nations of the world, and the previous leaders of our nation let the Japanese simply waltz in.

There will be no proclamation or announcement though: an increase of paperwork here, a few new tariffs there. Japanese goods will become less and less viable and profitable, while we work closer with our true friends and allies in the OFN. Soon, before anyone knows it, Japan's influence will be like that of the setting sun over the Andes Mountains.
strings.BRA_a_slow_drift_desc:
The threat from the Japanese is a clear and present danger to Brazil. However, after decades of investment and support, our nation is, for better or for worse, closely tied to the empire across the ocean. While some within Lacerda's administration advocate for a quick and decisive strike to end Japan's influence on our nation, the costs of doing so will be great: lost jobs, lost investment, slower growth and, horror of horrors, the possibility that Brizola and Vargas Jr. could use it against the UDN in the upcoming elections.

Lacerda has instead decided that we must take a careful approach. Using the tools of bureaucracy and the judicial system, fostering growth from our friends, and weaning ourselves off of the Co-Prosperity Sphere's grasp. While it will be slow, and one that will take time to be accomplished, it will be done without damaging our economy. After all, in Aesop's fable, the tortoise beat the hare by going slow and steady.
strings.BRA_trade_war_desc:
The greatest threat to Brazil's continued prosperity is the Japanese Empire. The Zaibatsu cliques that exploit and extract, the fascist drive to undermine democracy, and the imperialist arrogance will see our great nation reduced to a puppet state, a new colony for the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere.

Unfortunately, there are some useful idiots for the Japanese in our nation. Should Brizola or, heaven forbid, Vargas Jr., win the upcoming elections, then all our efforts to ensure freedom and liberty for Brazil will amount to nothing. Therefore, Lacerda has made the decision to put new trade tariffs on Japanese products, along with new regulations against Japanese businesses and ownership of our resources and factories.This will launch a trade war against Japan, one that could hamper our current growth. But, with American investment pouring in, the damage could be not only mitigated, but easily made up for.

A small price to pay to ensure our national sovereignty and safeguarding our fragile democracy.
strings.BRA_the_new_colossus_desc:
The Lacerda Presidency has made Brazil the new shining beacon of South America. Brazil is now a tropical colossus with a rapidly booming economy due to industrialization and millions in foreign investment. Of course, it is not only the economy that is booming. Brazil is also one of the most democratic countries in South America, with our people's freedom protected and a great social program.

Celebrating our economic gains, we will broadcast our success to the world. The media will proclaim that Brazil is a new shining city on a hill, and all are welcome to come to Brazil and participate in our great nation by becoming Brazilians.
strings.BRA_confront_argentina_desc:
The Lacerda presidency has dealt with many foreign policy issues during its years in office, but we still have one problem remaining. That issue is our long-running cold war with Argentina. This cold war with a potential major trading partner has always held Brazil back economically. However, the efforts of Lacerda and Cunha have given Brazil more allies than Argentina, and we have a way of displaying that fact.

We can show Argentina our strength by hosting a series of wargames in cooperation with our allies throughout Latin America and the OFN. These wargames will show Argentina who the true masters of the continent are. This show of force will hopefully force them to the negotiating table so that we can end this cold war once and for all.
strings.BRA_confront_argentina_tt: The President will host a series of wargames to intimidate Argentina and bring them to the negotiating table, while high risk if this gamble pays off the £GFX_BRA_udn_texticon UDN will see a major boost at the elections.
strings.BRA_bolster_the_bulwarks_desc: Of course, to conduct these wargames, we might need to convince our Latin American allies to join in. To convince them, we will send them money and weapons to both grease the wheels and ensure that their militaries are ready for the wargames. We will also send diplomats to convince our more cautious allies that they should join the wargames to mutually improve our armies through further training and supplies. We also can put some diplomatic pressure on governments who are still uncertain about their participation. All of these actions will likely convince our more cautious allies to participate.
strings.BRA_fear_is_the_mind_killer_desc: Sources are telling us that word of our wargames has reached the Argentine government, increasing tension between our two countries. The Argentine government has stated they are mobilizing troops along the Brazilian border in case the wargames are a smokescreen for an OFN-back invasion of Argentina. However, we must keep calm. The Argentine government is just mobilizing troops to scare us into canceling the war games. We must continue to organize them to show Argentina Our nation and our allies' strength.
strings.BRA_diplomatic_angle_desc:
Argentina is continuing to react negatively to our war game plans. While we want to use these wargames to end the Cold War in South America, however, the Argentine reaction is only increasing tension. We have reports that Argentina is mobilizing soldiers toward our shared border out of paranoia that this wargame is a cover for an actual invasion.

Our Foreign Minister Vasco Leitão da Cunha has suggested we set up a diplomatic backchannel with Argentina to defuse tensions. A piece of advice that we should follow on through to try to placate Argentina's fears over our international wargame.
strings.BRA_naval_manoeuvre_desc: A crucial aspect of this wargame will be the naval aspect. While most of our Latin American allies have only small navies, the OFN fleet is the central presence in the southern Atlantic, and we should learn how to better coordinate with them despite a decline in German presence in the region. These naval exercises will provide Brazil's navy with the opportunity to improve. Our sailors will get work and train with the American Navy, considered one of the best in the world. Hopefully, these exercises will improve the Brazilian navy and allow us both to secure the southern Atlantic and become the best in Latin America.
strings.BRA_joint_army_ops_lacerda_desc:
Soon, our military will join its Latin American allies in a joint exercise to test how our forces would respond to a hot war between Brazil and Argentina. The thing that this exercise will focus on is familiarization with the terrain of the Brazilian-Argentine border, river crossing, and ensuring all our allies are familiar with OFN equipment.

While the Americans will sadly not be sending a detachment of their military to Brazil, citing concern that American soldiers in Brazil will increase tension with Argentina to the point of no return. However, they will send advisors to provide advice and further training to the various armies at this exercise.
strings.BRA_cisplatina_70_desc:
With a name that recalls the first war fought between Brazil and Argentina, Cisplatina 70 shall be the most impressive military exercise ever seen in South American history. Cisplatina is a series of massive wargames ensuring that Brazil and its allies' militaries are better coordinated and prepared for any potential threat. After months of preparation, all our troops and allies are ready to begin the exercise.

With the likely success of Cisplatina 70, we will hopefully complete the two non-military objectives of this exercise. First, we show the Brazilian people how UDN rule has made the Brazilian military stronger and the primary defender of freedom in South America, which leads to more people voting for us in October. Second, this show of force should intimidate Argentina to the point of allowing us to open a series of backchannel talks to end the Cold War in South America finally.
strings.BRA_tavoras_masterplan_desc: We can learn an important lesson from the old saying “Divide and Conquer,” Virgílio Távora learned it after the UDN defeat in 1955. Távora has taken that lesson to heart for the 1970 election and is using it as the center of his strategy for Magalhães' election. Távora's strategy is already being implemented in his home state of Ceará. This strategy is creating splits within the PSD-PTB coalition by painting Brizola and his allies as radicals who will lead Brazil down the path of Communism. A strategy that, come October, will hopefully see some of the traditional PSD voters vote for the UDN instead.
strings.BRA_tavoras_masterplan_tt: £BRA_udn_texticon Raphael Magalhães's popularity rises by 3% in the North-West.
strings.BRA_repair_liberdade_desc:
While we often talk about the UDN's many successes during the Lacerda presidency, we are far from perfect. One of the blackest stains on the Brazilian government in the last couple of years was the racist riots destroying the Liberdade district of São Paulo. The damages, combined with the lack of reconstruction, have proven a problem for Magalhães polling well in the state.

To clean up this black mark on our administration, we should rebuild the city using federal funds and use the press to ensure that the people know it's our responsibility for this reconstruction effort. Both of these will then lead to an improvement in the UDN polling numbers in São Paulo.
strings.BRA_repair_liberdade_tt: £BRA_udn_texticon Raphael Magalhães's popularity rises by 1% in São Paulo.
strings.BRA_werewolf_nightmare_desc: Everybody in the UDN's leadership can agree that a potential Brizola presidency is a disaster for Brazil. However, polling tells us this sentiment is not as common among the average Brazilian as we would prefer. To ensure that your average Brazilian will agree with our sentiment, we must instill a sense of fear into them. That common fear would be that a Brizola presidency would create a radical agenda that would only lead to a communist revolution, which would destroy Brazil as it did Russia. If our campaign is successful, it should turn many members of the educated working class, middle, and ruling elites against Brizola. Hopefully, the many people who will turn against Brizola will contribute to our campaign fund and vote for the UDN come October. If the desired result of this campaign occurs, this fearmongering will ensure our victory in October.
strings.BRA_isolate_the_psp_desc:
While the PTB-PSD coalition is the main focus of our campaign efforts, the PSP is running a candidate, and we should at least keep tabs on them. However, our analyses see them as little threat.

The PSP is little threat because its proposed policies are too Varguist to win over UDN voters and too right-wing for PSD-PTB voters. This lack of their candidates' electability, combined with our administration's effort to expose the corruption of the PSP leadership, will make it easy for our campaign to isolate and splinter their campaign. If our efforts succeed, we will ensure that Vargas Jr. will never rise as high as his father.
strings.BRA_doomsday_clock_desc: Time is counting towards the election in October, and we must avoid any potential repeat of the upheaval surrounding the '65 election. To prevent any potential upcoming crisis in the coming months, we must ensure that the military is loyal and will not make any power plays if the election enters a deadlock. To help ensure military loyalty, we will identify any military officer with PTB sympathy and move them away from any critical locations, to avoid any potential crisis if the PTB loses. In these final months, we also need to gather our political strength to ensure that we can complete our final policies.
strings.BRA_squeeze_the_psd_desc: Brizola's policies and stances are radical even for the PTB, so radical some of the PSD view him as a communist. This view has benefited us as most PSD voters who opposed Brizola have switched to supporting the UDN. Of course, to secure Magalhães' future presidency, we need to go further. The PSD has sensible rightist leaders like Auro de Moura Andrade and Pascoal Ranieri Mazzilli. While we can't convince them to endorse Magalhães, we can persuade them not to endorse Brizola. If we can keep them silent, that is all we need to weaken the PSD part of the PSD-PTB coalition.
strings.BRA_squeeze_the_psd_tt: £BRA_udn_texticon Raphael Magalhães's popularity rises by 2% in the South.
strings.BRA_keeping_clean_desc:
We have the temptation to get our hands dirty during this election cycle. We could use all the usual tricks and slander Brizola all day until all our campaign efforts become just writing libelous newspaper articles. Our campaign staffers would be pressuring every major newspaper in Brazil to write an article a day about a new affair, bribery charge, and illegal turtle that a PTB politician was involved with.

However, this strategy could backfire on us. Brizola's base is loyal, and by attacking him and his allies, we would only be inflaming Brizola's supporters. They already see the Brazilian establishment as an enemy, so this libel campaign would only confirm those suspicions. These inflamed supporters would likely start riots and strikes if we used dirty tactics against Brizola. So, in the name of Brazil's stability, we must hold back our attack.
strings.BRA_getting_dirty_desc:
Brizola is doing better in the polls than expected, the UDN cannot lose yet another election.

Our loss to Kubitschek in 1955 doomed Brazil to another decade of stagnancy and high inflation. Our loss to Lott, despite him being a charisma vacuum, in 1960 allowed the rot to continue. 1965 appears to be an outlier where the people realized, for a brief time, the folly of Varguism. 1970 seems to tragically be a return to form for the Brazilian people.

We must avoid a loss in October, as it would vanquish all of the effort to lead Brazil down a proper path freed from Vargaism. We must use every dirty trick in the book to ensure that Brizola's campaign crashes and burns.
strings.BRA_getting_dirty_tt:
£BRA_udn_texticon Raphael Magalhães's popularity rises by 2% in Rio de Janiero.
£BRA_ptb_texticon Leonel Brizola's popularity falls by 3% in the South.
strings.BRA_globo_domination_desc:
Since its foundation in 1965, TV Globo has become a dominant force in the Brazilian media. As Brazil's most-watched television network, it holds a near-monopoly over the educated middle class and those in the working class who can afford a television.

Luckily for us, TV Globo's ownership is aligned with our party's agenda, with Roberto Marinho being a prolific donor to our campaign. We can use this connection to set up secret backroom talks to ensure that the UDN receives positive coverage from Jornal Nacional and other Globo news programming. We will also allow TV Globo exclusive rights to the first ever televised debate between Magalhães and Brizola as long as they ensure that coverage and questions are biased in Magalhães' favor.
strings.BRA_live_on_air_desc:
Soon, Brazil will have its first-ever televised debate being held and aired by TV Globo. Globo has invited the three leading presidential candidates, Magalhães, Brizola, and Vargas Jr. Given the impact that televised debates have had on the US presidential election, this debate will be a deciding factor in this year's election. In short, the 1970 Brazilian election will be the first election in Brazilian history to be decided by television.

We hope that the debate will make Magalhães appear as the sane and rational candidate compared to the radicalism of Brizola and the populism of Vargas Jr. If Magalhães keeps up his appearance and answers all the questions satisfactorily, this debate will determine the election in our favor.
strings.BRA_lacerda_judgement_day_desc:
The final moment of choosing dawns upon us: election day. Millions of people will go to the polls to decide whether or not our government made true to our promises of freedom and liberty, whether we handled the economy aptly, and whether we made Brazil a better place by the end of our time in power.

Considering the short time we have left, we can't do anything material to convince the people. Our capabilities to affect the people's support lie not with our government anymore but with the loudspeakers and voices of our election team. President Lacerda will make his final pleas to appeal to voting for liberty, democracy, and prosperity. The rest of our ministers will do the same.

Afterwards, all that remains is for us to wait until the results flood in...
strings.BRA_lacerda_judgement_day_tt: £BRA_udn_texticon Raphael Magalhães's popularity rises by 2% in the North-West.
strings.BRA_lacerda_udn_increase_x: Increase Verbal Attacks on Our Opponents
strings.BRA_lacerda_udn_info_tt:
The UDN has never been unified by any means, not since it was founded in 1950 on the sole principle of anti-Varguism. As much as the President wishes it weren't so, the party has factions that don't see eye-to-eye, and each faction offers benefits and drawbacks for leaning their way.

Focuses, event choices, and decisions affect how the administration leans. The liberalism-statism axis gauges Brazil's embrace of laissez-faire capitalism, influencing centralization and inflation. The cooperation-intransigence axis gauges the administration's willingness to strike consensus or stick to the President's convictions, determining how often opportunities arise to reach across the political aisle.

Lastly, keep an eye on Party Loyalty. Lose the faith of your senators and they may fall prey to the charms of other parties.
strings.BRA_lacerda_udn_party_loyal_loyal_desc: “The UDN's been good to me. It's my party, and it represents the things that I believe in. Party leadership's good, rank and file's good - truth be told, I can't imagine being anywhere else.”
strings.BRA_lacerda_udn_party_loyal_fence_desc: “Look, the UDN's my party, but I look at it sometimes and I don't recognise it. You've got some problems below and more above - truth be told, I'm finding reasons to support it when it should be handing me those reasons.”

strings.BRA_lacerda_udn_button_realistas_tt_dela:
Leader: Virgílio Távora







£GFX_Tavora_texticon








It was 1950 when Eduardo Gomes won the presidency, and a future beyond Vargas, beyond authoritarian developmentalism, seemed possible. Then, in 1955, after the disaster that was the Gomes regime, Kubitschek defeated Juarez Távora, the “Viceroy of the Northeast,” and the anti-Varguists' five years in the sun were over.

Sidelined after Juracy Magalhães' failed campaign in 1960, the Realistas tell themselves they're the only ones in the UDN who remember they're in a democracy. Although many still lean economically liberal, they fear that if they go too far, Varguism will simply rear its ugly head once more.

They know what the others say: that they're sticks in the mud, that they're pessimists and cowards. But they also know that respectability works, because Virgílio Távora, Juarez's nephew, had won the vice presidency. Now, while Juracy assures America that they will keep Brazil stable and sane, Virgílio watches Lacerda's every move, making sure his megalomania doesn't throw away the trust of the people and the future of the UDN.
strings.BRA_banda_de_musica_lacerda_leader:
Leader: Carlos Lacerda







£GFX_Lacerda_texticon








After his brush with death at the hands of Gregório Fortunato and the subsequent fall of the Estado Novo, Carlos Lacerda's meteoric rise to superstardom left a lasting mark on Brazilian history. It's no shock he's since assembled a band of economic liberals, die-hard anti-Varguists, and ardent firebrands who all pay lip service to the man who overthrew Vargas himself.

While initially supporting Jânio Quadros' vice presidential bid, his anti-American rhetoric alienated foreign policy hawks, many of whom would flock towards Lacerda's unabashed devotion to the OFN. Half a decade later, an election came and went, and now the Banda de Música is the headlining act.

With Raphael Magalhães as Chief of Staff, Sandra Cavalcanti as Governor of Guanabara, and Aliomar Baleeiro in the Senate, the faction acts like they own the place, speaking of a new radical vision of democracy awaiting Brazil. They've been cheering for Lacerda for years. Try not to disappoint them.
strings.BRA_banda_de_musica_maghallas_leader:
Leader: Raphael Magalhães







£GFX_Maghallas_texticon








Lacerda is gone, and the Banda de Música is in shambles. Once heralds of a liberal future for Brazil, their hopes were dashed by Távora's coup. The Realistas, cautious and pragmatic, took control, making the party a new, more restrained copy of itself. Meanwhile, Lacerda seems adrift, moving from safe house to embassy, clinging to the remnants of his relevance as his former allies charted a path forward without him.

Yes, they lost the battle, but not the war. Raphael Magalhães has taken charge of the faction, determined to keep the flame of economic liberalism alive through the storm. Sandra Cavalcanti, with her sharp tongue and uncompromising stance, Herbert Levy, the pragmatic economist, and Hélio Beltrão, the silent architect of reforms - are on his side. Together, they hold tight to the vision of a Brazil anchored firmly in the OFN, regardless of any concessions that the Realistas may make.

The Banda de Música may have been pushed into the background, but they refuse to fade away completely. The Braga Presidency will be a difficult pill to swallow, but the 1975 elections loom on the horizon. Their melody plays on, faint but resolute, waiting for the right moment to swell into a triumphant crescendo once more.
strings.BRA_lacerda_udn_button_bossa_nova_tt_del:
Leader: Magalhães Pinto







£GFX_Pinto_texticon








Not even the business-minded urban technocrats of the UDN can resist the spirit of populist reform. Emboldened by the unorthodox but successful campaign of Jânio Quadros for the vice presidency, the Bossa Nova, a faction of reformist politicians, grew to become the main opposition bloc within the party. Although guided by a gospel of developmentalism and statism, their strongly conservative social policies and fervent support from the Church set them apart from the PTB and the PSD.

In 1965, Magalhães Pinto, the governor of Minas Gerais and leader of the faction, ran for President but lost to the firebrand Carlos Lacerda. But perhaps as compensation, he found himself President of the UDN, helping to steady the ship as Lacerda explores uncharted waters. Now he is working with federal deputy José Sarney to maintain the UDN's commitment to the people and to keep the party in God's good graces.

And rumor has it, Pinto isn't done with the presidency just yet...
strings.BRA_lacerda_udn_button_liberais_tt_delay:
Leader: Milton Campos







£GFX_Campos_texticon








Few remember Eduardo Gomes' term fondly. Conservative pundits wrote polemics about his failure to join the OFN, as workers rioted in the streets over his abolition of the minimum wage. More than a decade later, even as he remains the eternal Minister of Aeronautics, most Brazilians have long since treated him as a bad memory. But not everyone.

Jokingly called the “Grupo de Bacharéis” by their opponents, the Liberais Históricos, as they like to style themselves, represent the oldest strands of conservatism in the party. While not as laissez-faire as their younger colleagues, they are the party's most ardent anti-Varguists, with decades of experience fighting the Estado Novo.

By far the weakest faction, they follow the guidance of Milton Campos, a federal deputy who retains some influence as a party founder. Dedicated to restoring the legacy of the Brigadier President, his faction will tempt Lacerda into harsher legalist measures. They no longer have a real shot at power, but perhaps it's worth learning a thing or two from them about how to run a state.

strings.BRA_lacerdas_dream_desc:
The last remnants of the economic fascism Vargas imposed on the Brazilian people are now firmly consigned to the wastebin of history. Liberated from corporatist shackles, Brazil's economy roars like an uncaged lion as free capital and foreign businesses rule the agenda, with the days of Kubitschek era inflation increasingly becoming a distant memory.

The PSD and PTB outwardly slam this move to free-market fundamentalism as a betrayal of Varguism. Privately, more and more members of both parties are swaying to the tune of this new economy as they see its benefits, reshaping their definition of Varguism to fit it.
strings.BRA_black_cat_white_cat_desc:
When Lacerda first became President, most assumed that the days of developmentalism were dead and buried, but this fear has not come to be. Pragmatism has won out as free-market fundamentalism has not overtaken the old Varguist orthodoxy, much to the relief of the international economic community. Some wonder if Lacerda is quietly fuming over this, that Brazil will continue to follow the economic structure set out by his hated rival.

Others believe that he has stopped caring — that ultimately, it doesn't matter if it's a black or white cat, but as long as it catches mice, it will do Brazil. And if developmentalism continues to aid capital, it will have done its job.
strings.BRA_permanent_polarization_desc:
The reputation left behind by the President will be that of a divider, a man who separated Brazilian society into Lacerdaists and Varguists. Each day in Brazil's parliament, the government and opposition fling insults of “fascist” back and forth as if it were going out of fashion. Any hopes of bipartisan cooperation, bar the odd defector, are dead in the water.

The Senate no longer feels like a place of democracy but a warzone. While the newshounds may lap up this consistent controversy, other pundits quietly worry about the state of Brazilian democracy now. Even foreign ambassadors hope this atrocious behavior won't rub off on other nations in the OFN.
strings.BRA_permanent_polarization_tt: The £BRA_psd_texticon PSD and £BRA_ptb_texticon PTB will not cooperate with us in the Senado...
strings.BRA_tripartite_system_desc:
There was once a crusade against Varguism by Lacerda's government — to eradicate it from Brazil's national consciousness — but those times are dead.

With Távora's guidance, Lacerda has shed his fundamentalist beliefs for a more conciliatory approach. UDN senators regularly shake hands with their PSD counterparts, and even the PTB grows more welcome to cooperation each day. As the darlings of the right drift center, it seems likely that Vargas' legacy will remain as the undisputed bedrock of the United States of Brazil.

strings.BRA_lacerda_paulista_riots_desc:
The fair city of São Paulo burns within a conflagration of racial tension, and the whole country has begun to feel the effects.

What began as an attempted lynching has steadily deteriorated into an orgy of violence directed at the Japanese immigrants of the Liberdade district. Shootings, hangings, and vehicular homicides continue to terrorize the Nikkei, forcing them to seek refuge far away from their homes. The Força Pública has been abnormally slow to respond to the riots, and it remains to be seen how the President will handle this crisis...

strings.BRA_Liberdade_in_Ashes_desc:
After a few tense days of violence and hatred, the city of São Paulo has fallen silent.

The Liberdade district, home to one of the largest Japanese communities outside of Japan itself, is in ruins, and while efforts are being taken to reconstruct it, there is no doubt that a deep wound has been struck within the Nikkei. Although racial crimes are on the decline for the first time since the riots began, the fallout continues to force many into an exodus away from Liberdade. The bleeding may have been stopped, but it is clear the healing will take a great deal of time.

strings.BRA_lacerda_conference_p2_v1: He opened his speech on economic matters. Távora remembered the long nights he spent keeping Lacerda's knife from ripping apart the budget. A little fat, here and there, to sate the blade. But staring at Magalhães on stage, Távora wondered if he could grab his hand once he took the knife. He brought the wine up to his lips, sipped nervously.
strings.BRA_lacerda_conference_p2_v2: Magalhães opened his speech with a line about their commitment to the Brazilian people. “Horseshit,” Távora muttered, sipping at his wine. Sure, the dreaded beast of inflation had been slain. But how many jobs had been lost, how many people had lost the government's guiding hand, when the Banda hacked the budget apart?
strings.BRA_lacerda_conference_p3_v1: Magalhães then turned his speech towards the Northeast, and the new initiative set up by the UDN to fight the ongoing droughts there. His name would never be mentioned, but the right people knew that was Távora's work. He would be satisfied with that. It was better for the UDN overall to look good. But he thought about his home, the parched and tired land given new life, and he let himself smile a little.
strings.BRA_lacerda_conference_p3_v2: With that telltale magician's flourish, Magalhães' hand flew into the air as he then spoke of the UDN's restoration of critical infrastructure. He was speaking of the compromised Hydroelectric Renewal Bill. It helped the Northeast a little bit, but there were still large pockets of desiccated land, still relying on candlelight to see through the night. Távora had seen those places. He took a longer sip.
strings.BRA_lacerda_conference_p4_v1: A hush had fallen over the room as Magalhães spoke of the Riots. Here, he was compelled to thank Távora by name, but it earned no smile from him. He was owed far more for pulling Brazil through that nightmare. Months of negotiation, late nights and bitter meetings, all to prevent further bloodshed in the streets, had earned him no more than some kind words. Távora brought the wine glass up and swallowed the rest of the contents.
strings.BRA_lacerda_conference_p4_v2: When the speech turned to the Riots, there was a solemn silence amongst the audience. It was thanks to the bravery of police units across Brazil that they were contained, that order prevailed against the growing chaos in the streets. A frisson of disgust rippled down Távora's arm. He saw the glass shaking in his hand, but he had drunk so much already that the liquid stayed in its glass.
strings.BRA_lacerda_conference_p5_v1: They had never seen eye to eye on much, but Lacerda knew when to listen to Távora. He respected that, or at least felt compelled to respect that. When the time came, and the campaign rolled out in earnest, the Northeast would rally for Magalhães. Távora felt he owed him that much.
strings.BRA_lacerda_conference_p5_v2: For five years, Távora had suffered the radical nonsense that Lacerda pushed upon Brazil. Yet Magalhães stood on stage to prolong those same impulses. When his campaign finally began, he would find nothing in the Northeast. The Realistas would campaign for themselves alone—just as the Banda had charged ahead on their own.

strings.BRA_OC_Goals: We will cut our GDP and inflation reduction targets in half for the next year, due to the Oil Crisis.
strings.BRA_new_cabinet_muller_tt: Filinto Müller will assume the Vice-Presidency.
strings.BRA_new_cabinet_goulart_tt: João Goulart will assume the Vice-Presidency.
strings.BRA_democracy_survives_desc:
The Army has played its hand, but found itself wanting. Regardless of the candidate we've installed as interim President, we've installed one.

Our democracy, though bleeding, still survives to live another day, at least until we hold proper elections. While we can't fool ourselves into thinking another coup attempt won't ever happen again, we can hold our heads high, look at the foes of democracy, say proudly:

Democracy lives.
strings.BRA_idea_rampant_corruption_desc:
If Brazil had a disease, even a child would tell you that it is corruption. Political corruption and its consequences plague Brazil, from the local town council, to state governments, to the army and federal government as well.

Its prevalence proves a problem to every leader, as people do not work for the greater good of Brazil but for personal benefits. Political corruption will need to be removed from its roots, lest future governments continue to be plagued by its consequences. But while some leaders may fight against it, some may embrace it.
strings.BRA_idea_rampant_corruption_med_desc: To stabilize our government we've turned a blind eye and cut some deals with the local oligarchs. After the Hundred Days, anything is fair game to keep our democratic government afloat, and if worsening our problem for the sake of longevity is what it takes, then so be it.
strings.BRA_idea_rampant_corruption_high_desc:
Adhemar stabilized his government, at the cost of the control of our own political corruption and system. But, as long as Brazil still keeps a President elect, then everything will sort itself out!

Right?
strings.BRA_idea_the_war_on_corruption_desc:
Corruption is a slow and insidious killer, sucking the efficiency away from our government like a leech. How can Brazil expect to make any progress with such a disease ailing it?

The only suitable course of action is to exterminate this plague without remorse. Offenders will be cast out from their governmental offices and sent to prison cells, paraded in front of the public as examples of what will happen if you accept money on the side. Only through ruthless action can any semblance of progress be made so that order is restored.
strings.BRA_idea_lacerda_corruption_reforms_desc:
The government should never function based on one's connections, but one's ability, a belief that Lacerda has championed during his time in office. To put this belief into actions, reforms have been passed to crack down on corruption, assessing the ability of the public service to actually serve the public through regularly scheduled audits.

The power of swing in Brazilian government will soon come to a standstill, replaced by the sleek efficiency championed in American public office.
strings.BRA_rapid_industrialisation_desc:
As time goes on, Brazil has found itself becoming an increasingly industrialized nation. Dozens of new factories are being set up to fuel Brazil's economy. This has caused a boom in population as well as GDP growth.

With the rapid pace of industrial growth, Brazil is becoming a state more reliant on oil from both Petrobras and the Middle East. If the oil supply remains stable, Brazil will soar.
strings.BRA_idea_Lobster_conflict_desc: A conflict known as the “Lobster War” has been occuring for months in the Atlantic waters near Brazil. African and German fishing vessels are constantly breaching Brazil's territorial waters, while Brazilian fishermen suffer from having their rightful catch stolen and boats attacked when confronting these vessels. It is up to Lott to address this threat and win the Lobster War, using any means necessary.
strings.BRA_idea_Lobster_conflict_2_desc: A conflict known as the “Lobster War” has been occuring for months in the Atlantic waters near Brazil. African and German fishing vessels are constantly breaching Brazil's territorial waters, while Brazilian fishermen suffer from having their rightful catch stolen and boats attacked when confronting these vessels. It is up to Lott to address this threat and win the Lobster War, using any means necessary.

African and German fishing vessels are constantly breaching Brazil's territorial waters, while Brazilian fishermen suffer from having their rightful catch stolen and boats attacked when confronting these vessels. It is up to Lott to address this threat and win the Lobster War, using any means necessary.
strings.BRA_idea_Lobster_conflict_4_desc: A conflict known as the “Lobster War” has been occuring for months in the Atlantic waters near Brazil. African and German fishing vessels are constantly breaching Brazil's territorial waters, while Brazilian fishermen suffer from having their rightful catch stolen and boats attacked when confronting these vessels. It is up to Lott to address this threat and win the Lobster War, using any means necessary.
strings.BRA_idea_Lobster_conflict_5: The Aftermath of the Lobster War
strings.BRA_idea_Lobster_conflict_5_desc:
Despite the Lobster War coming to an end after two years, Brazil's territorial waters are still being constantly breached by African and German fishing vessels.

This has left Brazilian fishermen suffering, with their rightful catch being stolen and their boats attacked when confronting these thieving vessels. The continuation of this conflict is not only a stain on Lott's political career, but also a national embarrassment for Brazil.
strings.BRA_idea_Bountiful_Harvest_desc: Thanks to the efforts of President Lott and the Brazilian government, the Lobster War has ended in a victory for our people. The Germans and other assorted parasites fishing in our waters have been successfully driven out, and our fishermen are now free to fish as much as they want, free from the risk of being harassed. We may expect a major uptick in lobster and other seafood revenues for about six months.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_desc: Negotiations for the Lobster War have concluded, with a fair deal that both sides have agreed upon. The conflict is over and stability can return to the region, with both parties getting what they wanted out of the negotiations.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_good_cg_desc: Negotiations for the Lobster War have concluded, and we have walked out of the negotiations with a massive bounty! The conflict is over and we have demonstrated our might over the opposing side; Brazil's seafood belongs to us, and us alone.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_small_good_cg_des: Negotiations for the Lobster War have concluded, and our negotiators were able to secure a favorable agreement for our side. The conflict is over, and our fishermen can return to Brazilian waters to safely fish and enjoy the fruits of their labor.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_small_bad_cg_desc: Negotiations for the Lobster War have concluded, but there is a general sentiment that we could have gotten much more out of the negotiations. The conflict is over at least, and we are still receiving some compensation over the fishing in Brazilian waters.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_bad_cg_desc:
The Lobster War has ended... But at what price?

Our negotiators have given much concessions, and received very little guarantees in return. At home, public opposition has not been contained to those who make a living from the sea's bounty. The people ask why their leadership has given up so easily to the enemy. After all, more than lobster was at stake!

Popular anger is not everything, however. The War is over, and our government is free to focus on new concerns. Our former enemies might have conceded little, but this imperfect peace is much preferable to the uncertainties of war. The people will get over their disappointment.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_manpower_desc: Negotiations for the Lobster War have concluded, with a fair deal that both sides have agreed upon. The conflict is over and stability can return to the region, with both parties getting what they wanted out of the negotiations.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_good_cg_mp_desc: Negotiations for the Lobster War have concluded, and our negotiators were able to secure a favorable agreement for our side. The conflict is over, and our fishermen can return to Brazilian waters to safely fish and enjoy the fruits of their labor.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_small_bad_cg_mp_d: Negotiations for the Lobster War have concluded, but there is a general sentiment that we could have gotten much more out of the negotiations. The conflict is over at least, and we are still receiving some compensation over the fishing in Brazilian waters.
strings.BRA_idea_RK_settlement_bad_cg_mp_desc:
The Lobster War has ended... But at what price?

Our negotiators have given much concessions, and received very little guarantees in return. At home, public opposition has not been contained to those who make a living from the sea's bounty. The people ask why their leadership has given up so easily to the enemy. After all, more than lobster was at stake!

Popular anger is not everything, however. The War is over, and our government is free to focus on new concerns. Our former enemies might have conceded little, but this imperfect peace is much preferable to the uncertainties of war. The people will get over their disappointment.
strings.BRA_overbearing_military_desc:
While the constitution states that the elected Presidency and Legislature hold the power in Brazil, this is not the reality in practice.

Brazil relies on its military. This is not just a fact, but a reality made all the more uncomfortable for any ambitious statesman by its exceptional power. The conclusions made over barracks poker tables or by senior generals define Brasília's political thinking, keeping military status and funding intact, and the room for maneuver minimal.

Stakes are high. If army sensibilities are offended, or instability reigns, the Fourth Republic might well end as it began... and fall to yet another coup.
strings.BRA_constitutionalist_dominance_desc:
A new era has dawned for the Brazilian Military, and for President Lott, it is exactly as it should be. Currently, the directive of the armed forces is of respect for the elected Presidency and Legislature, just as the constitution intended.

With the passing of the Lott Act and Denys' seditious coup in tatters, only unruly elements remain of the formerly imposing factions, which are not yet in the position to resist. Still, only hope ensures this status quo does not become an anomaly of Brazilian history.
strings.BRA_militarist_rebirth_desc:
Lott's attempt to suppress the pride of the nation, its military, could not stop his successor from handing back power. Adhemar rules through a system of mutual benefit between his PSP and military benefactors to restore the military's voice in politics as it was before the Lott Act. A little back-scratching here and there, and the PSP will be the party of the army, and the army a stronghold for the party.

No longer will the armed forces serve one man's interests. It is time to find its true place in the sun. But the President is playing a dangerous game, and he must be careful to ensure this situation does not spiral out of his control.
strings.BRA_day_of_the_jackboot_desc: As the sound of thousands of infantrymen clamors through the streets of Brasília, democracy in Brazil remains but a dying husk. The hardliners in the military have used their constitutionally-given rights to remove the President from power in the name of national security, stamping out dissent nationwide as they promise to restore the status quo at a date deemed suitable to them. Civilian politicans can only hope this day does not last a decade.
strings.BRA_divisions_of_cardinals_desc:
In the Vatican, popes are chosen by cardinals in isolation in the Sistine Chapel. The illusion persists that Brazil is more democratic than that. However, when replacing the Vatican with Brasília and the Chapel with the Army HQ, there is not much difference. Brazil's top brass consider the presidential ballots as a band of cardinals consider their new messenger of God.

Every year this spirit further cements itself into the state edifice. So too does the political risk for any prepared to confront it.
strings.BRA_sword_of_damocles_desc: Many thought that when the military stormed into Brasília and suspended the civilian government, it was the death knell for Brazilian democracy. This turned out not to be the case, as the junta removed itself from power as authority was handed back to the civilian politicans. Despite this merciful transfer of power, uncertainty still remains within the country and the military is now stronger than ever. The murky political situation gives the military room to easily reassert its power, and if that happens, Brazil may never see democracy again.
strings.BRA_bastion_of_the_crow_desc:
No matter how hard Lacerda tries to feed Brazil her medicine, the people refuse the taste of his policies, and Congress throws a tantrum at the slightest whiff of his proposals. It seems that only the military understands what makes the nation healthy and strong.

The armed forces remain an important ally, but if the UDN ever falters, they won't hesitate to seize what's left of the country's democracy.
strings.BRA_institutionalised_military_desc: Brazil has come home to roost, back into the hands of the armed forces. Just as it did in 1889, when the military forced the onset of the Republic. Just as it did in 1930 and 1949, the military has stepped in to restore order as bungling politicians gambled it away. The army, the centerpiece of the nation now and forever, will bring it back and take orders from nobody.
strings.BRA_institutionalised_military_2_desc: Brazil has come home to roost, back into the hands of the armed forces. Just as it did in 1889, when the military forced the onset of the Republic. Just as it did in 1930 and 1949, the military has stepped in to restore order as bungling politicians gambled it away. The army, the centerpiece of the nation now and forever, will bring it back and take orders from nobody.
strings.BRA_military_stalemate_desc:
Pessedistas and Udenistas file to their seats. Never before had their parties held such power in Congress.

And never had that dominance felt so uneasy. Soldiers stand stern on the balcony, shadows against the gilded ceiling, kept at bay, but only just. This is the Sorbonne promise of stability, a suffocating stalemate where nobody wins and everybody is searching for any chance to regain control.
strings.BRA_hundred_days_desc: Brazil is paralysed, the line of succession has been shattered. With the resignation of both Lott and Quadros from the government, the politicans have failed to appoint a new one and have fallen into infighting. Multiple claimaints to the Presidency have presented themselves and Pascoal Ranieri Mazzilli has been appointed President as a temporary solution, until the legislature votes for a new President. While the politicans in Brasília bicker, the country falls further into chaos as the military watches. If nothing is done to resolve the crisis, they will certainly intervene.
strings.BRA_idea_japanese_inmigration_desc: President Quadros has removed several legal blocks on immigrating to Japan, primarily regarding Japan and the Co-Prosperity Sphere. Brazil is now seeing an immigration boom, with many Japanese immigrants attracted to a new life and the growing business potential within Brazil, though they have yet to assimilate perfectly to life here.
strings.BRA_idea_joint_military_operations_desc: The Brazilian Expeditionary Force in South Africa has overcome initial teething problems to become a well respected part of the OFN war effort in the dark continent. Working closely with American counterparts, the soldiers of the Southern Republic have contributed a few novel infantry tactics to the conflict as they've adapted to their twin roles on the frontline and in the counter-insurgency efforts.
strings.BRA_idea_trans_amazon_complete_desc: The Trans-Amazonian Highway, the fruit of ex-President Lott's work, has been finally finished. We've braved the untamable North and now we can reap its fruits!
strings.BRA_Agrarian_Reform_Weaker_desc:
President Lott's Agrarian Reform Act has passed. Now the law of the land, rural citizens are now feeling the effects of its implementation.

The bill has not passed unscathed through the law-making process. Its scope curtailed from the President's original intentions, the Agrarian Reform Program has begun expropriating land from large landholders and redistributing it to peasants. The process is being held up in several areas by lawsuits, as larger magnates struggle against the turning tide. The peasants who have received their land have received little relief and support against competition from the remaining large landholders.

As disappointing a start as it has been, the reforms have been mostly well received by poor rural communities. Change is finally coming to the Brazilian interior, and future Presidents will be able to build upon these foundations.
strings.BRA_Agrarian_Reform_desc:
President Lott's Agrarian Reform Act has passed. Now the law of the land, rural citizens are now feeling the effects of its implementation.

The bill has emerged in good shape through the law-making process. Having steered his program through the Senado, the President's original intentions, the Agrarian Reform Program has begun expropriating land from large landholders and redistributing it to peasants. The magnates have mostly accepted their losses of land, their ego soothed by compensations duly voted on by the Senado. Newly independent peasants are given assistance to get started, as they face competition from large landholders.

The program is rolling out smoothly, and rural communities are being given the tools needed to earn their own prosperity. President Lott will no doubt secure his legacy with the launch of this era of reform in the Brazilian countryside.
strings.BRA_Agrarian_Reform_Stronger_desc:
President Lott's Agrarian Reform Act has passed. Now the law of the land, rural citizens are now feeling the effects of its implementation.

Backed by energized allies in the dominant coalition as well as a few populists within the opposition, President Lott's reform package has gained speed as it has sailed through the Senado. The scope of the project and the resources attributed to it are beyond the President's initial targets.

In the countryside, a quiet revolution has begun as large magnates are seeing their empires parceled off to dispossessed families. The new independent farmers are enrolling into agricultural colleges in great numbers, as the state prepares them for their new life. Not all will become prosperous, but an overwhelming majority will be given the dignity of providing for their family.

The reforms are progressing at a breakneck pace. While the ever cautious President Lott is putting on the brakes here and there to prevent possible corruption or legal mishaps, he has been delighted at the speed at which his plan is proceeding. His joy has been matched by thousands of rural families, their life forever improved by this new era.
strings.BRA_army_nepotism_6_desc: The Army has escaped completely out of our control. Shadowy puppetmasters, with their own interests, define who moves within the bureaucracy, and what happens within it, and any actions we take against this beast is dilluted by the raw corruption laid within. Either we purge this disease, or they will get delusions of control.
strings.BRA_army_nepotism_5: Nepotism in the Army: Very High
strings.BRA_army_nepotism_5_desc: Nepotism is slowly becoming a foundation that our Army is built upon. Salaries are increasingly being taken from private interests, as those who resist this effort are being replaced with those more complicit. If we do not act now, this problem may become unstoppable.
strings.BRA_army_nepotism_4_desc: Many in the bureocratical branches of the army turn to their benefactors rather than our authority, and many “promotions” are sketchy at best. While unacceptable, it is still remediable, if we keep our chin upward and keep chipping at their hold.
strings.BRA_army_nepotism_3_desc: The Army, as it stands, is split apart. The Constitutionalists refer to the government as the final authority, but it's no secret that many generals and marechals have their loyalty not the Republic and Brazil, but to whoever put them in place. If we desire to not constantly watch our back against our own protectors, we need to excise this cancer from our armed forces.
strings.BRA_army_nepotism_2_desc: The Beast, to the shadowy puppets discontent, bleeds. Members of the army, long neglected a real chance of promotion, are seen now for their value to the armed forces, not by favours. The tug of war, however is not over yet.
strings.BRA_army_nepotism_1_desc: Only in an utopia would our army be a true meritocracy, but we've reached as close as possible to this ideal. Effort will be due rewarded in the Army, and not by the whims of corrupt Marechals, but by the devotion they've had for Brazil, and our nation. Army and State, for the first time in a long time, walk as equal, not as rivals.
strings.BRA_the_populist_republic_desc:
Walk through the avenues of Brasília, and it's easy to forget that half the world had fallen to fascism. A new modernist capital for one of the few liberal democracies left.

But inside every government building you'd pass, Varguists and anti-Varguists conspire for control, ever conscious that any sign of weakness could compel military opportunists to take over at any sign of incompetence.
strings.BRA_false_dawn_desc: With the dust settled and rumors confirmed or denied, democracy has prevailed once more... but how many days will it see? The problems of the past have merely grown worse, and the uncertainties of yesterday are now the fears of tomorrow. Brazilian democracy hangs on life support, and its fate lies on a further polarized political class and an increasingly influential military establishment. In this new false dawn, only time will tell if this is a momentary crossroad or an illusion about to end.
strings.BRA_death_of_the_dream_desc: The death knell of Brazilian democracy has been sounded throughout the country. Its institutions are held under an oppressive iron fist, answering only to the military, and while the junta has promised to restore democracy, that day seems to be slipping further and further away as the days ahead grow increasingly bleak. The dream of Brazilian democracy has faded into history.
strings.BRA_the_brazilian_miracle_desc:
With strong state-based industrialization and government programs, Brazil is experiencing further economic successes. With these factors in mind, it is no wonder that Brazil's standard of living has only increased.

Surely this, alongside heavy American investment, is more than enough to satisfy the Brazilian people. Brazil today finds itself with both a strong military and a strong economy.
strings.BRA_the_tropical_titan_desc:
With the ongoing trend of rapid industrialization, living standards in Brazil are increasing. This has all culminated in continued economic development throughout the country, and at the moment it appears these good fortunes are not stopping any time soon.

Dubbed by some media outlets as “The Tropical Titan”, Brazil is a nation which looks to the future with hope. For Brazil, the sky's the limit.
strings.BRA_brazils_black_swan_the_oil_crisis: Brazil's Black Swan: The Oil Crisis
strings.BRA_brazils_black_swan_the_oil_crisis_de:
The steady growth in economic prosperity for Brazil was fueled by cheap oil from the Middle East and our neighbor Venezuela. With the outbreak of civil conflict in the Middle East, oil prices have drastically increased.

With an economy so dependent on oil, Brazil has been hurt badly. Unless Brazil handles the inflation and deficit problems effectively, an entire decade of success could be lost.
strings.BRA_brazilian_phoenix_desc:
Brazil's economy was strong enough to survive the Oil Crisis. The successes enjoyed previously have returned, and the future only sends good fortune.

While the Oil Crisis has undoubtedly hurt Brazil's industries, the trend of economic growth was too strong to be stopped by one mere hiccup. This miracle will continue for years, potentially decades. Brazil's future as an industrial power is certain.
strings.BRA_the_lost_decade_desc:
The Oil Crisis has proven too much for Brazil to handle. Economic growth has stagnated, and the deficit continues to rise to match the rate of high inflation Brazil is experiencing.

It is unknown how long this will last, but it cannot last forever. Inevitably, the debt will be too much for Brazil to handle, and a new crisis will emerge. The last period of economic prosperity has been lost.
strings.BRA_psp_revolution_adhemar_desc: Since the end of the Estado Novo, Brazil has been in a tumultuous cycle of political rivalries. Varguists vs. anti-Varguists, developmentalists vs. free-market capitalists. In the midst of the endless disputes, one party stands as an outlier, and at its head, Adhemar de Barros will lead Brazil into a new era. The PSP is a unique force, its departure from partisan politics and populist ideals have caught the eye of the people, and even if its goals fail, it will change Brazilian politics forever.
strings.BRA_UDN_Counterrevolution_desc:
Every action has an equal and an opposite reaction. Vargas, the PTB, and all his cronies scattered across the Brazilian government have gone without an opposite reaction to their decadence for far too long. And now that Carlos Lacerda has ascended to the Presidency proper, that reaction has come. If they wish to call themselves the Revolution, then the UDN is the Counter-Revolution.

Vargas and his legacy will be swept away. High inflation, high debt, and corruption will be things of the past. The excesses granted to labor mobsters will be curtailed and the free market will finally be allowed to reign unchecked. Under the Crow, Brazil will finally embrace liberalism and capitalism - forces long kept at bay that will not be denied.
strings.BRA_imperial_presidency_desc:
Cheaters never win, and winners never cheat. João Goulart thought he could cheat his way into the presidency. Well, he thought wrong. Carlos Lacerda saw through his fraudulent victory and, invoking the use of emergency powers, saved Brazil from another five years of Varguist mayhem. Now the Crow sits upon his iron perch in Brasília, backed fully by the military and completely assured that his reign will last uninterrupted.

Of course, the usual suspects are quick to denounce this victory, branding Lacerda a tinpot dictator on the same level as the fascists across the Atlantic. Complete nonsense, as expected; unlike the despots of the world, Lacerda's rule will harken much closer to that of Ancient Rome - a dictatorship, yes, but one bound by the constitution and used for the good of the nation.

With these emergency powers, Lacerda will sweep away what remains of Varguism in Brazil, destroying its fraudulent legacy and saving the country - for the price of freedom is eternal vigilance.
strings.BRA_general_strke_lacerda_desc:
With riots all across the nation, President Lacerda now faces the greatest crisis of his presidency. The General Strike has paralysed all facets of public life. Lacerda's proposal to significantly change the Vargas Era labor laws has made him a target of the workers.

As the President tries to crackdown on the movement with the help of the police and his trade unions on his good side, the whole economy seems to be heading downhill. Lacerda has now a choice to fix this situation or threaten an early end to his career.
strings.BRA_Vai_Passar_desc:
From little nothings on the banks of the Araguaia comes the potential to change Brazil forever.

The military regime has shown its true face, phony paternalism unravelling into psychopathy, as the people of the Mid-North have been moved to revolutionary action against the countless injustices they have suffered. For the Communist Party of Brazil, the widespread discontent necessitates entering the third phase of their ongoing people's war, mobilizing into a revolutionary government out to displace both bourgeois and reactionary movements.

Chairman João Amazonas and his trusty allies Pedro Pomar and Mauricio Grabois have built themselves a base in the region, operating in Fortaleza, and enjoying an all-time high of popularity. Their primary difficulty lie in the material conditions of being based in the poorest parts of Brazil, suffering from underdeveloped infrastructure that hurts both war efforts and maintaining order. But as with all things, this will pass in time, once the revolution succeeds...
strings.BRA_crise_petrolifera_dynmod_desc:
The steady growth in economic prosperity for Brazil was fueled by cheap oil from the Middle East and our neighbor Venezuela. With the outbreak of civil conflict in the Middle East, oil prices have drastically increased.

With an economy so dependent on oil, Brazil has been hurt badly. Unless Brazil handles the inflation and deficit problems effectively, an entire decade of success could be lost.
strings.BRA_latifundos_crisis_desc:
Despite how much has changed throughout Brazil's history, one element has remained consistent. In rural communities nationwide, agricultural barons dominate both the local economy and politics like their fathers and grandfathers would have in eras past.

These conditions have led impoverished rural workers to lash out in violent displays. The government must step in before it is too late.
strings.BRA_countryside_strikes_desc:
The crisis in the countryside has only worsened. The government has proven ineffective in dealing with these protests. Each day, clashes between workers and thugs hired by the rich become more common.

All of this violence and protest have led more and more people to flee to cities in the hopes of a better life. If a solution is not found soon, the situation will continue to spiral out of control.
strings.BRA_the_burning_farmland_desc:
The situation across rural Brazil has continued to escalate. Guerillas are behind further violent attacks against the land-owning class, and at the moment, it appears these rebels are gaining ground.

Unless drastic action is taken now, this crisis ravaging the countryside will only get bloodier. This state of affairs could lead to the undermining of our legitimacy. This cannot be allowed to happen.
strings.BRA_minor_agrarian_reform_desc:
The safest path is the moderate one. To avoid further instability, it is vital to only take small steps towards reform, carefully thought through before implementation.

Some larger estates have already been broken up, with portions of the land being redistributed to poorer farmers. While there may still be protest from unhappy elites and peasants wanting more, tensions have eased. For now.
strings.BRA_radical_agrarian_reform_desc:
To address the rural issues plaguing Brazil, drastic reform is vital. Estates across the nation are being divided among poor farmers. Once completed, it could finally solve this crisis.

Of course, these steps were taken without input from the rural elite, who are openly hostile to these reforms. There is a real possibility it could all fall apart, but no one gains anything by playing it safe.
strings.BRA_completed_agrarian_reform_desc:
Due to heavy intervention in the rural crisis, the oligarchical system in the countryside has ended. Hundreds of thousands of farmers have benefited from these reforms, now owning property and not having it leased to them by the rich.

While there has been dissent from the dissatisfied elite regarding these changes, they need not be listened to. With their land gone, they are no longer relevant.
strings.BRA_the_silent_country_desc:
Where once were cries of protest, there is only silence. Using the strength granted to us by the constitution, the foolish rural communists and their filthy Marxist sympathizers have finally been stifled.

Our policies have proven most effective at achieving peace throughout the countryside. This victory was inevitable. Who else would dare to test Brazil's immeasurable might and resolve? Nobody.
strings.BRA_agro_industrial_complex_desc:
Kubitschek's plans have now been implemented. Instead of engaging in the battle on agrarian reform as others would, agriculture has become a vital part of Brazil's economy.

With large sums of land granted to agricultural corporations and the rural elite soothed, agricultural output has increased. While the PTB may not like it, these policies have achieved fifty years of progress in only five.
strings.BRA_idea_nationwide_chaos_max_desc: The immediate aftermath of the coup has left Brazil paralyzed, its inhabitants reeling after the dust has settled. Workplaces remain empty as Brazilians hide in their homes, fearful of some form of retaliation. For their part, the soldiers patrol the streets, arresting those they deem suspicious, who are then never heard from again. Nobody quite knows what will happen next, and all sides seem to be waiting for the other to take the first breath.
strings.BRA_idea_nationwide_chaos_high_desc: Brazil has shifted out of its initial paralysis into a state of nationwide panic. As the populace has begun to come to terms with the reality of military rule, and with the idea that this may be more permanent than some had initially hoped, demonstrations, riots, and overall resistance now threaten to break out across the nation. Brazil has found itself a powderkeg, and one errant spark might be all that is needed to set it all ablaze.
strings.BRA_idea_nationwide_chaos_medhigh_desc: The situation on the streets has cooled a bit, as the military was able to put a stop to the worst of the demonstrations and riots. For now, the situation is under control; the military once again roams the streets without fear, and the worst of the dissidents have fled into the countryside to hide, waiting for everything to blow over. Even still, it will take time for the military can cement their governance over Brazil, as few among the populace find themselves willing to collaborate.
strings.BRA_idea_nationwide_chaos_med_desc: Even though the worst seems to have passed, an air of uncertainty still filters through the streets of Brazil, covering everything like an immutable fog. Anyone brave enough, or stupid enough, to have spoken out against the regime had fled, or was dealt with some time ago. All that remains are those smart enough to keep quiet, knowing that collaboration with the military regime is better than the alternative: to become yet another nameless face, lost forever.
strings.BRA_idea_nationwide_chaos_lowmed_desc: The situation in Brazil has calmed immensely since the coup. For the first time in months, shops and workplaces forced to shut down in the panic find themselves slowly reopening, and while the constant presence of the military in the streets hasn't subsided, they find themselves able to keep order even without employing the more brutal tactics that they have so often used. It may be slow going, but the people of Brazil finally have started to accept military rule.
strings.BRA_idea_nationwide_chaos_low_desc: It seems that the tendency for life to recover from disaster applies even in Brazil. The chaos and fear that was omnipresent in the early days of military rule are long past; people have come to know and expect the military presence on the streets. While a few isolated incidents still occur now and again, it seems the great majority of Brazilians are content simply to go about their days in peace, life under military rule having become completely normalized.
strings.BRA_idea_build_more_roads_desc: There is currently a massive road construction program ongoing. Roads are being laid down all across Brazil to link cities and rural areas to one another. If all goes well, we may expect a significant improvement to our nation's overall infrastructure situation.
strings.BRA_idea_formalised_high_command_desc:
One of the greatest legacy of the Sorbonne faction's stewardship of the Brazilian Republic has no doubt been its reforms of the Brazilian high command.

Unlike many other modern nations, our country had never had a centralized defense ministry. Nor had it ever incorporated the army, navy and air force into one unified command structure. Even within the army itself, barracks throughout the country reassembled a patchwork of local military grandees, often using their men as muscle for regional policy interests rather than the Brazilian nation.

These memories of a disorderly army will now become a thing of the past. Under Castelo Branco's leadership a new formalized high command has been established. All branches of our armed forces are accountable to an empowered ministry of war. Within the army itself the hierarchy has been much reinforced; where once colonels and generals strutted and argued about the pecking order, there is now order and purpose.
strings.BRA_idea_formalised_high_command_2_desc:
One of the greatest legacy of the Sorbonne faction's stewardship of the Brazilian Republic has no doubt been its reforms of the Brazilian high command.

Unlike many other modern nations, our country had never had a centralized defense ministry. Nor had it ever incorporated the army, navy and air force into one unified command structure.
