Even within the army itself, barracks throughout the country reassembled a patchwork of local military grandees, often using their men as muscle for regional policy interests rather than the Brazilian nation.

These memories of a disorderly army will now become a thing of the past. Under Castelo Branco's leadership a new formalized high command has been established. All branches of our armed forces are accountable to an empowered ministry of war. Within the army itself the hierarchy has been much reinforced; where once colonels and generals strutted and argued about the pecking order, there is now order and purpose.
strings.BRA_idea_american_advisor_desc: The Hardliners have been calling for further collaboration with America against internal and external threats. We shall invite American military advisors into Brazil for joint training programs, similar to what we have in the 40's and 50's. This will deepen relations and improve our troops training.
strings.BRA_idea_american_advisor_2_desc: The Hardliners have been calling for further collaboration with America against internal and external threats. We shall invite American military advisors into Brazil for joint training programs, similar to what we have in the 40's and 50's. This will deepen relations and improve our troops training.
strings.BRA_guanabara_dreaming_state_modifier_de:
Hailed as a triumph of Carlos Lacerda's economic planning, Guanabara has been transformed into a model example for Brazilian drive towards modernity.; With the impoverished relocated and the favelas cleared out, the Lacerda-Doxiadis plan has given way to state of the art infrastructure, booming industrial sectors and burgeoning residential neighborhoods. For the first time in a long time, Rio de Janeiro now lives up to its name as The Marvelous City.

Tourism is at an all- time high, the new industry breathes life into commerce and a developing middle-class now rapidly migrating to Guanabara's reinvigorated suburban landscape. A window into Brazil's future is seen in the Guanabara Dream.
strings.BRA_Janio_Quadros_hog_desc:
Vice President
Populist Conservatism
--------------
Born in 1917, Jânio Quadros has always been a prodigy wherever he went. His career started in 1943 as a geography teacher at the Dante Alighieri College in São Paulo, where he gained fame for his gregarious personality and eccentric behaviour.

The end of the New State dictatorship and the reopening of the parties allowed Quadros to gather enough support to be elected as a São Paulo city councillor in 1950 by the Christian Democrat Party. Quadros' Lusotropicalist behaviour won him the graces of Caudilho Salazar, who granted him the medal of the Military Order of Christ. In 1955 he won the graces of the Paulistan electorate and won the city mayoral election and finally ran as Juracy Magalhães' Vice President in the 1960 election. In a cruel twist of fate, Juracy was defeated, and now Jânio finds himself as the VP to a man he is a political opposite. He has to make the best of the situation to keep himself afloat.
strings.BRA_Walther_Salles_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberalism
--------------
Walther Moreira Salles is something common in Brazil: a politician from an old, traditional family who enjoyed an easy path to success. Born in 1912 to a rich banker, Salles began his political career as the Brazilian ambassador to Washington during the later stage of the New State dictatorship where he gained the reputation of a great negotiator and appeaser. His success led him to a close friendship with Vargas and allowed him to become Juscelino Kubitschek and now Lott's foreign minister.

Salles now finds himself at a crossroads in his career. His resources are endless, his fame is universal and his connections are everywhere. He contemplates moving on to other projects such as his newspaper “A Última Hora” or the family banking complex, the Banco Moreira Salles. But one thing that he is certain to do while he remains in office is fight any attempt to impose a new dictatorship in Brazil.
strings.BRA_Tancredo_Neves_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
National Liberalism
--------------
Tancredo Neves is a well-known figure on the Brazilian political scene. Eloquent, good natured, optimistic and strongly nationalistic, Neves began his political career in 1935 being elected as a city councillior by the Progressive Party. His mandate was extinguished by the New State coup; most of the 1940s were spent improving his public image as a reliable lawyer in São Paulo.

The post-Vargas democratisation brought him to the Social Democratic Party, where he became a close ally of Juscelino Kubitschek, having used his connections to guarantee stability in all sections of the government. As a minister of economy, Neves is a reliable banker who gets things done. Sometimes he comments about his future plans to be President of Brazil, a position that he is clearly capable of exercising with utmost diligence.
strings.BRA_Odilio_Denys_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Odílio Denys is a special kind of officer - one crafted by the events of early 20th century Brazil. Being trained by the Prussian mission in the old republic, taking part in the 1930 revolution that put an end to the oligarchic governments and in the New State coup, and serving as a close ally to General Goés Monteiro, Denys took part in every major change in Brazil during the first half of the 20th century.

His authoritarian tendencies didn't divorce him from his strong sense of duty and discipline. A friend of Henrique Teixeira Lott, he was one of the officers responsible for aborting the Novembrada coup orchestrated against Juscelino Kubitschek in 1955. Now approaching the end of his career, Denys can look back to his life of accomplishments with pride as someone who did what was necessary when it was necessary to protect his country's independence from foreign and internal threats.
strings.BRA_Milton_Campos_hog_desc:
Vice President
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
For many, Milton Campos is a memory of a time long past. A traditional liberal raised during the old republic, Campos began his political career as a member of the Progressive Party in 1934, but had his ambitions cut soon after, when his mandate was extinct by the New State coup in 1937, forcing him to work as a lawyer for the Caixa Econômica Federal Bank. Campos worked actively with other liberal politicians to end the dictatorship, being elected a deputy in 1950 and governor of Minas Gerais in 1955, his path towards the vice presidency was consolidated.

Campos carries a strong distaste towards Varguism, both for its authoritarian measures and nationalist rhetoric. He instead prefers a cosmopolitan, liberal state similar to the Old Republic. As such, he plans to spend the final years of his political life attempting to move Brazil in the direction of political, social, and economic freedom.
strings.BRA_Alfonso_Arinos_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
Afonso Arinos de Melo Franco is the perfect Brazilian intellectual, having a long academic history beginning in 1927 at Rio's law school, getting his first PhD in Geneva and three more in Montevideo, Paris, and Buenos Aires. Politically speaking, he was one of Brazil's most notorious white supremacists and supporters of eugenics through the 1930s and early 40s, but after seeing the implementation of his beliefs within the Third Reich and the enslavement of Europe, he claimed to have a change of heart and turned into one of Brazil most notorious anti-racist and tropicalist advocates, even formulating the “Afonso Arinos Law” that outlawed racist policies in 1951.

As Quadros' foreign minister, Afonso Arinos devised the plan for an “independent foreign policy”, preaching that Brazil shouldn't be tied to the OFN or other power blocs, but instead follow his own direction in foreign policy, and even establish his own sphere of influence, in some ways distancing himself from the pro-OFN right.
strings.BRA_Artur_da_Silva_Bernardes_Filho_eco_d:
Minister of Finance
Conservatism
--------------
Son of the first Brazilian dictator of the 20th century, Bernardes Filho began his political career through nepotism working as his father's secretary in 1928. Being a supporter of the 1930 revolution, he broke with Vargas and was elected as a deputy in 1934, but had his mandate ended by the New State coup in 1937, resulting in his exile after political protests. In the aftermath of the New State dictatorship, he was elected as a senator for the state of Minas Gerais and supported the “Petróleo é nosso” along with his father during Juscelino's government.

As Quadros' minister of economics, Artur is favorable for balancing the government spending and a responsible economic policy, while also keeping Brazil's economic independence and favoring Quadros' idea of a Christian welfare state.
strings.BRA_Ernesto_Geisel_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
A German-Brazilian, Ernesto Geisel had a very active military life, being a soldier in the 1930 revolution, fighting against the Constitutionalists in 1932, and being friendly to Vargas despite his attempts to assimilate German-Brazilians. During the war he led the 3rd military region in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, being under surveillance for his German heritage. In the aftermath of the revolution, he received American training and became an influential member of the Sorbonne.

Neutral during the coup against Kubitschek, he was trusted by Lott as a diplomat between the Constitutionalists and the Sorbonne, sometimes cooperating with them against the hardliners. Now as Quadros' minister of security, he's prepared to protect Brazil and its democracy against internal threats, be they the hardliners, communists, or fascist scum underground.
strings.BRA_Golbery_do_Couto_e_Silva_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Golbery do Couto e Silva, born in the city of Rio Grande, Rio Grande do Sul, has always been a man of military intellectual thinking. Joining the Military School of Realengo at only age 16, he followed an officer's career to eventually serve as an expeditionary intelligence officer to the United States at the time of the Second World War. Following the conclusion of the war, Golbery continued to ascend the ranks, becoming one of the influential leaders of the Sorbonne faction. Becoming the director of the Escola Superior de Guerra, he now advocates for a modern and technocratic army, promoting the innovation of strategy and technology as a means to strengthen the Exército Brasileiro.
strings.BRA_Vasco_Leitao_da_Cunha_lacerda_for_de:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
Leitão da Cunha is not a man of much ideological preference, having worked under Vargas and now under Lacerda. Having been a diplomat since the 1930s and being the former Brazilian ambassador to the now-defunct Soviet Union, Leitão is content with his position- as long as he has a free hand to do what he wants.

More than anything, what da Cunha wants is a Brazil tied up to the most graceful democratic nation ever born from human strength, the United States of America, the leader of the OFN, the perfect enlightened state to ever grace mankind since its inception, and he shall fight to keep Brazil tied to their interests, as it is their right as they fight for a rightful cause, a cause that Brazil shall fight for, too.
strings.BRA_Helio_Beltrao_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
A devout technocrat, Hélio Beltrão now forms an important part of Brazil's economic planning strategy. Born in 1916, he graduated in law in the university of Rio de Janeiro and found relevance following his term as Rio de Janeiro's planning secretary. Finding his way into the Federal government in a similar position following Lacerda's rise, he hopes to make efforts to deregulate and, more broadly, move the economy of Brazil to the economic right.
strings.BRA_Virgilio_Tavora_hog_desc:
Vice President
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
Even as he reclined in his sleek new residence in Brasília, Virgílio de Morais Fernandes Távora couldn't quite relax. From his moderate uncle, Juarez Távora, the UDN's candidate for the 1955 election, he inherited a sacrosanct duty. He had to make sure the President wasn't lost in his own fantasies.

As Governor of Ceará, he was known for his many construction projects, most of which were only possible because he had the energy and patience to collaborate with the local PSD. With this tendency towards dialogue, he knew he now played an important role in keeping Lacerda in check, ensuring he never forgets he is a mere President, not an emperor.
strings.BRA_Vasco_Leitao_da_Cunha_lacerda_for_an:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Anocracy
--------------
Leitão da Cunha is not a man of much ideological preference, having worked under Vargas and now under Lacerda. Having been a diplomat since the 1930s and being the former Brazilian ambassador to the now-defunct Soviet Union, Leitão is content with his position- as long as he has a free hand to do what he wants.

More than anything, what da Cunha wants is a Brazil tied up to the most graceful democratic nation ever born from human strength, the United States of America, the leader of the OFN, the perfect enlightened state to ever grace mankind since its inception, and he shall fight to keep Brazil tied to their interests, as it is their right as they fight for a rightful cause, a cause that Brazil shall fight for, too.
strings.BRA_Helio_Beltrao_eco_anocracy_desc:
Minister of Finance
Anocracy
--------------
A devout technocrat, Hélio Beltrão now forms an important part of Brazil's economic planning strategy. Born in 1916, he graduated in law in the university of Rio de Janeiro and found relevance following his term as Rio de Janeiro's planning secretary. Finding his way into the Federal government in a similar position following Lacerda's rise, he hopes to make efforts to deregulate and, more broadly, move the economy of Brazil to the economic right.
strings.BRA_Virgilio_Tavora_hog_anocracy_desc:
Vice President
Anocracy
--------------
Even as he reclined in his sleek new residence in Brasília, Virgílio de Morais Fernandes Távora couldn't quite relax. From his moderate uncle, Juarez Távora, the UDN's candidate for the 1955 election, he inherited a sacrosanct duty. He had to make sure the President wasn't lost in his own fantasies.

As Governor of Ceará, he was known for his many construction projects, most of which were only possible because he had the energy and patience to collaborate with the local PSD. With this tendency towards dialogue, he knew he now played an important role in keeping Lacerda in check, ensuring he never forgets he is a mere President, not an emperor.
strings.BRA_Vasco_Leitao_da_Cunha_tavora_for_des:
--------------
Leitão da Cunha is not a man of great ideological principles, having worked under Vargas, Lacerda and now Távora. Ever the flexible diplomat, da Cunha remains within the Brazilian government as its stalwart Minister of Foreign Affairs, maintaining good relations with the only superpower he feels worthy of Brazil's attention.

Following the one-two punches of the General Strikes and the Race Riots, da Cunha has been working overtime to assure the United States of Brazil's commitment to liberal democracy. Having earned a great deal of leeway from the State Department during his previous tenures, Washington remains largely supportive of da Cunha—so long as Brazil continues fighting for the righteous cause.
strings.BRA_Helio_Beltrao_tavora_eco_desc:
--------------
A devout technocrat, Hélio Beltrão feels the descent of former President Lacerda like a knife in his side. Having failed to convince the Brazilian people of deregulation, having failed to help Lacerda suppress the unions during the General Strike, he can only watch as Távora cuts deals with leftist parties and maintains state control over the economy.

Beltrão sits in his office, all his plans locked away in a cabinet, in a vault, where they will languish for a generation or more. He acts as Minister, but he does little more than sign papers and offer criticisms he suspects will go unheeded. And he will replay, again and again, all his missteps and failures, and at his lowest he will see the mirage in the eternal distance, the free market Brazil that he could not bring into being.
strings.BRA_Golbery_do_Couto_e_Silva_tavora_sec_:
--------------
Though he holds some measure of respect for former President Lacerda in his heart, when the time came to remove him from office, Golbery do Couto e Silva did not shy away from his duty. He had failed to resolve the General Strike, and his administration had created the conditions for the Race Riots. Had he been allowed to oversee a third crisis, Couto e Silva and the Sorbonne feared the rise of radical forces.

The Minister of War remains at his post, keeping a watchful eye on Távora. The man seems reasonable enough, willing to compromise to maintain national stability. Yet Couto e Silva keeps a close eye on him. He generally likes what Távora has to say, and he thinks it would be a shame to have to throw out another President.
strings.BRA_Laudo_Natel_hog_desc:
Vice President
Right-Wing Populism
--------------
Often called a prudish zealot, Vice President Laudo Natel hides his genius under false impressions. As common as it is to connect his reactionism with someone behind the times, Natel is technocratic, believing both in self-made men and ordained destiny. Even with many understandably ridiculing this hypocrisy, Natel's competence, as he proved in time, provides the faintest evidence that he might be right.

Although his formal career already showed a diligent networker, Natel excelled as Adhemar's advisor during his governorship in São Paulo. Under his careful watch, the densely populated state underwent an unprecedented economic boom, for which Vargas Junior later took credit. The heir to the Brazilian throne is not an ungrateful man, and he's sure the wily courtier will serve him equally well on the national stage, for he understands a fellow traveler better than any naysayer.
strings.BRA_Vasco_Leitao_da_Cunha_adhemar_for_de:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
Leitão da Cunha is not a man of much ideological preference, having worked under Vargas and now under Adhemar. Having been a diplomat since the 1930s and being the former Brazilian ambassador to the now-defunct Soviet Union, Leitão is content with his position- as long as he has a free hand to do what he wants.

More than anything, what da Cunha wants is a Brazil tied up to the most graceful democratic nation ever born from human strength, the United States of America, the leader of the OFN, the perfect enlightened state to ever grace mankind since its inception, and he shall fight to keep Brazil tied to their interests, as it is their right as they fight for a rightful cause, a cause that Brazil shall fight for, too.
strings.BRA_Benedito_Manhaes_Barreto_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Right-Wing Populism
--------------
An engineer by profession, Benedito Barreto's first major governmental job was as President of the Banco do Brasil during the Washington Luís Presidency. During most of the New State dictatorship, he kept a low political profile working for private banks and firms, finally joining the newly created PSP in 1950.

As Adhemar's minister of economics, a strong supporter of Petrobras and the continuation of the industrialization of Brazil and already possessing some experience on political matters, Barreto's extensive knowledge has allowed him to use Adhemar's influence and corruption to support his plans with more efficiency than he would have under any other President.
strings.BRA_Amaury_Kruel_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Grandson of German immigrants, Amaury Kruel had a very standard career in the Brazilian military, from the Forgotten Revolution in 1924 through the 1930 revolution, the 1932 civil war and World War II, being one of the field commanders of the Expeditionary Force in Britain. In the aftermath of the war Kruel became one of the most inspirational anticommunist and antifascist officers, documenting every suspect from his wide range of informants and ruining the careers of many in the process.

While Kruel has his own ideals, his actions are sometimes driven by the interests of local oligarchs and friendly politicians, having worked with members of the Superior War School on every single coup attempt through the 1950s and 60s. His ministry is seen by many as the antithesis of what Lott planned, promoting the politicization of the army and its cooperation with foreign - especially American - agents.
strings.BRA_Luis_Gonzaga_Novelli_Junior_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Right-Wing Populism
--------------
Just like Adhemar, Luís Gonzaga Novelli Júnior hailed from São Paulo. Just like Adhemar, he graduated in Rio as a doctor. Just like Adhemar, he fought with the Paulistas in 1932. And under Adhemar, he served as vice governor of São Paulo.

After marrying the stepdaughter of a certain Eurico Gaspar Dutra, the old marshal instilled in him the need for law-and-order and good relations with Germany. Together with Filinto Müller, Novelli led a staunchly pro-German faction in the PSP.

Now that the Itamaraty needed someone with a few German contacts, there was no one else in the PSP more obvious a choice than Novelli.
strings.BRA_Tancredo_Neves_hog_desc:
Chief of Staff
National Liberalism
--------------
Tancredo Neves is a very known figure on the Brazilian political scene, eloquent, good natured, optimistic and strongly nationalistic, Neves began his political career in 1935 being elected as a city councillior by the Progressive Party. His mandate was extinct by the New State coup, thus most of the 1940s were spent improving his public image as a reliable lawyer in São Paulo.

The democratisation brought him to the Social Democratic Party, where he became a close ally of Juscelino Kubitschek, having used his connections to garantee the stability between all sections of the government. As a minister of economy Tancredo is a realiable banker who get things done. Sometimes he comments about his future plans to be the President of Brazil, a position that he's cleary capable of exercising with the utmost diligence.
strings.BRA_Edna_Lott_hog_desc:
Vice President
Left-Wing Populism
--------------
Born in 1919, Edna Lott's personality can be explained by the words of Sebastião Nery, “sweet and charismatic, enchanting with her words and her charm.” Coming from a family of strong military tradition, Edna became influential in conservative and progressive women's movements for her work during Lott's presidency, making her a natural big tent female candidate.

In terms of ideals, Edna is an uncompromising supporter of democracy, favorable to civilian supremacy over the army, and a supporter of female participation in politics. If there is anything Edna Lott is known for, however, it's her unquestionable inability to take an insult sitting down.
strings.BRA_Hermes_Lima_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Left-Wing Populism
--------------
To Hermes Lima, politics is like a football game, where someone can start his career on a team and through a series of negotiations move towards the rival team in the future. Beginning his career as a progressive lawyer, Lima was arrested in 1935 after the failed communist coup due to his leftist sympathies, though with the democratization, Hermes jumped through parties until finally joining Vargas' PTB in 1953 through the influence of San Tiago Dantas, eventually becoming labor minister under Lott.

As a foreign minister, Hermes supports Afonso Arinos' ideal of an independent foreign policy, where Brazil won't be shackled by its European and North American masters and instead build its own sphere of influence trading with the Sphere, the Pakt, and OFN for its own gain. It is up to see if his promise can be kept, or if Brazil will remain under the American umbrella for the foreseeable future.
strings.BRA_Celso_Furtado_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Left-Wing Populism
--------------
When Brazilians typically discuss economic policy, most of them think of Celso Furtado. A WWII veteran, Furtado saw some combat stationed in Northern Ireland through most of the war, being recalled after the late Allies' defeat. After serving at various foundations, Furtado was appointed the Minister of Economics of Juscelino Kubitschek, where he established the Plan of Goals and directed his Five Year plan for economic development.

Furtado's objective is to build a great power out of Brazil, comparable to the USA or Japan, a country where the poorest don't suffer from hunger, and the richest don't have to deal with his plans failing, a “patriotic and humane capitalism” if you will. His plans, however, usually hit the wall of reality by not reaching the designed goals and being plagued with the constraints of corrupt government officials and lack of a specialized workforce, but Furtado is adamant that the dream is possible one, and with enough effort, Brazil will be not the country of the future, but the country of the present.
strings.BRA_Argemiro_de_Assis_Brasil_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
A military man through and through, Argemiro de Assis Brasil's career has been fraught with power struggles, revolution, and controversy. Born in 1907 in Canoas, he participated in the Constitutionalist Revolution of 1932 as a Lieutenant; eventually ending in his exile to Portugal for two years after the revolution's defeat. Fearing the growing influence of fascism within Europe affecting Brazil, his fears amplified following the Estado Novo coup only a year after he had been able to return. Now, however, he serves with much greater power - an influential leader of the Brazilian military, he hopes to strengthen the Army's recognition of the legitimacy of the current government, although privately relaying that such a task seems impossible.
strings.BRA_Joao_Goulart_hog_desc:
President of the Chamber of Deputies
Social Republicanism
--------------
Born from a family of Azorian immigrants, João Belchior Marques Goulart was already an adult when Getúlio Vargas chose him as his protégé when Vargas was vacationing in his home state of Rio Grande do Sul in the mid 1940s.

Goulart, called “Jango”, is now working under {leader_name} in the aftermath of his election. He plans to use this position to the best of his ability to improve the lives of the Brazilian people, prop up the economy, and support his own political ambitions, taking pride in Vargas' support for him.
strings.BRA_Francisco_Negrao_de_Lima_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberalism
--------------
Negrão de Lima started his political career as a deputy in 1933, being elected to a higher office in 1935 and later working as Brazil's ambassador to Venezuela in 1941 during the New State dictatorship. A natural ally of Vargas, Negrão worked as governor of Guanabara during Gomes' government and also as Juscelino Kubitschek, minister of Justice.

With the reelection of Juscelino, Negrão got recalled to his job from the Brazilian embassy in Iberia. In his new position he plans to keep to the diplomatic orthodoxy of balancing Brazilian independence with cooperation with the USA, Iberia and other Latin American nations. “Steady as she goes” shall be the operating term of his ministry.
strings.BRA_Roberto_Campos_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
National Liberalism
--------------
Vocally economically right wing and technocratic, Roberto Campos now serves as a vital figure in Kubitschek's economic planning policy. Spending much time in the United States during his education, he developed an affinity for both the United States and the policies that it had developed - fiscal responsibility, prioritizing a balanced budget, and keeping government spending restrained. An ambassador to the United States in the past, Campos hopes to ensure that the Brazilian economy can naturally grow through a stable currency and low interest rates.
strings.BRA_Peri_Constant_Bevilacqua_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
A man of long career, Peri's first great act was helping Augusto Tasso Fragoso to depose Washington Luís during the 1930 Revolution, preventing a civil war. Having worked under Field Marshal Dutra during the early years of the New State, Peri organized the Brazilian defences on the coast in case of a German invasion. In the 1950s he was one of the officers who worked with Lott to prevent the coup that tried to prevent Juscelino Kubitschek from taking power.

Now as Juscelino's minister of security, Peri plans to keep the military in order, the hardliners under control and the Brazilian interests protected from enemies inside and outside.
strings.BRA_Augusto_Frederico_Schmidt_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberalism
--------------
Born on April 18th, 1906 in Rio de Janeiro, Augusto Frederico Schmidt is a very unique figure in President Kubitschek's cabinet. Grandson of the Visconde de Schmidt, one of the richest men in the former Brazilian empire, Schmidt is first and foremost an impresario and an intellectual. Known for his fortune and adventures such as his own line of Bookstores and his very own soccer club, Botafogo. He is, however, mostly known by the Brazilian people for his poetry books of a modernist and melancholic style. His bohemian lifestyle and Modernist ideals quickly brought to his eye the then young Juscelino Kubitschek, of whom he soon became an ardent supporter, a close ally, and close friend.

This would eventually result in him being nominated by JK during his presidency as Brazil's official ambassador in the OFN, and as the presidential Chief Foreign Policy Advisor, where he would be the main architect of JKs Pan American Operation. Now having achieved his long dream of becoming Brazil's very own foreign minister he alongside JK shall work to put Brazil in its rightful place alongside the great powers of the world.
strings.BRA_Pascoal_Ranieri_Mazzilli_hog_desc:
Interim President
Interim Government
--------------
A veteran, Mazzili fought in the Constitutionalist Revolution against Getúlio Vargas in 1932 and later had his first federal level position in 1942 as Director of the National Public Treasury. After democratisation he was elected as a federal deputee by the PSD in 1950 and has been reelected well into Lott's administration.

Now with the country in crisis, Mazzilli is entrusted as Brazil's head of government under Auro de Moura Andrade. Being harmless, he poses no threat to democracy - nor will he be its great savior - instead, he simply spends his days hoping that maybe, by not looking at the problems, they might just go away.
strings.BRA_Auro_de_Moura_Andrade_hog_desc:
President of the Federal Senate
Interim Government
--------------
Member of one of São Paulo's most influential oligarchic families, Auro de Moura Andrade knew what he wanted, and where he was going, since his youth. Having taken a hard stance against Vargas' censorship, both of his newspapers, “A urna” and “O Democrata”, got clausurated for failing to comply with said censorship. Elected to office in 1950, he changed parties between the PTN and the PSD, eventually reaching the position of President of Congress during Lott's government.

Being a great orator, Andrade proudly took it upon himself to announce the military coup that placed Denys on the presidency. Now as his second-in-Command, he expects that after this brief time of political hygienization, civility and the rule of law shall be restored for Brazil, something that HAS to be done, but, in passing thoughts, he begins to feel that maybe he might have done something that's gotten out of hand, of which not even he is safe from.
strings.BRA_Juracy_Magalhaes_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
Juracy's career began in the 1930 Revolution, fighting through the Northeast against Loyalist forces. Being appointed as Governor of Bahia in 1931 and elected in 1934, he kept his position until the New State was established in 1937, which resulted in his resignation and made him turn into a bitter enemy of Vargas. With the definitive end of the dictatorship, he became a founding member of the UDN.

Now, after the military coup, Juracy has been appointed as Minister of the Exterior by General Denys. His diplomatic position is clear from his words: “What is good for the USA is also good for Brazil”, and it reflects the mindset of many under the new government, Brazil shall work along with the Leader of the Free World to protect their shared interests over the Americas.
strings.BRA_Filinto_Muller_hog_desc:
Vice President
Military Junta
--------------
Müller, known as the one “who tortures,” is notorious for his service as the head of Vargas' political police during his reign. Born in 1900, Filinto Müller participated in the Paulista Revolt, expelled after being deemed a deserter. Finding a role in the political and police spheres, he has continually amassed political clout over the course of his career; starting as a harsh police chief, then serving under Vargas as a key architect of the Estado Novo, he was able to gain prominence in the Senate under the PSD after Vargas' demise. Always sympathetic to the German Reich, he frequently uses his influential position in the current regime to drive policy in a pro-German, authoritarian bent.
strings.BRA_Delfim_Netto_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Liberalism
--------------
“Who is Delfim Netto?” was a common reaction when he got appointed as Minister of Finance. Being the Secretary of Planning of São Paulo during the early 1960s, Delfim Netto made enough connections to win Denys' favour, getting appointed to his cabinet after the coup.

Delfim Netto is known for his unholy levels of corruption, cronyism, and for his wide net of connections.
strings.BRA_Siseno_Ramos_Sarmento_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Military Junta
--------------
The son of veterans of the Paraguayan war, Syseno began his military career in 1923, fought for the 1930 Revolution, and helped to suppress the Constitutionalists in 1932 . Despite being an Integralist through the 1930s, he was ironically appointed to lead Brazilian troops in Britain during the Second World War. In the aftermath, he became a very known troublemaker, supporting the coup that tried to prevent Juscelino Kubitschek from taking power in 1955.

Now as the Minister of Security under Costa e Silva, Sarmento also serves as a bridge between Plínio Salgado and the new government, while also trying to guarantee that the recently defeated forces won't try to bring the new government down, something he will kill for in order to prevent.
strings.BRA_Costa_e_Silva_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Military Junta
--------------
Costa e Silva has had a long career, one where his talent has allowed him to rise to the top of the military. He began his military career by entering the Military College of Porto Alegre, where he finished first of his class and commander of the cadet corps. From this moment he slowly rose through the ranks of the military, with only a slight stumble due to this involvement in the 1922 Tenentist rebellion where he was imprionsed for six months. Costa e Silva was finally promoted to general by his ally Eduardo Gomes and was further promoted by President Lott in 1961.

During his career Costa e Silva has developed a few key ideological thoughts. The first was from his close career with the United States, where he briefly trained at. Silva believes Brazil's future remains tied to America and both nations should collaborate against the worlds threats. His second belief, was that the left wing was an ever present danger to Brazil and its way of life.

His final belief, is that it is the military who are the best group to run Brazil and this has made Silva a major figure within the hardliner movement.
strings.BRA_Emilio_Medici_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Military Junta
--------------
The child of immigrants, Médici is nothing if not diligent. This is an adjective demonstrated throughout his career, ever since he worked his way up from being an apt pupil of the Military College of Porto Alegre to becoming a general in 1961, defending Brazil each step of the way. Perhaps it is this loyalty to Brazil that sees him believe in the supremacy of the military over civilian institutions.

Or perhaps it is his close friendship with Artur da Costa e Silva. Nevertheless, unlike many other hardliners, Médici knows when to shut his mouth and when to speak. This endearing characteristic to any potential leader, alongside his extensive connections across the military and supreme work ethic, has neatly landed him in the position of Minister of War within the President's cabinet.
strings.BRA_Pedro_Aleixo_hog_desc:
President of the Chamber of Deputies
Right-Wing Populism
--------------
Quintessentially Mineiro in his ways, Pedro Aleixo was one of the many who went through the traditional pipeline from the School of Law in the University of Minas Gerais into policymaking. A fervorous man at his youth, as the city councilor for Belo Horizonte years ago, he pitched his lot in with the liberal revolutionaries in 1930 and became a part of Mineiro Revolutionary League.

However, just as his career was moving upwards, Vargas' dissolution of the federal congress quickly ruined the ambitions of the young congressman. In disgruntlement, he signed the Mineiros Manifesto and became a founding member of the UDN. Now a jaded old man, he did not expect one of Vargas' lot was returning to power so soon, but perhaps with Natel's and his own influence in the Chamber, he can make it as if this Labourist honeymoon never happened.
strings.BRA_Evandro_Lins_e_Silva_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Progressivism
--------------
A Pernambucanan born in Piauí to a household of law practitioners, Evandro Lins spent his childhood moving around Maranhão and Pernambuco for his father's duty as a municipal judge. When he left for Rio to study law and became a Media Lawyer, he grew more cosmopolitan as he worked with many newspapers throughout the years — until he joined the Order of Attorney Generals in Brazil in 1944.

Although one of the signatories of the Mineiros Manifesto, Evandro Lins found himself leaving the UDN for the PSB as he grew to sympathize with Varguist populism, even once defending the Última Hora against Lacerda in court. Never before a diplomat, he nonetheless believes in his ability to adapt as Foreign Minister and bring about a more independent strategy to Brasília. Yet as many worry, he may still be too afraid and inexperienced to break away from the Great Game.
strings.BRA_Vasco_Leitao_da_Cunha_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
At youth, he once had an ambition to perform theatrics, the Rio native Vasco da Cunha nonetheless had a vivid diplomatic career not dissimilar to that of an actor, and now as Foreign Minister, it is his mission, the culmination of his life's work, to act and save the Brazilian majesty from the Pakt's bottomless malevolence — bringing her back to America's guardianship.

Beginning his career in 1927, he had the chance of being the Second Officer stationed across Lima, Lisbon, and Buenos Aires, and at one point, appointed for peacekeeping in the Chaco. When he was later promoted to First Officer, he earned Vargas's trust and became the interim Justice Minister in 1942, pioneering Brazil's pro-American policies. Since then, he has consistently sided with Osvaldo Aranha's OFN-aligned clique, and so far, there seems to be little reason for that to change.
strings.BRA_Romeu_de_Campos_Vergal_edna_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Social Nationalism
--------------
Originating from an old and locally-influential Coroneis family in São Paulo, Romeu seemed destined to become the iron-minded economist he is today. Spending most of his youth in preparatory schooling befitting his class, he had, at the time, a particular passion for teaching which he made into a decade-long task. However, his entrance into politics was still inevitable, as he was elected a congressman of the Constituent Assembly of São Paulo in 1934 and remained until Vargas' putsch.

During the Estado Novo, Romeu became a consultant for the CEDPEN, the predecessor of Petrobras. As Varguism fell out of favor, Romeu joined Adhemar's PSP and was reelected congressman, around the time founding a nationalist congressional coalition. Now as Economic Minister, it is up to him to consolidate the state's grip on natural resources, while bringing his old love for education to the masses.
strings.BRA_Alfeu_de_Alcantara_Monteiro_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Brought up in Rio Grande do Sul, Alfeu entered Realengo in 1941 before transferring to be educated in aeronautics, where he earned the qualifications of an airman. Despite never having served at the frontlines, during the Second World War, he'd been stationed across the many airfields all across the vast expanses of Brazil. After the war, he was promoted to Senior Lieutenant out of seniority and has since then instructed B-25 bombers in Natal's air base.

Called upon to the duty of Security Minister for his non-ideological stance towards the PTB, contradictory to almost all of his contemporaries, Alfeu has long despised the treacherous politics within the Air Force. Now with the tools to enact his will, perhaps it's high time to instill some respect to the constitutional order, no matter how free-willed pilots may be.
strings.BRA_Ignacio_Rangel_eco_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Ignácio Rangel, coming from a lineage of Maranhense legal practitioners, embraced leftist militancy as a teenager after reading extensively on Marx as a bookish young lad. In 1935, influenced by his magistrate father's anti-government stance, the 21-year-old PCB activist joined Prestes' rebellion, landing in a São Luís jail before being moved to Rio, where he founded a reading club with a couple other inmates.

Released back to Maranhão in 1937, Rangel worked as a writer for the Conference of Productive Classes during Vargas' Estado Novo. A meeting in Rio with Rômulo Almeida led him to Vargas' economic advisory, where he curated national projects such as Petrobras and Eletrobrás before becoming the Economic Chief for the BNDE. Now serving again in Lott's administration, he sees a future most grim — a hyperinflation crisis only preventable by Agrarian Reform beyond empty promises.
strings.BRA_Rubens_Paiva_hog_desc:
Vice President
Progressivism
--------------
The fact that PTB grandee Rubens Paiva, of opposing political stripes, of opposing opinions and even opposing personalities, must share the Planalto Palace with a conservative President must seem like a strange arrangement. That would be because it is, but as the saying goes, a bad agreement is better than a good fight.

Paiva has not been known to make friends to the right of him: a furious supporter of the student movement in his university days and Vargas' nationalization campaign, his Chamber of Deputies speeches had much and yet little of it good to say about Germany's man Adhemar, or the coup apologist Lacerda. Nonetheless, with few remaining colleagues to his left in the workplace, he will have to try to work together with them, or bear the weight of failure alone.
strings.BRA_Jose_Richa_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
The youngest Minister of Finance since the Proclamation of the Republic and a son of Lebanese immigrants, José Richa, at the age of 36, is truly an unlikely story in Brazil's political history. Many a President would fear they have appointed a liability in this case, but not Ney Braga, who has confided in one of his staunchest Christian Democrats to steer Brazil's economy away from the abyss.

What he lacks in political veteranship, he makes up for in his voraciousness in all things economics, particularly agronomics. He may thus have his strong opinions, but his time in Brasília has also equipped him with an instinct for moderation and compromise. And there will need to be compromise - for this crisis, the nation will need all its limbs to get out.
strings.BRA_Ernesto_Geisel_Braga_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Being in charge of the Ministry of War, as much as the name implies otherwise, is as much about the military as it is about order. In that, however, Ernesto Beckmann Geisel is a more than suitable pick. A leader of the Sorbonne wing of the armed forces, with values of discipline inculcated from his Lutheran upbringing to his rise as one of the nation's senior generals, his approach to his new job is simple: follow the rules.

But then, even the state's policeman has his principles. If it is believed by his friends in the barracks of the nation that the government is not fit for purpose, his arm might get twisted in the wrong direction, and it will be much more than the rules he has sworn to that might get broken. A man you can trust, but beware, for as with any military man, trust comes with many conditions.
strings.BRA_Magalhaes_Pinto_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Christian Conservatism
--------------
There are few who know their own value like José de Magalhães Pinto. Blacklisted in 1943 from his old banking career as a co-signatory of the Manifesto dos Mineiros, he was a UDN federal deputy in two years and the mouthpiece of the Bossa Nova faction decades later. Needless to say, he has learned much about the game of musical chairs from the countless switches in careers and posts, and consequently no longer just speaks for a party faction, but for Brazil on the world stage.

His notorious views on the state might seem to make him incapable of the soft touch that the Itamaraty Palace might require. Far from it: once the papers reach his desk, it is pure pragmatism that wins his vote of confidence. After all, a wise decision must leave some people unhappy. One must be careful dealing with Magalhães Pinto: from the very first phone call, all bets are off.
strings.BRA_Magalhaes_Pinto_hog_raphael_desc:
Vice President
Christian Conservatism
--------------
The fast-thinking radical of the liberal coalition that is the UDN, Magalhães Pinto is the very idea of hardline nationalism manifest. After being blacklisted from his banker job for signing the famous Manifesto dos Mineiros, Pinto became a full-time politician and climbed the ranks into becoming the UDN's federal deputy in two year's time. Excellent in the game of musical chairs, he had played both allies and enemies to many of his colleagues, and now, his expert maneuvering has paid off as he sits in the Planalto alongside young Raphael.

While many doubt his controversial views will do any good in the second most public office of Brazil, Pinto is a man who knows what he is looking for in everything. Despite taking the authority of Vice Presidency, he will remain the pragmatist as always, waiting for the mice to tire themselves out before striking them down.
strings.BRA_Oscar_Dias_Correia_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
Modernity is sobering for many folks — for either its oppressiveness or unfamiliarity. But Oscar Dias Correia sees no so-called “hegemony of the capital” as an impediment to becoming the Minister of Finance. If anything, Correia's acumen for working within the institution propelled his public career and, perhaps more importantly, made him an honored chair within the Academy of Letters, which the one-time author is not afraid of flaunting.

A veteran of the UDN for decades, Correia is a self-proclaimed “anti-socialist.” As he once worked under Vice President Pinto's governorship of Minas Gerais as the Secretary of Education, Correia is still a grandiose man. In his mind, Brazil's crises are entirely solvable under the free market's tenets. Whether this dogmatism may be the nation's saving grace remains to be seen, for if it proves a misconception, his legacy shall be marred eternally.
strings.BRA_Jurandyr_De_Bizarria_Mamede_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Since the beginning of mankind, those most inclined to handling the brass had never been the ones most benign or amicable, and a man driven by a cause which he would die for makes the best of commanders. Jurandyr de Bizarria Mamede was one of those grunts who stood for the anti-Varguist cause even during the peak of Kubitschek and Vargas' command. Nowadays, in Lacerda's stance of taking Brazil into an opposite direction from gutless populism, he has become the Minister of War, both against intrusion and subversion.

Arguably a key figure who brought about Lott's ascendency, Mamede is no brainless brute either, yet he knows no restraint in championing for righteousness. The very general who hollered about deposing Kubitschek in a funeral will likely prove an indispensable, yet uncontainable political asset.
strings.BRA_Juracy_Montenegro_Magalhaes_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Liberal Conservatism
--------------
A former military man and the one-time governor of Bahia, Juracy Magalhães is a proper tenentista who stood by Vargas when he reigned undisputed, and has now obtained a seat as the Minister of Foreign Affairs in Raphael's gilded elite circle. He was one of those moderates who aligned with the Varguists in hopes of ending the oligarchy of the Republicans, and eventually, became known as one of the Estado Novo's finest in suppressing the Integralists.

Nowadays, Magalhães has become the figurehead of the centrist “Realistas” bloc within the UDN, bringing along an amenable strategy into party politics and pushing for a strengthened alliance with the United States. Ultimately, against the accusations he'd received from the far-right for being a “foreign bootlicker”, he does not see himself as any kind of traitor. For if anything, Brazil can only survive the Cold War with her good allies.
strings.BRA_Romeu_de_Campos_Vergal_vargas_jr_eco:
Minister of Finance
Right-Wing Populism
--------------
Varguism is a foregone faith that becomes rarer every day with the liquidation of old guards. Romeu Vergal, as one of its final stewards, maintains no delusion of reviving an ember that has no place in the contemporary PSP. Although Vargas Junior had sidelined most populist influences from his father's era, somehow Vergal remained a player within the government as a dead man walking. One salmon cannot swim against the current, and he becomes the Minister of Finance with the knowledge of this grim parable.

Vergal never endorsed the degenerate individualism that has now corrupted the Brazilian spirit, and perhaps his new post is the merciful euthanization of this age past. Recognizing his comrades either gone compromising or left in shallow graves, Vergal is not just himself close to retirement — he is emblematic of a disappearing breed of men formed by idealism and vigor.“
strings.BRA_Filinto_Muller_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
As Trujillo had the caliés and Hitler had the SS, Filinto Müller is Brazil's most influential sanctioned thug. Born a German, Müller's career began when he engaged in the São Paulo revolt of 1924. As expected, Müller promptly deserted when the tide turned against the mutineers. Later on, as his military life grew into the Vargas presidency, he became Rio's Chief of Police, which quickly turned a bloody affair under the dictatorial regime.

For a decade, Müller earned a name as the 'executioner' of the Estado Novo, ordering the arrests of any suspected communist elements, as well as enforcing the antisemitic measures of the regime. Those days are long behind, however, and today, his reputation does not precede an aging body and declining cognition. No one celebrates a butcher appointed the Minister of War, but who is more reflective of Brazil's rotten realities than PSP's dying tiger?
strings.BRA_Luis_Gonzaga_Novelli_Junior_for_varg:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Right-Wing Populism
--------------
Getúlio Vargas was always accused of fascistic tendencies; the experience of the Estado Novo clung to the man's reputation like a shroud which he could not (or perhaps did not want to) take off. Many preferred to repudiate the prospect, but there were some who embraced the reputation regardless of the hit to personal prestige or political influence. Minister of Foreign Affairs Luís Novelli Júnior is just such a man.

The Foreign Affairs Minister admires order and hierarchy above all else—and looks to Germany for a model thereof. He looks, therefore, to distance himself from the American juggernaut of hedonism and individualistic disorder in small steps. While avoiding retaliation to the best of his ability, Novelli Júnior aims for an independent Brazil adopting at least some of the ideals of the triumphant Reich.
strings.BRA_Ulysses_Guimaraes_hog_desc:
Vice President
National Liberalism
--------------
Ulysses Silveira Guimarães has always bound himself to act as a defender of the rule of law, free elections, and other similarly important democratic mores. Today, above all else, that attitude is crucial—for Guimarães finds himself deputy to an executive power that is under siege.

Guimarães does not like this juxtaposition, not one bit. An arch-democrat subordinate to a volatile, authoritarian quasi-fascist trying to create an “integral” republic and demolish all that his predecessors slaved away to achieve? This cannot be borne. Small wonder, then, that there are rumours of a civilian democratic conspiracy.
strings.BRA_Santiago_Dantas_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Integralism
--------------
San Tiago Dantas travelled to several political homes after the first demise of integralism. He found himself among the Trabalhistas for a long while, and spent a long time militating for a “positive” leftism against what he called the negative left led by Brizola. But Dantas felt that the man was gaining too much influence, and in any case Salgado had just been elected president—so he rekindled his old acquaintances and was abruptly made Minister of Foreign Affairs. “Probably because Salgado's deputies would manage to insult a brick wall,” Dantas snarks to himself.

Dantas seeks an anti-capitalist and anti-socialist way forward, adhering to his own version of the PEI—Independent External Politics—theory to render Brazil a more powerful and most importantly neutral actor on the world stage. This theory appeals to Salgado, which is why they have a good rapport. But the Foreign Minister has colleagues in the more mainstream parties whose opinion he also very much values. Dantas wants the Executive Power to watch itself in respect to foreign affairs, avoiding unilaterally doing things of which Dantas may not approve.
strings.BRA_Jose_Alkmin_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Despotism
--------------
A backstabber and opportunist par excellence, José Maria Alkmin is trusted by very few people. There are those that have complained that it is better to have God himself as an enemy than Alkmin as a friend. Undeterred by disgust or popular distaste, Alkmin stabbed one person after another in the back. Eventually enough people fell over thus that Alkmin was finally able to see his plans come true—but in such a disgusting manner? Perhaps God has in fact gone to war with him, Alkmin muses.

What sort of merit or dignity is there in serving as minister of finance under a crazed, unpredictable man with a hodgepodge ideology and a fanatical, violent mob adhering to his every word? The Minister of Finance obsesses about the permanency of his position, and is prepared to return straight to his usual norms to keep it.
strings.BRA_Magalhaes_Pinto_hog_neves_desc:
Vice President
Christian Conservatism
--------------
It is well known that Magalhães Pinto, despite his many talents, is not a man to be trusted. A consummate politician, he is adept at making friends and building influence - and just as quickly betraying them and spending it. A native of Minas Gerais and prominent critic of the Vargas regime, he was a prominent signatory of the Mineiro Manifesto, heralding the fall of the Estado Novo. A longtime peer and political competitor of Neves, Pinto even defeated him in the 1960 Minas Gerais gubernatorial election - and yet now finds himself subordinate. Though outwardly conciliatory on the outside, his new position makes it clear that Neves well understands the maxim about keeping enemies close.
strings.BRA_Sebastiao_Almeida_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
National Liberalism
--------------
A longtime figure in the Kubitschek administration, first as the head of the Banco do Brasil and later as the Governor of Minas Gerais, Sebastião Paes de Almeida is a PSD loyalist, well-known dealmaker, an industrial expert, and a staunch proponent of state stimulus spending. Agreed upon as the natural choice for the Finance Ministry in the Neves cabinet, his long experience in financial matters nonetheless will be well challenged. The ongoing effects of the Oil Crisis weigh heavy on Brazil, and past missteps regarding inflationary controls have given rise to a growing body of critics.
strings.BRA_Euler_Monteiro_sec_desc:
Minister of War
National Liberalism
--------------
Many consider Euler Bentes Monteiro to be a man inextricably bound to the ghost of Vargas. He was there in 1945, removing the dictator. He was there in 1950 to oppose Vargas upon his return. He signed the Manifesto dos Coronéis to oppose Vargas' attempts to double the minimum wage, causing the downfall of the then-Minister for Labor, João Goulart. And now he finds himself the Minister of War in the Cabinet of the man who was once Vargas' Minister of Justice. A staunch nationalist, he was among the earliest proponents of oil nationalization and the creation of Petrobras, and though he may have personal conflicts with Naves, all would agree that for Montiero the stability of Brazil is, was, and always will be first in thought and deed.
strings.BRA_Jose_Rodrigues_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
National Liberalism
--------------
An unexpected, but by no means unknown, pick for the Foreign Affairs Ministry, José Honório Rodrigues is a well-known and flamboyant figure, devoted just as much to the Flamengo football club as he is to his careful knowledge of history. A Rockefeller scholar to Columbia University during the war, he rapidly ascended the ranks of the National Library of Brazil, quickly becoming the director of the National Archives. A pioneer in the field of Brazilian historiography, a frequent contributor to the Jornal do Brasil (with a well-known anti-UDN perspective), and possessing a noted interest in exploring Brazil's links to Africa, he was personally selected by Neves as a 'perfect' candidate for the position.
strings.BRA_Darcy_Riberio_hog_desc:
Vice President
National Liberalism
--------------
A native of Minas Gerais who'd moved to São Paulo to pursue fame and prominence — Darcy Ribeiro was an anthropologist by trade. Joining the world of public services as an ethnologist for the SPI, one of his early achievements was the opening of the Museu Nacional do Indio in 1953, the crowning jewel of his myriad of works concerning decolonization. His dedication to his craft was rewarded by Juscelino Kubitschek when he was invited alongside his friend, Anísio Teixeira, to found the University of Brasília.

Although not much of a political adventurist, Ribeiro has become captivated by Leonel Brizola's nationalist methods, which prompted his decision to advance through the PTB hierarchy. Now nominated as the Vice President, although comparatively inexperienced, Ribeiro is motivated by nothing but a selfless desire to aid the president in shaping Brazil's future properly.
strings.BRA_Romulo_Almeida_eco_desc:
Minister of Finance
Reformist Socialism
--------------
Industry is a gift that few can master, and the Bahian Rômulo Almeida found himself the rare ones given such a privilege. A law graduate who had moved to Rio, young Rômulo was immediately enamored by economics despite his unrelated qualifications. Under similar circumstances, he was also introduced into politics by a friend — whose influence had made him a lifelong nationalist.

Having gone from a socialist to an AIB agitator, Rômulo had been arrested during Vargas' regime like many Integralists. However, in 1945, the President chose to invite the autodidact into the position of economic advisor in CHESF Electrics. Shortly after the dictatorship's end, he returned to the political world and joined the PSF as a congressman — advocating for developmentalism and self-sufficiency, the same values which he hopes to bring to the impoverished North now as Economic Minister.
strings.BRA_Oromar_Osario_sec_desc:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Well-respected for his command over both the living and the machine, Oromar Osório was the commander of the 1st Cavalry Division in Rio Grande do Sul since 1961. Coming from Rio, the good-hearted general has been an open supporter of Brizola throughout the fledgling politician's entire career, being one of the few providing him endorsement during his tenure as governor.

Appointed out of both the prestige he wields and political loyalty, Osório sees his peers progressively more disaffected by Brizola's plans of radical military reforms. Between the collapse of national unity and retaining the regressive methods of the Brazilian Armed Forces, he shall be the president's whip to enforce constitutional order upon his more unruly colleagues.
strings.BRA_Azeredo_da_Silveira_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
National Liberalism
--------------
Like many other scions of political dynasties, Azeredo de Silveira was born with one foot in the playing fields of Brasília, his father a congressman for Mato Grosso and Guanabara, and his grandfather a senator. While regional politics was his family's expertise, Azerado, the rebellious fifth child of seven, chose to pursue the unconventional profession of diplomacy. Entering the international world stationed in Argentina during Vargas' final days, he had a stint in Japan when Gomes came to power.

A pariah opposed to the Itamaraty's rigid pro-American approach, Azeredo believes in the swaying force of Brazil's geopolitical potential. Although seen by many contemporaries as too “soft” against the Argentinians, it remains undoubted that he has realized the nation must go beyond being a pawn in America's games, even if it means warming up to Tokyo and Buenos Aires.
strings.BRA_Ulysses_Guimaraes_edna_hog_desc:
Vice President
National Liberalism
--------------
Ulysses Silveira Guimarães has always bound himself to act as a defender of the rule of law, free elections, and other similarly important democratic mores. Today, above all else, that attitude is crucial—for Guimarães finds himself deputy to an executive power that is under siege.

Guimarães is happy that Edna is in power. Despite being more centrist himself, he admires her ideas. There is fear, though: he knows that there are any number of lunatics that do not share that admiration and might threaten Edna's position. Though Edna's military relatives and loyalists may defend her, their work may not suffice; the jackals of degenerate radicalism are always ready to try and maim the President. So Ulysses braces himself for impact and gets back to work, forever ready to act as a shield of democracy.
strings.BRA_Tancredo_Neves_edna_eco:
Minister of Finance
National Liberalism
--------------
Tancredo de Almeida Neves, a born diplomat, relies on moderation and compromise above all else. It is for this reason that the Varguist coalition respects him as a nonpareil political operator. His financial knowledge, on the other hand, is unmatched by most outside of economics faculties. It made sense to the PSD-PTB coalition, then, that Edna appointed Tancredo Minister of Finance.

Tancredo's remit is straightforward only in theory. The economic crisis must be solved, and the rocky financial landscape bedeviling all levels of society and business must be smoothed out. Brazil's economy must return to normality, if not to prosperity. Tancredo hopes, as does Edna, that a moderate course will bring that about.
strings.BRA_Peri_Constant_Bevilacqua_edna_sec:
Minister of War
Despotism
--------------
Any army being attacked on all fronts will know that what it needs above all else is good defense. For Edna Lott's encumbered cabinet, that job goes to Peri Bevilacqua, who takes charge not only of defending the nation, but also the government from his fellow military brass: sure enough, the vultures already seem to be circling overhead.

General Constant Bevilacqua, a no-nonsense Constitutionalist yet artillery general who fought in Europe all those years ago, has his work cut out for him as Minister of War: an administration with such an abundance of enemies has left the more radical wing of the armed forces smelling blood. He must find that their love of country outsizes their love of power, or it will be on his watch that the khaki green swarms flood Brasília to take it for themselves, just as they have always been itching to do.
strings.BRA_Hermes_Lima_edna_for:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Left-Wing Populism
--------------
Like many senior politicians before him, Hermes Lima is a former legal professional who has now transferred his power to interpret into power to lead. In his case, this will mean leading the public relations campaign that is Brazilian foreign relations, and thus he will become President Edna Lott's diplomat in chief and key contact overnight.

However, he is unlikely to be a pioneer of very much else. A fierce opponent of the Estado Novo and equipped with mildly socialist or rather humanistic instincts, Lima's true convictions are on human rights and the law which he has seen abrogated so unjustly for so long. What will come of many of Mrs. Lott's new appointments is not yet known, but with Lima it may as well be: following the script and reading it tactfully, with only vague pretences of the greater good.
strings.BRA_progressivism_party_long:
Partido Trabalhista Brasileiro
--------------
When Vargas founded the Brazilian Labor Party as “a buffer between the unions and the Communists,” the PTB would find itself the leading defender of workers' rights. Members range from populist reformists who seek nationalization and sweeping agrarian reform, to social-democratic intellectuals who try to moderate the party's centralizing tendencies. Between them, there are also many dedicated Varguists tied to union bureaucracy and the civil service. Uniting them all is the constant struggle against capitalist oppression and the belief in democracy to create a truly egalitarian Brazil.
strings.BRA_liberalism_party_long:
Partido Social Democrático
--------------
Founded by Vargas's own appointees, the Social Democratic Party remains deeply tied to the establishment and receives much of its support from the agrarian oligarchy, businesses, and the middle class. While populist and pragmatic, the party is mostly united by its moderate developmentalist platform and its stalwart defense of democratic freedoms. However, divisions emerge within its ranks between those who long to continue regular collaboration with its long-time ally and Varguist sister party, the PTB, and those who seek to make further inroads with the right-wing opposition party, the UDN.
strings.BRA_liberal_conservatism_party_long:
União Democrática Nacional
--------------
As long as there have been Varguists, there have been anti-Varguists. Out from the political currents that opposed the Estado Novo dictatorship sprang the National Democratic Union. Since then, the UDN has been committed to the defense of morality against encroaching totalitarianism, believing in the American model of democracy and the OFN's efforts against fascism. While some pragmatic members prefer cooperation with the PSD on its developmentalist approach, the UDN is also home to supporters of classical liberal economics and firmly believe in Brazil's ability to have a free robust economy.
strings.BRA_conservatism_2_party_long:
União Democrática Nacional - Lacerdaists 
--------------
As long as there have been Varguists, there have been anti-Varguists. Out from the political currents that opposed the Estado Novo dictatorship sprang the National Democratic Union. Since then, the UDN has been committed to the defense of morality against encroaching totalitarianism, believing in the American model of democracy and the OFN's efforts against fascism. While some pragmatic members prefer cooperation with the PSD on its developmentalist approach, the UDN is also home to supporters of classical liberal economics and firmly believe in Brazil's ability to have a free robust economy.
strings.BRA_paternalism_party_long:
Partido Social Progressista
--------------
What is unique about the Social Progressive Party's vague populist agenda is that corruption is an accepted reality. While conservative at its core, the party is willing to ally with anyone across the political spectrum, using bribes and under-the-table deals to maintain stable relationships with other parties and the military. Within the party, there also runs a pro-Reich undercurrent, coupled with skepticism of American influence, arising from German-Brazilian voters and some members' personal ties to the Nazis. The PSP is the party of pragmatism, laying bare the political machinations of Brazil.

strings.BRA_mosquito.1.desc:
Odílio Denys tapped onto his chin lightly, somewhat phased from the talks occurring before and around him. He paid much attention, not allowing himself to be completely disconnected from the matter at hand, but not actively participating in the pointless murmurs and whispers traveling around the table. Though he knew he had to launch himself in.

Amidst the chatter stood men like Costa e Silva, General Kruel and Frota, and some air force officers he could barely recognize, apart from Burnier. Scanning the different faces among the room, he finally lifted his voice, “We will allow Goulart one of two choices,” the room fell dead silent, all men moving their heads to meet Denys' gaze at the head of the table.

“He will be allowed to either flee the country,” he gave a short pause, tasting some of the meeting standard mineral water at his disposal, “Or capture him on his arrival to Brasília, while he plans to drive the PTB to his side.”

No one voiced any opposition. Only bobbing and nodding heads, technical speech and operational inquiries occupied the room as the officers schemed and planned while under the guidance of Denys' watchful eye. As the scheming was done and the day came to rest, Denys uttered one last sentence before taking his leave.
strings.BRA_mosquito.2.desc:
Brizola almost launched himself forward to grasp unto Jango's arm, “You will be captured, or worse, killed!” he mustered, giving a true attempt to stop his friend from running straight on into the lion's jaw. Jango, however, only shook his head reassuringly, switching the bag from his left hand to the right only so he could give Brizola a pat on the back.

“I must leave for Brasília. To fight for the presidency, to fight for freedom, and democracy. If I cannot do it, then what can we expect from Brazil?” Goulart queried, giving another repeated back to his comrade. In response, Brizola pressed his hands unto his face anxiously, “You could always prepare against the fight in Rio Grande do Sul, Jango. When the coup comes, it will be most safe...”

“I must go no matter the cost,” he interrupted, taking his bag with both hands, “If I am arrested, though, I will need my family taken care of, and Edna safely transported to Uruguay. Our fate rests in her hands should I be unable to.”

The brothers-in-law embraced each other then, a final goodbye as the speaker called for all passengers to board their planes. The South would be unguarded by Jango now, Goulart knew, and with all his force he could only muster one last prayer.
strings.BRA_mosquito.3.desc:
“Like a mouse to cheese,” Denys snickered to himself, his lonely abode inhabited only by fellow military personnel or caffeine addicted politicians arriving early before work hours. Soon enough, Jango Goulart would rest easily into his palm, with the SNI and some of his Armed Forces men awaiting his arrival at the airport to finally capture him.

Though Denys had little time to celebrate, as a young army officer stormed into his room unannounced, panting and puffing air, allowing little time for the General to ask his purpose as he held up an envelope, “You must read this, Senhor Denys!”

The envelope was practically thrown onto his desk, and before he could scold the officer's indecent behavior his jaw dropped as his eyes skimmed through the contents of the letter. He could barely believe his eyes, standing to give the words another read, and yet another, repeatedly, as his hand collided against his head in a desperate attempt to comprehend.

“Dead... in the wreckage of his plane. Crashed... How can this be?” stuttered Denys, his eyes so fixated on the document he barely noticed the presence of Costa e Silva. “Senhor Denys,” Silva muttered, finally speaking up, “I've seen what's happened.”

Denys perked his furrowed brows unto Silva, an increasing ache of rage making him almost tumble and drop onto his desk, “Do you have anything to do with this, Silva?” Denys asked, remaining respectful though adorned with a stern tone, “How would you know this quick, hm? Is there something I must know?”

Though Silva was known as conniving, and a man of little honesty, it was most likely in that moment that for the first time in his life he meant something in most truth, “I have no knowledge of this unfortunate event, Senhor Denys. I do not know...”
strings.BRA_mosquito.3.a: “Out of my office, I need to think.”
strings.BRA_mosquito.4.desc:
Denys was nearly fuming at the mouth, controlling himself from a tantrum still as he processed Jango's death. It was not discussed. He was to be kept alive, arrested when he arrived at the airport, not shot down out of the sky by some fighter jet to level him into the ground and ensure his death. Sure, it could put an end to some immediate issues, but it made everything worse in the long run.

Lott's daughter has fled to Uruguay, giving some crippling speeches about Brazil's government, and then dematerialized to Cuba to do whatever it may be. The USA loses confidence rapidly in an impressive show of cold feet, and resistance to the government becomes increasingly more apparent, to proportions larger than expected.

Costa e Silva gave his grandiose inauguration feast, surely one to remember, if only Denys had been paying enough attention. Instead, he was wandering his own thoughts. Which pilot could have done the shoot down? Most likely the air force covering up their tracks to protect one of their own, being prone to hide the truth when in times of such need. That will be an issue for Silva to resolve.

Silva stood down from the dais, and walked to shake the hand of a plethora of military officials, politicians and legislators all celebrating the jubilation of a new President. Silva said nothing when grasping onto Denys' hand, shaking it intently while a smile of content rested upon his face. That moment, Denys couldn't hold it any longer.

He was too old for politics. He had served well, very well, and deserved now some time to rest alone and in peace until death came to take its price. He wanted to retire to a beach, yes. Perhaps not too far from Rio, close enough to hot beaches covered in yellow sand, but far enough from tourist-ridden cities which bothered the scenery he would enjoy.
strings.BRA_mosquito.4.a: An epoch comes to an end.
strings.BRA_mosquito.5.desc:
Her father was right. Politics are just like a pool full of crocodiles with sharp teeth, waiting to feed on innocent men who simply wanted change seen in the home they loved. She was determined to ensure the lives of those innocent men were not lost in vain, but first, she had to step onto the stage.

Edna gave her best attempt to shield her anger, though her face still showed blushes of red that gave away her blood melting rage. The American journalists had asked her a few questions, most of which were about her life and career, though one risky pretender approached with a very peculiar inquiry.

“What do you make of the situation in Brasília?” the reporter asked, with a pen and notebook at the ready. Edna had to give it some time to sink in, though the answers came flowing out with little forethought as a machine gun with live ammunition.

“The death of Jango Goulart is possibly the worst thing to happen to Brazil. Murdered by its dictatorial oppressors, his legacy is left in shambles and his work unfinished. Though I remain, and with me the opportunity of a future for Brazil. As his Vice-President, it is pertinent for me to reinforce the fact that the current government is completely illegitimate and no rightful President resides in office.”

The questions rained after the comment, with increasing interest from the Journalists who simply could not have enough. It mattered little if those who questioned her for being a woman, it was time to rid Brazil of the political crocodiles preying for its democracy, one small step at a time.
strings.BRA_oil_crisis_tt: This will have disastrous effects on our economy...
strings.BRA_nuclear_security_leak_tt:
Our careless handling of the secrecy of our project has led to disaster, Argentina is furious and all of our supporters have pulled their aid from our program. We will have to lay low for a while now...

Our Nuclear Progress will decrease by 30%.
strings.BRA_sacw_nuclear_tooltip: Argentina's aggressive behaviour shows they can not be trusted. The only way to prevent war is to build the atomic bomb, before the Argentinians can. God Speed Senhor Presidente.
strings.BRA_deforestation.1.desc:
Maniwa stood knee deep in the water. His eyes were tired yet here he still stood looking for a sign of movement in the murky water. Every day it seemed like the water was murkier and the fish were fewer. Every day. In the swirling mud at least he could find a moment of respite. Things had started to look up. He barely remembered the measles outbreak that so reduced his tribe but he could see the hurt on his mother's face still. There had been days where he had caught a bounty of fish. Those days however seemed long gone. The hardship she had known he was coming to know.

It started with the tractors, the power lines and bunkhouses. The boots and the workers. They were building a highway. Politicians had said it would be a life giving artery but here he was with no catch to feed his family. As he walked forlorn back to his village with a single fish in hand he looked at the treeline. It had been retreating year on year and now he could see the beasts roaming the now dead forest. Brown, grazing every so often. He wondered where all that meat went.
strings.BRA_deforestation.1.a: As the fish retreat the cows come home.
strings.BRA_deforestation.2.desc:
Year on year, month on month like a wave receding the trees fell back. The lands only they had known became known to others and unknown to them. All that remained lay separated from their world by a single stream and there were already makeshift bridges and scouting parties threatening to push even further.
