strings.BRA_gp_balance_meter_psd_leaning_tt: The Conselho do Desenvolvimento is leaning toward PSD members.
strings.BRA_gp_balance_meter_ptb_unbalanced_tt: The Conselho do Desenvolvimento is very unbalanced, leaning heavily toward PTB members. This could prove disastrous to the coalition!
strings.BRA_gp_balance_meter_psd_unbalanced_tt: The Conselho do Desenvolvimento is very unbalanced, leaning heavily toward PSD members. This could prove disastrous to the coalition!
strings.BRA_lacerda_coup_category_description:
The serpent-tongued João Goulart somehow secured enough votes to become President. This cannot stand.

Lacerda will need to secure sufficient support among the £BRA_mil_support Military and £BRA_govt_support Government. To ensure things go over smoothly, he will also need sufficient £BRA_voter_apathy Apathy among the Voters, and must convince the £BRA_us_backing United States to back his plan.

Lacerda must acquire 10 points in all measures or Goulart may just have room to outmaneuver him...
strings.BRA_init_lacerda_mechanic: Decisions are now available to respond to Goulart's election...
strings.BRA_coalition_partners_abandon_UDN:
£BRA_govt_support Government Support: +4

Our partners in the PR, PDC, PTN, and PL will abandon Lacerda and the coalition

They will face consequences in due time...
strings.BRA_lacerda_timeout_tt: We should be ready to take action before João Goulart can assume the Presidency
strings.BRA_lacerda_ask_mil_desc: While some in Brazil's military are driven by ideology, many are just looking to make a career. By promising a nice bonus to key officers, Lacerda can ensure their support for his plot.
strings.BRA_lacerda_help_anticom_desc: The armed forces in Brazil have been historically anti-communist, and many in the Hardliner faction carry on this proud tradition. These officers will recognize Goulart for what he is: a communist bent on destroying Brazil.
strings.BRA_lacerda_ask_govt_desc: In order to make his move, Lacerda needs his own party to stand firmly behind him. By hosting important party functions, he can solidify his identity as the leader of the UDN.
strings.BRA_lacerda_bend_the_knee: Make the Senado Bend the Knee
strings.BRA_lacerda_bend_the_knee_desc: Brazil's legislature may on occasion offer token opposition to the President, but its true role is to enact his will. Lacerda will ensure the loyalty of the Senado, at any cost.
strings.BRA_lacerda_bend_the_knee_tt:
Lacerda will call a meeting and wrangle the UDN coalition, increasing Government Support.
Traitors and cowards may abandon the UDN.
strings.BRA_lacerda_ask_voter_desc: There are certain to be some irregularities in the election results that Lacerda can use to put Goulart's victory into question.
strings.BRA_lacerda_confuse_media_desc: Lacerda knows how to manipulate the media, and in this situation they are rife for exploitation. Sending conflicting statements to opposing papers, fabricating sources, and publishing disinformation will take the steam out of Goulart's victory.
strings.BRA_lacerda_ask_usa_desc: During his short stint in office, Lacerda developed close relationships to several members of the US State Department. Surely he can get a few of them on his side.
strings.BRA_lacerda_resource_concessions_desc: In dealing with Americans, a fistful of dollars will do what a handshake won't. Lacerda will dial up business leaders likely to have the ear of those in power, promising discounted prices on mineral deposits across Brazil in exchange for a kind word.
strings.BRA_lacerda_usa_torch_tt_delay: During his brief stint as President, Lacerda has made it a priority to build close ties with the United States and OFN more broadly. Now, he must secure the US's Backing for his plot to overturn Goulart's illegitimate election.
strings.BRA_lacerda_mil_torch_tt_delay: It was the military's intervention that allowed Lacerda to reach the Presidency during the Hundred Days Crisis. Lacerda must rely on them again to keep him there. While arguments about legitimacy may be traded, it is whoever has the Military's Support that has the true claim to power.
strings.BRA_lacerda_govt_torch_tt_delay: It is only with the Support of the Government at large that Lacerda will remain the acting President. The backing of the cabinet and legislature will be necessary in order to unearth the fraud that Goulart has undoubtably committed.
strings.BRA_lacerda_voter_torch_tt_delay: While there is no doubt he played dirty, Goulart sold a large portion of Brazil's population on his snake oil. The last thing that Lacerda needs is an angry crowd of Getulists protesting his actions, so it would be prudent to ensure that Voters are sufficiently Apathetic before he makes his move.
strings.BRA_lacerda_coup_secure_power_not_yet: Until preparations are fully made, Lacerda is unable to secure power.
strings.BRA_lacerda_coup_secure_power_ready: The time has come to expose Goulart as the Getulist traitor that he is!

strings.BRA_hundred_days_info_tt:
The Hundred Days Crisis will only be resolved once one of the four contenders reaches 50% support, becoming interim President.

The military's threat of intervention dangles over the Senado, a Sword of Damocles ready to strike if the 100 day period elapses or the political situation grows too unstable.

Total Support:
Kubitschek has [?BRA_hd_kubitschek_support|1]% support.
Goulart has [?BRA_hd_goulart_support|1]% support.
Lacerda has [?BRA_hd_lacerda_support|1]% support.
Adhemar has [?BRA_hd_adhemar_support|1]% support.
strings.BRA_hd_category_description:
Brazil is facing an unprecedented leadership crisis. While the Senado scrambles to settle on a new President in the next hundred days, Juscelino Kubitschek, João Goulart, Carlos Lacerda, and Adhemar de Barros call in favors and strike deals to try to come out on top.

Once a contender reaches 50% support, the Senado will confirm their appointment. {bra_hd_leader_info}

strings.BRA_hundred_days_successor_desc: The contenders have just a hundred days to mobilize whatever resources they have at their disposal in order to secure the Presidency. As the candidates agonize over their campaigns, others fret that factionalism will make any consensus impossible.
strings.BRA_campaign_trigger: Another successor action is not in progress
strings.BRA_offer_concessions_desc: While offering political concessions to certain senators will hurt our campaign, it gives us more opportunities to act later.
strings.BRA_hd_can_secure_support_goulart: Unlocks decision to Secure Support for Goulart.
strings.BRA_hd_can_secure_support_adhemar: Unlocks decision to Secure Support for Adhemar.

strings.BRA_hd_can_bribe_chosen: Unlocks decision to Buy Backing for the chosen contender.
strings.BRA_secure_support_desc: Through favors, political promises, and shrewd negotiation, we can build support among the senators who will decide the presidency's fate.
strings.BRA_buy_backing_desc: Sometimes negotiation requires a little extra something to sweeten the pot. In exchange for senators' support, we will ensure a little extra funding goes their way once we are in power.
strings.BRA_hundred_days_making_moves_desc: The other contenders aren't sitting idly by as we aim to take the presidency. Behind the scenes, they are striking deals and finding their own sources of support.

strings.BRA_pl_info_support_required_constitutio: Passing a Constitutional Change through the Senado Federal requires securing the support of at least 45 Senators.

strings.BRA_test_dummy_act_Desc: This act will give free weed cocaine and metaamphetamine to all brazilians. it will also establish new facilities known as DRUG HOUSES where you can get drugs for free unlimited.
strings.BRA_test_dummy_act_2_Desc: this act will give guns to everyone in the world. and make it legal to kill everyone with new guns so everyone can be killed with guns we give to everyone with this act.
strings.BRA_NATIONAL_ELECTRIC_ACT_Desc: One of the major factors that exacerbates the current energy crisis in Brazil is the fact that a substantial fraction of the electrical infrastructure is owned by foreign corporations. Poorer and rural citizens bear the brunt of this injustice. This bill will nationalize these electrical corporations in order to provide electricity at low cost to the people.
strings.BRA_VOTING_RIGHTS_ACT_Desc: Our Republic is supposedly “democratic”, but there is very good reason to doubt this when the illiterate, low-ranking military officers, and other marginalized groups are denied the vote. Accordingly, in order to promote the interests of democracy, this bill will expand the franchise to all Brazilian citizens without exception.
strings.BRA_AFRICAN_SURGE_RESOLUTION_Desc: The war against the Reichskommissariate in southern Africa continues to rage; the conflict with the three German colonial tyrannies is nowhere near over. It is clear to any observer that additional support will be required if we are to drive the so-called “Aryan master race” back from the South African border. This law will send more reinforcements to the frontier so as to ensure that the Hitlerites are driven back.
strings.BRA_UNWAVERING_TORCH_ACT_Desc: In light of the unprecedented German aggression witnessed in South Africa and other places in the last two years, Brazil must find allies; the Americans and their Organization of Free Nations could not be better candidates for this. This bill gives the legislatures support and consent and thus arranges for Brazil's immediate admittance to the Organization of Free Nations as a full member.
strings.BRA_HIGHWAY_TO_PROSPERITY_ACT_Desc: The Trans-Amazonian Highway connecting Brazil to its hinterlands and to the rest of South America has languished for lack of resources and funding since the fall of the Lott government. This bill will restore the lost funding and provide more money with a view on seeing the project through to completion. Whatever is required, Brazil will provide.
strings.BRA_SOUTH_AFRICAN_WITHDRAWAL_ACT_Desc: Brazilian blood has been shed on South African soil for a useless proxy boxing match between America and Germany. Ships and ships of Brazil's youth and treasures have been sent east, to no return. No more. This act, proposed by President Quadros, will bring our boys home from the lawless hellhole of Africa and save them from having to play the catspaw for America. As the act to enter South Africa was passed overwhelmingly by Congress, Quadros must ensure an act to ensure Brazil withdrawal from South Africa can also pass. Otherwise he will lack the legislatures approval and consent to do so. While Quadros could just ignore the legislature, arguing directly to the Supreme Court that they have no authority over foreign policy, it would be best to pass this bill through the legislature to prevent any unneeded political battles.
strings.BRA_LOTT_ACT_Desc: This bill will once and for all prevent armed forces interference in Brazilian politics by setting new ground rules for military officers and harshly enforcing the rules already on the books to kick politics out of the armed forces and protect democracy in the Republic of Brazil. If it goes through, the Constitutionalists in our military will finally be empowered to help ensure our military fully embraces its rightful role of “uniformed civilians” and nothing more or less.
strings.BRA_AGRARIAN_RELIEF_ACT_Desc: This bill aims to begin the process of agrarian reform. We will redistribute land from inefficient, money-gorged landowners, and hand it over to more deserving people - smallholders, peasants - who are better-placed to make sure it prospers. The bill also has emergency relief and loans to ensure the agriculutural sector does not suffer but continues to grow and improve. This will hopefully also put an end to the protests currently paralyzing our country.
strings.BRA_ENTRY_INTO_THE_ANDEAN_PACT_Desc: Ferocious debates are taking place all over the United States of Brazil as the ratification of the treaty for Brazilian entry into the Andean Pact is debated in the Congresso Nacional. The stakes are quite high: if the treaty is ratified, it means that Brazil will enter the Andean Pact as a full member. This will subject it to all that was agreed to in the negotiations. As the lists of people that support and oppose this move are large and often transcend party lines, careful political manoeuvring will be required to see this treaty ratification through.
strings.BRA_ANTI_RESTRICTION_ACT_Desc: This Act proposed by President Jânio Quadros will push through measures preventing excessive restrictions on economic activity of the sort that the previous Varguist governments were all too prone to doing. Not only will this prevent a large amount of taxpayer money from being syphoned off by the government in the course of enforcing these restrictions, it will also enable Brazil to do what it needs with state-owned companies one way or the other.
strings.BRA_ANTI_CORRUPTION_ACT_Desc: This Act proposed by President Jânio Quadros in the aftermath of the collapse of the Lott administration will decisively remediate a recent, glaringly obvious problem that feckless general left behind; that of corruption. By taking measures that are certain to immediately resolve the situation, we will sweep corruption out of Brazil. Reports to the effect that the proposed measures in the Act are mere bandages at best and exacerbate the issue at worst are propaganda by Lott loyalists.
strings.BRA_ANTI_TRUST_ACT_Desc: This Act proposed by President Jânio Quadros will push through measures preventing trusts from being formed by politicians and permitting investigations to be launched into any current or future attempts to form them. Those that say that this act somehow is meant to target the prominently corrupt PSP politician Adhemar de Barros, a known rival of the President, are spouting propaganda fed to them by hostile actors and should not be believed.
strings.BRA_ADHEMAR_DE_BARROS_IMPEACHMENT_Desc: This act proposed by Ulysses Guimarães in the Chamber of Deputies, calls for the Impeachment of President Adhemar de Barros due to the President falling into a coma. The nation lacks a head of state to lead it and is instead being run by Laudo Natel, the Chief of Staff. This is blatantly unconstitutional and must be stopped. As the constitution holds no mechanism to remove a President incapable of fullfilling their duties, the legislative chambers will remove President de Barros.
strings.BRA_HEALTHCARE_BILL_Desc: Easily accessible healthcare is a right all Brazilians deserve but have been deprived of for far too long - this is something Adhemar de Barros is intimately familiar from his time as a doctor. This is something that the PSP will make into a reality with the healthcare bill. Of course, there is some debate as to the content of the bill - the UDN would prefer co-operation with private enterprise whereas the PTB petition for a public healthcare system. Regardless, passage of the bill is imperative if we wish to set a strong base for the rest of the presidency.
strings.BRA_NATIONAL_SCHOOL_EXPANSION_PROGRAM_De: While education is present in all states, the extent of it is limited. Not all children have the privilege of going to school. This is a major factor holding Brazil back from further economic growth. Proposed on behalf of the President, the bill will seek through massive investment to ensure all children have access to schools, whether they live in cities or the countryside, and to ensure education reflects the patriotic values of Brazil.
strings.BRA_SOCIAL_SECURITY_REFORM_ACT_Desc: This act proposed by Romeu de Campos Vergal seeks to build upon the social security laws established by Juscelino Kubitschek in his presidency. There exists many gaps in the security net that allow the old, disabled, and working poor to fall through and enter poverty. This bill will ensure this ends immediately.
strings.BRA_ADHEMAR_AGRARIAN_REFORM_ACT_Desc: This act proposed by Filinto Müller has been called by the President as one of the most impressive and important pieces of legislation in Brazilian history. Designed to solve the latifúndio crisis and redistribute land in the countryside. However the bill has been criticised by those in the PSD and PTB for being less ambitious than the Ex-President Lott's bill on agrarian reform and more limited in scope.
strings.BRA_NATIONAL_STANDARDIZATION_OF_WAGE_IND: The National Standardization of Wages Indexation Act

Inflation has long been a runaway figure in Brazil's economy, soothed only by exceptional growth in recent decades. Recently, however, the situation has grown delicate; any lack of government prudence could trigger an inflationary spiral the likes of which has been unseen since the 1890s.

In response, the lengthy National Standardization of Wages Indexation Act has frozen public sector wages, in nationalized industries and in government, to meet targets set by Brasília. It also grants the government more power to ensure consistent wage indexation nationwide, aiming for greater financial stability.

Roundly criticized by both right and left, the Act is likely to be repealed after upcoming elections. To the incumbent PSP, however, economic security demands economic sacrifices.
strings.BRA_LABOR_LAW_REFORM_ACT_Desc: Far more than mere bureaucrats are employed by the government. Thousands of steel workers, manual laborers, and similar workers rely on the state for employment. A group of people so directly working for the benefit of the nation should have their livelihoods protected. They should know that, when they go home at the end of a long day's work, they won't wake up without a job. Through official processes, severance payments, and fewer justifications for sacking, these workers will rest easy knowing their profession is safe and sound. Of course, the opposition believe we are merely doing this to protect the so-called 'corrupt' government officials we've employed. The reality is that they simply can't imagine we care for the people.
strings.BRA_EDNA_AGRARIAN_REFORM_ACT_Desc: Agriculture is our nation's largest industry and the one that it was founded on. However, land ownership has increasingly fallen into the hands of the few rather than the people. The government must intercede and pass a law that will further the cause of agrarian reform and the redistribution of property. Building on the work of Henrique Lott and surpassing the progress of the Adhemar de Barros government, the Agrarian Reform Act will act quickly to redistribute land so that more citizens will have access to land. Then, they and our nation can grow its access to capital and build generational wealth.
strings.BRA_VOTING_LAW_REFORM_ACT_Desc: Millions of patriotic Brazilians are barred from voting because they are illiterate. Citizens should not have their voices silenced due merely to the station of their birth and the failure of the system to educate them properly. While universal suffrage cannot be granted overnight, the literacy requirements can be weakened. Now, an understanding of the alphabet will determine one's eligibility to vote. While only a rule change, this step will enfranchise millions of citizens and weaken the classism built into the current democratic system.
strings.BRA_NULLIFICATION_OF_EMBARGO_AGAINST_THE: Nullification of Embargo Against the Pakt

Proposed by Senator Filinto Müller of the State of Mato Grosso, the bill calls for the end of trade restrictions with Germany and other members of the Einheitspakt. While restrictions will remain for goods produced in the conquered eastern Reichskommissariats, this act, if passed, will normalize relations between Brazil and Germany.
strings.BRA_IMPEACHMENT_OF_VICE_PRESIDENT_EDNA_L: Impeachment of Vice President Edna Lott

Due to recent revelations about the conduct of Vice President Lott and her collusion with foreign powers, Senator Filinto Müller has proposed the act of impeachment against the Vice President. Supported by Adhemar de Barros, impeachment would remove all PTB influence from government and ensure the next in the line of succession is the President of the Chamber of Deputies, Pedro Aleixo.
strings.BRA_UNIVERSAL_LITERACY_ACT_Desc: What can a nation be judged by if not by its literature? By how well-read the common man is, how accessible its great plays, novels, and art are for its people? By how easy it is for the people to read the laws which govern them? And what does it say about Brazil if our people cannot read or write at all? This great disservice cannot stand. Expanded education facilities, in both urban and rural areas alike, will teach Brazil's youth the Brazilian word. Adult literacy programs will be implemented to help those that past administrations have left behind. All of Brazil will rejoice with pen and paper.
strings.BRA_AFFORDABLE_HEALTHCARE_BILL_Desc: Health is the basis of all people. There is a reason when people celebrate and toast, they cheer for health. For Saúde. Therefore, we must support the health of all our citizens. Some, specifically within the PTB, have called for a state-run healthcare service. While this is nice in theory, in practice it is far beyond what the state can manage. That being said, Brazilians need help, and so we shall help them. Expanded programs and subsidies for lower-income patients, caps on certain drug prices, and new medical regulations to keep treatments affordable will ensure that when Brazilians call for help, help will arrive.
strings.BRA_NATIONAL_HEALTHCARE_ACT_Desc: Health is the basis of all people. There is a reason when people celebrate and toast, they cheer for health. For Saúde. Therefore, we must go above and beyond for Brazil's health. Let no cost or expenditure dissuade us, Brazilians will receive the finest treatments the world can offer. A new, state-run healthcare service will be created to the benefit of all of Brazil's patients. Government-run hospitals, expanded scholarships for doctors working under the state, and little to no cost treatments will turn Brazil from a land of the sick and neglected to a land we can truly toast to.
strings.BRA_STANDARDS_IN_GOVERNMENT_ACT_Desc: So many civil servants and politicians have gotten far too comfortable acting as if the system works for them, rather than vice versa. It's high time to remind them that no, corruption is not an acceptable part of life, and no, they are not the exception. With a set of strict standards and guidelines put into place with this bill, even a singular fudged digit will be noticed,swiftly investigated, and punished if found guilty. Never another Adhemar!
strings.BRA_NATIONAL_DEREGULATION_ACT_Desc: The lifeblood of a society is its local businesses. The influence they have over the daily life of Brazilians far outstretches the size of any one business. Unlike larger companies they have neither the time nor resources to satisfy the byzantine laws controlling them. Start up costs, planning requirements, and many other regulations hold back the potential found in the hidden corners of our economy. The National Deregulation Bill shall remove many of the restrictive barriers around small and medium businesses to help speed up economic growth.
strings.BRA_EDNA_REPEAL_OF_JAPANESE_IMMIGRATION_:
For years, the Japanese-Brazilians have been persecuted by elements in government for their seeming inability to assimilate into local culture, their language and culture banned, and their rights taken away, with legislation by PSD giving the final blow to the weakened rights of the Japanese-Brazilians with the Immigration Ban of 1946.

Or so they thought.

Recognizing the malefic consequences of the immigration ban, the Senate has mobilized itself to repeal the ban on Japanese Immigration, getting this ghost to stop haunting the Japanese-Brazilian community that lived both in the city and in the countryside. This, however, is but one step towards ending the prejudices and discrimination that still are prevalent in Brazil, only time and effort will be able to turn these wounds into memories.
strings.BRA_WEST_AFRICAN_INTERVENTION_ACT_Desc: As a staunch ally of freedom across the globe, it is only natural that Brazil should come to the aid of the OFN's benighted allies in West Africa. Of course, this would not be direct intervention - the sheer size and distance of the conflict would make such involvement impossible, and that is without considering the international implications of such an act. This Bill, however, will allow the President to authorize a less direct form of aid via a simple peacekeeping force, as to secure the region for liberal democracy.
strings.BRA_BRAZIL_AMERICA_ARMS_TREATY_Desc:
Recently agreed upon by the American and Brazilian governments, our Arms Treaty is now on the Senado floor. If ratified, it would further entrench the existing alliance with the United States, enshrine military cooperation with the nation into law and would involve American research and technical assistance to Brazil's armed forces, particularly in regard to its burgeoning nuclear program.

Some senators have already come out against the treaty, decrying it as a crossing of the Rubicon into the U.S. sphere of influence that future governments may be powerless to reverse, but we must stress the overall strength this would grant Brazil on the world stage.
strings.BRA_BRAZILIAN_LABOR_ACT_Desc: Many of the more offensive Varguist laws are thoroughly entrenched into the Brazilian political system - the key word being many. But luckily for us, a good chunk of them are just vulnerable enough for the UDN to strike decisively against them. In one streamlined Bill, the unions will no longer be able to hold the nation ransom over every single petty dispute. If they wish to continue existing they will either work with the state, or against the state.
strings.BRA_ERADICATE_ILLITERACY_ACT_Desc:
One matter that has continued to hold Brazil back is our high illiteracy rates. At a time when the major powers have relegated illiteracy to irrelevance, Brazil has continued to languish in the den of iniquity and ignorance. Few areas have faced this more intensely than rural regions. Cut off from wider education systems and with priority placed on the prosperity of the cities, these areas have seen their education systems only bleed away their strength further.

I will not stand this any longer. With this measure, the trend of ignoring Brazil's expansive rural regions shall be quashed, substituted with a new formula that increases support for rural education systems. These won't solve the crisis of rural illiteracy, but I know this measure will put us a lot closer to doing so, and will level the playing field entirely. By itself, that is already a fundamental triumph.
strings.BRA_NATIONAL_TRUTH_COMMISSION_ACT_Desc: For far too long, victims of the Estado Novo have been crying out for justice as previous Varguist governments turned a blind eye to their forebear's crooked ways. The repression. The violence. The censorship. No more. A National Truth Commission will be introduced into the Senado, with the aim to uncover and atone for the crimes of the Estado Novo. This is no partisan attack, as many may accuse us of - indeed, the commission will be staffed by independent experts and Vargas himself will be excluded. The goal here is not political power, but closure for the innocent and the wronged.
strings.BRA_ANTI_RIOT_BILL_Desc: The riots in São Paulo against Nikkei citizens in the Liberdade district are unacceptable and must be dealt with immediately. Our government has proposed a bill to enable the necessary precautions and actions to do so. The Anti-Riot Bill will permit the police and military to use exceptional powers, now and in any future rioting, to tackle and prevent cases of harm to innocents or to property of any kind. They will be given the right to arrest any civilian if there is a reasonable degree of suspicion such crimes have occurred, so that they may be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.
strings.BRA_RACIAL_DEMOCRACY_BILL_Desc:
Lacerda may not have always gotten along with the figureheads of the Nikkei community, but that hasn't rendered him blind to their plight or woes. Recent reports surrounding the state of discrimination have made their way up to the Presidential Palace itself. Outraged, Lacerda has ordered the creation of a bill officially extending civil rights, providing legal recognition for Japanese and officially barring discrimination targeted against the Nikkei community.

This is only a limited first step. Laws against discrimination may be on the books, but they only prosecute the most blatant examples, and they only provide minor penalties. The Japanese language may be recognised, but only through the lens of education, and its use elsewhere is still mostly written off. Even still, however, it is a bright step in the right direction in the fight for a true, equal racial democracy within Brazil.
strings.BRA_LACERDA_REPEAL_OF_JAPANESE_IMMIGRATI: For many years now, Japanese immigration has been seen by the establishment as a political inconvenience at best, and an active risk to our nation's security at worst. This ban, however sensible it may have seemed at the time, was born of racism. This prejudice has prevented incalculable amounts of otherwise hard-working people seeking a better life in Brazil from entering and contributing to our nation - a grave error that this bill will soon put right.
strings.BRA_LACERDA_NATIONAL_SECURITY_LAWS_REFOR:
Though it was Eduardo Gomes' administration that, in the name of national security, first put into law the banning of communist parties and the sanctioning of military intervention when deemed to be of national interest, Carlos Lacerda greatly expanded these powers. Military ministers have been granted the right to veto any laws pertaining to the armed forces. Allegiance with the OFN is now codified law. Military courts are sanctioned to handle cases related to dissident and radical forces within society.

From its approval in Chamber and Senate, the laws were immediately used to purge constitutionalists from the armed forces. For the UDN, and for Lacerda himself, they are working as intended. The expanded National Security Laws shall forever vanquish the spectre of Varguism from military life—and provide a bulwark against its emergence in civilian spheres.
strings.BRA_LACERDA_HYDROELECTRIC_BILL_Desc:
Not all bills have to be written with a partisan lean, and to be backed only by specific parties. Távora has proposed a new bill relating to hydroelectric power, encouraging its expansion across the entirety of Brazil, suggesting a number of key sites to use. This is an incredibly unusual step from Távora himself, not least with the corollaries of investment oming from the national government, rather than private investors.

The logic, Travora argues, is that such action is a legitimate place for the government to intervene. Only through government intervention, he argues, can such wide-reaching efforts be attained, and only through such government intervention combined with strong policies discouraging it can the risk of corrupt bargains be restricted. It is certainly an unusual development, but a nation like Brazil not being a major power is an unusual development in of itself.
strings.BRA_PRESIDENTIAL_LEGACY_FUND_ACT_Desc: Each president is given a small fund they may use however they wish. Adhemar will create a presidential library in São Paulo to help education and combine this with his charity for healthcare.
strings.BRA_PRESIDENTIAL_PENSION_AND_PARDON_ACT: The Presidential Pension and Pardon Act
strings.BRA_PRESIDENTIAL_PENSION_AND_PARDON_ACT_:
All good things have to come to an end. The strengths of my administration aside, it is impossible to deny that a lot of people have grown tired of my continued hegemony over the party, and over the wallets of Brazil. With how many donations I've made across Brazil, it seems likely that the next administration will try to prosecute me. As such, I will advance a measure to write off these expenses as legal and to pardon their recipients.

There is already a lot of opposition towards this measure in the Chamber and Senate, and the biggest names in opposition parties are putting in the work to make sure that this bill is defeated. As it stands, I realise that this bill is likely doomed, and few people seem inclined to directly support it. But, thankfully, I'm not out of office yet. A couple of targeted bribes could help to remind those wavering voices just who is in their corner.
strings.BRA_5TH_REPUBLIC_CONSTITUTION_Desc:
So much of Lacerda's term has been focused on fighting the stain of Varguism, and now, he stands on the cusp of total victory. Should this bill pass, Lacerda will call a new constitutional convention, seeking the total rewriting of the constitution with the aim of dismantling the protections and advantages it gives to Varguist principles. With its current contents, it's only a matter of time before another Estado Novo is formed.

Beyond achieving his ambition, rewriting the constitution allows the UDN to secure its dominance. It's difficult to reject the trustworthiness of a party willing to follow their principles like this. And if the right wording is used, the UDN can ensure that only they will be in line to benefit from the electoral system, and can certify their dominance for a generation. What other party, after all, could be trusted to defend the constitution's liberty?
strings.BRA_national_security_act_law_0_desc:
While the £GFX_BRA_constitutionalists_texticon constitution of the fourth republic has on paper made Brazil a democracy ruled by politicians, the reality could not be more different. In the £GFX_BRA_constitutionalists_texticon constitution there lies the £GFX_BRA_NSA_texticon National Security Acts. These acts grant the Military the £GFX_BRA_constitutionalists_texticon constitutional duty to intervene if the country is in danger of collapsing, legitimizing the Military's intervention in politics. In it there lies other laws weakening Brazil's democratic political culture, including the banning of subversive £GFX_BRA_pcb_texticon £GFX_BRA_pcdob_texticon communist and £GFX_BRA_pnb_texticon national socialist political parties.

Until the £GFX_BRA_NSA_texticon National Security Acts can be nullified by another law, this Sword of Damocles is ready to fall at any time.
strings.BRA_national_security_act_law_1_desc:
Though it was Eduardo Gomes' administration that, in the name of national security, first put into law the banning of communist parties and the sanctioning of military intervention when deemed to be of national interest, Carlos Lacerda greatly expanded these powers. Military ministers have been granted the right to veto any laws pertaining to the armed forces. Allegiance with the OFN is now codified law. Military courts are sanctioned to handle cases related to dissident and radical forces within society.

The expanded National Security Laws shall forever vanquish the spectre of Varguism from military life—and provide a bulwark against its emergence in civilian spheres.
strings.BRA_varguist_labor_law_desc:
On the 1st of May, 1943, inspired by the Vatican's 1891 Rerum novarum, Getúlio Vargas signed one of the most important documents of Brazilian history: a leatherbound manual of legislation that holds in its pages the livelihoods of every laborer, every farmhand, every pé-de-boi, and every Brazilian who toils for someone else's profit.

While the £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon  Consolidation of Labor Laws £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon includes laws from well before Vargas' time in office, the CLT persists as a defining piece of his legacy. Among many of its protections are the right for the Brazilian to have vacations, receive a minimum wage, and work in suitable conditions. Loopholes and corruption have tested its effectiveness, but the CLT remains the closest the Varguists have to sacred scripture.

For the £GFX_BRA_udn_texticon anti-Varguist, the CLT stinks of Mussolini, its similarities to Fascist Italy's Carta del Lavaro too close to comfort. An unassailable monument to corporatism, its chokehold on the Brazilian factory continues to taunt its opponents who want nothing more than to tame it of its power or tear it all down.
strings.BRA_racial_democracy_law_desc:
£GFX_BRA_racial_texticon Racial Democracy is a unique facet of Brazilian society. While in Eurasia, the jackboot stomps down on groups deemed lesser, and in America segregation is the status quo in many states, in Brazil racism, indeed race itself, is a thing of the past. In Brazil, all races and cultures are welcome to share in our beautiful country and take on the values of our enlightened and progressive society.

At all levels our government we will ensure that all peoples regardless of color or creed will have access to a robust Portuguese language education, taught of our historical triumphs, and have the opportunity to show their loyalty to the republic through patriotic associations.

The Brazilian people have defined themselves by what they stand against. Fascism will never reach Brazil, as there is only one people united under a single flag. We will continue marching forwards, expecting the rest of the world to join us one day soon.
strings.BRA_lgbt_rights_lgbt_allowed_law_desc:
Sexual Minorities rights exist in a gigantic loophole, a policy deemed too insignificant and unimportant for politicians to deal with while military coups occupy the day to day political system of the country. In 1830 Brazilian Emperor Dom Pedro I signed into law the new imperial penal code, which eliminated all references to sodomy, and the laws have remained the same since.

However, discrimination remains rampant and for many homosexuality is defacto illegal, with it considered a mental illness by the Federal Council of Medicine and with the police taking overt action against any stepping out of line with societal norms.
strings.BRA_the_lott_act_law_desc: In order to curb the ever present militarist influence in Brazilian politics, President Lott and his allies mobilized and successfully managed to pass the £GFX_BRA_constitutionalists_texticon The Lott Act. Under this act, the officer corps all throughout the Brazilian armed forces would see reform, removing £GFX_BRA_hardliners_texticon Hardliner elements and replacing them with £GFX_BRA_constitutionalists_texticon Constitutionalists who would contribue to the democratic transfer of power and prevent military intervention in future elections.
strings.BRA_anti_jap_law_0_desc:
As £GFX_GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japanese immigrants arrived at São Paulo at the beginning of the 20th century and settled into agriculture, the government accused them of being unable to assimilate, prohibited their language and culture, and hotly debated their rights.

During World War II, many were displaced and imprisoned in concentration camps. In 1946, the £GFX_BRA_psd_texticon PSD's Miguel Couto Filho, the son of a famous eugenicist, would propose a constitutional amendment blocking all Japanese immigration. Despite token opposition from the £BRA_udn_texticon UDN, the ban proved popular in the postwar mood and passed.

Even as Japanese-Brazilian communities dwindled, many did not have the money to return to £GFX_TNO_game_rule_flag_JAP  Japan or chose to stay out of genuine love for their new homeland. Due to widespread discrimination and police harassment, these communities have only become more insular. Now some are talking about radical action, but whether they represent a real threat or exist mostly in the minds of paranoid officials is hard to say.
strings.BRA_anti_jap_law_1_desc: There has been a major stain on Brazil's reputation for the past couple of decades - ever since the war, there has been a complete and total ban of immigration from Japan, largely motivated by fear of fascist infiltration. Many have justified it by invoking this fear of the other, but the nation of Brazil has recongised this as the flawed, short-sighted, and bigoted law that it is. While Japan is indeed run by fascists, there is no shortage of dissidents and free thinkers seeking a better life elsewhere. By opening our doors to these dispossessed, we are tapping into a vast potential labor market, as well as validating Brazil's long-standing claim of being a nation that stands above race.
strings.BRA_healthcare_bill_adhemar_law_desc: Easily accessible healthcare is a right all Brazilians deserve but have been deprived of for far too long - this is something Adhemar de Barros is intimately familiar from his time as a doctor. This is something that the PSP has made into a reality with the healthcare bill.
strings.BRA_presidential_legacy_fund_adhemar_law: Each president given a small fund that they can use in the ways they wish. Adhemar will create a presidential library in São Paulo to help education and combine this with his charity for healthcare.
strings.BRA_presidential_pension_and_pardon_law_: Each president will be given a pension and wage following their presidency that they can use. Presidents will be pardoned on completion of their term for actions they took during it.
strings.BRA_national_school_expansion_law_desc: While education is present in all states, the extent of it was limited. Not all children have the privilege of going to school. Proposed on behalf of the President, the bill saught through massive investment to ensure all children have access to schools, whether they live in cities or the countryside, and to ensure education reflects the patriotic values of Brazil.

strings.BRA_national_standardization_of_wages_in: £BRA_psp_texticon  National Standardization of Wages Indexation Act £BRA_psp_texticon

It also grants the government more power to ensure consistent wage indexation nationwide, aiming for greater financial stability.

Roundly criticized by both right and left, the Act is likely to be repealed after upcoming elections. To the incumbent PSP, however, economic security demands economic sacrifices.”
strings.BRA_labor_law_reform_act_law_desc:
If any newcomer in 1970 thinks they can erase Adhemar and the PSP's legacy at a pen stroke, they need to think again. The newly passed Labor Law Reform Act quashes any future zealous action to fire corporate or government appointees, from senior civil servants to service workers.

By mandating a higher rate of severance pay and more documentation to sack employees, the post-Adhemar administration has won the working class' support, if temporarily. Critics, however, decry this as a greedy power grab, keeping PSP officials in even when voted out or giving them a handy payout instead. In any case, it remains to be seen if the party's Laudo Natel can be the next “Pai dos Pobres” or if Brazil's workers have been orphaned for good.
strings.BRA_pakt_embargo_law: £GFX_GNG_Germany_texticon  Nullification of Embargo Against the Pakt £GFX_GNG_Germany_texticon
strings.BRA_pakt_embargo_law_desc: Proposed by Senator Filinto Müller of the State of Mato Grosso, the bill calls for the end of trade restrictions with Germany and other members of the Einheitspakt. While restrictions will remain for goods produced in the conquered eastern Reichskommissariats, this act, if passed, will normalize relations between Brazil and Germany.
strings.BRA_german_brazilian_law_desc:
Brazil's relationship with Germany has been marked with suspicion ever since the end of the Second World War, with Brazil's sizable German population profoundly affected by legislation brought on by wartime hysteria. After over 20 years of tight restrictions, the German-Brazilian Organization Act has finally granted all Brazilians of German origin to organize themselves as they see fit, allowing German-Brazilian communities to come together without fear of repression at the hands of the Brazilian government.

Although this law has been praised by civil rights activists, others are less enthusiastic. Critics of Adhemar's policies towards Germany are now worried that the lifting of these restrictions will open the door to the spreading of Nazi influence and ideology within Brazil, and it remains to be seen if these fears are founded.
strings.BRA_national_truth_commission_law_desc:
The National Truth Commission is an independent body set up to investigate the crimes committed on the government's behalf during the Estado Novo regime, spanning from the fall of the Old Republic in 1930 to Vargas' resignation from the Presidency in 1949. The body is designed to bring about restorative justice for the victims of state violence during this time and against its perpetrators responsible for the pain they experienced.

To most, this is a step towards righting the many wrongs of the bygone dictatorship. However, the £GFX_BRA_psd_texticon PSD and £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon PTB see this commission as nothing more than a political attack against Vargas' legacy, an attempt to undermine democracy by tarring them with accusations of years-old brutality. The £GFX_BRA_udn_texticon UDN's counter is that the commission's powers are limited to reporting and publicizing crimes, not charging and imprisoning people.
strings.BRA_ENAP_law_desc:
The National School of Public Administration is a federal public foundation founded by President Carlos Lacerda. It is part of the Brazilian Ministry of Planning, Budget, and Management, with its function being crucial to increasing the state's efficiency. The school is now responsible for training the future of Brazil's government.

From now on, entering the National School of Public Administration and passing its exams will be the only way to become either a government official or a civil servant in Brazil. Proponents of this policy state that this will prevent cronyism from becoming a viable method to enter the civil service, allow for better public policy, and for its effective implementation in the future.
strings.BRA_rio_cocapital_law_desc:
Previously, Rio de Janeiro was the sole capital of Brazil. Then, that title was inherited by Brasília, the city created by former President Juscelino Kubitschek. To rectify the controversy over this changing of titles, it has been decided by President Carlos Lacerda that both Brasília and Rio de Janeiro will be recognized as the capital cities of Brazil.

In practice, this means that Brasília will still remain Brazil's political and administrative capital, where the seat of government is held. As co-capital, Rio de Janeiro has regained its status as the cultural heart of the country and will become the new home of several government departments in the coming years, even if Brasília remains the legislative heart of the country.
strings.BRA_state_of_siege_law_desc:
Though Getúlio Vargas may be gone, his ideas still haunt Brazil. Varguist candidates such as £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon  João Goulart fought to steal the presidency from £GFX_BRA_udn_texticon  Carlos Lacerda, in order to enact their sinister plans. Should the Varguists win, Brazil will be plunged into stagnation and corruption.

Now, with the blessing of the military, Lacerda has near total control of the state apparatus. With these surgical tools, Lacerda will excise the Varguist cancer from Brazil for once and for all. History will remember Carlos Lacerda as the greatest president of Brazil, not Getúlio Vargas.
strings.BRA_national_literacy_campaign_law_desc:
Personally championed by President Carlos Lacerda, a legion of teachers, scholars and bureaucrats set forth to eradicate the scourge of illiteracy from Brazil. Inspired in part by the works of both Marxist professor Paulo Freire and the Ação Básica Cristã, the National Literacy Campaign sought to improve the state of Brazilian education by ensuring that every citizen is given the means and the opportunity to learn how to read and write.

The Campaign guarantees access to literacy classes in both children's and adult education, sets funding and manpower for running said classes, and sets periodic goals for the improvement of Brazil's literacy rate. This is a campaign measured in decades, one that will long outlast President Lacerda's own terms in office, but there is universal consensus among the political class of Brazil that full literacy is necessary for the development of the nation.
strings.BRA_UDN_moderate_healthcare_law_desc:
Signed into law by President Carlos Lacerda, the £GFX_Healthcare Affordable Healthcare Act guarantees fair and inexpensive health insurance to all Brazilian citizens. By subsiding healthcare costs for Brazil's poorest and providing funds for the expansion of hospitals, clinics and professional training, the Act attempts to expand services.

While progressive critics have argued against the establishment of insurance schemes and subsidised costs, preferring a national health service closer to the Beveridge model, the passage of the £GFX_Healthcare Affordable Healthcare Act has improved conditions. All across Brazil, the quality and quantity of life has increased thanks to this Act.
strings.BRA_UDN_radical_healthcare_law_desc:
The £GFX_Healthcare National Healthcare Act, considering health to be 'a right of all and an obligation of the State', established a health care system funded and managed by the Brazilian state. Its remit is expansive and its costs are high, but the Unified Health System has seen a rapid expansion in the health and wellbeing of Brazilian citizens.

The Act itself was signed into law by President Carlos Lacerda of the £GFX_BRA_udn_texticon UDN. Despite his history of supporting free-market policies, and despite rumours that his circle would have preferred a system of support rather than direct management, it was by his pen that this Act was signed into being.
strings.BRA_america_arms_treaty_law_desc: The product of a series of highly secretive negotiations, this treaty between the £GFX_GNG_USA_texticon  United States and Brazil £GFX_GNG_Brazil_texticon  promises to grant the rising country one of the most powerful arguments available to a nation in the modern age: nuclear weapons. In exchange for closer military cooperation between Brazil and the OFN, the United States has pledged its most skilled scientists and technicians to aid in the country's nuclear weapons program. To possess weapons of mass destruction is no small responsibility, and such confidence on the part of the United States has only further enshrined Brazil's role as a key component of the Organization of Free Nations.
strings.BRA_dismantled_labour_laws_desc: Lacerda has long waged an ideological war against the lingering influence of the Estado Novo, and with this piece of legislation, he has won a key victory. A new series of laws has been implemented according to the £GFX_BRA_udn_texticon UDN's vision for Brazil: Union protections have been largely removed, while tighter regulations and a new mandatory minimum percentage of union participation have made it far more difficult to legally organize strikes. These laws have primed the country for the second blow: protections to the practice of union busting, and reduced regulations governing the minimum wage. Indeed, while the defeat of Varguism within Brazil's labor sector will no doubt make the country an attractive hotspot for investment, various unions affected by the legislation, as well as the £GFX_BRA_ptb_texticon PTB, have decried it as a brazen assault on the rights of the Brazilian worker.
strings.BRA_5th_republic_desc:
There is a new Emperor of Brazil and his name is Carlos Lacerda.

Under the £GFX_BRA_udn_texticon UDN and Lacerda, Brazil has entered a new era, for better or for worse. There is no more opposition, and the people have been subdued. Every day the legacy of Vargas is being destroyed, while Lacerda further cements himself as one of the greats in Brazil's history, with his near unlimited power.

While Lacerda may be Emperor, the military has become his Shogun, holding the true power in Brazil. As the military grows further divided, however, many fear for the future of Brazil.

strings.BRA_lottquadros_category_description: The 1960 Presidential election left Brazil's executive divided between President Teixeira Lott, supported by the left-wing PSD-PTB coalition, and Vice President Jânio Quadros, backed by the UDN. Both have publicly promised to work with the other, but behind closed doors, tensions are high and a power struggle is brewing. As Brazil navigates turbulent times, both have the opportunity to grow their influence, but drastic moves may tear their relationship apart.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_info_tt:
President Lott and Vice President Quadros' relationship is unsteady, with both attempting to gain the upper hand and make their vision for Brazil a reality.

While the decisions their administration makes may shift the balance of power, the strength of their relationship will affect how their government weathers a potential crisis.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_bar_tooltip_quadros_domi: Vice President Quadros is currently dominant.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_improve_relations_0_desc: The President and Vice President will host a joint press conference where they will outline their strategy to address Brazil's problems.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_improve_relations_2_desc: Lott and Quadros will set aside time to speak with visiting foreign diplomats and to attend a banquet in their honor.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_improve_relations_1_desc: The Presidential cabinet will meet to ensure implementation of the current agenda goes as planned.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_improve_relations_3_desc: Lott and Quadros will hear out governors, working in concert to placate their concerns.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_increase_lott_influence_: As Minister of War, Lott built relationships with both Gomes and Kubitschek's appointees. He will meet with those who are still around and build support for his reforms.
President Lott will sit down with some of his connections in the military, keeping his line of communication with the armed forces open.

The PTB-PSD coalition propeled Lott to victory in the 1960 election, and it is only with their support that he will be able to accomplish what he has planned. The President will strategize with coalition leaders to finalize the congressional agenda.
Lott will reinforce his position as figurehead of the Brazilian government through a public speech. Quadros' presence will not be necessary.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_increase_quadros_influen: Vice President Quadros is willing to hear out the administration's detractors in the UDN and PSP, reminding them that Lott, not he, is to blame for its failings.

Bureaucracy is one of the biggest obstacles to solving Brazil's problems. Quadros will instruct the executive to implement his agenda using whatever powers they are allowed, bypassing the congress. Surely Lott won't mind.
Quadros will clarify the administration's foreign policy stance with a radio appearance praising Brazil's independence and redoubling his pledge not to bend to the whims of the Sphere, Pakt, or OFN.
The church have been longtime supporters of the UDN, so the Vice President will meet with religious leaders to hear out their concerns.

strings.BRA_lottquadros_decrease_cooperation_low: Lott and Quadros' relationship worsens slightly.
strings.BRA_lottquadros_impending_resignation_tr: Lott and Quadros have found common ground.

strings.BRA_lottquadros_over_good_effect_tooltip: Lott and Quadros' relationship is cemented.
strings.BRA_development_info_tt:
The Development Panel is the place to manage the nation's economic development.

Clicking on a Region displays possible Development Edicts which can be invested in.

Special Projects, such as the Trans-Amazonian Highway, consume resources and political power monthly until they are completed.

Only one Development Edict can be active at a time nationwide. Each lasts 60 days and affects the level of Development in the Region, spurring economic growth.

Lastly, the graphs below the map display the progress of Development in the current region, as well as economic development in the nation as a whole.

strings.BRA_rehabilitate_the_railways_desc:
During the times of the empire, it was Barão de Mauá that built the first railway and connected the city of Rio de Janeiro to its countryside, hoping that soon the whole country would be linked by the iron highway. Today, the reality is far different from what he envisioned as railroads are forgotten and replaced by roadways.

As Kubitschek made roadways his main priority during the first term as President, the railways of Brazil were becoming more and more forgotten, to the point where riding them would be like time traveling back to the 1920s. In his second term, JK will rehabilitate the railways and modernize them 50 years from where they currently are, welcoming Brazil into a new iron age.
strings.BRA_fund_rede_ferroviria_desc:
In the 50s, Kubitschek incorporated every railway in the country and consolidated them into the Rede Ferroviária Federal with the ambition to standardize and expand the rail networks around Brazil. But unfortunately, due to his focus on building large highways around the country, the company was underfunded, and the iron highways only declined even more.

If our goal is to fix the railways and expand them, we must inject money into the underfunded business, even if it costs us millions. Then, the trains shall pick up steam.
strings.BRA_embrace_diesel_desc: To modernize railways, we must give our trains brand new diesel-run engines that will allow them to travel at high speeds never seen before in Brazil and that can run for long distances! In short, if we wish to see our railroads become first-rate and respected worldwide, we must import all the latest diesel designs from around the world.
strings.BRA_resume_standardization_desc: The Brazilian railways are heavily outdated, with many parts dating back to the old days before the 1930 revolution. The only reason why they haven't torn up yet is because of Kubitschek's own Rede Ferroviaria. If we want to introduce our railways into a new age and ensure their co-operability, we must standardize them. From building signals, giving our drivers the necessary instructions, to building broader rail gauges so newer trains can drive through.
strings.BRA_expand_the_network_desc: For a railway network to be valuable, it must reach essential destinations, opening up various opportunities and easier access. Therefore, while the development of the railways in the rural areas is critical, we must ensure their expansions and connection to Brazil's most prominent urban centers. Only then will our great railroads be noticed by the whole world.
strings.BRA_cementing_lotts_legacy_desc: Lott, despite being controversial at first and just an intermission between terms, is still important especially with his loyalty to constitutionalism, and his efforts to enforce it on the military. Kubitschek will pay respect to Lott by bolstering the efforts and powers of the constitutionalists to ensure he stays in power. Lott saved Kubitschek in 1955; it's only fair he returned the favor
strings.BRA_reassess_our_ambitions_desc:
When Kubitschek was named the mayor of Belo Horizonte, the old dirt roads became modern pavements. Then, as the President, he connected the country by building highways that allowed Brazilian citizens to drive from São Paulo to Mato Grosso. For Brazil to advance another 50 years in just 5, Juscelino will make infrastructure a priority once again.

After handing the presidency to Lott, Kubitschek took the time to reflect on a new strategy for when he returned to the presidency. Since the end of the old oligarchical republic, railroads have been neglected in favor of highways as Brazilians started to take their trips in cars more and more. Some visionaries have suggested that air travel will be the future of transportation, with others even saying to take advantage of Brazil's vast waterways and turn them into “marine highways.” Now is the time for JK to show the country his new plans.
strings.BRA_resume_building_roadways_desc:
Over 20 years ago, Vargas envisioned that Brazil's vast and rich interior would be conquered by the paved road, giving Brazilians the opportunity to travel and commerce through the rest of the country. Such an idea would be in action first by Kubitschek by finally connecting the heart of the country with the highly populated coastal areas with the creation of Brasília and great highways that would facilitate travel. Later, it would be Lott's turn to turn Vargas' dream into reality by finally opening up our majestic rainforest to the rest of the country by creating the Trans-Amazonian Highway. These are genuinely beautiful sights to behold, and to think they were all done in nearly less than a decade...

But there is still much work to do - many areas of Brazil remain isolated, and Kubitschek's job is to continue what he started. Soon, every single Brazilian will be connected by the highway!
strings.BRA_send_out_the_surveyors_desc:
Building new roads to connect all of Brazil is our foremost goal. Still, we must ensure that the current ones continue to serve the Brazilian people with the highest quality they deserve.

To make sure our highways aren't deteriorating, we must send out surveyors to analyze them and send us reports.
strings.BRA_repair_neglected_routes_desc: In the years since Juscelino Kubitschek's first term as President, the roads he built have seen a great amount of use. That is a double-edged sword. It is good in that the roads are and have been an infinitely superior replacement to the shoddy paths and outdated roadways that crisscrossed Brazil before their construction; trade and transport are conveyed far better over these new roads than they were in the past. It is bad in that use of any structure especially under so-called 'cyclic loading'—the scientific term for a situation in which periods of load are followed by periods of zero load—is guaranteed to lead to wear and tear, if not outright failure. That is exactly what has happened on these roads. It is time to begin a widespread repair campaign to fix them. This will preserve and improve their integrity, preventing Brazilian roads succumbing to the old joke about a given roadway being a road full of potholes or a pothole full of roads. More importantly, it will pave the way for any further expansions we wish to conduct.
strings.BRA_expand_lanes_on_the_highways_desc: The currently extant highway system in the Republic of Brazil, even after the expansions we and our more sensible predecessors embarked upon, is used by hundreds and hundreds of thousands of vehicles per day. That figure is growing day after day, resulting in a situation in which our highways are reaching their capacity—especially the routes between the largest cities. This cannot be borne. We must widen our national highways to allow for more lanes. That will reduce congestion and, just as importantly, permit more traffic flow for commerce, commuters, and travelers alike.
strings.BRA_support_urban_initiatives_desc: In Belo Horizonte and Brasília during his tenures there, our President Kubitschek oversaw the development of modern city infrastructure. On his watch roads were seamlessly integrated into city life to allow Brazilians to go wherever they needed: to work, to the shops, to visit friends, to go to church, you name it. The result is two cities that, Kubitschek often says, are easier to navigate than the likes of D.C. or Germania. Now that Kubitschek is President once more, he knows that now is the time to ensure that all Brazil's major cities can benefit from the structures he made for Belo Horizonte and the Federal Capital. Let us, in accordance with his suggestion, put forth a fund to support city roadwork initiatives and incentivize cities to improve their road networks.
strings.BRA_break_ground_on_the_perimetral_norte: Break Ground on the Perimetral Norte

Lott's grand Trans-Amazonian Highway allowed expansion into the underdeveloped jungle, but his ambition can be taken even further. Kubitschek will propose a new addition, a Northern Perimeter Highway, linking Amapá to the Guiana-Caiena administration and towards Colombia, where the new highway will meet the southern part of the Trans-Amazonian Highway.
strings.BRA_ready_airways_for_the_future_desc:
During the past years, the number of foreign tourists and visitors, coming to see our beautiful nation, has been steadily growing - most of them arriving not through our borders or ports, but via planes. It is more than clear now that the future of transportation lies in the skies above our heads. Kubitschek, a man focused on the future himself, cannot ignore this fact.

We cannot afford our grand, proud nation to fall behind the rest of the world. The government will begin to take actions to improve the condition of Brazil's airways, along with other necessary steps, so that our country shall face the new age of travels with heads up high!
strings.BRA_a_crown_jewel_in_brasilia_desc: What better place to show that Brazil is committed to the transport of the future than its very own city of the future, Brasília? Kubitschek will request his good friend Oscar Niemeyer to design a special building for Brasília - a fantastic airport, which can welcome tourists, businesspeople, and world leaders alike to Brazil's shining new capital!
strings.BRA_terminals_in_the_cities_desc: The modernization of airports in major cities of Brazil, as Brasília, São Paulo and others will be the first step in Kubitschek's grand plan of air expansion - after all, these areas are the industrial, financial and tourist hubs of the country, and we must ensure that they're well-connected to the world, if we ever want to achieve an effective, sound economy, and call ourselves a modern nation.
strings.BRA_airstrips_in_amazonia_desc: Região Norte has long been the most remote and desolate area in Brazil - its rainforests made it extremely hard to transport goods or establish cities there. To fix that, the Kubitschek government will order the establishment of small and primitive, yet functional airstrips in the north of the country, so they can act as future points of expansion for settlements, building enterprises and new trade routes with Venezuela and Suriname.
strings.BRA_the_integrated_regional_system_desc:
The advent of air travel in Brazil is relatively recent, and much of the country's system is underdeveloped. Many destinations are economically infeasible for airlines to serve, and this isn't helped by the fact the industry is in constant competition with each other, slowing potential progress.

But Kubitschek's administration has vowed to fix the pressing use of domestic aviation. Air regulation shall be transferred to 5 administrative regions, overseeing flights in and out of Brazil, hopefully reducing the administrative burden and simplifying aviation in general.
strings.BRA_a_bandeirante_for_the_skies_desc: The majority of our neighbors on the continent already have their own “Bandeirantes”, or flagbearer airlines - not mentioning the three superpowers. Thus, a decision has been made to create our own, state-controlled airline, which will focus on travelling to underserved regions of Brazil, where it just might not be feasible for private companies to service. While costing us some cruzeiros, this shall link the populated areas of the country to more isolated ones and easen their burden, along with improving our trade and the economy in general.
strings.BRA_concessions_for_regional_carriers_de: With the advent of the Integrated Regional System, we are now faced with the question of what to do with the numerous airlines currently operating in Brazil. Air traffic rights shall be granted exclusively to airlines in each region, hopefully streamlining aviation and forming the backbone of a new air industry in Brazil.
strings.BRA_acquire_the_flagship_jet_desc:
What is a modern national transit system without a modern airline service? And what better way to demonstrate a modern airline than with a 190,000 pound aircraft with a top speed of 588 miles per hour and range of almost 3,000 miles? We paid a damn good price for that Douglas DC-8, let's show it off!

To show the people this was more than just a pet project bought with their tax dollars we're going to take it on a national tour, city by city. From our capital of Brasília to the Joyful Harbour of Alegre, from industrious São Paulo to venerable Rio de Janeiro, to Salvador, Recife, hell, maybe even a brief trip over the Amazons! The age of aviation has come to Brazil and is here to stay!
strings.BRA_link_urban_centers_desc: Japan has built the astonishing “Dangan Ressha” - trains that travel up to 200 kilometers per hour! Between Brazil's biggest cities, Rio and São Paulo, it takes half a day to travel with congested traffic and slow rail. This is a perfect opportunity to create the “Rio-São Paulo Line”, a high-speed rail linking both cities together. With the help of Japanese advisors, we can shorten the trip between the cities to just two hours, allowing transit to be faster than ever before, and cementing both cities' reputation as modern business hubs.
strings.BRA_span_the_nation_desc: Kubitschek has finished his term by completing the Belém-Brasília Highway, bridging North and South. Truly a marvel of the ages, but there is still much work to be done. No corresponding line exists for the nation's rail network; the rail system in the northeast and south of the country are disconnected. It's time for a new project. An ambitious North-South Railway will stretch from Goiás to Maranho, a project to unite the nation and the people!
strings.BRA_requisition_brazils_waterways_desc: With routes standardized and obstacles clear, navigating the Amazon river is feasible. Now for the master stroke; a series of inland ports throughout the river and its tributaries, forming the Sistema Aquaviário Amazônico, allowing transport of goods along the river from the heart of Brazil. Alongside the Highway will be a ferry system for all to use.
strings.BRA_modernize_shipping_vessels_desc: Petrobras has been a tremendous success for Brazil's energy sector thus far, though a few minor roadblocks have begun to hamper the company's continued growth. The most pressing issue is the rather appalling state of the transport fleets. As Brazil relies heavily upon its waterways for transportation, upgrading the fleet is paramount to clearing up infrastructural bottlenecks. A generous investment into retrofitting the aging vessels will hopefully be sufficient to keep the money flowing.
strings.BRA_provide_tax_incentives_desc: Brazil's many waterways were once the arteries of the nation, through which supplies, commerce, and domestic transport flowed. This is still the case in the modern age, but the rise of Brazil's highway and high-speed rail system have provided far cheaper alternatives to going by boat, and as a consequence, they have become overcrowded by traffic. The waterways remain underused by comparison, and, by providing tax incentives for maritime transportation, we can hopefully inject some life into these unencumbered routes.
strings.BRA_chart_existing_routes_desc: The age of exploration is a thing of the distant past, and yet, much of Brazil's land remains an enigma to this very day. The snaking rivers of the rainforest are maze-like and unpredictable in the extreme, and even the most experienced captains are forced to rely on word-of-mouth in order to navigate effectively. Instead of allowing our ships to stumble about in the dark, we can begin official efforts to map out the rivers of Brazil, so that even novice captains can rely on more than just a trail of breadcrumbs to find their way.
strings.BRA_deal_with_navigation_hazards_desc: The Amazon Rainforest is a place of great beauty, but also of tremendous danger. From unpredictable flow rates to hidden sandbars, unforeseen hazards await river vessels at nearly every turn. We can build as many roads and rails through the jungle as we wish, but until the rivers have been tamed, the Amazon will never truly be conquered. We shall send fleets of workers to clear up potential roadblocks on the most active river routes, so that vital supply trains will no longer have any unwelcome surprises during their journeys.
strings.BRA_build_inland_terminals_desc: With routes standardized and obstacles clear, navigating the Amazon river is feasible. Now for the master stroke; a series of inland ports throughout the river and its tributaries, forming the Amazon Fluvial Highway, allowing transport of goods along the river from the heart of Brazil. Alongside the Highway will be a ferry system for all to use.
strings.BRA_five_more_years_desc: The party is over now, for we have won! But what that means is that the time for real work has now begun. For JK this may be a new administration, but the age-old task of leading Brazil through the road of progress into the promised land. Although Henrique continued many of his old projects, he also left many, if not most unfinished. Yes, there are indeed many projects in the books such as improving Brazil's transport and energy infrastructure, reforming the government's public health and public education programs, a new strategy which shall boost Brazilian industrialization with the aim of financing a broad South American focused foreign policy, And finally, perhaps the most ambitious out of them, both a Brazilian nuclear program and a Space Program, that shall cement Brazil's rightful place amongst the great powers of the world. And with his brand new cabinet, with both Tancredo at the helm of the Finance Ministry and the daughter of his predecessor, Edna Lott, as his VP, he has all that he needs to achieve all his goals if not even more.
strings.BRA_assemble_development_council_desc: Just like everyone always has a first, most people also have a second too. In this case, JK's first cabinet meeting has been an astounding success. It was just what Juscelino needed to remind him of his mission of progress and reinvigorate his passion and will to fulfill it whatever it may cost. Thus, there is no better moment than now to officially announce the second Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento, National Development Council, or just CD for short. A body composed of captains of industry, scientific experts, trade union bosses, and political appointees of the ruling Varguist coalition that shall council and help guide JK's many projects in the glorious road towards progress and Brazil's shining destiny.
strings.BRA_assemble_development_council_tt: The chosen members of the Development Council will meet in Brasília, beginning our first Planning Phase.
strings.BRA_announce_second_goals_plan: Announce the Segundo Programa de Metas
strings.BRA_announce_second_goals_plan_desc: With the Cabinet rightfully formed, and with all the CD members correctly appointed, JK now is more than ready to continue his job in guiding Brazil on the glorious road towards progress. There is only one thing missing, the people's morale, for if we don't have the people's support then all our efforts will be for not. They must be reminded that there's nothing that can possibly stop the Brazilian people, that there is no such great challenge that they can not possibly beat. Thus with the necessary objective of emboldening our Brazilian compatriots, there is no better action than to give a public speech in Brasília, that shall announce the “Segundo Programa de Metas”, 2nd Goals Program, with its deadlines and parameters. Such speech shall be broadcasted by radio, and the few existing Brazilian TV stations, throughout all of the nation. It shall serve as the call to action to the people and the perfect statement to raise their morale and support for the tasks to come.
strings.BRA_announce_second_goals_plan_tt: Our ambitions will be announced to the world, beginning the first Execution Phase.
strings.BRA_varguist_stands_strong_desc:
“We were elected as a coalition, and we shall govern as a coalition!”

That is the intention that dominates JK's goals in his first months. Our support and hold of the legislative for now remains strong as ever. And if we wish for it to remain in such a way then we must address the fact that although united on paper, many things could drive the PSD-PTB coalition apart.

On one hand, the PSD, influenced by its oligarch and business sector electoral base, is focused on economic and industrial development alone, thinking that Brazil is almost at the point of finally reaching “its place in the sun”. While on the other hand the PTB, influenced by the many trade unions and social movements it controls, believes that the task of reaching full industrial and economic development has been achieved, and thus that the main objective of the new administration should be to solidify and create new social programs so that the dividends of the new booming Brazilian economy may be shared by all. One of them, for the time being, must be appeased if the coalition is to remain united, however, which of them might it be remains JK's decision alone.
strings.BRA_ednas_path_to_compromise_desc: Edna Lott is not only the daughter of one of JK's most important political allies, but she is also more importantly his Vice-President. This makes her the most important and influential PTB member currently holding political office. And considering her well-known record of being a vocal and vehement activist for many social causes while also being one of the most conciliatory, rational, and cooler heads inside the PTB, especially when considering her other co-religionaries like Brizola or even Jango. Thus, she is in a perfect position, to be the person that influences and negotiates with the PTB on JK's behalf, for if they and their leadership aren't appeased the coalition and any possible dream of governing Brazil are dead.
strings.BRA_concessions_to_the_ptb_desc:
As expected, Edna did not disappoint! Her conciliatory ways pleased the moderates, saying that if they didn't support the current administration then Varguism in any shape or form is practically dead. While her staunch and vehement commitment to their noble cause pleased and calmed the radicals, stating that if they went along and achieved JK's economic objectives then the prosperity for the Brazilian people would be immense, and the bounty to be shared even larger. Thanks to her efforts the PSD-PTB coalition has stood firm and is now more united than ever.

However, our partners in the PTB are not fully satisfied. They demand an active voice in our administration and in the designing of our development plans. According to them, they wish that our plans have the interests of the Brazilian people in mind. Thus, JK has decided to give them a seat in the Developmental Council, DC. That shall satisfy them.
strings.BRA_tancredos_political_maneuvers_desc:
Tancredo Neves isn't just one of the greatest finance ministers Brazil has ever had, he is also one of Juscelino's closest friends and allies since the very beginning of his political career, but more importantly, he is also one of if not the most influential figure inside the PSD party structure. Being known for his moderate and very pragmatic stance on most issues, to the point of him being one of the very few Varguist politicians who can cross the aisle and negotiate with the UDN on friendly terms. Due to this he personally holds much sway with most PSD congressmen and in our Party's business sector benefactors.

Thus, this makes him the ideal person to help JK in making the PSD hold the line and support his administration come what may.
