The unions are stacked to the brim with Brizolist and Janguist degenerates that prioritize their own welfare and prestige over that of the nation; they are, moreover, more than willing to resist our Divinely-mandated rule over Brazil.

This must and shall be cracked down upon, until the unions know only the military as their friend and disabuse themselves of any funny ideas about relying on 'socialist solidarity' or what have you.
strings.BRA_eliminate_the_peasant_leagues_desc:
The leadership of the Peasant Leagues as it currently stands is a clear and present danger to the Republic of Brazil. The Peasant Leagues themselves are filled to the brim with communists; obviously, this makes them a clear and present danger to our economy and way and life. The military has no illusions about this. Accordingly, they have been talking to President Castelo Branco, their colleague, and have convinced him that decisive action must be taken to prevent these nuisances from turning into something more than that.

For the sake of Brazil, let the Peasant Leagues be outlawed and then eliminated. Our socio-political welfare demands it.
strings.BRA_eliminate_varguist_elements_desc:
Even while we take the unions under our more direct control, the Varguists and their degenerate, senseless personality cult remains a threat to Brazil and to our elevated and correct rule over it.

This must be put to an end; Brazil cannot be made great if Varguism is not crushed. Though we are not degenerate enough to slaughter Vargas - we will leave him in his house but keep him under watch - we are more than willing to force him to watch as his heretical, egocentric, and manifestly undeserved cult of personality is dismantled, destroyed, and left to rot for all eternity, until the people itself reject him in his old age.
strings.BRA_occupy_the_university_of_brasilia_de:
We have restricted student gatherings in an attempt to prevent them from wasting their precious time in pointless protests against a government they foolishly refuse to accept is set up for their own benefit. We have also shut down the various student unions. But they keep protesting all over the place; it is at its worst in the University of Brasília. Obviously, this cannot be tolerated.

“Shut the whole place down by deploying troops within its grounds and have done with it. That'll do to keep the little ingrates quiet,” Geisel tells us. Geisel is right. We will do just that.
strings.BRA_invite_us_advisors_desc:
The United States, the last hope of sanity and freedom amidst a decaying world oppressed by Japanese madmen on one side and Germanic egomaniacs on the other, is our strongest and staunchest ally. Even Getúlio Vargas in his rare moments of lucidity recognized this.

If we are to defend against a possible Brizolist insurrection or an invasion on our borders, we must invite US advisors to assist our military; this will improve our training methods and help strengthen our soldiers. “It will also increase our reliance on America,” you say?

Since when was that a bad thing?
strings.BRA_train_with_the_school_of_the_america: Train with the School of the Americas

If we are to defend against a possible Brizolist insurrection or an invasion on our borders, we must invite US advisors to assist our military; this will improve our training methods and help strengthen our soldiers. But that isn't all; we can also send troops to enroll at the School of the Americas in the Panama Canal Zone.

Further cooperation at that level will reinforce our prior work in improving soldier cohesion and competence. Accordingly, we have already taken out the tickets to send the first batch of officers north.
strings.BRA_control_the_press_desc:
Unfettered newspapers of the sort that Wainer and other Varguist fools promoted before our assumption of power are filled to the brim with just the type of subversives that forced us to seize control of Brazil and prioritize their own welfare and prestige over that of the nation. Obviously this cannot be tolerated for much longer, since the press is a vital part of the country that must be controlled one way or the other.

If you control the news and what people hear, the people will support you. For the sake of Brazil let the truth be made relative.
strings.BRA_parachute_in_loyal_governors_desc:
As the leadup to the passage of Institutional Act Number Two makes clear, many states are under the thrall of governors who do not put Brazil first or respect the new military government. Obviously, if they continue to hold on to power, it can only lead to one form of disaster or another.

Let us remove any and all disloyal governors throughout the states and parachute in those loyal to the State and to ARENA. However, we will leave a few opposition or ARENA dissident governors in place in unimportant states to give the illusion of an opposition.
strings.BRA_delay_the_transition_desc:
The election and transition to the next President will once more be delayed so that our current President - who is, after all, the best man for Brazil - is freed to hold on to power and make all necessary changes for the Republic and its welfare. Though that screeching jackdaw or that corrupt, pitiful excuse for a physician might throw a snit, it is worth it. Unlike them, we are acting for their benefit and that of the whole nation.

It must be done, you see. It is for the good of Brazil and its people.
There is no other reason. Treasonous accusations of 'love of power' will be afforded no tolerance.
strings.BRA_humberto_stands_defiant_desc:
“'Delay the election'? 'Hold on to power indefinitely'? Insanity! Madness! What need have we for such undemocratic, fascist- and communist-adjacent political policy? Have these insubordinate, hardline military officials no shame before Brazil or before Our most blessed Lady of Aparecida?”

“No, we will do no such thing!” President Castelo Branco shouts. “I will not contemplate, still less will I agree, to cancel the elections! Why do I need to do that when all I want is to be rid of the communists? No, the elections will proceed, and I'll see that Costa e Silva kicked to the curb for his insolence!”
strings.BRA_use_the_crows_charisma_desc:
President Castelo Branco, like most of Brazil, holds Carlos Lacerda in some contempt; with good reason, Castelo Branco believes. He has heard the strange rumors of Lacerda's behaviour towards the poor, and, like any truly good Catholic, is not entirely sure that that is the right way to go about things. And then it helps nothing that Lacerda seems a bit too friendly towards deviants and avant-gardists for his own good.

Even so, that does not detract from Lacerda's usefulness to Castelo Branco's plans. His media and charisma will more than suffice to help the President gather the support he needs to repel the hardliners.
strings.BRA_utilise_adhemars_contacts_desc:
President Castelo Branco, like most of Brazil, holds Adhemar de Barros in some contempt; with good reason, Castelo Branco believes. Corruption is well beneath any truly competent politician, after all, still less someone of Adhemar's alleged seniority. Just because one “faz”-es when one “rouba”-s, it doesn't justify the “rouba”. On the balance, Adhemar is essentially a corrupt snake.

Even so, Adhemar is still useful to the Marshal's plans. He can be convinced to use his contacts to ensure people don't join Costa e Silva in anything foolish.
strings.BRA_fire_costa_e_silva_desc:
Costa e Silva made his demands and left, yes, but he will not wait forever. Geisel tells the President that he's pacing around back and forth waiting for the elections to be cancelled any day now. But that is not what Costa e Silva will get the next time the President calls him to a meeting.

Instead, Costa e Silva will get a very nice surprise: he will be fired and forced out of military command. This will ensure the fall of the last obstacle standing in the way of normal elections.
strings.BRA_proceeding_as_planned_desc:
“'Delay the election'? 'Hold on to power indefinitely'? What insanity, what madness. What need did we have for such undemocratic, fascist- and communist-adjacent political policy? None, of course. None,” President Castelo Branco says in his peaceful office as he sits back and enjoys a glass of water.

No coup attempt has taken place. No major instability is present. No disquiet has been fomented. Having at last purged both the hardliners and the socialist-Varguist crackpots, it is time for Brazil to focus on the elections again...

...just as Castelo Branco had always planned.
strings.BRA_keeping_everything_under_control_des: After the attack at Recife International Airport and the recent attempt by Costa and the hardliners to stage an internal coup, we must keep the situation stable and under control. If Brazil were to fall into political instability, Lacerda might not be able to secure his victory and Kubitschek could win a shock victory. Not only that, but instability gives further legitimacy to the radical Nazi-communists, and that must be prevented.
strings.BRA_discussing_with_the_crow_desc: Kubitschek has already begun to present a strong opposition, and detailed discussions with Lacerda on the matter of the election and how it will play out are suggested as soon as possible. We will call Lacerda and summon him to a meeting in Brasília as soon as possible.
strings.BRA_let_the_election_play_out_desc: Lacerda's media connections, his position as governor Guanabara and the strength of the UDN, may just be enough to let the election commence without interference. This will prevent any hostile suspicions of unfair democratic practices and will lower any insatbility or fuel the far left can use against our regime.
strings.BRA_minimal_interference_desc: Unnecessary interference may backfire - those who learn of it will come to assume the election had been planned out, despite us having very little say over the will of the people this soon after seizing power. If we are to change this, we must keep out. For now.
strings.BRA_minimal_interference_tt:
Rio de Janeiro
   £BRA_udn_texticon Carlos Lacerda's popularity rises.
strings.BRA_keep_the_bull_out_desc: Adhemar Pereira de Barros has proven a popular choice, and by his means announced participation in the upcoming election. He is blissfully unaware that, at the moment, this isn't an option. He can not use his style of right wing populism to potentially split the vote with Lacerda, allowing a Kubitschek victory, just so he can make money for his hidden vault. It's fallen on us to tell him.
strings.BRA_allow_adhemar_desc: Although Adhemar Pereira de Barros is not a preferable alternative either, and does not pass many of the checks required for presidency, we cannot do much to stop him from running. His electoral campaign may however divide the left-wing Varguist vote. Adhemar is a wildcard and could harm either us or the opposition, all while he aims for his own personal wealth and not for a proper shot at the presidency this time. Let us hope it hurts them.
strings.BRA_aid_the_crow_desc: So sure of victory at first, Lacerda has conceded that some rare internal polling indicates him at a narrow loss. Despite our policy of minimal electoral interference, we must come to his aid as soon as time allows to ensure that he prevails.
strings.BRA_fine_on_his_own_desc: Lacerda is a great leader and a fine orator. His help against Costa e Silva using his natural charisma is part of the reason this election is even going ahead. Not only this but his time as governor of Guanabara has reduced homelessness rates, improved infrastructure and boosted the economy. Surely everyone can see that. Why would he need any more of our help, when he is fine on his own and when we have already given him so much?
strings.BRA_allow_a_debate_desc: The performance of an election depends more on agreement than popularity. The more transparent our vision, the better our chances. With Lacerda's media connections, hosting a radio debate between him and Kubitschek may not be that bad an idea. However, this runs the risk of the opposition candidate spreading his message on his own time. However Lacerda is a skilled enough orator that he could prevent this.
strings.BRA_keep_an_eye_on_things_desc: Although we have made it clear that Lacerda is the country's only option forward, Kubitschek has rallied nearly all opposing organizations behind him. If we do not pay attention to his actions, we may find ourselves trapped.
strings.BRA_the_crow_new_look_desc: Lacerda's current vision aligns far too much with what many consider 'status quo'. This is not good for appearances. By making widespread populist promises and creating new policies, we can prep Lacerda for a fresher show before the media.
strings.BRA_use_them_to_our_advantage_desc: When we do a little trickery, the pieces come together. By allowing the military to send covert and anonymous support to small left-wing candidates, we can diminish the Kubitschek vote while also making the election look fairer. This paradoxical plan is perfect.
strings.BRA_use_them_to_our_advantage_tt:
Northeast
   Minor Left Candidates' popularities rise.
strings.BRA_suppress_the_left_desc: Supporting left-wing splinter groups may run the risk of them growing, and eventually aligning themselves with the rest of the opposition and even giving them legitimacy and pushing more into the communist movement. By keeping them divided and weak, we can tackle one threat at a time.
strings.BRA_a_bridge_too_far_desc: Direct actions against Kubitschek have proved to be a mistake, disrupting the election cycle and threatening the possibility of maintaining control even within the upcoming year. We must do all we can to pose a better strategy for this process, and the projects to come.
strings.BRA_work_against_kubitschek_desc: Fellow officers and hardliner generals such as Sílvio Frota have advised to directly work against Kubitschek and his campaign. This will almost certainly ensure Lacerda's chances at an inauguration.
strings.BRA_use_the_envelope_system_desc: In conscript's terms, the 'envelope system' used by Adhemar is essentially bribery, used as a way of gaining support. Utilizing this may be either our last-minute resort or additional effort to ensure Lacerda gains better chances.
strings.BRA_eternal_vigilance_desc: Although the coup has secured the Sorbonne's power, radicalisation and political violence still roams free. Overlooking the state of affairs to ensure political violence does not disrupt the flow of plans is the preferable option. “The price of freedom is eternal vigilance.”
strings.BRA_keep_the_integralists_happy_desc: Although the Far Right movement and paramilitaries such as the CCC is not without controversy, they have helped secure control of the country in the weeks following the coup. To keep them on our side, however, we must pay a substantial amount in political influence and monetary funds
strings.BRA_and_the_communists_quiet_desc: If we are to prevail, we must repress the hardline opposition with the full extent of our force, to ensure they cannot influence other extremist factions that may align themselves against us in the long run.
strings.BRA_cool_down_the_north_desc: Communist saboteurs have long threatened Brazilian democracy - and our reports have indicated their general location. More and more reports of communists are occuring from army commands in the north. We will transfer our means of repression in their direction to ensure victory against their threat and ensure they make no attack on election day.
strings.BRA_cool_down_the_north_tt:
Bahia
   Minor Left Candidates' popularities fall.
strings.BRA_guard_the_polling_stations_desc: Major clashes at polling stations would result in a public relations disaster and embarrass the military authorities for not being able to hold up peace. By limiting the influence of protesters over polling stations, we may also be able to stop extremists from voting altogether.
strings.BRA_soldiers_on_high_alert_desc: When election day comes, soldiers have already been placed on high alert, patrolling for possible ploys, assassination attempts, or poll violence. With military assistance in peacekeeping, and the intimidation meant to secure democratic processes, a smooth transition of power - to our candidate - will soon occur.
strings.BRA_silva_victorious_desc:
The unworthy Humberto de Alencar Castelo Branco, who was too soft of head and hear to lead our country, now leaves the Presidency of the Republic of Brazil in ignominy, shaking his head in disgust as his former subordinate, Artur da Costa e Silva, takes power.

Costa e Silva had been the target of an unjust, militarily ridiculous plot by the previous President to force his resignation. However, the new President had enough support to force Branco out instead.

Now the victorious Costa e Silva is free to fix the problems Brazil faces.
strings.BRA_silva_victorious_tt: Humberto rolled snake eyes and now Silva is in control.
strings.BRA_ban_political_parties_desc:
The new President is of the conviction that all political parties are worthless and potential threats. Even ostensibly loyal parties such as the UDN can serve as an umbrella beneath which potential opponents can come in and wreak havoc, organizing against our government and handing the whole country over to the Hitlerites and communists.

This possibility, of course, cannot be tolerated. Banning these organizations - left, right, or centre - will ensure that the opposition is kept disorganized and most political plots are kept at the stage of imagination only.
strings.BRA_exile_the_opposition_desc:
The degenerates that forced us to seize control of Brazil, that prioritized their own welfare and prestige over that of the nation, have absolutely zero, z-e-r-o, place in the Brazil that we are going to build. Good-for-nothing scum such as Jânio Quadros, Carlos Lacerda, and Juscelino Kubitschek, will be made to realize their failure to serve and love the country and its leadership disqualify them from being referred to as truly Brazilian.

And countless other fools will follow them. Let the motto of the new order in Brazil become thus: “Brasil, ame-o ou deixe-o” - “Brazil, love it or leave it”!
strings.BRA_close_the_legislature_desc:
The Congress is the symbol of everything wrong in this country. Corruption. Nepotism. Inefficiency.

At the start of the Revolution, the rot began from it; not a single moment passed where the Congress did not egg the Brazilian government to further and further depths of corruption and folly. And then of course the rule of the degenerate Getúlio Vargas and his cronies only worsened the situation.

This cannot be borne any longer. Until a more opportune time, let this accursed pesthole of folly and immorality be shut down. There is no need for anyone but one or two cleaners to be there.
strings.BRA_integrate_loyalist_conservatives_des:
It is true that even ostensibly loyal parties such as the UDN can serve as an umbrella beneath which potential opponents can come in and wreak havoc, organizing against our government and handing the whole country over to the Hitlerites and communists.

On the other hand, beneath that potentially treasonous umbrella there are also faithful and true conservatives, men who understand the necessity of our actions and the need to suppress the Amazonist-adjacent leftist faction.

Let them be taken under our umbrella and induced to join hands with our regime. This will ensure us significant support from large segments of Brazilian society.
strings.BRA_nationwide_censorship_desc:
Unfettered newspapers of the sort that Lacerda and other democratic imbeciles promoted before our assumption of power are filled to the brim with just the type of degenerates that forced us to seize control of Brazil and prioritize their own welfare and prestige over that of the nation. Obviously this too cannot be tolerated for much longer.

Let everything and anything be censored until only what the state agrees with and permits to be published is published. This is certain to help curtail dissent.
strings.BRA_weaken_the_sorbonne_desc:
The Sorbonne, though not as insane as the Amazonists, are still a threat. After all, they supported our weak-minded former President in his attempt to restore democracy to Brazil. On the other hand, they are still good military men, and their influence is nothing to sneeze at. Let us try to weaken it.

Moving Geisel from the armed forces to the Supreme Military Tribunal (without demotion, of course; this is not a purge) and placing our own man in charge of his SNI will probably be of great help in defending our nation's interests. It'll also no doubt provide that poor life-hating, misanthropic bastard with a well-deserved rest from his labours.
strings.BRA_implement_martial_law_desc:
We have gone far, but it is nowhere near enough.

Unless we take direct, decisive action, our nation will burn. The communist bastards are plotting a revolution and we need to stop them.

“Do you mean the Brizolistas?” we hear you ask.

Yes and no, we reply. To us a communist and a fascist is anyone that dares defy the Brazilian government or disagree with our control over it.

To President Artur da Costa e Silva, the way is clear. Martial law must be declared to save the nation, he says; he is right, and so it will be done. A temporary suspension of civil liberties and implementation of martial law will be necessary to destroy the plotters trying to ruin our nation from the inside.

And it will persist for as long as is necessary to protect the glory of the Brazilian nation from all that would attack it.
strings.BRA_announce_the_second_programa_de_meta: Announce the Second Programa de Metas
strings.BRA_the_quadros_presidency_desc:
Jânio Quadros is now President! Misunderstood by many, mocked by more than a few, and underestimated by all, the former teacher has been elected to the nation's highest office.

There is much work to be done. The economy must see liberalizing reforms, the vampiric state hacked apart to allow small business owners and ordinary Brazilians to break free from mountains of debts and taxes. Corrupt officials must be purged before they can discredit the ship of state any further. This economic renewal must be combined with a moral renewal, as the nation rediscovers its Christian roots, the ties that bind us all in the great project of civilization.

To this domestic renewal we will marry a strong foreign policy. Brazil must be a leader of the global south, a colossus among nations breaking free from a colonial heritage and into their wonderful destinies. The super powers, the great eagles of America, Japan and Germany shall be forced to deal with us as equals. Brazil's honor demands it.

And President Quadros will make it so.
strings.BRA_anti_corruption_campaign_desc:
Perhaps the greatest pillar of domestic policy for President Quadros remains the fight against corruption.

At all level of society corruption saps the trust that ordinary Brazilians have about the government. Greedy tax officials, purchasable police officers, amoral judges; all serve as examples of our nation's failure to live up to its goals of equity and justice.

President Quadros plans to strike at the roots by reducing government spending, the endless fount of wealth that has lured the corrupt and ambitious during Kubitschek and Lott's presidencies. Quadros also plans to eradicate those that have already been tainted by the vice. A great anti-corruption campaign will begin, dismissing any public servant or government employee found tainted.

No matter the cost, the spread of this plague must be halted. The lord willing we shall triumph over the enemies of society.
strings.BRA_use_presidential_decrees_desc:
The start of our great crusade against corruption must come from new laws against this kind of criminality. However, this places our President in a problematic situation.

The congress has never done anything against corruption, and it is likely that many of its members are corrupt to the bone. Asking them to legislate on the matter would be akin to asking the foxes to keep an eye on the hen house. This delicate situation requires a different approach.

Quadros will use his presidential power to take action by decree. This will allow him to move rapidly and avoid dealing with corrupt self-serving politicians. The opposition senators and the supreme court will no doubt argue some of the President's actions are unconstitutional. This does not worry our government too much. Let the fools come out on the public record as allies of corruption and inaction. President Quadros will only be strengthened by this.
strings.BRA_consult_the_udn_desc:
Purity of morals and actions is a desirable dream, but not one often possible in this crass mortal world. Knowing that the perfect is the enemy of the good, President Quadros has decided to discuss with the UDN the upcoming anti-corruption campaign.

Many politicians of the UDN have no doubt been skimming a little too much off the top. Letting those scoundrels prepare themselves for the upcoming storm by destroying evidence irks Quadros. Yet this is an important step. The President's PTN party is small, much smaller than the UDN. While elected on the basis of his personal popularity, President Quadros must work with the UDN as a part of his coalition if he's to achieve anything.

Keeping the UDN on friendly terms is worth a few sacrifices.
strings.BRA_only_when_neccessary_desc:
The upcoming anti-corruption campaign is sure to hit a great deal of politicians. Many of them will be within the UDN, Brazil's leading conservative party and President Quadros' begrudging coalition partners. The President has no pity for corrupt men, no matter how politically convenient.

The UDN will not be warned of the upcoming anti-corruption probe. The guilty will have their day in court, no matter their political party. This is likely to infuriate the UDN, and Lacerda's newspaper will no doubt attack the President over this. Let the Crow squawk as long as he cares to; the anti-corruption campaign must not be tarnished by petty politics.

President Quadros has many enemies. Let us be comforted that many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the Lord delivers his faithfuls out of them all.
strings.BRA_create_an_anti_corruption_ministry_d:
The anti-corruption crusade draws to an end. Our thorough sweep has flushed out corrupt politicians and bureaucrats at all levels of society. Great progress has been made in our efforts to clean Brazil's economic life. That said, our government now enters the most difficult part: consolidating our gains.

Arresting so many corrupt officials through presidential decree has worked out well enough. However, to make lasting institutional changes President Quadros desires to build a permanent task force whose mandate would be keeping Brazilian politics clean. Such an organization will require congressional funding to operate throughout the entire country and to have enough bite to back its bark.

Skeptics may point to the political class's irritation with President Quadros as an obstacle to passing the bill in the Senado. Surely our opponents are mistaken. The senators, the ones we haven't caused to go jail, will certainly be convinced to lend their strength to our cause.
strings.BRA_proclaim_the_ifp_desc:
All his political career, Quadros has pursued the dream of an Independent Foreign Policy. Of a Brazil unshackled from automatic alignment with America and its neocolonialist ambitions. President Lott looking to Japan for funding was a small start; it falls to President Quadros to go out in the wider world to talk with nations big and small to pursue the interest of a strong Brazil.

This will generate strong opposition both within Brasília and in Washington D.C. President Quadros will not be moved, however. Our great southern republic must seek its own path throughout these turbulent times. While the great American republican and democratic project will always be an inspiration, Brazilians must remember that only through a cautious balancing of rival powers can they find the breathing room for their country to grow in stature and prestige.

The Independent Foreign Policy, or IFP, has arrived. Let the great adventure begin!
strings.BRA_an_african_adventure_desc:
Africa, the cradle of humanity, has lost a century to the basest of colonial behaviours. Yet the light of hope and freedom endures in the heart of all Africans and within the nations of Sub-Saharan Africa.

The end of the German bombings in Western Africa have left us an opportunity, as fledgling states expand in the area. By being one of the first countries to openly offer our help and friendship, we can make great gains in the new Africa and ensure that Brazil is a strong player in the South Atlantic.

Some may accuse our government of jumping with both feets into a tangled mess of post-colonial conflict and great power shadow politics. Those fools are simply unable to grasp the importance of the Independent Foreign Policy to our future.
strings.BRA_condemn_colonialism_desc:
Colonialism has been one of the defining evils of the modern era. The subjugation of countries in the Americas, in Asia and Africa by self-aggrandized bullies has unfortunately endured into the post war era as new players such as Germany and Italy have expanded their holdings in Africa.

Our government will condemn colonialism at full strength, especially on African soil. Uncompromising support for newly independent African states will no doubt endear us to local leaders. This, however, is likely to have a cost, as the Italian Empire is one of the few non-aligned independent powers we seek to court for our Independent Foreign Policy.

Denouncing colonialism will irritate the Italians and delay our efforts to get closer to them. This is the cost of truth, honesty, and full brotherhood between all nations.
strings.BRA_a_more_cautious_approach_desc:
Colonialism is a great evil, but also a multi-faceted system whose dismantling will take time and a cautious approach. Nations such as Italy are both perpetrators of colonialism as well as important independent poles of power in an increasingly radicalized world. Equally important are nations such as South Africa who are examples of minority ruled nations that stand outside the American or German systems of empire. The needs of the Independent Foreign Policy makes rapprochement with those nations crucial to President Quadros' goals.

We will thus measure our words. Colonialism will be sternly opposed, but the specifics will have to remain vague for now. We will have harsh words for the German empire, leaving our options open with regards to other colonialist powers. The people of Africa, used to playing colonial powers one against the others, will surely understand our prudence.
strings.BRA_reach_out_to_cameroon_desc:
It is often times as difficult to get news from the African interior as it is to obtain information on what is going on in Central Siberia. Nevertheless both region have vastly profited from the German retreat, of late.

North of what had once been Reichskommissariat Zentralafrika stands the Cameroon African State. A beacon of anti-colonialism in the region, the Cameroonians have fought for years now against Germans as well as French, Italian and American influence in the region. As such Cameroon has been shackled with an unfair reputation as a rogue nation. We must reach out to Cameroon and reiterate our support for all those that oppose colonialism!
strings.BRA_ban_the_bikini_desc:
A specter haunts Brazil.

Throughout the nation's beaches, an evil ideology from Europe infects our youth. Left unchecked, this movement will ruin our country as surely as communism or fascism would. We speak of nothing other than the fashion trend of the Crimini.

A devilish piece of garment invented in France as a confirmation of their nation's degradation, the Crimini has spread over to Brazil. Our young men, the finest flower of Brazilian manhood, spend their days mocked by a vulgar display of crude feminine wiles. Their precious spiritual essence is being stolen away from them!

Banning the Crimini is but the first step in President Quadros' restoration of proper Christian mores. Police officers will be empowered to patrol the nation's coastline in search of these immoral swimmers, these rapidly proliferating salt water weeds. The battle for Brazil's soul has begun!
strings.BRA_embrace_opus_dei_thought_desc:
An organization founded some four decades ago, the Opus Dei has grown into one of the most quietly influential groups within the Catholic Church. Encouraging their members to seek the divine in day to day life, and to do one's best in professional life, the Opus Dei has cautiously entered the political arena through the development of a new political philosophy.

Arguing that Christian law does not apply to the secular world, the Opus Dei argues for liberalization, for free markets and for a moral society led by talented and pious men. This line of thinking is very agreeable to President Quadros' view of Brazil's future. Some may criticize the Opus Dei for remaining silent on the Iberian dictatorship; President Quadros sees this restraint from the public sphere as evidence of them rendering unto Caesar what is his.

At the heart of being a pious man, after all, is doing one's best to follow the Lord's plan.
strings.BRA_outlaw_gambling_desc:
The honest man seeks not any other source of money than the day's honest wage. Yet there are those that remain obsessed by the desire for rapid gain. Such desires conceive and give birth to sin, and that sin when it reaches full growth can give birth to death.

The sin of gambling does more than break up families and enrich organized crime. It damages the immortal soul of those it has ensnared. It is thus a moral imperative for President Quadros to strike at the heart of this societal ill.

Unfortunately gambling is also a very popular pastime. Eradicating it will be difficult. Some say the attempt is futile. The moral imperative remains, however, to do as best as one can to save fellow citizens from damnation. No matter the political cost, or backlash to the edict, President Quadros will ban gambling and dedicate additional police resources to crack down on illegal gambling operations. The poor souls addicted to this vice will have to find strength in the lord to free themselves from this earthly poison.
strings.BRA_travel_to_cuba_desc:
Not even two hundred kilometers from Florida lies the island of Cuba. Its leader, Fidel Castro, has surprised the world through his successful revolution against the forces of Fulgencio Batista. Taking place in America's backyard as it has, the Cuban Revolution has maintained a good neighbor policy with the American giant to the northwest. Even so, Castro remains one of the rare leaders in the Americas to stand independent of America.

Some may decry Castro as a socialist, a populist and an autocrat. President Quadros understands that providence works through mysterious agents, and that Fidel Castro represents a new breed of leaders in and around the continent. The Independent Foreign Policy demands closer ties between Brazil and Cuba, to establish our own credentials as an independent voice in the chorus of nations.
strings.BRA_a_pawn_makes_its_first_move: A Pawn Makes Its First Move
strings.BRA_upholding_our_end_of_the_bargain: Upholding Our End of the Bargain
strings.BRA_expand_the_franchise_goulart_desc: In principle, every Brazilian receives exactly one vote to speak their mind in our democracy. In practice, disenfranchised and marginalized groups, such as soldiers, the elderly or illiterate, struggle daily to attain suffrage. It is as much their country as it is ours.
strings.BRA_the_voting_rights_bill_desc: Our legislation concerning pending voting rights is finally complete, and it is time to present it to Congress. Although the bill puts us in a susceptible spot in view of the remaining opposition, we have plans for the country regardless. Let us retain our eyes open.
strings.BRA_keep_an_eye_on_the_military: Keep an Eye on the Military
strings.BRA_keep_an_eye_on_the_military_desc: If the military were not opposed to Goulart by the hurdle of the new regime, we have surely antagonized them through our bills, speeches and proposals now, with a possible few exceptions. By accumulating the defense ministry's top brass behind our cause and keeping open tabs on the situation, we can avoid a potential catastrophe.
strings.BRA_the_stick_for_the_lot_of_them: The Stick For the Lot of Them
strings.BRA_the_land_calls_to_us_desc: i am the lorax and i speak for the land
strings.BRA_no_its_us_who_have_a_point: No, It's US Who Have a Point
strings.BRA_a_kettle_of_fish_for_everyone: A Kettle of Fish for Everyone
strings.BRA_black_gold_in_the_green_land: Black Gold in the Green Land
strings.BRA_olive_branch_to_the_cherry_blossom: Olive Branch to the Cherry Blossom
strings.BRA_que_luta_contra_os_governos_populare: Que Luta Contra Os Governos Populares
strings.BRA_65_candidate_no_content_tt: Developer note: this candidate has no content after winning the 1965 election.
strings.BRA_colombia.1.desc:
It was already a long and tumultuous day for {bra_getleader}, after all, being the leader of Brazil was no easy task. But it seemed that he must now shift his worries outside the land of 'order and progress.' Just as he entered his office in the Planalto, he was met with generals from all over the country, from the Amazonian jungle to the Riograndense pampas. On his table, there were at least ten different maps of Colombia, each differing only in the most minute details.

“Good evening Mr. President, I hope your day has been tranquil. Please, have a seat.” said one of the generals as they pulled a chair for {bra_getleader}. “Let's get on with this already, shall we?”

“As you may know from the news, the illusion of peace in Colombia is about to come to an end. Capitão Salcedo's forces have been engaged in heavy combat with the Central Government for the last few days, and it's only going to get worse with each bullet that leaves their guns.” - explained the general - “With the collapse of the 1957 ceasefire imminent, it's crucial that we increase our involvement in the conflict and ensure that the victor will be amenable to our interests.”

“I must recommend that we support the Revolutionary Union, they-”

“Those Varguists all buddy-buddy with communist bandits? Give me a break!” - One general yelled in protest - “We shouldn't be helping out their lot, their only goal is being the ones doing the looting! If anyone is going to help us, it's the government in Bogotá. They've been a bastion of anti-communism and stability ever since the war started. If it weren't for those...”

“Have you forgotten what Gaitán meant to this damn continent? He may have been a socialist, but he fought for unity in the Americas and democracy, now his dream's under attack by the very fascists he was warning us of. We should be promoting democratic governments around this continent, not tinpot dictators.”

The general who had protested scoffed as soon as the other described the Revolutionary Union as “democratic”, then turned to the president. “Well, which one will it be, Mr. President?”

As he held his chin with his hands, {bra_getleader} responded:
strings.BRA_colombia.1.c: “We need to think more about this.”
strings.BRA_colombia.1.e_tt: The Armed Forces already have enough to deal with internally, best not to entangle ourselves in Colombia as well.
strings.BRA_colombia.2.d:
“Listen, Mr. President, I'm telling you that every other option is either a sockpuppet for the Iberians, the Italians, even worse, the Germans,” one general exclaimed to the Crow, who couldn't stop cawing.

“So you're telling me our only option are the goddamned Gaitanistas? This war is already lost, then. I am absolutely not approving this. I loved Gaitán like everyone else, but they're fools if they can't see that his followers are worse than Varguists!” the Crow continued to caw as the generals tried to explain the same thing over and over. Minutes passed until, eventually, the Crow seemed to have run out of energy, one general noticed this and took the opportunity to explain the necessity to support the Revolutionaries.

“I hate those populistic socialists as much as you do, but we must be pragmatic when it comes to who we support in this continent. We don't know how Colombia could end up if we just choose to ignore it. The CRU is a wide front, the Gaitanistas have made clear they are only in an alliance of convenience with those Bolsheviks. Dr. Michelsen has made clear his intentions to end the arrangement once the war is over.

After one cup of water to help his hoarse voice, the Crow chirped: ”Right, well. I suppose it's better take our chances with them than risk finding out what flavor of tinpot dictator we can end up with. You have my authorization, then.“

”Thank you, Mr. President,“ said one of the generals as they left the room, leaving Lacerda to think for himself.
strings.BRA_colombia.2.a: “A self-serving Varguist is the best that country could scrounge up...”
strings.BRA_colombia.3.desc:
There's a kind of hush that settles over a land immediately after war. People stumble out of their shelters and foxholes, tentative steps towards their old routines, instinctively dreading the moment in which chaos returns once again. A man might lose control of his horses, his mind occupied by the wife he lost in a skirmish, and the entire town locks themselves away against the stampede. Fishermen and tappers hesitate to set sail across the border in the Amazonas. Burned-out villages and towns reduced to rubble litter the landscape, the memory of their past fading as the days pass.

Bogotá felt that hush at first. People walked hesitantly, close to the entrances of buildings, ready to dive into cover once the shooting started again. But slowly, people understood that it was over. Brazil's men won in Colombia, and peace was in their foreseeable future.

And with peace came foreign investment. Though foreign the encroaching foreign ships startled many residents of the Colombia's ruined ports, the Brazilians came bearing heavy purses, not weapons of war, ready to help the rebuilding effort and reap a good reward in response. Delegations met in the least-affected hotels of Bogotá to draw up trade deals, presidents exchanged telephone calls to congratulate Colombia on their newfound victory.

There's still a hesitation in the air. La Violencia clouds the minds of many Colombians. Indeed, for many not enjoying the luxury of an urban sprawl, the conflict persists. Yer for those lucky few, an alluring sentiment beckons. The call of peace, of a world once present only in their dreams. One where they needn't fear the return of paramilitaries, burning families alive in their homes and pillaging what scraps the flames leave behind. A world without nightmares...
strings.BRA_colombia.3.a: One they will work to turn into reality.
strings.BRA_colombia.4.desc:
Less than a mile north of the Cuiari River was a small campfire around which lost sons of Brazil huddled for warmth. The collapse of the frontlines had driven them all into the jungle, in a pathetic display of panic and disorganisation that saw agents and officers of the Brazilian army stranded in the Colombian jungle. On the edge of the camp's light Lieutenant Vitor Pires Cabral carved his and six other names into a tree with his clip-point knife: LEAL, ALVARES, CLEMENTE, MARTINS, FONTANA, ESTEVES. He expected them all to die; he did not want them all to be forgotten.

The other six gathered around the campfire and discussed their next move. All were in broad agreement that they had two options: follow the Cuiari to the Amazon, and follow the waters to somewhere populated. Risky, for they may risk capture by the enemy, no doubt patrolling for the stragglers they routed on the battlefield. Leal proposed the other option: they head south, through the jungle, and hope they hit Brazil.

Álvares pointed to the map, pointed out they are only twenty klicks from the Içana River, within Brazil's borders. Clemente chewed them both out: don't they know how lost they are in the jungle? Martins tried to calm them all down, but cannot deny that he thinks entering a town is dangerous if they are allied with the new government. Fontana pointed out the obvious: whatever the outcome, if they stay here, they are dead.

When Cabral returned to the group, Esteves was putting out the fire. He told him to rest up. They will march south at first light. He crawled into his bedroll and tried to go to sleep, but chirping insects, soft rains and the fear of an enemy patrol kept him from truly resting.
strings.BRA_colombia.4.a: So close to home, yet so far away.
strings.BRA_colombia.5.desc:
Adhemar de Barros was rearranging his desktop when his phone rang for the fifth time today. “Good afternoon, Mr. President.” The Colombian Ambassador greeted warmly. “From all of us, we hope you're settling well into your new office.” Adhemar chuckled, already wondering what they wanted from him. He still decided to play along.

“I certainly am.” He responded, leaning back in his leather chair. “Likewise, I hope all is going well back home.” There was an awkward silence as the ambassador seemingly steeled himself. “Hello?”

“Truth be told, Mr. President, things could be far better here.” The Ambassador admitted. Away from the telephone's receiver, Adhemar snorted and nodded his head. It was Colombia, things were never going well there. “We understand that the previous administration has been sending aid to the Revolutionary Union.”

Adhemar flipped through a stack of papers on an intelligence brief, withdrawing the one on Colombia. “We ask you to shift your aid to the government here in Bogotá. It's in our mutual interest.” The President withdrew another paper from the stack as the Ambassador continued his pitch. A half-written memo asking for abandonment of the leftist radicals. “If you are still unconvinced, It will also be in your interest, Mr. President. We can guarantee a possible... gift for your generosity.” Adhemar grinned, withdrawing his pen.

“You have my word. Today will mark the day of a great partnership.”
strings.BRA_colombia.5.a: “Thank you, Mr. President. We promise you won't regret this decision.”
strings.BRA_colombia.6.desc:
“Good afternoon Mr. President. I hope you're getting settled in nicely.” Lincoln Gordon greeted. Carlos Lacerda took his notepad and a pencil. If the American Ambassador called personally, it would be important. “I've been told that you've been briefed accordingly on the situation in Colombia?” Lacerda exhaled.

“Yes I have, Mr. Gordon.” Lacerda responded, pinching the bridge of his nose. God, what a mess. So far, he hadn't modified any policy of the previous administration. Security on the border, and arms to the Bogotá government. “Is there anything further I need to know?” There was a moment of silence before Gordon spoke.

“Actually, I have a request from Washington, Mr. President.” The ambassador answered. “We'd like you to shift support from the central government to the Revolutionary Union. They're far more co-operative.” Lacerda grimaced, scrawling down “URC support” on his notepad. “That's all we ask, Mr. President. Have a good day.”

“You as well, Mr. Gordon.” Lacerda placed the phone down, looking at the three letters before him. He knew firsthand that socialists were dangerous people. Yet, if the United States was willing to support the Union, that meant they wouldn't be causing trouble for Brazil should they take control of the country. Besides, it would be far more dangerous for Lacerda to oppose their most powerful friend.
strings.BRA_colombia.6.a: He punched in the number for Intelligence.
strings.BRA_colombia.7.desc:
The Itamaraty Palace was quieter than usual, aside from the sound of shuffled papers and murmurs, but President Lott knew that the peace and quiet wouldn't last for much longer. A series of maps and folders documenting the factions in Colombia's Violencia clutter across different desks and bulletin boards. Brazil, officially, had yet to support any faction in the conflict publicly, but had no plans to let fascism run over its northern neighbor. What was not determined, however, was who to support.

“The Americans have made their position on the matter clear,” Salles began while gesturing to a map detailing the Revolutionaries' movements and positions in Colombia's jungles, “the Gaitanists are their favorites in this fight, and our safest bet once the battle lines start shifting again.”

“Safest? For whom?” Jair Ribero shook his head, “They're in bed with radicals almost as bad as the fascist rats, with just as much potential for harm.” The general continued as he pointed a finger at a photo of a military man giving an address before a crowd in Colombia's capital, “If this is about making sure who gets to rule Bogotá, we should side with the man who already holds it; he's shaping up to be another Floriano Peixoto from what we've seen of him.”

Lott perked up at the comparison and rubbed his chin before Salles spoke up again. “The Yankees find him a touch unpredictable; they're set on working with the Reds. It wouldn't be impossible to change their minds, but Pinilla would need to do a lot of convincing to make it happen.”
strings.BRA_colombia.7.a: “Bogotá has potential, let's try to set up a line between him and Washington.”
strings.BRA_colombia.7.b: “The Americans have it right, we'll support the Gaitanists.”
strings.BRA_colombia.8.desc:
The Itamaraty Palace was quieter than usual, aside from the sound of shuffled papers and murmurs. A series of maps and folders documenting the factions in Colombia's Violencia clutter across different desks and bulletin boards. Brazil, officially, had yet to support any faction in the conflict publicly, but had no plans to let fascism run over its northern neighbor. What was not determined, however, was who to support.

Never one to enjoy a long silence, President Lacerda made his feelings on the matter known. “Those Gaitanists aren't any better than those Justicialists in Argentina,” he began with a huff, “the day they can establish a working democracy is the day pigs can fly.” The rest of the room responded with a round of nodding heads and murmurs of agreement, before another voice broke through.

“Be that as it may, the Americans are dead set on them,” Magalhães shrugged his shoulders. “The only other choice that isn't wearing lederhosen or some different type of fascist is {col_getleader}, and they don't trust him.”

“And they shouldn't! He's no different from the bastards in Iberia!”

“Be that as it may,” Golbery interjected, “if we could get ourselves and the Americans a foot in the door inside of his government, it could be a real boost to the liberals and other moderates in Bogotá. Maybe they could put a leash on his worst parts.”
strings.BRA_colombia.8.a: “Better than the Reds, let's see if he and Washington can play nice.”
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Folder.101: The End of the Third Republic
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.1:
During the Estado Novo, Brazil had stronger economic ties to the United States than its President Getúlio Vargas had to the fascist states in Europe.

Significant commercial deals in 1939 and the purchase of surplus guns to Brazil in March 1940 led the Germans to conclude that Brazil was firmly on the side of the Allies. Accordingly, Brazilian ships, civilian and military, were torpedoed by U-boats under the policy of unrestricted submarine warfare. This led Vargas to lead Brazil into joining the Allies in 1942.

Three army divisions formed the Brazilian Expeditionary Force, which arrived in Britain and fought the Germans when Sealion was launched. Under the leadership of generals such as Castelo Branco and Henrique Lott, the “Smoking Snakes” fought well; however, it was not enough. The Allies were pushed back, and the Axis won in 1945.
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.2:
Despite foreign policy successes in Latin America and with the United States, Brazil suffered economically from the war. Trade embargoes and American economic downturns combined with inflation to create a disaster.

This, combined with Vargas' hypocrisy in sending troops to fight for democracy while running an authoritarian dictatorship at home, led to a loss of civilian and military support. In 1949, achievements such as the creation of Petrobras were disrupted by the attempted assassination of journalist Carlos Lacerda, ordered by one of Vargas' men without his knowledge.

After the ensuing chaos the military staged a coup. Vargas initally said he would resist and nearly shot himself. In the end, he resigned and fled to São Paulo, before moving to São Borja, where he now resides. A compromise constitution was hastily drafted; elections were held in 1950, resulting in the election of the UDN's Eduardo Gomes as President.
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Folder.102: The Chaotic Fifties - The Fourth Republic
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.3:
Eduardo Gomes, the new President, was an air force man well-used to plotting. At first allied to Vargas, he rejected him during the Estado Novo. One of his first acts as President was to use so-called 'National Security Laws' to ban the PCB after its surprise success in the elections.

Gomes' prime aims were to deal with the economic crisis and align with the U.S. He acted to slow inflation, attracted U.S. and other private investment, and rebuffed Lacerda's demands to privatize Petrobras. He also increased the size of the military and allowed America access to bases in the north.

But Gomes also signed the party's death warrant in one foolish move. In 1953, acting with the backing of the UDN, he abolished the minimum wage implemented by Vargas post-WW2. This caused a mass popular revolt, sunk Gomes' attempt to join the OFN, and ultimately lost the 1955 election. The Varguists regained power under Juscelino Kubitschek of the PSD.
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.4: Many UDN members and conservative military officers, outraged at the Varguist victory—which they feared was a harbinger of a “Nazi communist” takeover—attempted a coup, which was foiled by the constitutionalist minister of War, Marshal Henrique Lott, with backing from Odílio Denys and other officers.
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.5:
Kubitschek promised a Varguist restoration and “fifty years of progress in five”. Mass foreign investment, industrial and infrastructural development, imports of tools, and, crucially, the construction of the new capital Brasília led to rapid economic growth at the cost of a rise of inflation to 45%.

In foreign policy, when the U.S. rejected further investment to focus on the WRW, the Japanese took over, resulting in détente. However, no such improvement was seen with the Germans; as the African RKs took hold and West African order broke down, illegal fishing vessels and pirates entered the Brazilian waters from 1959, causing the Lobster War.
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.6:
Marshal Henrique Lott won the 1960 election for the Varguists by rallying the PTB and exploiting the fact that Juracy Magalhães, the candidate of the anti-Varguist UDN, was no more charismatic than he. However, Lott's running mate João Goulart was felled by the idiosyncratic Jânio Quadros, a member of the UDN-aligned PTN.

Now, within the coalition Goulart and Leonel Brizola push him towards the left and Kubitschek sits around in expectation of a second presidency in 1965. Lott's fellow “Pessedista” Tancredo Neves is practically the only person he can totally rely upon.

Outside the coalition, there are anti-democratic elements in the military, who are just waiting to succeed where the coup of '55' failed. Worse yet, politicians such as the wildly corrupt opportunist Adhemar de Barros of the PSP and the perennial nuisance Carlos Lacerda of the UDN are willing to back them if they can see something in it for themselves.
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.7:
Domestically, Brazil's situation is mixed. The economy is dealing with high inflation. Tancredo Neves was able to cut inflation by 8% in 1961, but further reductions will be needed if the developmentalist industrialization of the Lott administration is not to be brought to naught.

One of the largest initiatives currently being pushed by the President is the Trans-Amazonian Highway that is planned to cross the continent. This has garnered a lot of support but met with resistance from natives and Lacerda, who calls it typical Varguist waste.

Finally, in 1961 Lott was faced with coffee strikes paralysing one of the largest sectors of the Brazilian economy. To get the strikes to end for the time being, he pledged—despite his own views—to push through land reform. How this succeeds or fails will no doubt be a determining factor of his administration.
strings.BRA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.8:
As has been the case for several decades, Brazil is broadly aligned with the OFN and America, primarily due to common military training (the military is more pro-American than politicians) and deep socio-economic links. However, Brazil is not cowed by their American allies and has the latitude to oppose America when there are differences.

Significant Japanese investment is welcomed by even pro-OFN politicians such as Lott and Kubitschek and there is therefore strong pro-Japan sentiment. No such sympathy is spared for Germany, who frequently denounces Brazil for its 'mongrelization'. Brazilian efforts in the Lobster War have total support.

Brazil aspires towards Latin American economic integration; its aim in this is to strengthen economies and increase Latin countries' global influence. However, this does not extend to Argentina; there, foreign-policy conflicts are hardening into what is being known as the South American Cold War.
strings.BRA_Hegemon_of_South_America_desc:
The bells of war toll as Brazilians march in their millions to fight for their motherland's status as hegemon of South America. They are joined hand-in-hand by those nations persuaded or forced into Brazil's arms by the Itamaraty, spinning tales about the havoc an unchallenged Argentina will wreak upon the continent without a police to watch over them, to stop their evil.

It is a battle they will not use; God is on their side, the side of the righteous who will inherit South America.
strings.BRA_SAW_begin_blockade_desc: Admiral Toscano will be charged with organizing a partial naval blockade of the Afrika-Schild's Atlantic ports, blocking resupply from Germania or its allies.
strings.BRA_saw_blockade_desc: With Brazil's intervention in the South African War, Brazilian ships have begun to restrict trade and resources reaching our nations. This has begun to severely impact our industrial production and will strangle us in the long run unless we win soon.
strings.BRA_SAW_reassign_hardliners_desc: The so-called Hardliners' overambition is their weakness. Assigning some of their rank to the African frontlines will ensure they will be out of our hair for a time.
strings.BRA_SAW_reassign_sorbonne_desc: The Sorbonne are plagued by their sense of duty. Many are more than willing to serve on the frontlines of the South African War, where they will have little say in how the nation is run.
strings.BRA_SAW_reassign_const_desc: The Constitutionalists left in Brazil's armed forces are those who have kept their mouths shut. They will hardly object to being reassigned to the South African front, happy to escape scrutiny.
strings.BRA_SAW_reassign_tt: Effects when the South African War concludes:
strings.BRA_SAW_weapons_category_desc:
It was just a few decades ago that Brazilians fought valiantly against the Nazi threat across the Atlantic, fighting to defend Britain when the Germans launched Operation Sealion. Now, the jackboot threatens once again to stamp out democracy in South Africa.

Our involvement in the South African War is necessarily limited, but Brazil is uniquely positioned to help control the Atlantic and act as a backdoor for American weapons. From the Lobster War we have gained invaluable experience striking against the Nazi threat, and intelligence on their colonial forces, and we have not forgotten about the damned fascists attacking our convoys, forcing us into the war.

It's true that the war in South Africa is largely a ground war, and our recent past anti-fascist experience has been in naval affairs. And there are some at home who would prefer we have nothing to do with the Americans. But we cannot risk the Lobster War happening again, we must protect our nation from fascist influence, and we must do everything to stop another country falling to the cruel Nazi imperialists!

Brazil must succeed!
strings.BRA_SAW_brazilian_tech_assistance_desc: Due to the chaos of the war and frequent bombing raids by the Schild's air force, the South African industrial and technical spheres are in chaos. Brazil will provide technicians and engineers to South Africa to help increase production of infantry equipment and ensure there are enough guns for the South African troops to use.
strings.BRA_brazilian_tech_assistance_desc: Brazil is aiding our industry and research in researching and producing infantry equipment for the war effort.
strings.BRA_SAW_operation_search_destroy_desc: The nature of the South African War is a logistical nightmare with partisans under every bush. Boer troops with knowledge of the terrain are able to ambush our troops and then disappear without a trace. Meanwhile Schild werewolf troops have managed to penetrate through our lines and wreck havock. This must be brought to an end. We will launch Search and Destroy Operations to crush these partisans and commandos.
strings.BRA_brazilian_search_and_destroy_operati: Brazil has begun engaging in search and destroy operations. Hunting down resistance cells and Cameroonian commando units and destroying them. This will reduce the amount of resistance we face in this war from captured territory.
strings.BRA_SAW_operation_withdraw_desc: Despite the Brazilian military's best efforts, the war situation has developed not necessarily to Brazil's advantage. The Schild's advance into South Africa has not stopped and the country is on the verge of collapse. To stay any longer in the war may risk us being unable to bring our soldiers home and would be a catastrophic disaster. We can not allow this to occur and will immediately send the orders to withdraw our troops. We will send our best wishes to South Africa and the remaining Yankees, but they must fight the rest of the war on their own.

strings.BRA_MiningWar_update_desc: Our enemies will not sit idly by while we attempt to cool the situation in Bolivia. They will act behind the scenes to shore up their own support.
strings.BRA_wac_desc:
President Lacerda is eager to prove that his vocal support of a close partnership with the United States and the OFN is more than just empty prattle. With the explosion of conflict in West Africa, the Americans are once again rallying the alliance for an intervention, and Brazil shall answer the call. A wide range of operations are already in consideration: from anti-piracy operations in the Gulf of Guinea, to the deployment of both air power and ground troops to aid Free France.

Should this adventure bear fruit, we will have proven to both our partners and rivals that Brazil is not a nation to be underestimated. Failure to produce quick and decisive results, however, could easily be spun against us; casting a rather dark cloud over the President's foreign policy...
strings.BRA_WAC_reassign_hardliners_desc: The so-called Hardliners' overambition is their weakness. Assigning some of their rank to the African frontlines will ensure they will be out of our hair for a time.
strings.BRA_WAC_reassign_sorbonne_desc: The Sorbonne are plagued by their sense of duty. Many are more than willing to serve on the frontlines of the West African Crisis, where they will have little say in how the nation is run.
strings.BRA_WAC_reassign_const_desc: The Constitutionalists left in Brazil's armed forces are those who have kept their mouths shut. They will hardly object to being reassigned to the West African front, happy to escape scrutiny.

strings.BRA_WAC_brazilian_tech_assistance_desc: Due to the chaos of the war and frequent bombing raids by the PALF's air force, the Free French industrial and technical spheres are in chaos. Brazil will provide technicians and engineers to Free French to help increase production of infantry equipment and ensure there are enough guns for the Free French troops to use.
strings.BRA_WAC_operation_search_destroy_desc: The nature of the West African Crisis is a logistical nightmare with partisans under every bush. PALF troops with knowledge of the terrain are able to ambush our troops and then disappear without a trace. Meanwhile their troops have managed to penetrate through our lines and wreck havock. This must be brought to a end. We will launch Search and Destroy Operations to crush these partisans and commandos.
strings.BRA_WAC_stranglehold_desc: An army can only function as long as they have the weapons of war necessary to act. By strategically using our navy to blockade against PALF imports and shipments, Cameroon will be forced to focus on domestic production, limiting its ability to conduct military operations.

strings.BRA_SATW_hold_buenos_aires_tt: If we hold onto Buenos Aires, Argentina will be forced to capitulate

strings.BRA_Plane_Bombing_desc:
The outbreak of war with the Brazilian puppet has brought the wrath of the Brazilian Air Force down upon us. Bombs rain down upon critical infrastructure and military installations and our ability to offer resistance in the air is minimal.

This will disrupt the organisation of our forces and will damage domestic support for the war effort, but we have little choice but to press on and hope that this bombardment does not escalate further.
strings.BRA_military_advisors_desc: Our friends in Brazil have seen fit to dispatch advisors from the Brazilian Army to aid our armed forces in the current conflict. With their support we shall see a significant improvement in the overall performance of our soldiers, as well as learning important lessons about modern warfare which will improve the efficiency of our armed forces in the future.
strings.BRA_technician_aid_desc: Brazil has seen fit to dispatch technicians to aid our war effort and we are already seeing significant benefits to a range of different areas of our military and economy as a result. We can only hope that aid such as this continues to be forthcoming.
strings.BRA_sabotage_effort_desc:
The outbreak of war with the Brazilian ally has resulted in the Brazilian Intelligence Agency being unleashed against us. A wave of sabotage has swept our country as their agents set to work stealing state secrets, sabotaging military operations, and assassinating officials.

This is proving detrimental to the war effort, not only because of the direct consequences of the sabotage but also because of the paranoia gripping our government as our own agents struggle to prevent further damage.
strings.BRA_CCW_desc:
Violence. That's the best word to describe Colombia's current situation. It doesn't matter how many other ceasefires besides the 1956 one were to be put up; peace was never an option for the Colombians.

Nevertheless, this coming war is also an opportunity to secure ourselves a new ally in the northern Andes, and if we don't help to end this war as soon as possible, we will suffer from its side effects. It's time for the snake to drink some coffee in Colombia.

If successful, both us and the Yankees will aid them in La Violencia.
strings.BRA_CCW_support_none_tt: We will not intervene in the Colombian Civil War.

strings.BRA_VEN.1.desc:
The Itamaraty Palace hovered over the mirror - like the surface of its reflecting pool like a concrete mirage materialized from Kubitschek's dreams in the middle of the plateau. Walther Moreira Salles stood by the panoramic window of his office, through which the harsh, almost surgical light of the capital poured, bouncing off Niemeyer's snow-white arches. In this temple of modernism, where silence seemed part of the architectural design, the presence of the bustling FBI men felt like a violation of the laws of aesthetics - as if someone had tracked construction mud into a sterile operating room.

Grainy photos landed on the polished surface of Salles's table: empty barracks in Venezuela, silhouettes of Dominican frigates off the Colombian coast, lists of missing officers. Socialists in Caracas, a mutiny on the doorstep, the Dominican Republic preparing an invasion.

“We are stretched thin, Mr. Minister,” the FBI agent spoke harshly, chopping his sentences. “Our resources are burning in South Africa. Washington cannot open a second front. This is your job now. Brazil must become the shield of democracy on the continent.”

Salles turned slowly, adjusting the impeccable knot of his tie. Another 'polite' request. Brazil was being asked to pull the chestnuts out of the fire while Uncle Sam was busy with another blaze.

“We understand the gravity of the situation,” Salles said. “Brazil will fulfill its duty to continental security. I will contact the SFICI immediately. If a storm breaks in Caracas, we will be ready.”

When the Americans left, he sank wearily into his chair and poured himself a whiskey. He had just been handed a dirty shovel to clear the shit that Nixon was afraid to touch with his own hands.
strings.BRA_VEN.1.tt:
